title: Smaller and Faster 3DGS via Post-Training Dictionary Learning
summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is a promising neural scene representation for real-time rendering, but trained models often suffer from large memory footprints, limiting deployment on less powerful devices. Existing compression techniques often lead to architectures with several additional trainable parameters. While achieving outstanding compression ratios, they introduce noticeable drops in image quality. In this work, we introduce the first dictionary-learning-based compression framework for 3DGS. The proposed post-training compression pipeline can be deployed in virtually any 3DGS model without the need for re-training or modifications to existing 3DGS models. Our compression framework is straightforward to implement, yet provides significant compression capabilities, preserves image quality, and improves real-time rendering performance. Across 13 benchmark scenes, our approach achieves an average compression ratio of 3.95x, 3.10x, and 4.55x when applied to 3DGS, 3DGS-MCMC, and PixelGS, respectively. This yields consistent rendering speedups of 23.3%, 24.3%, and 25.3%, while maintaining image quality.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a simple post-training dictionary-learning compression method for 3DGS that works on existing models without retraining, cuts memory by about 3-4.5x, and speeds up rendering by about 23-25% without hurting visual quality.
AI.motivation: 3DGS enables real-time rendering but suffers from large memory consumption, which limits deployment on resource-constrained devices. Prior compression methods often add trainable parameters and cause visible quality degradation despite strong compression ratios.
AI.method: The paper proposes the first dictionary-learning-based compression pipeline for 3DGS. It is a post-training method that can be applied to existing 3DGS variants without modifying model architectures or retraining. The framework compresses model representations through dictionary learning to reduce memory footprint.
AI.result: Across 13 benchmark scenes, the method achieves average compression ratios of 3.95x on 3DGS, 3.10x on 3DGS-MCMC, and 4.55x on PixelGS. It also improves rendering speed by 23.3%, 24.3%, and 25.3%, respectively, while maintaining image quality.
AI.conclusion: A post-training, dictionary-learning-based compression framework can compress 3D Gaussian Splatting models substantially without retraining, while preserving image quality and improving rendering speed.

title: BijectiveRemesh: Maintaining Bijective Mappings for Data Transfer Across Remeshed Manifolds
summary:
We introduce BijectiveRemesh, a robust algorithm for maintaining a continuous, bijective mapping across complex remeshing sequences on both 2D triangle surfaces and 3D tetrahedral meshes. Unlike traditional data transfer methods that rely on interpolation or projection, our approach constructs a mathematically rigorous composite map from the input mesh to the output mesh by chaining local bijective atlases defined for each primitive remeshing operation.
  Our framework represents the overall mapping as a composition of local bijective atlases, one per remeshing operation. Building upon successive self-parameterization, we introduce a Shared Scaffold structure for 2D triangle meshes that enforces global bijectivity through local orientation preservation. We extend this approach to handle edge splits, edge swaps, and vertex smoothing beyond the original edge collapses. For 3D tetrahedral meshes, we generalize the local atlas construction using Steinitz's Theorem and Maxwell-Cremona lifting to ensure valid embeddings. This enables exact tracking of geometric entities, including points, curves, and surfaces, across remeshing, with applications from texture transfer to volumetric simulations.

AI.tldr: BijectiveRemesh tracks exact correspondences through remeshing by composing per-operation bijective maps, giving robust continuous mappings on 2D and 3D meshes without relying on interpolation or projection.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to overcome the limitations of traditional remeshing data transfer methods based on interpolation or projection, which may lose exact correspondence or fail to preserve bijectivity across complex remeshing sequences.
AI.method: The method builds a global map by composing local bijective atlases for each primitive remeshing operation. For 2D triangle meshes, it uses successive self-parameterization and a Shared Scaffold structure to enforce global bijectivity and extends support to edge collapses, edge splits, edge swaps, and vertex smoothing. For 3D tetrahedral meshes, it constructs local atlases using Steinitz's Theorem and Maxwell-Cremona lifting to guarantee valid embeddings.
AI.result: The result is a framework that can exactly track points, curves, and surfaces across remeshing operations in 2D and 3D while preserving continuity and bijectivity, making it useful for applications such as texture transfer and volumetric simulation.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that BijectiveRemesh provides a robust and mathematically rigorous way to maintain a continuous bijective map through complex remeshing sequences for both 2D triangle meshes and 3D tetrahedral meshes, enabling exact transfer and tracking of geometric entities across mesh changes.

title: SWIM: Single-Instance Whole-Body Imitation for swiMming
summary: We propose a new method for synthesizing physically-based swimming motions. Physically-based character animation aims to generate physically valid, controllable, and natural-looking motions which can respond to unexpected disturbances, where one dictating factor of difficulty is the complexity of the task, especially the level of sophistication of the required interactions with the environment. Existing research has succeeded in various tasks in static and dynamic environments. We push the difficulty further to swimming, which requires full-body coordination and continuous interactions with fluids, a new level of complexity when it comes to interacting with the environment. This complexity imposes challenges in learning control under volatile environmental forces, generalizing control to different environments and swimming styles, lack of data references, and prohibitively slow physical simulation which is inevitable during control learning. To this end, we propose SWIM, a new imitation method for swimming motions, which can learn from a single swimming motion and generalize to unseen environments, body conditions, and swimming styles. Extensive evaluation and comparison demonstrate that SWIM is data-efficient, stable, robust, and generalizable, outperforming alternative methods across multiple classes of tasks and metrics.

AI.tldr: SWIM is an imitation-learning approach for physically-based swimming animation that learns from one motion clip and generalizes well to new environments, bodies, and styles, beating prior methods on several benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Swimming is a harder physically-based animation problem than many prior tasks because it requires full-body coordination and continuous interaction with fluids. Existing methods face difficulties with unstable environmental forces, poor generalization across environments and styles, scarce motion data, and expensive simulation during learning.
AI.method: The paper proposes SWIM, a new imitation-learning method for physically-based swimming animation. It learns swimming control from a single motion example and is designed to handle continuous fluid interaction, volatile environmental forces, and slow physical simulation while enabling transfer across different conditions and styles.
AI.result: Extensive evaluations show that SWIM is data-efficient, stable, robust, and generalizable. It outperforms alternative methods across multiple task classes and evaluation metrics.
AI.conclusion: SWIM can synthesize physically-based swimming motions from a single reference motion while generalizing across unseen environments, body conditions, and swimming styles, and it outperforms alternative methods in efficiency, stability, robustness, and generalization.

title: DSD-GS: Dynamic-Static Decomposition of Gaussian Splatting for Efficient and High-Fidelity Dynamic Scene Reconstruction
summary: Dynamic scene reconstruction and novel view synthesis are fundamental to next-generation visual intelligence applications such as virtual reality, robotics, and digital twins. However, high-fidelity reconstruction of complex, time-varying scenes from arbitrary viewpoints remains a significant challenge. Existing dynamic 3DGS methods suffer from computational inefficiency, since they model all Gaussians as dynamic components. While recent decomposition-based approaches address this issue, they still struggle with degraded reconstruction quality and prolonged training time. To mitigate these limitations, we propose a novel dynamic reconstruction framework built upon an efficient static-dynamic decomposition strategy using a Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting encoder and an optical flow model. By eliminating redundant computations on static regions, our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing baselines across rendering quality, training and rendering speed, and storage efficiency. Notably, on the Neural 3D dataset, our framework requires only 10 minutes for training and achieves a rendering speed of over 700 FPS on a single NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPU at resolution of 1352x1014. Furthermore, our decomposition strategy eliminates the need for COLMAP preprocessing and enables deterministic initialization, thereby enhancing both efficiency and reproducibility.

AI.tldr: 提出一种基于静态-动态分解的高效动态 3D Gaussian Splatting 框架：少算静态区域，多关注动态变化，因此训练更快、渲染更快、占用更小，且重建质量更好，还无需 COLMAP。 / A fast dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting framework separates static from dynamic content, avoids wasted computation on static areas, improves quality and efficiency, and removes the need for COLMAP preprocessing.
AI.motivation: 动机在于现有动态 3DGS 方法通常将全部高斯视为动态成分，导致计算开销大；而已有分解式方法虽然更高效，但仍面临重建质量下降和训练时间过长的问题。作者因此希望在效率、质量和可复现性之间取得更优平衡。 / The motivation is that existing dynamic 3DGS methods are computationally inefficient because they treat all Gaussians as dynamic, while prior decomposition-based methods still suffer from lower reconstruction quality and long training time. The work aims to improve efficiency, fidelity, and reproducibility simultaneously.
AI.method: 方法上，作者将场景划分为静态区域与动态区域，仅对动态部分进行重点建模；静态部分通过高效的前馈式 Gaussian Splatting 编码器处理，动态变化借助光流模型捕获。这样可减少对静态区域的冗余计算，并实现确定性初始化。 / Methodologically, the paper decomposes scenes into static and dynamic regions, processes static content with a feed-forward Gaussian Splatting encoder, and models temporal motion with an optical flow network, reducing redundant computation and enabling deterministic initialization.
AI.result: 实验结果表明，该方法达到 SOTA 水平，在渲染质量、训练与渲染速度以及存储效率上优于现有基线。尤其在 Neural 3D 数据集上，训练仅需 10 分钟，并可在单张 NVIDIA RTX 5090 上以 1352x1014 分辨率实现超过 700 FPS 的渲染速度。 / Results show state-of-the-art performance across rendering quality, training speed, rendering speed, and storage efficiency. On the Neural 3D dataset, the method trains in only 10 minutes and renders at over 700 FPS at 1352x1014 on a single NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPU.
AI.conclusion: 该论文提出了一种基于静态-动态分解的高效动态场景重建框架，结合前馈式 Gaussian Splatting 编码器与光流模型，在保证高保真重建质量的同时显著提升训练、渲染与存储效率，并去除了 COLMAP 预处理需求。 / The paper concludes that an efficient static-dynamic decomposition framework, built with a feed-forward Gaussian Splatting encoder and an optical flow model, can substantially improve dynamic scene reconstruction quality and efficiency while removing the need for COLMAP preprocessing.

title: Conservation-Based Feedback-Circuit Decomposition for Linear Forced Systems
summary: We present a conservation-based feedback-circuit decomposition specifically for general linear forced systems. In a role parallel to that of eigenvalues and eigenvectors for initial-value problems, the complete set of independent intrinsic circuit gains and their associated forcing-transformation vectors provide a complete analytical representation of both transient and equilibrium forced solutions. The sign of intrinsic circuit gains determines whether successive feedback cycles exhibit monotonic or oscillatory convergence to transformed forcing, while the forcing-transformation vectors determine the structure of transformed forcing. The exact transient and equilibrium solutions are represented analytically through the convergence of the finite-cycle forcing-transformation kernel to the equilibrium forcing-transformation kernel, which is guaranteed regardless of whether the magnitudes of circuit gains exceed one or unstable modes exist in the system. The feedback-circuit decomposition provides a new generic foundational mathematical tool for understanding, predicting, and controlling forced responses in a broad range of coupled linear systems across science and engineering.

AI.tldr: A new circuit-based decomposition for linear forced systems plays a role similar to eigen-analysis, fully describing transient and steady forced responses and remaining reliable even in systems with large gains or unstable modes.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to provide a generic mathematical tool for analyzing, predicting, and controlling forced responses in coupled linear systems, where traditional eigenvalue/eigenvector analysis is mainly tailored to initial-value problems rather than forced dynamics.
AI.method: The method decomposes a general linear forced system into independent intrinsic feedback circuit gains and associated forcing-transformation vectors, then represents transient and equilibrium forced solutions through the convergence of finite-cycle and equilibrium forcing-transformation kernels.
AI.result: The result is an exact analytical representation of both transient and equilibrium forced solutions. The sign of intrinsic circuit gains explains monotonic versus oscillatory convergence behavior, while forcing-transformation vectors characterize the structure of the transformed forcing.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that conservation-based feedback-circuit decomposition offers a complete analytical framework for forced responses in general linear systems, analogous to eigen-analysis for initial-value problems, and remains valid even when circuit gains exceed one or unstable modes are present.

title: SubsurfaceGen: Procedural Generation of Field-Scale Earth Models and Seismic Data
summary: Full waveform inversion (FWI) is the gold standard for subsurface imaging, with applications from carbon sequestration to energy and mineral exploration to earthquake hazard assessment. Machine learning approaches to FWI need field-scale, geologically diverse, and physically realistic training data, but existing resources such as Marmousi, SEAM, and OpenFWI fall short on spatial extent, temporal extent, geological diversity, and physical realism. We address these limitations with SubsurfaceGen, a GPU-accelerated generator for 3D velocity models and seismic data. Along with SubsurfaceGen, we release a paired dataset of 4,276 2D velocity slices, 5 s wavefields, and 8 s shot gathers drawn from 42 realistic, field-scale 3D velocity models, each spanning 10 km x 10 km laterally and 6.19 km deep at 10 m resolution. The dataset spans six geological settings -- four built with SubsurfaceGen and two drawn from prior sources -- relevant for carbon sequestration and hydrocarbon exploration. We use this dataset to evaluate neural operators on wavefield prediction and encoder-decoders on end-to-end velocity inversion, holding out one geological setting for out-of-distribution testing. These experiments surface failure modes at field-scale and demonstrate how SubsurfaceGen and the associated dataset can impact ML-based FWI.

AI.tldr: The paper presents SubsurfaceGen, a GPU-based system for generating realistic large-scale seismic training data for ML-based full waveform inversion, releases a new benchmark dataset, and shows that current neural models still fail in important ways, especially on unseen geology.
AI.motivation: Existing FWI training datasets such as Marmousi, SEAM, and OpenFWI are insufficient for modern machine learning because they lack enough spatial scale, temporal duration, geological diversity, and physical realism needed for field-scale generalization.
AI.method: The paper introduces SubsurfaceGen, a GPU-accelerated generator for 3D velocity models and seismic data. Using it, the authors build a paired dataset containing 4,276 2D velocity slices, 5-second wavefields, and 8-second shot gathers from 42 realistic 3D velocity models across six geological settings. They then benchmark neural operators for wavefield prediction and encoder-decoder models for end-to-end velocity inversion, with one geological setting held out for out-of-distribution evaluation.
AI.result: The authors release a large-scale dataset derived from 42 field-scale 3D velocity models covering six geological settings relevant to carbon sequestration and hydrocarbon exploration. Their experiments show that current ML models exhibit notable failure modes at field scale and struggle with generalization to unseen geological settings.
AI.conclusion: SubsurfaceGen fills a major gap in ML-ready FWI data by generating field-scale, geologically diverse, and more physically realistic 3D subsurface models and seismic data, and the resulting benchmark reveals important failure modes in current ML approaches, especially under out-of-distribution geological conditions.

title: Cosm: Collective Switched Motion for Fast and Accurate Sparse Ising Optimization
summary: We introduce Collective Switched Motion (Cosm), a heuristic algorithm for solving sparse Ising-type optimization problems. Cosm combines locally interacting continuous circular variables with global coordination rules that facilitate collective dynamics. Pairwise interactions occur sequentially over a set of conflict-free edge partitions, resulting in an interaction network that switches periodically. Unlike conventional gradient-based approaches, Cosm enables structured, non-gradient dynamics that promote exploration beyond local minima. A correlated perturbation mechanism helps enable collective variable rotations. On the three largest Gset instances, which have 10,000-20,000 variables and represent 2D spin glasses, Cosm attains improved solutions that are verified as optimal using an exact solver. On two large bounded-degree Gset instances, a CPU-based implementation of Cosm reduces the state-of-the-art times-to-target from hundreds of hours to 36-303 s, reductions of 2-4 orders of magnitude. Additional tests on planted-solution benchmark instances show a lower scaling exponent than previous dynamical systems heuristics. These results highlight the effectiveness of Cosm in harnessing collective computation for improved sparse combinatorial optimization.

AI.tldr: Cosm is a new collective, switched-interaction heuristic for sparse Ising optimization that beats prior dynamical heuristics on very large benchmarks, reaches exact-optimal solutions on key Gset cases, and is dramatically faster on some large instances.
AI.motivation: Existing gradient-based or dynamical-system heuristics for sparse Ising optimization can get trapped in local minima and scale poorly on large sparse combinatorial problems, motivating a collective, non-gradient approach that better exploits sparse interaction structure.
AI.method: The paper proposes Collective Switched Motion (Cosm), which uses locally interacting continuous circular variables, periodically switched conflict-free edge partitions for sequential pairwise interactions, global coordination rules, and correlated perturbations to induce collective non-gradient dynamics for escaping local minima.
AI.result: On the three largest Gset instances with 10,000-20,000 variables, Cosm finds improved solutions verified as optimal by an exact solver. On two large bounded-degree Gset instances, a CPU implementation cuts state-of-the-art times-to-target from hundreds of hours to 36-303 seconds, improving by 2-4 orders of magnitude. It also shows a lower scaling exponent on planted-solution benchmarks than prior dynamical systems heuristics.
AI.conclusion: Cosm is an effective heuristic for sparse Ising-type optimization, achieving verified optimal solutions on very large Gset spin-glass instances and dramatically reducing time-to-target on large bounded-degree benchmarks.

title: Polynomial Histograms for Memory-Efficient Representation of Long-tailed System Distributions
summary:
Distributed systems must frequently keep track of many different types of performance metrics across many different computers. For example, the latency distribution of certain operations may be computed for a large combination of computers, users, and operations. These empirical distributions need to be collected at minimal expense on the individual software components, efficiently aggregated across multiple dimensions, and stored in a compact representation for a variety of downstream data analysis applications.
  We describe an information loss metric for binned data that allows us to optimize cost of information loss from different histogram representations. We explore the use of polynomial histograms where each bin of a histogram is annotated with moments of the underlying distribution in that bin. These polynomial histograms are compared to traditional histograms using the same storage cost for additional bins instead of annotations in each bin. We describe an application of these techniques for file system metrics for a large production system, and analytically characterize when polynomial histograms offer more information at lower cost.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes an information-loss framework for histogram design and shows that adding moments inside bins can beat simply adding more bins when summarizing large-scale system metrics.
AI.motivation: Large distributed systems need to collect, aggregate, and store many empirical performance distributions across multiple machines and dimensions with minimal computational and storage cost. Traditional histogram representations may waste budget or lose too much information.
AI.method: The paper defines an information-loss metric for binned data, then uses it to compare standard histograms against polynomial histograms, where each bin is augmented with moments of the data distribution. It also provides an analytical characterization of the conditions under which polynomial histograms are preferable.
AI.result: The study shows that polynomial histograms can achieve better information retention under the same storage cost than standard histograms in some regimes, and demonstrates their applicability on file-system metrics from a large production system.
AI.conclusion: Polynomial histograms can preserve more information than traditional histograms at the same storage budget by storing within-bin moments, and they are especially useful for large-scale distributed-system metrics aggregation when compactness and low overhead matter.

title: Protocol for evaluating ChatGPT in biomedical association generation and verification using a RAG-enabled, cross-model majority voting workflow
comment: Main Manuscript and Supplementary Information. Both are equally important
summary: We present a protocol to evaluate ChatGPT's ability to generate disease-centric biomedical associations. It outlines how we generate the associations, validate the biological entities using biomedical ontologies, and verify associations using literature. The protocol includes a self-consistency strategy to assess generative reliability across ChatGPT models. To address ontology exact-match limitations, we provide a use case performing semantic verification through a workflow enabled by Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) powered by open-source large language models (LLMs). This enables LLMs to establish truth over content generated by other LLMs and expose hallucination.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a protocol to test whether ChatGPT can generate trustworthy disease-related biomedical associations, combining ontology validation, literature verification, self-consistency checks, and a RAG-based semantic review to catch hallucinations.
AI.motivation: LLM-generated biomedical associations may appear plausible but can contain hallucinations or fail under exact ontology matching. A structured evaluation and stronger semantic verification method are needed to assess reliability and truthfulness.
AI.method: The paper proposes a protocol that generates disease-centric biomedical associations with ChatGPT, validates biological entities using biomedical ontologies, verifies associations against the literature, and measures reliability through a self-consistency strategy across ChatGPT models. It also demonstrates a use case of semantic verification using RAG with open-source LLMs.
AI.result: The protocol provides a practical framework for entity validation, literature-based association checking, and model self-consistency assessment. The RAG-based semantic verification use case shows how one LLM system can evaluate content produced by another and expose hallucinated associations.
AI.conclusion: A protocol can systematically evaluate ChatGPT-generated disease-centric biomedical associations, and a RAG-based semantic verification workflow can help detect hallucinations beyond strict ontology exact matching.

title: Lightweight SAR Ship Detection via Contrastive Distillation
comment: Accepted in GLSVLSI'26 special session 74: Efficiency In Computer Vision: From Image Generation to Decision"
summary: Deep convolutional and transformer-based detectors achieve strong performance for SAR ship detection but are often computationally prohibitive for real-time or onboard deployment. Lightweight models offer improved efficiency yet struggle to capture the complex structural relationships inherent in SAR backscatter. Most existing SAR knowledge-distillation approaches rely on feature or logit matching, which enforces localized activation similarity while neglecting the geometric relationships among object representations. We propose a Structured Unified Relational knowledGE distillation framework for SAR Ship detection (SURGE) that transfers relational geometry from a powerful teacher detector to a compact student detector using a contrastive InfoNCE objective in a shared projection embedding space. To the best of our knowledge, this work presents the first transformer-based SAR ship detector knowledge distillation framework in SAR domain. The framework is architecture-agnostic in the sense that it provides a common region-level distillation interface for two-stage, one-stage and transformer-based detectors without modifying their deployed architectures. Experiments on the SSDD and HRSID benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed method yields substantial improvements for two-stage detectors, achieving up to 6.2 mAP and 8.0 AP75 gains over baseline student and even surpassing teacher performance

AI.tldr: SURGE distills relational geometry, not just features, from a strong SAR ship detector into a lightweight one using contrastive learning, delivering large accuracy gains across detector types without changing deployed architectures.
AI.motivation: Existing high-performing SAR ship detectors are too computationally expensive for real-time or onboard use, while lightweight models lose important structural understanding. Prior SAR distillation methods focus on localized similarity and overlook geometric relationships among object representations, motivating a relational distillation approach.
AI.method: The paper proposes Structured Unified Relational knowledGE distillation (SURGE), which performs region-level distillation across two-stage, one-stage, and transformer-based detectors. Instead of only matching features or logits, it projects teacher and student object representations into a shared space and uses a contrastive InfoNCE objective to preserve geometric relations among regions.
AI.result: On SSDD and HRSID, SURGE substantially improves student detectors, especially two-stage models, with gains up to 6.2 mAP and 8.0 AP75 over baseline students, and in some cases even exceeds teacher performance.
AI.conclusion: SURGE is an architecture-agnostic knowledge distillation framework for SAR ship detection that transfers relational geometry from a strong teacher to a lightweight student through a shared embedding space, improving compact detectors without changing deployment architectures.

title: PhyDrawGen: Physically Grounded Diagram Generation from Natural Language
comment: 9 figures, 7 tables. Under review at EMNLP 2026
summary: Generating physics diagrams from text requires strict adherence to physical laws. While current generative models produce visually plausible outputs, they systematically hallucinate force vectors, ignore conservation laws, and violate geometric constraints. We present PhyDrawGen, a neuro-symbolic pipeline that decouples semantic scene understanding from physical constraint satisfaction. First, a large language model extracts a typed scene graph from the problem text. A deterministic solver then converts this graph into a Planar Straight-Line Graph (PSLG), encoding force balance, optical paths, and field topologies as exact geometric primitives. Finally, a fine-tuned Qwen-VL model implements a visually grounded propose-verify loop to iteratively correct any constraint violations. Evaluated on a benchmark of 1,449 problems spanning mechanics, optics, and electromagnetism, PhyDrawGen significantly outperforms GPT-5-image, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Gemini 3 Pro, demonstrating robust physical accuracy even on unusual-object problems.

AI.tldr: PhyDrawGen把“理解题意”“满足物理约束”“视觉修正”拆成三个阶段，用符号几何约束保证物理正确性，因此比纯生成式模型更会画对物理图。 / PhyDrawGen splits the task into scene understanding, symbolic physical constraint satisfaction, and visual correction, which makes it much better than end-to-end generative models at drawing physically correct diagrams.
AI.motivation: 动机在于现有生成模型虽然能画出表面上合理的物理图，但经常产生力矢量幻觉、忽略守恒定律并破坏几何约束，因此需要一种把视觉生成与物理一致性显式结合的方法。 / The motivation is that current generative models produce visually plausible physics diagrams but often hallucinate force vectors, ignore conservation laws, and violate geometric constraints, so an approach is needed that explicitly enforces physical consistency rather than relying on implicit visual plausibility.
AI.method: 方法上，论文提出一个神经符号流水线：先由大语言模型从题目文本中抽取带类型的场景图；再由确定性求解器把场景图转换为PSLG（平面直线图），以精确几何原语编码受力平衡、光路和场拓扑；最后由微调的Qwen-VL执行基于视觉的提出-验证迭代修正约束违例。 / The paper proposes a neuro-symbolic pipeline: an LLM first extracts a typed scene graph from text; a deterministic solver converts it into a Planar Straight-Line Graph (PSLG) that encodes force balance, optical paths, and field topology as exact geometric primitives; a fine-tuned Qwen-VL model then runs a visually grounded propose-verify loop to iteratively fix constraint violations.
AI.result: 在包含1449道力学、光学和电磁学问题的基准上，PhyDrawGen显著优于GPT-5-image、Gemini 2.5 Flash和Gemini 3 Pro，并在不常见物体问题上仍表现出稳健的物理准确性。 / On a benchmark of 1,449 problems across mechanics, optics, and electromagnetism, PhyDrawGen significantly outperforms GPT-5-image, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Gemini 3 Pro, with robust physical accuracy even for unusual-object problems.
AI.conclusion: PhyDrawGen通过将语义理解、符号约束求解与视觉校验解耦，能够比现有通用生成模型更稳定地生成符合物理规律的图示，尤其在非常规物体场景下仍保持较高物理准确性。 / PhyDrawGen shows that decoupling semantic understanding, symbolic constraint solving, and visual verification leads to substantially more physically accurate diagram generation than general-purpose image models, including on unusual-object cases.

title: MultiAct: Text-to-Motion Generation from Composite Text via Tailored Attention Guidance
comment: Accepted to SIGGRAPH 2026 conference. Project page: https://natsala13.github.io/multiact.github.io
summary: Text-to-motion generation has progressed rapidly in recent years, offering an expressive interface for animation and human-computer interaction. However, current models remain brittle when handling prompts that describe multiple actions occurring at the same time. Rather than realizing all components of a composite description, models frequently prioritize a single dominant action and neglect the rest, leading to incomplete or ambiguous motion. We present MultiAct, an unpaired, inference-time framework for compositional text-to-motion synthesis that operates directly on pretrained motion generators without retraining or architectural modification. Our method counteracts semantic collapse by adaptively amplifying cross-attention scores associated with underrepresented prompt components. We note that effective modulation depends on prompt-specific choices, such as which tokens and layers to target, and introduce a lightweight auxiliary decision scheme that determines the most effective attention-strengthening parametrization. Extensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations demonstrate that MultiAct consistently outperforms existing baselines on composite prompts, achieving improved semantic coverage while preserving motion realism. Project page: https://natsala13.github.io/multiact.github.io.

AI.tldr: MultiAct boosts neglected parts of a multi-action text prompt at inference time through adaptive cross-attention strengthening, enabling pretrained text-to-motion models to better realize composite actions without retraining.
AI.motivation: Existing text-to-motion models often fail on prompts containing multiple simultaneous actions, collapsing to one dominant action and ignoring other semantic components, which causes incomplete or ambiguous motion.
AI.method: The paper proposes MultiAct, an unpaired inference-time method that directly works on pretrained motion generators by adaptively amplifying cross-attention scores for underrepresented prompt components. It also uses a lightweight auxiliary decision scheme to choose prompt-specific token/layer targeting and attention-strengthening parameters.
AI.result: Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments show that MultiAct consistently outperforms prior baselines on composite prompts, improving semantic coverage while maintaining motion realism.
AI.conclusion: MultiAct is an effective inference-time framework that improves compositional text-to-motion generation for multi-action prompts without retraining or modifying pretrained motion generators.

title: Learning effective Sargassum transport dynamics from limited drifter observations
summary: Floating-material transport is influenced by unresolved processes that are often absent from available circulation products. We develop a data-driven transport-learning framework for learning effective transport corrections from limited Lagrangian observations using physically motivated ocean--atmosphere diagnostics and finite-memory representations motivated in part by inertial-particle memory effects. The diagnostic representation is analyzed through predictive and sparse symbolic-discovery approaches under leave-one-trajectory-out validation. Applications to Sargassum-following drifters in the Puerto Rico region and the Gulf Stream show that the diagnostics contain transport-relevant information beyond the baseline circulation products. Multilayer perceptron (MLP) ensembles provide flexible predictive trajectory corrections, while Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) tests whether instantaneous or delayed sparse symbolic transport structure can be extracted from the diagnostics. The results differ across flow regimes: (i) in Puerto Rico, delayed sparse symbolic corrections provide modest but systematic improvement; (ii) in the Gulf Stream application, dynamically useful sparse symbolic corrections remain primarily instantaneous even though delayed predictive information persists. These results support finite-memory transport effects in coarse-grained floating-material transport while also illustrating the difficulty of obtaining stable delayed sparse symbolic closures.

AI.tldr: A data-driven framework uses physics-based diagnostics and memory features to improve floating-material transport prediction from sparse drifter data. Neural models learn useful corrections in multiple regions, while sparse symbolic models reveal that memory effects matter but are hard to capture robustly, especially in complex flows.
AI.motivation: Available circulation products miss unresolved processes that affect floating-material transport. The work is motivated by the need to recover these missing transport effects from limited trajectory observations in a physically interpretable way, including possible finite-memory effects related to inertial-particle dynamics.
AI.method: The paper develops a transport-learning framework that learns effective transport corrections from limited Lagrangian observations using ocean-atmosphere diagnostics and finite-memory features. It evaluates these diagnostics with leave-one-trajectory-out validation, using multilayer perceptron ensembles for predictive correction and SINDy for sparse symbolic discovery of instantaneous and delayed transport structure.
AI.result: In both the Puerto Rico Sargassum-drifter case and the Gulf Stream case, the diagnostics provide transport-relevant information beyond baseline circulation products. MLP ensembles produce useful flexible corrections. SINDy shows regime-dependent outcomes: delayed sparse symbolic corrections yield modest but systematic gains in Puerto Rico, whereas in the Gulf Stream the useful sparse symbolic structure is mostly instantaneous despite persistent delayed predictive information.
AI.conclusion: The study concludes that data-driven corrections built from physically motivated diagnostics and finite-memory representations can improve coarse-grained floating-material transport estimates beyond baseline circulation products, but extracting stable delayed sparse symbolic closures is difficult and regime dependent.

title: Testing the physical reality of tidal bulges in the world's oceans
comment: 18 pages, 6 figures, 1 table. Sci. China Earth Sci. (2026)
summary: Persistent alternation of high and low water in coastal and oceanic regions has attracted human attention for millennia. This movement of water is generally explained through the double water bulge model. Although this model has been widely adopted in the scientific literature on tides since the 18th century, the physical existence of water bulges on the Earth's surface has yet to be verified. Herein, we establish a lunar angle phase-dependent statistical analysis of tide patterns at 362,370 oceanic locations spotted by Jason-3 satellite of AVISO in 2021 to address this issue. We show that during lunar angle phases of 0 degree-45 degree and 135 degree-180 degree, which spatially correspond to the water bulging regions expected in the double water bulge model, the number of low tides consistently exceeds that of high tides. Conversely, during lunar angle phase of 45 degree-135 degree, which spatially correspond to the water-depressing region expected in the model, high tides predominantly outnumber low tides. These findings evidently contradict the physical existence of two water bulges in the world's oceans, suggesting that the scientific community should pay additional attention to alternative explanations for tides, such as gravitational forcing mechanism and oceanic basin oscillation-generated driving mechanism.

AI.tldr: Using 2021 Jason-3 satellite data from 362,370 ocean locations, the paper statistically compares tide states across lunar-angle phases and finds the observed global pattern is opposite to what the classic double water bulge model predicts, arguing for renewed consideration of alternative tide mechanisms.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to test whether the physically assumed ocean-surface water bulges in the long-accepted double water bulge model actually exist, since the model is widely used but the bulges themselves have not been directly verified.
AI.method: The authors perform a lunar-angle-phase-dependent statistical analysis of tide patterns across 362,370 oceanic locations observed by the Jason-3 AVISO satellite in 2021, comparing the frequency of high and low tides within angular phase ranges associated with predicted bulging and depressing regions.
AI.result: They report that in lunar angle phases 0°-45° and 135°-180°, where the model would predict water bulges, low tides outnumber high tides; in 45°-135°, where the model would predict depressed water, high tides outnumber low tides. They interpret this pattern as contradicting the double water bulge model.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that the classic double water bulge model is not supported by their global statistical observations from satellite-derived tide patterns, and that alternative mechanisms for tides deserve more attention.

title: CamGeo: Sparse Camera-Conditioned Image-to-Video Generation with 3D Geometry Priors
summary: Sparse camera-conditioned image-to-video generation presents a pivotal challenge: synthesizing geometrically consistent 3D motion from minimal pose cues. Existing methods, which largely rely on dense supervision or naive interpolation, suffer from severe pose drift and motion discontinuities due to the lack of robust 3D priors. In this paper, we introduce CamGeo, a novel framework that distills rich 3D geometric knowledge from a pre-trained video-to-3D model (VGGT) directly into the diffusion backbone. To achieve this without incurring inference latency, we propose a training-only distillation strategy. Specifically, CamGeo incorporates: (1) keyframe trajectory distillation that enforces cycle-consistency with sparse input poses, (2) cross-frame consistency distillation with both camera trajectory and depth constraints to generate consistent structure across unsupervised frames, and (3) a three-stage coarse-to-fine curriculum learning, progressively scales geometric complexity, from global structure coherence to fine-grained refinement, achieving stable optimization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CamGeo achieves consistent improvements under various sparsity ratios.

AI.tldr: CamGeo把预训练视频到3D模型的几何知识在训练阶段蒸馏进扩散模型，通过关键帧、跨帧约束和分阶段课程学习，在不增加推理成本的前提下显著改善稀疏相机条件下的视频生成一致性。 / CamGeo distills 3D priors from a pretrained video-to-3D model into a diffusion model during training only, using keyframe constraints, cross-frame consistency, and curriculum learning to improve sparse camera-conditioned video generation without extra inference cost.
AI.motivation: 动机在于现有稀疏相机条件图像到视频方法过度依赖密集监督或简单插值，缺乏稳健3D先验，因而容易出现位姿漂移和运动不连续。作者希望利用现有强大的视频到3D模型知识来缓解这些问题，但又不牺牲推理效率。 / The motivation is that existing sparse camera-conditioned image-to-video methods depend on dense supervision or naive interpolation and lack robust 3D priors, leading to pose drift and motion discontinuity. The paper aims to exploit strong knowledge from a pretrained video-to-3D model while keeping inference efficient.
AI.method: 方法核心是从预训练VGGT蒸馏3D几何知识到扩散模型，并采用三部分设计：1）关键帧轨迹蒸馏，用循环一致性约束稀疏输入位姿；2）跨帧一致性蒸馏，同时施加相机轨迹与深度约束，提升无监督帧之间的结构一致性；3）三阶段由粗到细的课程学习，从全局结构到细粒度细化逐步提升几何复杂度。 / The method distills 3D geometric knowledge from pretrained VGGT into the diffusion model using three components: (1) keyframe trajectory distillation with cycle-consistency under sparse poses, (2) cross-frame consistency distillation with trajectory and depth constraints for unsupervised frames, and (3) a three-stage coarse-to-fine curriculum that progressively increases geometric complexity.
AI.result: 实验表明，CamGeo在不同相机稀疏率设置下都取得了一致改进，表现为更好的几何一致性、结构稳定性以及更连续的3D运动生成。 / Experiments show consistent gains across multiple sparsity ratios, with improved geometric consistency, structural stability, and smoother 3D motion generation.
AI.conclusion: CamGeo通过仅在训练阶段进行几何蒸馏，将预训练视频到3D模型中的几何先验注入扩散主干，在稀疏相机条件下显著提升了图像到视频生成的几何一致性与运动稳定性，同时不增加推理时延。 / CamGeo shows that training-only geometric distillation can inject strong 3D priors from a pretrained video-to-3D model into a diffusion backbone, substantially improving geometric consistency and motion stability for sparse camera-conditioned image-to-video generation without added inference latency.

title: Energy-Efficient Aggregation and Minimum-Degree Spanning Trees in Radio Networks
summary:
We study the aggregation problem in synchronous multi-hop radio networks with $O(\log n)$-bit messages and no collision detection. Each node initially holds a value, and the goal is to compute a global aggregate such as the sum of all values. Aggregation tasks arise naturally in wireless sensor networks, where nodes are often battery-powered and radio activity is the dominant source of energy consumption. Accordingly, our main objective is to minimize the energy complexity, defined as the maximum number of rounds in which any node is awake.
  Our main result is a randomized distributed algorithm that, with high probability, constructs and executes an aggregation schedule in $O(n \operatorname{polylog} n)$ rounds and using $O(Δ^\ast \operatorname{polylog} n)$ energy, where $Δ^\ast$ is the minimum possible maximum degree of a spanning tree of the network graph. This guarantee is nearly optimal: for any aggregation schedule and any graph, there exists a node that must be awake for at least $Δ^\ast$ rounds.
  As a by-product, the algorithm also computes a spanning tree whose maximum degree is within an $O(\log n)$ factor of $Δ^\ast$, with the same round and energy guarantees. For every tree edge, both endpoints learn that the edge belongs to the tree.

AI.tldr: A randomized algorithm achieves near-optimal energy-efficient aggregation in radio networks by building a low-degree spanning tree and running aggregation in O(n polylog n) rounds and O(Δ* polylog n) energy.
AI.motivation: Aggregation is a core task in wireless sensor and radio networks, where nodes are often battery-powered. Since radio usage dominates energy consumption, the key motivation is to minimize energy complexity rather than only round complexity.
AI.method: The authors design a randomized distributed algorithm that constructs and executes an aggregation schedule in synchronous multi-hop radio networks with O(log n)-bit messages and no collision detection. The algorithm also builds a spanning tree and schedules communication so that both time and per-node awake rounds are controlled.
AI.result: With high probability, the algorithm completes aggregation in O(n polylog n) rounds using O(Δ* polylog n) energy, where Δ* is the minimum possible maximum degree among all spanning trees of the graph. It also produces a spanning tree with maximum degree within an O(log n) factor of Δ*, and both endpoints of every tree edge learn that the edge is in the tree.
AI.conclusion: The paper shows that aggregation in synchronous multi-hop radio networks can be performed with nearly optimal energy complexity: a randomized distributed algorithm achieves O(n polylog n) rounds and O(Δ* polylog n) energy with high probability, and this is near-optimal because some node must spend at least Ω(Δ*) awake rounds in any schedule.

title: Exploring Autonomous Agentic Data Engineering for Model Specialization
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong performance on general tasks, while often struggling to adapt to specialized domains without high-quality domain-specific data. Existing LLM-based data curation methods primarily rely on human-designed workflows, leaving it unexamined whether LLMs can autonomously execute an end-to-end data engineering pipeline for model specialization. We formalize \textbf{Autonomous Agentic Data Engineering}, a novel task designed to evaluate LLMs as autonomous data engineers that drive model specialization through end-to-end data curation. We frame data as an optimizable component and study agents that plan, generate, and iteratively optimize training data across multiple domains, guided by post-training performance improvement. Experiments show that autonomous LLM data engineers yield substantial gains, as GPT-5.2 constructs a training curriculum that improves a student model by \textbf{57.29\%}, entirely through iterative, agent-driven data adaptation. By illuminating both potential and bottlenecks, our study establishes autonomous data engineering as a measurable capability and charts a path toward agent-driven model specialization\footnote{Code will be released at https://github.com/zjunlp/DataAgent.}.

AI.tldr: The paper asks whether LLMs can autonomously run the full data-engineering loop for domain adaptation, and shows they can significantly improve a student model by iteratively creating and refining training data.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that LLMs perform well generally but adapt poorly to specialized domains without strong domain data, and existing data curation pipelines still depend heavily on human-designed workflows.
AI.method: The authors formalize Autonomous Agentic Data Engineering as a task where an LLM agent plans, generates, evaluates, and iteratively optimizes training data across domains, using post-training performance as the optimization signal.
AI.result: Experiments show substantial improvement from autonomous data engineering; specifically, GPT-5.2 builds a training curriculum that improves a student model by 57.29% through iterative agent-driven data adaptation.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that LLMs can act as autonomous data engineers for end-to-end domain data curation, and that this capability can materially improve downstream model specialization while also exposing current bottlenecks.

title: SANA-Streaming: Real-time Streaming Video Editing with Hybrid Diffusion Transformer
summary: Real-time streaming video-to-video editing (V2V) is critical for interactive applications such as live broadcasting and gaming, yet it remains a formidable challenge due to the stringent requirements for temporal consistency and inference throughput. In this paper, we present SANA-Streaming, a system-algorithm co-designed framework for high-resolution, real-time streaming video editing on consumer GPUs, with the following three core designs: (1) Hybrid Diffusion Transformer architecture introduces softmax attention in part of the blocks to improve local modeling capabilities while preserving the efficiency of linear layers. (2) Cycle-Reverse Regularization is a novel training strategy that enforces semantic consistency by predicting source frames from generated content via flow matching, improving temporal consistency without requiring paired long edited videos. (3) Efficient System Co-design combines fused GDN kernels and Mixed-Precision Quantization (MPQ) optimized for the NVIDIA Blackwell (RTX 5090) architecture. By profiling real-world throughput, our MPQ maximizes Tensor Core utilization while maintaining generation quality. The resulting system achieves real-time 1280 x 704 resolution editing at 24 end-to-end FPS on a single RTX 5090 GPU, with the DiT core running at 58 FPS. Experimental results demonstrate that our co-design approach significantly outperforms existing SOTA methods in both temporal coherence and system throughput.

AI.tldr: SANA-Streaming enables real-time high-resolution video-to-video editing on an RTX 5090 by jointly redesigning the model, training strategy, and GPU execution stack.
AI.motivation: Real-time streaming V2V editing is important for interactive scenarios like live broadcasting and gaming, but existing methods struggle to simultaneously satisfy temporal consistency and real-time inference speed, especially at high resolution on consumer hardware.
AI.method: The paper proposes three coordinated components: a Hybrid Diffusion Transformer that mixes softmax attention with efficient linear layers, Cycle-Reverse Regularization to improve semantic and temporal consistency through reverse prediction via flow matching, and an efficient deployment stack using fused GDN kernels plus Mixed-Precision Quantization optimized for NVIDIA Blackwell/RTX 5090.
AI.result: The system reaches real-time editing at 1280 x 704 and 24 end-to-end FPS on a single RTX 5090, while the DiT core runs at 58 FPS. Experiments report better temporal coherence and higher system throughput than existing SOTA approaches.
AI.conclusion: SANA-Streaming shows that a system-algorithm co-design can deliver high-resolution, real-time streaming video-to-video editing on a consumer GPU, achieving stronger temporal coherence and higher throughput than prior state-of-the-art methods.

title: Physically Viable World Models: A Case for Query-Conditioned Embodied AI
comment: 21 pages; Adam J. Thorpe and Stepan Tretiakov contributed equally
summary: World models for embodied AI must be physically viable: constructed to answer intervention queries by representing the physical structure governing action outcomes, rather than merely predicting future observations. Existing observation-predictive world models can produce visually plausible but physically wrong rollouts. This failure is structural; distinct physical systems can look identical yet diverge under intervention. We expose this problem with controlled benchmarks that fix the visible scene while varying latent physics. We show that such models may recommend infeasible actions, mispredict interaction outcomes, or certify unsafe behavior. We argue that embodied AI requires world models that identify the simplest physical abstraction sufficient to answer an intervention query. Such a model comprises modular components, including environment representation, latent state and parameter estimation, action specification, interventional dynamics, and query-level response. An autonomous orchestrator should identify the relevant abstraction and compose compatible learned and structured components per query. When closed-form physics is unavailable, uncertain, or costly, the transition model may be analytic, simulated, learned, or hybrid, but it must preserve the structure that determines interventional outcomes. This decomposition makes the model interpretable, its components verifiable, and its outputs auditable against the query. It also provides a design principle for new world models and a feasibility test for existing ones: the right abstraction is not the most detailed model of the world, but the simplest model that preserves the distinctions relevant to the query. We demonstrate this approach on queries that existing systems fail to answer correctly, and outline how an orchestrator can dynamically assemble and adapt physically viable models for planning, control, and verification.

AI.tldr: World models for robots should model the physical structure that determines what happens when actions are taken, using the simplest query-relevant abstraction, because predicting what scenes look like is not enough for correct planning or safety.
AI.motivation: Current world models can generate visually plausible rollouts while being physically incorrect under intervention, which makes them unreliable for planning, control, and safety-critical verification in embodied AI.
AI.method: The paper critiques observation-predictive world models, introduces controlled benchmarks where visible observations are fixed but latent physics varies, and proposes a modular decomposition of physically viable world models with an autonomous orchestrator that selects and composes analytic, simulated, learned, or hybrid components per query.
AI.result: The authors show that existing models fail on intervention-sensitive queries, sometimes recommending infeasible or unsafe actions, and demonstrate that a modular, query-conditioned physically grounded approach can correctly answer cases where current systems fail.
AI.conclusion: Embodied AI needs physically viable world models that answer intervention queries using the simplest physical abstraction that preserves intervention-relevant distinctions, rather than relying on observation prediction alone.

title: Gait2Hip-60: A Unified Deep Learning Benchmark for Predicting Hip Muscle Forces and Joint Moments from Multi-Cadence Gait Kinematics
comment: 16 pages, 9 figures. Code and dataset publicly available
summary: Estimating hip muscle forces and joint moments during gait typically relies on musculoskeletal simulation, which is informative but time-consuming and difficult to apply in clinical settings. This study developed a deep learning framework to predict these hip dynamics parameters directly from lower-limb gait kinematics and compared three representative sequence models under a unified protocol. Gait data were collected from 60 healthy adults under three metronome-guided cadence conditions. Ten bilateral lower-limb joint angles were used as inputs, and OpenSim-derived hip muscle forces and hip joint moments were used as reference outputs. Three deep learning models of LSTM, Transformer, and Mamba were trained and evaluated using the same subject-level split, preprocessing pipeline, and metrics. The best model was then directly tested on an external cohort of 9 patients with osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) without retraining. In the healthy-subject benchmark, Transformer achieved the best subject-level mean performance for both hip muscle force prediction (RMSE = 1.33 N/kg, MAE = 0.57 N/kg, R2 = 0.819) and hip joint moment prediction (RMSE = 0.11 Nm/kg, MAE = 0.07 Nm/kg, R2 = 0.862), with similar advantages across walking cadences. In zero-shot external validation, Transformer retained moderate predictive ability in ONFH for hip muscle force prediction (RMSE = 1.51 N/kg, MAE = 0.70 N/kg, R2 = 0.537) and hip joint moment prediction (RMSE = 0.17 Nm/kg, MAE = 0.12 Nm/kg, R2 = 0.569). These findings support the feasibility of estimating hip dynamics from gait kinematics, identify Transformer as a strong baseline, and highlight the need for broader pathological validation and improved generalization before clinical application.

AI.tldr: This paper replaces slow musculoskeletal simulation with a deep learning approach that predicts hip muscle forces and joint moments directly from gait kinematics. Among LSTM, Transformer, and Mamba, Transformer performed best on healthy subjects and generalized moderately to ONFH patients without retraining, making it a strong baseline but not yet ready for clinical use.
AI.motivation: Traditional estimation of hip muscle forces and joint moments depends on musculoskeletal simulation, which is accurate and informative but time-consuming and difficult to integrate into routine clinical workflows. The paper aims to develop a faster, more clinically practical alternative that can infer these dynamics directly from gait kinematics, while also comparing representative sequence models fairly under a unified benchmark.
AI.method: The authors collected gait data from 60 healthy adults walking under three metronome-guided cadence conditions. Ten bilateral lower-limb joint angles were used as model inputs, and OpenSim-generated hip muscle forces and hip joint moments served as reference targets. Three sequence models—LSTM, Transformer, and Mamba—were trained and evaluated under the same subject-level split, preprocessing workflow, and performance metrics. The best-performing model was then tested zero-shot on an external cohort of 9 ONFH patients without retraining.
AI.result: In healthy subjects, the Transformer achieved the best mean subject-level performance for hip muscle force prediction (RMSE 1.33 N/kg, MAE 0.57 N/kg, R2 0.819) and hip joint moment prediction (RMSE 0.11 Nm/kg, MAE 0.07 Nm/kg, R2 0.862), and it maintained similar advantages across different walking cadences. In zero-shot external validation on ONFH patients, the Transformer preserved moderate predictive performance for hip muscle force prediction (RMSE 1.51 N/kg, MAE 0.70 N/kg, R2 0.537) and hip joint moment prediction (RMSE 0.17 Nm/kg, MAE 0.12 Nm/kg, R2 0.569).
AI.conclusion: The study concludes that hip muscle forces and hip joint moments can be estimated directly from lower-limb gait kinematics using deep learning, with the Transformer model providing the strongest and most consistent performance among LSTM, Transformer, and Mamba. However, external validation on ONFH patients showed only moderate generalization, indicating that broader pathological validation and improved model robustness are still required before clinical deployment.

title: A non-intrusive approach to index-aware learning
summary: We present a non-intrusive version of the index-aware learning framework introduced in arXiv:2309.00958. Index-aware learning itself is an approach for learning the time and parameter dependent solutions of differential-algebraic equations (DAEs), in particular those of electrical circuits. A key feature of the approach is that it ensures the learned solutions to remain physics-consistent, i.e.\ inherent constraints of the solution, such as e.g.\ Kirchhoff's laws, remain fulfilled. In general, this is achieved by leveraging a decoupling of the DAE into its differential and algebraic parts, while the non-intrusive version of the approach additionally relies on results from arXiv:2604.20475 and arXiv:2107.07755. We illustrate the overall workflow and compare the non-intrusive and intrusive versions using a buck converter as an example.

AI.tldr: A non-intrusive version of index-aware learning is proposed for DAEs in circuit models; it preserves physical constraints by separating differential and algebraic parts, and is demonstrated on a buck converter against the intrusive approach.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to learn time- and parameter-dependent solutions of DAEs, especially in electrical circuits, in a way that remains physics-consistent without requiring an intrusive formulation.
AI.method: The method extends index-aware learning for DAEs by using a decoupling into differential and algebraic components to enforce constraints, and in the non-intrusive setting additionally incorporates ideas/results from arXiv:2604.20475 and arXiv:2107.07755.
AI.result: The reported result is a complete non-intrusive workflow for index-aware learning and a comparative study between intrusive and non-intrusive versions using a buck converter.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that a non-intrusive extension of index-aware learning can learn solutions of DAEs while preserving physical consistency, and that its workflow can be practically demonstrated and compared against the intrusive variant on a buck converter example.

title: A Datalog Framework for Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types
comment: Paper presented at the 42nd International Conference on Logic Programming (ICLP 2026), Lisbon, Portugal, July 20 to July 23, 2026
summary:
Distributed applications increasingly support local-first collaboration over shared data, allowing multiple users to perform updates concurrently without global coordination. Such collaboration requires careful design to capture the intended semantics of the concurrent interactions.
  We introduce a declarative framework for specifying and reasoning about the semantics of conflict-free replicated data types (CRDTs) and CRDT-based applications in Datalog. The framework models CRDT semantics as executable logic programs over operation contexts, making concurrency explicit and compositional, and thus amenable to automated analysis. As one application, we use property-based testing to compare implementations. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to systematically use Datalog as a foundation for prototyping and analyzing complex CRDTs and their compositions.
  We evaluate our methodology using a collaborative graph data editing case study and report experimentation results assessing correctness validation and scalability with an increasing number of operations and replicas.

AI.tldr: 论文提出了一个基于 Datalog 的 CRDT 语义声明式分析框架，可显式建模并发、支持组合推理，并通过性质测试和协同图编辑案例验证其正确性与可扩展性。/ The paper presents a Datalog-based declarative framework for modeling and analyzing CRDT semantics, explicitly captures concurrency, supports compositional reasoning, and validates correctness and scalability through property-based testing and a collaborative graph editing case study.
AI.motivation: 动机在于本地优先协作应用允许多个用户在无全局协调下并发更新共享数据，而要正确表达这些并发交互的预期语义非常困难，因此需要一种既精确又可分析的形式化方法。/ The motivation is that local-first collaborative applications allow multiple users to update shared data concurrently without global coordination, and accurately capturing the intended semantics of such concurrent interactions is difficult, creating a need for a precise and analyzable formal method.
AI.method: 作者提出了一个声明式框架，用 Datalog 将 CRDT 语义建模为基于操作上下文的可执行逻辑程序，使并发行为显式化并支持组合分析；同时结合基于性质的测试来比较具体实现。/ The authors propose a declarative framework that models CRDT semantics in Datalog as executable logic programs over operation contexts, making concurrency explicit and compositional; they also use property-based testing to compare implementations.
AI.result: 论文通过协同图数据编辑案例评估该方法，并报告了在正确性验证以及随操作数和副本数增加时的可扩展性方面的实验结果，表明该方法具有实践可行性。/ The paper evaluates the approach with a collaborative graph editing case study and reports experimental results on correctness validation and scalability as the number of operations and replicas increases, indicating practical feasibility.
AI.conclusion: 该论文表明，使用 Datalog 可以作为一种可执行、可组合且便于自动化分析的基础，用于系统化地原型设计、推理和验证复杂 CRDT 及其组合语义。/ The paper concludes that Datalog can serve as an executable, compositional, and automation-friendly foundation for systematically prototyping, reasoning about, and validating the semantics of complex CRDTs and their compositions.

title: Domain Adaptation and Reasoning Frameworks in Language Models: A Controlled Experiment with Historical Cosmology
summary: We investigate how domain adaptation reshapes explanatory behavior in language models using historical cosmology as a controlled setting. In Phase 1, we train a small language model from scratch on a pre-Copernican corpus from which explicit heliocentric references were removed, and evaluate whether Earth-motion or heliocentric continuations nevertheless emerge. In Phase 2, we fine-tune a larger pretrained model using QLoRA on the same corpus in order to study how adaptation modifies explanatory framing and cosmological stance. Model outputs are evaluated using an LLM-as-judge framework that labels both cosmological stance (geocentric, heliocentric, or ambiguous) and explanatory frame (premodern versus modern). In the constrained setting of Phase 1, the smaller models occasionally generate local Earth-motion continuations, but these remain globally unstable and insufficient to support coherent cosmological reasoning. In Phase 2, fine-tuning induces a large and statistically significant shift toward premodern explanatory framing, while the conditional cosmological stance distributions remain comparatively stable within those frames. As a result, increases in geocentric outputs arise primarily from redistribution over explanatory regimes rather than from direct modification of stance. These results suggest that domain adaptation may primarily reshape the linguistic frameworks from which continuations are generated, with changes in stance emerging secondarily from those shifts.

AI.tldr: Training on a historical corpus does not directly make a model truly geocentric; instead, adaptation mostly makes it explain things in a premodern way, and that framing indirectly increases geocentric-seeming outputs.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to understand how domain adaptation changes not just what language models say, but the explanatory style and conceptual framing from which their responses are generated.
AI.method: The study has two phases: (1) train a small language model from scratch on a pre-Copernican corpus with explicit heliocentric references removed, then test whether heliocentric or Earth-motion continuations still emerge; (2) fine-tune a larger pretrained model on the same corpus using QLoRA, then evaluate outputs with an LLM-as-judge that labels cosmological stance and explanatory frame.
AI.result: In Phase 1, small models sometimes produce local Earth-motion continuations, but these are unstable and do not support coherent global cosmological reasoning. In Phase 2, fine-tuning causes a strong shift toward premodern explanatory framing, while stance distributions within each frame remain relatively stable. The rise in geocentric outputs is therefore mainly due to more outputs being generated within premodern frames.
AI.conclusion: Domain adaptation mainly changes the explanatory framework used by language models, and shifts in cosmological stance appear mostly as a secondary consequence of that reframing rather than direct stance change.

title: DTG-Restore: Training-Free Diffusion Refinement for Generative Video Super-Resolution
summary: Recent progress in video diffusion models has enabled remarkable generative fidelity, yet leveraging these priors for restoration remains limited by the strong coupling between conditional and unconditional branches in standard classifier-free guidance. We introduce a training-free framework that enhances distorted and low-resolution videos by decoupling these signals in time. Our proposed Decoupled Time Guidance (DTG) evaluates the unconditional branch at a cleaner diffusion timestep, providing a lookahead prior that preserves geometry while suppressing replication of warped content. This temporal bias is annealed throughout sampling, allowing the model to transition from structure correction to detail refinement without retraining. Combined with any off-the-shelf restoration module in a plug-and-play manner, our approach improves perceptual coherence and restores plausible structure in AIgenerated and real-world videos alike. To facilitate evaluation, we curate GenWarp480, a benchmark of 4,400 distorted 480p videos synthesized from diverse text-to-video models. GenWarp480 focuses on characteristic generative degradations such as warped faces, body misalignments, and spatial artifacts, providing a purpose-built testbed for assessing robustness to generative errors. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves significant improvements in structural fidelity and temporal stability without any model training.

AI.tldr: A training-free video restoration method, DTG, improves distorted videos by using the unconditional diffusion branch at a cleaner timestep as a lookahead prior, then gradually reducing this bias during sampling. It works with existing restoration modules and shows better structure and temporal consistency on a new benchmark and real-world videos.
AI.motivation: Standard classifier-free guidance in video diffusion restoration tightly couples conditional and unconditional branches, limiting the ability to exploit strong generative priors for correcting distortions and low-resolution content. The paper aims to leverage video diffusion priors more effectively for restoration without retraining.
AI.method: The method introduces Decoupled Time Guidance (DTG), which evaluates the unconditional branch at a cleaner diffusion timestep than the conditional branch during classifier-free guidance. This creates a lookahead prior that corrects geometry and suppresses distorted content replication. The temporal bias is annealed during sampling so the process shifts from coarse structural correction to fine detail refinement. The framework is training-free and can be combined with existing restoration modules.
AI.result: The paper reports significant gains in perceptual coherence, plausible structural restoration, structural fidelity, and temporal stability without model training. It also introduces GenWarp480, a benchmark of 4,400 distorted 480p videos designed to evaluate robustness to generative errors such as warped faces, body misalignment, and spatial artifacts.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that Decoupled Time Guidance (DTG) is a training-free and plug-and-play way to improve video restoration by decoupling conditional and unconditional guidance across diffusion timesteps, yielding better structural fidelity and temporal stability on both AI-generated and real-world videos.

title: Transforming and Encoding FTS for SAT Solving: What Helps, What Hurts (Extended Version)
summary:
Factored tasks are a classical planning representation that extends SAS+ with limited forms of disjunctive preconditions, conditional effects, and angelic nondeterminism. This allows for a more compact representation of tasks than traditional formalisms such as STRIPS or SAS+, and supports a wide range of task transformations. However, existing planning approaches for factored tasks have been limited to heuristic search methods.
  In this work, we investigate how to encode factored tasks in SAT. We propose several ways to encode the tasks, focusing on different strategies for translating the factored transition relation into propositional logic. We also analyze how to exploit parallelism at various levels in this setting and study the impact of common task transformations on the performance of SAT-based planners.

AI.tldr: The paper shows how to turn expressive factored planning tasks into SAT, compares several encoding strategies, and studies how parallel execution and task preprocessing affect SAT-based planning performance.
AI.motivation: Factored tasks provide a compact and expressive extension of SAS+ with limited disjunctive preconditions, conditional effects, and angelic nondeterminism, but prior planning methods for this formalism have mainly relied on heuristic search. The paper is motivated by the need to bring SAT-based planning techniques to this richer representation.
AI.method: The paper proposes multiple SAT encodings for factored tasks, with particular emphasis on different translations of the factored transition relation into propositional logic. It also studies several levels of parallelism and evaluates the effect of common task transformations on SAT-planner performance.
AI.result: The work establishes concrete SAT encodings for factored tasks and provides an analysis of the tradeoffs among encoding choices, parallelism strategies, and task transformations. From the abstract, the exact quantitative performance results are not stated, but the paper reports an empirical study of these factors for SAT-based planners.
AI.conclusion: SAT-based planning is a viable approach for factored tasks, and its effectiveness depends strongly on how the factored transition relation is encoded, how parallelism is exploited, and how preprocessing/task transformations are applied.

title: Unicorn: Scaling High-Dimensional Time Series Forecasting via Universal Correlation Modeling
summary: Modern time series architectures face a fundamental trade-off: channel-independent models scale well with increasing data volume but ignore critical inter-channel dependencies, while channel-dependent models are expressive but remain ``dimension-bounded'', struggling to generalize across heterogeneous datasets.To bridge this gap, we introduce Unicorn (Universal Correlation Network), a framework for scalable, multi-dataset pretraining on high-dimensional time series. At the core of Unicorn is a latent prototype codebook that decouples correlation modeling from specific channel identities. By projecting heterogeneous channels into a shared latent space, UniCorN learns identity-agnostic, reusable interaction patterns that transfer across domains with diverse dimensionalities and semantics. Extensive experiments show that Unicorn significantly outperforms state-of-the-art forecasting architectures, particularly in few-shot transfer scenarios, offering a scalable path toward multivariate time series foundation models.

AI.tldr: Unicorn uses a latent prototype codebook to learn channel-identity-free correlation patterns for multivariate time series, enabling scalable cross-dataset pretraining and better forecasting, particularly for few-shot transfer.
AI.motivation: Existing time-series architectures face a trade-off: channel-independent methods scale but miss important inter-channel dependencies, while channel-dependent methods capture correlations but are tied to fixed dimensional settings and generalize poorly across heterogeneous datasets. The work aims to overcome this limitation for multi-dataset pretraining.
AI.method: The paper proposes Unicorn, a Universal Correlation Network built around a latent prototype codebook. Heterogeneous channels are projected into a shared latent space, where the model learns prototype-based interaction patterns that are decoupled from specific channel identities, enabling correlation modeling across datasets with different dimensions and semantics.
AI.result: According to the abstract, extensive experiments show that Unicorn significantly outperforms state-of-the-art forecasting architectures, especially in few-shot transfer settings.
AI.conclusion: Unicorn provides a scalable way to pretrain on high-dimensional multivariate time series by modeling reusable, identity-agnostic inter-channel correlations, and it achieves strong transfer performance across heterogeneous datasets.

title: On the Application of Hybrid Mixed Domain Decomposition Methods to Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines
summary: In this work, we study the application of a hybrid mixed domain decomposition (HMDD) method for the rotor-stator coupling of a permanent magnet synchronous machine. For this, we derive a variational formulation on the electric machine inspired by hybridized discontinuous Galerkin methods using a mixed magnetostatics problem, an affine material law and boundary conditions respecting the symmetry of the motor. We are then able to locate the resulting finite element method within the HMDD framework presented in arXiv:2604.22543. This enables us naturally to transfer the well-posedness results and error estimates for the HMDD method to the finite element method considered in this work. Lastly, as a proof of concept, we consider an academic example and compare the resulting magnetic flux density and potential lines to their counterparts obtained by a well-established in-house code using iso-geometric analysis.

AI.tldr: They formulate rotor-stator coupling for a permanent magnet synchronous machine as an HMDD-compatible finite element problem, inherit theory for stability and error bounds, and validate the approach on an academic benchmark against an iso-geometric analysis code.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to obtain a mathematically sound and computationally suitable rotor-stator coupling approach for permanent magnet synchronous machines, while leveraging the HMDD framework to gain theoretical guarantees such as well-posedness and error control.
AI.method: The authors derive a variational formulation for an electric machine rotor-stator coupling problem using a mixed magnetostatics model, an affine material law, and symmetry-respecting boundary conditions. They build a finite element method inspired by hybridized discontinuous Galerkin techniques and then interpret it within the hybrid mixed domain decomposition (HMDD) framework.
AI.result: The main results are: a rotor-stator coupling finite element formulation is successfully placed inside the HMDD framework; existing HMDD theory directly provides well-posedness and error estimates; and a proof-of-concept example shows magnetic flux density and potential lines that compare favorably with those from a well-established in-house iso-geometric analysis solver.
