We then define a Korean ERRANT-style annotation scheme that preserves the MRU core while distinguishing functional morpheme errors, spelling errors, word boundary errors, and word order errors. We also augment the KoLLA corpus with an additional reference correction, yielding a multi-reference evaluation setting for Korean GEC. Empirical validation shows that the refined NIKL targets yield lower perplexity, the converted \texttt{m2} files achieve higher agreement with source-target edit representations, and the refined resources improve KoBART-based correction under the same model setting. Multi-reference KoLLA evaluation further reduces the penalty imposed on valid corrections that diverge from a single reference, especially for neural and prompted GEC systems. These results show that Korean GEC evaluation depends not only on correction models, but also on reference data and edit annotations that reflect Korean morphology, spacing, and correction variability.

AI.tldr: The paper upgrades Korean GEC data and evaluation by rebuilding cleaner targets, creating Korean-aware word-level edit labels, and adding multiple references, leading to more reliable evaluation and better model results.
AI.motivation: Existing Korean GEC resources are misaligned with the nature of Korean learner errors: evaluation is typically word-based, while many errors occur at the morpheme level, especially in postpositions and verbal endings. This causes problems in target realization, annotation, and single-reference evaluation.
AI.method: The paper reconstructs target sentences from the NIKL L2 corpus using morphologically constrained realization rules, converts morpheme-level annotations into word-level m2 edits, defines a Korean ERRANT-style annotation scheme tailored to functional morphemes, spelling, word boundaries, and word order, and augments the KoLLA corpus with an additional reference for multi-reference evaluation.
AI.result: Refined NIKL targets have lower perplexity, converted m2 files align better with source-target edit representations, the refined resources improve KoBART-based correction under the same model setting, and multi-reference KoLLA reduces unfair penalties for valid corrections that differ from a single reference, especially for neural and prompted systems.
AI.conclusion: Korean GEC evaluation should be built on morphologically faithful reference data and annotation schemes; better target reconstruction, Korean-specific word-level edit annotation, and multi-reference evaluation materially improve both evaluation quality and model performance.

title: Controllable Lung Nodule Synthesis via Histogram-Regularized Latent Diffusion Models
summary: While automated diagnosis systems have achieved remarkable success in computed tomography (CT)-based lung cancer screening, their development remains limited by the scarcity of diverse, annotated pulmonary nodule datasets. Diffusion-based generative models offer a promising strategy for data synthesis; however, many existing conditional approaches primarily optimize spatial reconstruction losses, which encourage voxel-wise similarity but may inadequately constrain lesion-level intensity distributions. As a result, these methods may produce over-smoothed texture profiles and underrepresent the distinct attenuation characteristics of different nodule subtypes, including solid, part-solid, and ground-glass nodules. To address this challenge, we propose a controllable latent diffusion model that synthesizes pulmonary nodules within full 3D CT volumes while accurately modeling nodule-specific intensity distributions. Specifically, rather than relying solely on spatial losses, we introduce a histogram-based regularization term that constrains voxel intensity distributions during the generative process. The model combines subtype, spatial mask, and Hounsfield unit (HU) histogram conditioning with the differentiable feature-space histogram regularization term to better align lesion-level intensity distributions, improving the visual plausibility and subtype consistency of synthesized nodules. Extensive experiments on lung CT data demonstrate that our framework achieves strong visual realism, validated through both quantitative metrics and a visual Turing test. Furthermore, when used for data augmentation, the generated nodules improve performance in downstream clinical tasks, particularly for underrepresented nodule subtypes, and show a potential benefit for subtype-informed malignancy classification.

AI.tldr: A 3D controllable latent diffusion model with HU-histogram conditioning and histogram regularization generates more realistic, subtype-consistent lung nodules in CT and improves downstream augmentation performance.
AI.motivation: Existing CT lung nodule synthesis methods are limited by scarce annotated data and often overemphasize voxel-wise spatial similarity, which can produce overly smooth textures and fail to capture intensity differences among solid, part-solid, and ground-glass nodules. The paper aims to improve subtype-faithful synthetic data generation.
AI.method: The method is a controllable latent diffusion model for full 3D CT nodule synthesis. It conditions generation on nodule subtype, spatial mask, and HU histogram, and introduces a differentiable feature-space histogram regularization term to explicitly constrain lesion-level voxel intensity distributions beyond standard spatial reconstruction losses.
AI.result: Experiments on lung CT data show strong visual realism according to quantitative metrics and a visual Turing test. The generated nodules also improve downstream task performance when used for data augmentation, especially for underrepresented subtypes, and may help subtype-aware malignancy classification.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that adding histogram-based regularization to a controllable latent diffusion framework enables more realistic 3D pulmonary nodule synthesis in CT, with better preservation of subtype-specific attenuation characteristics and practical value for data augmentation in downstream clinical tasks.

title: SLAT: Segment-Level Adaptive Trimming for Efficient CoT Reasoning
summary: Recent advances in Large Reasoning Models have significantly improved chain-of-thought (CoT) capabilities via reinforcement learning (RL). However, generated reasoning chains frequently suffer from structural redundancy (i.e., \emph{overthinking}), incurring high computational overhead without improving answer correctness. Existing mitigation strategies typically rely on token-uniform length penalties, which provide coarse, segment-agnostic pressure toward shorter outputs and can inadvertently suppress useful reasoning alongside redundancy. To address this, we demonstrate that inefficiency concentrates in high-probability segments with low marginal utility. We derive a theoretical characterization of segment suboptimality under the correctness-length trade-off objective and propose \textsc{SLAT} (Segment-Level Adaptive Trimming), an RL framework that selectively suppresses redundant segments based on this criterion. Empirical results on standard benchmarks indicate that \textsc{SLAT} establishes a superior accuracy-efficiency Pareto frontier, reducing reasoning length by $50\%$ relative to uncompressed baselines while maintaining competitive accuracy. Overall, our results suggest that theoretically grounded, segment-aware trimming is a promising direction for efficient CoT reasoning in large language models.

AI.tldr: SLAT uses RL to trim low-value reasoning segments instead of penalizing all tokens equally, cutting chain-of-thought length by about half while keeping accuracy strong.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that Large Reasoning Models often overthink: their chain-of-thought contains structurally redundant segments that increase computational cost without improving correctness, and existing token-uniform penalties are too coarse and may remove useful reasoning together with redundancy.
AI.method: The method is SLAT (Segment-Level Adaptive Trimming), a reinforcement learning framework that identifies and suppresses redundant reasoning segments using a theoretical criterion of segment suboptimality under a correctness-length trade-off objective.
AI.result: Empirical results on standard benchmarks show a better accuracy-efficiency Pareto frontier than prior approaches, with roughly 50% reduction in reasoning length relative to uncompressed baselines while maintaining competitive accuracy.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that segment-aware, theoretically grounded trimming can reduce redundant chain-of-thought reasoning much more effectively than uniform length penalties, achieving about 50% shorter reasoning traces while preserving competitive accuracy.

title: Scalable Constrained Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via State Augmentation and Consensus for Separable Dynamics
summary: We present a distributed approach for constrained Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) that combines state-augmented policy learning with distributed consensus over dual variables. Our method targets systems where agents have separable dynamics but must coordinate to satisfy global resource constraints, a setting in which, as we demonstrate empirically, independent learning fails to produce feasible solutions because agents cannot determine appropriate individual contributions toward collective constraint satisfaction. The key technical contribution is showing that lightweight neighbor-to-neighbor consensus over Lagrange multipliers suffices for globally coordinated constraint enforcement while preserving the scalability of independent training. Each agent learns a single augmented policy offline, conditioned on both its local state and a dual variable encoding constraint feedback. During execution, agents reach agreement on this dual variable through local communication alone. We prove that under mild connectivity assumptions, the consensus error among agents' multipliers is bounded, and show that this translates to a bounded constraint violation that decreases with graph connectivity and the number of consensus rounds. Unlike centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) approaches, whose complexity grows at least quadratically with agent count, our method scales linearly in both training and execution. Experiments on smart grid demand response demonstrate that consensus coordination is \emph{essential for feasibility}: without it, agents satisfy grid capacity constraints only by indefinitely postponing demand, a degenerate non-solution. With consensus, agents converge to a shared dual variable and satisfy both grid constraints and demand fulfillment, scaling to thousands of agents while CTDE baselines are limited to dozens.

AI.tldr: Train each agent independently with a policy that also takes a dual variable as input, then make agents agree on that dual variable through lightweight neighbor communication at runtime. This gives scalable constrained MARL that preserves feasibility, unlike independent learning, and scales far better than CTDE.
AI.motivation: In separable multi-agent systems with shared global resource constraints, purely independent learning cannot infer how much each agent should contribute to satisfying the collective constraint, often leading to infeasible or degenerate behaviors. The goal is to retain the scalability of independent learning while adding enough coordination to ensure feasibility.
AI.method: Each agent is trained offline with a single policy conditioned on its local state and a dual variable representing constraint feedback. At execution time, agents communicate only with neighbors to run consensus on Lagrange multipliers, enabling coordinated constraint enforcement under separable dynamics and global constraints.
AI.result: The paper proves bounded consensus error under mild graph connectivity assumptions and shows this yields bounded constraint violation that improves with stronger connectivity and more consensus rounds. Empirically, in smart-grid demand response, the method satisfies both grid capacity and demand fulfillment, scales to thousands of agents, and outperforms CTDE baselines that scale only to dozens.
AI.conclusion: A distributed constrained MARL approach using state-augmented policies plus consensus over dual variables can enforce global resource constraints with only local communication, achieving scalable and feasible coordination where independent learning fails.

title: Generating and Refining Dynamic Evaluation Rubrics for LLM-as-a-Judge
summary: LLM-as-a-Judge is a scalable alternative to human evaluation, yet existing rubric-based methods rely on human-annotated data such as reference answers or expert-crafted rubrics. We propose to automatically generate fine-grained evaluation rubrics without any human annotation. Our training-free method generates rubrics at dataset-specific and instance-specific granularities, achieving performance competitive with existing methods across four benchmarks. We further present a method that iteratively fine-tunes a rubric generator model via meta-judge reward signals. The fine-tuned generator outperforms all existing baselines in both pairwise and pointwise evaluation. Notably, a fine-tuned 14B rubric generator outperforms a much larger proprietary model at rubric generation, showing the effectiveness of our fine-tuning strategy.

AI.tldr: The paper automates rubric generation for LLM-based evaluation without human labels, then improves it through reward-driven fine-tuning; the final system beats prior baselines and even larger proprietary models.
AI.motivation: Existing rubric-based LLM-as-a-Judge methods depend on costly human annotations such as reference answers and expert-designed rubrics. The motivation is to build a scalable evaluation framework that removes this dependency while retaining strong evaluation performance.
AI.method: The paper proposes a training-free rubric generation approach that creates fine-grained rubrics at both dataset-specific and instance-specific levels without human annotations. It also introduces an iterative fine-tuning method for the rubric generator, guided by meta-judge reward signals.
AI.result: The training-free method achieves competitive performance with prior methods on four benchmarks. The fine-tuned rubric generator outperforms all existing baselines in both pairwise and pointwise evaluation, and a 14B fine-tuned model exceeds the rubric generation performance of a much larger proprietary model.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that evaluation rubrics for LLM-as-a-Judge can be generated automatically without human annotation, and that iterative fine-tuning of a rubric generator using meta-judge reward signals further improves quality. The fine-tuned generator surpasses existing baselines and even a larger proprietary model in rubric generation.

title: COMPASS: Cognitive MCTS-Guided Process Alignment for Safe Search Agents
summary: LLM-powered search agents enable multi-step reasoning and tool use. However, these capabilities introduce retrieval-induced safety degradation, as harmful intents may decompose into seemingly innocuous sub-queries that lead to unsafe outcomes. Existing alignment methods struggle to capture sparse safety signals and fail to supervise diverse violations across multi-step interactions. We propose COMPASS, a Cognitive MCTS-Guided Process Alignment framework designed to achieve robust safety alignment throughout the agent workflow while preserving general utility. COMPASS integrates cognitive tree exploration (CTE) to efficiently synthesize stealthy attack trajectories, and introspective step-wise alignment (ISA) to isolate risky intermediate actions for fine-grained process supervision. Empirical results show that COMPASS achieves a favorable safety-utility trade-off while requiring substantially less training data.

AI.tldr: COMPASS improves the safety of multi-step LLM search agents by finding stealthy unsafe reasoning paths and supervising risky intermediate steps, yielding better safety with lower data cost.
AI.motivation: LLM-powered search agents can perform multi-step reasoning and tool use, but this also creates retrieval-induced safety degradation: harmful goals can be decomposed into benign-looking sub-queries, making unsafe behavior hard to detect. Existing alignment methods miss sparse safety signals and do not supervise diverse violations well across multi-step interactions.
AI.method: The paper proposes COMPASS, a Cognitive MCTS-Guided Process Alignment framework. It combines cognitive tree exploration (CTE) to generate stealthy multi-step attack trajectories and introspective step-wise alignment (ISA) to identify risky intermediate actions and apply fine-grained process supervision.
AI.result: Empirical results indicate that COMPASS achieves a favorable trade-off between safety and utility while requiring substantially less training data.
AI.conclusion: COMPASS can robustly improve safety alignment for LLM search agents across multi-step workflows, achieving a strong safety-utility balance with much less training data than prior methods.

title: idSCD: Identifying Training Datasets through Semantic Correlation Descriptors
summary: Can a dataset be recognized from the spurious correlations it induces during training? We argue that datasets leave dataset-specific traces in a model's learned semantic correlation structure: incidental regularities that are predictive within a dataset, but not causal for the underlying task, can be internalized during training. We use this insight to study dataset-level membership inference, moving beyond existing methods that rely on behavioral or distributional evidence such as confidence scores, losses, margins, generated samples, or query responses. We introduce a white-box semantic fingerprinting approach based on semantic correlation descriptors (SCDs), which capture the semantic correlation structure learned by a model and make it comparable across dataset mixtures. In a controlled leave-one-dataset-out diagnostic, SCDs recover dataset-specific changes and perfectly separate matching from non-matching dataset pairs. We then propose a practical SCD-based membership score that tests whether a target dataset is part of a model's training mixture using only the model's SCD and the target dataset's standalone SCD, without requiring leave-one-dataset-out models. Across three diverse experimental settings, with dataset groups for natural language inference, emotion classification, and medical text classification, we test both the advantages and limitations of SCD-based membership inference with different degrees of semantic separation and keyword support between dataset splits. On average, the classifier based on this score achieves the highest performance and the lowest std, outperforming black-box baselines RMIA, Attack-P, and LiRA, as well as the white-box SIF baseline. These results show that dataset membership can be traced through internal semantic correlations, with the largest relative gain exceeding 60% in ROC-AUC when dataset groups expose distinct semantic particularities.

AI.tldr: 这篇论文提出用模型内部的“语义相关性指纹”判断某个数据集是否参与过训练。核心做法是构造SCD来表示模型学到的语义伪相关结构，并据此做白盒数据集成员推断。实验表明，该方法在多个文本任务上比RMIA、LiRA、Attack-P和SIF更稳，平均效果最好；当不同数据集具有明显语义特征时，优势尤其大。
AI.motivation: 现有数据集级成员推断多依赖置信度、损失、边距、生成样本或查询响应等行为/分布证据。作者认为，训练数据中的伪相关和偶然语义规律会被模型内化，并在模型内部留下数据集特定痕迹，因此可以从内部语义相关结构出发进行更稳健的数据集成员推断。
AI.method: 作者提出白盒语义指纹方法，使用语义相关性描述符（SCD）刻画模型学到的语义相关结构，并据此比较不同训练数据混合下的模型；先在leave-one-dataset-out诊断中验证SCD能识别数据集特异变化，再设计一个实用的基于SCD的成员分数，仅用目标模型的SCD和目标数据集单独训练得到的SCD来判断该数据集是否属于训练混合。
AI.result: 在自然语言推断、情感分类和医疗文本分类三类实验中，基于SCD成员分数的分类器平均取得最高性能和最低标准差，优于RMIA、Attack-P、LiRA和白盒SIF基线；在语义差异明显的数据集组上，ROC-AUC的最大相对提升超过60%。
AI.conclusion: 论文表明，模型内部学到的语义相关性结构中存在可追踪的数据集特异性痕迹，可用于数据集级成员推断；基于SCD的白盒方法在多种文本分类设置下总体优于现有黑盒和白盒基线，尤其在数据集具有明显语义特性差异时效果显著。

title: Probing the Prompt KV Cache: Where It Becomes Dispensable
summary: Prior KV cache compression schemes empirically demonstrate that the prompt cache is partially redundant during decoding, dropping or summarising entries with little accuracy loss. We ask when and what kind of redundancy: at which layers, after how many decoding steps, and in what form can the prompt span KV cache be replaced without breaking the task. A controlled splice intervention swept over layer cutoff and decoding steps shows this redundancy is about form (chat template scaffolding) rather than content. Replacing the upper layer prompt span KV cache with KV cache from a chat template scaffold whose user content is a neutral filler recovers near clean accuracy, while zeroing the same slots collapses accuracy. The dissociation replicates across the Qwen3, Gemma 3, and Llama 3 families on multiple datasets.

AI.tldr: TL;DR：模型上层在解码中后期对 prompt KV 的依赖更多是聊天模板的“结构外壳”，不是原始用户内容本身；因此可用中性模板 cache 替换，但不能简单置零。 / Upper layers later in decoding rely on the chat-template shell more than the original user content, so neutral scaffold cache can substitute for prompt KV, but zeroing cannot.
AI.motivation: 现有 KV cache 压缩工作表明解码阶段 prompt cache 存在冗余，但尚不清楚这种冗余何时出现、存在于哪些层、以及究竟是哪些信息可以被替换而不损害任务性能。本文旨在把这些经验现象拆解成可检验的问题。 / Prior KV cache compression results suggest prompt cache redundancy during decoding, but it remains unclear when it emerges, in which layers it lives, and what information can be replaced without harming task performance. This paper aims to isolate and test those factors directly.
AI.method: 论文采用受控的 splice intervention，系统扫描两个维度：层截断位置和解码步数；随后比较三种处理上层 prompt-span KV cache 的方式：保留原始 cache、用带中性填充内容的聊天模板 scaffold cache 替换、以及直接置零，并在 Qwen3、Gemma 3、Llama 3 多个家族及多数据集上验证。 / The paper uses a controlled splice intervention that sweeps layer cutoff and decoding step, then compares preserving the original prompt-span KV cache, replacing upper-layer cache with cache from a chat-template scaffold containing neutral filler, and zeroing the same slots, across multiple datasets and the Qwen3, Gemma 3, and Llama 3 families.
AI.result: 实验发现：当替换发生在上层且经过一定解码步数后，用聊天模板形式相似但语义内容中性的 scaffold KV cache 进行替换，可恢复接近原始的准确率；而对相同位置直接清零则导致准确率崩溃。这一“形式-内容”解耦在 Qwen3、Gemma 3、Llama 3 以及多个数据集上均复现。 / The experiments show that after sufficient decoding and in upper layers, replacing the prompt-span KV cache with semantically neutral but structurally matched chat-template scaffold cache recovers near-clean accuracy, while zeroing the same positions collapses accuracy. This form-vs-content dissociation replicates across Qwen3, Gemma 3, and Llama 3 on multiple datasets.
AI.conclusion: 上层 prompt-span KV cache 的冗余主要来自“形式”而非“内容”；在一定解码步数后，可用仅保留聊天模板脚手架、将用户内容替换为中性填充的 KV cache 替换上层 prompt KV，而几乎不损失性能，但直接清零会显著破坏任务能力。 / The redundancy in upper-layer prompt-span KV cache is primarily about form rather than semantic content; after some decoding steps, those cache slots can be replaced by cache from a chat-template scaffold with neutral filler content with little accuracy loss, whereas zeroing them causes severe failure.

title: WristCompass: Kinematic Coupling as a Learnable Visual Concept for Ego-Camera Orientation
summary: Recovering ego-camera orientation from manipulation video is a prerequisite for disentangling hand motion from camera motion, a key step in imitation learning from egocentric demonstrations. The obvious approach, inferring orientation from scene geometry, fails when hands occlude the frame: VGGT, a 1B-parameter scene reconstruction model, scores worse than a constant predictor on the TACO benchmark. We identify an alternative visual concept that is present precisely when scene geometry is absent: kinematic coupling dynamics, the structured physical relationship between wrist motion and camera orientation imposed by the arm-shoulder-head chain. We find that this concept is compact (4D inter-wrist features outperform 126D full hand keypoints), temporal (requiring a GRU over short windows rather than per-frame retrieval), and physically grounded (transferring zero-shot across datasets because it is rooted in anatomy rather than scene appearance). Trained only on tabletop manipulation, WristCompass transfers zero-shot to Epic Kitchens cooking video, achieving 14.3$^\circ$ median geodesic error and approaching the performance of a 1B-parameter scene model at 200K GRU parameters.

AI.tldr: The paper predicts ego-camera orientation from wrist-motion dynamics instead of scene appearance. A compact GRU-based model using inter-wrist features transfers zero-shot across datasets and nearly matches a 1B-parameter scene model with far fewer parameters.
AI.motivation: Scene-geometry-based orientation estimation breaks down in egocentric manipulation videos when hands heavily occlude the view, yet recovering camera orientation is necessary to separate hand motion from camera motion for imitation learning.
AI.method: The paper models ego-camera orientation using compact inter-wrist kinematic features and a short-window GRU to capture temporal dynamics imposed by the arm-shoulder-head chain, instead of relying on scene reconstruction or full-hand geometry.
AI.result: On TACO and cross-dataset transfer to Epic Kitchens, WristCompass substantially outperforms scene-geometry baselines under occlusion and reaches 14.3 degrees median geodesic error zero-shot on Epic Kitchens, approaching a 1B-parameter scene model with only 200K GRU parameters.
AI.conclusion: WristCompass shows that ego-camera orientation in manipulation videos can be recovered effectively from wrist-motion-based kinematic coupling rather than scene geometry, enabling strong zero-shot transfer with a very small model.

title: Distilling LLM Feedback for Lean Theorem Proving
summary: Post-training for reasoning models typically combines supervised fine-tuning with reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards, most commonly with GRPO. However, this algorithm suffers from sparse rewards, limited exploration, and mode collapse. Building upon recent works on self-distillation, we propose Feedback Distillation, a training method where the model is trained to match, at the token level, its own distribution conditioned on privileged feedback produced by a language model. Feedback Distillation offers token-level supervision and can inject external knowledge. Evaluating our method for Lean4 theorem-proving, we find that Feedback Distillation maintains greater diversity in generated trajectories than GRPO, yielding higher policy entropy and better pass@k scaling. The two methods are complementary: initializing GRPO from a Feedback Distillation checkpoint outperforms either method alone. All in all, our results suggest a promising avenue to improve post-training for complex reasoning.

AI.tldr: The paper replaces sparse-reward GRPO-only post-training with token-level self-distillation guided by privileged LM feedback. This yields more diverse reasoning trajectories and stronger theorem-proving performance, and combining it with GRPO works best.
AI.motivation: Standard post-training for reasoning models often uses supervised fine-tuning plus GRPO-based reinforcement learning, but GRPO suffers from sparse rewards, weak exploration, and mode collapse. The authors aim to improve reasoning post-training with denser feedback and better diversity preservation.
AI.method: The paper proposes Feedback Distillation, which trains a model with token-level supervision to match its own output distribution conditioned on privileged feedback generated by a language model. This provides denser supervision than reward-only reinforcement learning and can incorporate external knowledge.
AI.result: On Lean4 theorem proving, Feedback Distillation achieves higher policy entropy and better pass@k scaling than GRPO by maintaining more diverse generated trajectories. Moreover, GRPO initialized from a Feedback Distillation checkpoint outperforms either method used alone.
AI.conclusion: Feedback Distillation is a promising post-training method for complex reasoning models; it preserves trajectory diversity better than GRPO, improves pass@k scaling, and works best when used to initialize subsequent GRPO training.

title: Can Subgraph Explanations Be Weaponized to Steal Graph Neural Networks?
comment: 28 pages, 8 figures, 10 tables. Under review at NeurIPS 2026
summary: Graph Machine Learning as a Service (GMLaaS) platforms increasingly implement explainability interfaces to meet regulatory transparency requirements. However, this transparency creates exploitable vulnerabilities for model extraction attacks. We present the first model extraction attack specifically designed for graph classification under strict black-box constraints where the attacker observes only discrete class labels and binary explanation masks (no probability scores, gradients, or confidence values). Our method (1) uses model explanation outputs to guide Monte Carlo edge sensitivity estimation toward decision boundaries, with Hoeffding concentration guarantees on estimation accuracy and (2) exploits explanation subgraphs to efficiently narrow the boundary search space. Extensive experiments on benchmark graph datasets across multiple domains demonstrate our method's superiority over comparable baselines. These findings demonstrate that such explainability interfaces create exploitable attack surfaces, informing both defensive mechanisms and policy frameworks for explainable AI mandates. The implementation code is provided in https://github.com/LabRAI/XSTEAL/.

AI.tldr: 这篇论文说明：给图分类模型开放“解释结果”并不只是提升透明度，也可能成为模型抽取攻击的入口。作者提出一种只依赖预测标签和二值解释掩码的黑盒攻击，利用解释信息更快找到决策边界，并在实验中显著优于基线。 / This paper shows that exposing explanations for graph classification improves transparency but also opens a path for model extraction. It introduces a black-box attack using only predicted labels and binary explanation masks, leveraging explanations to find decision boundaries more efficiently and outperform baselines in experiments.
AI.motivation: 随着GMLaaS平台为满足监管透明度要求而提供可解释性接口，这些接口可能反而泄露足够的信息，使攻击者能够抽取模型。现有研究对图分类场景、且在仅有标签与解释掩码的严格黑盒条件下的攻击研究不足，因此需要专门方法进行评估。 / As GMLaaS platforms add explainability interfaces to satisfy transparency regulations, these interfaces may leak enough information to enable model extraction. Prior work is insufficient for graph classification under strict black-box access with only labels and explanation masks, motivating a dedicated attack study.
AI.method: 论文提出首个面向图分类、严格黑盒设定的模型抽取攻击方法。核心包括两点：1）利用模型解释输出，引导基于Monte Carlo的边敏感度估计朝向决策边界，并给出Hoeffding集中不等式下的精度保证；2）利用解释子图缩小边界搜索空间，从而提升攻击效率。 / The paper proposes the first model extraction attack for graph classification in a strict black-box setting. It has two main components: (1) explanation-guided Monte Carlo edge sensitivity estimation toward decision boundaries, with accuracy guarantees via Hoeffding concentration bounds; (2) use of explanation subgraphs to reduce the boundary search space and improve efficiency.
AI.result: 作者在多个领域的基准图数据集上进行了广泛实验，结果表明该方法优于可比基线方法。实验支持其主张：解释接口显著增强了攻击者进行模型抽取的能力。 / Extensive experiments on benchmark graph datasets from multiple domains show the method outperforms comparable baselines. The results support the claim that explainability interfaces materially strengthen an attacker’s ability to extract models.
AI.conclusion: 可解释性接口在图分类GMLaaS中会暴露可被利用的攻击面；即使在严格黑盒条件下，仅凭离散类别标签和二值解释掩码，也能高效进行模型抽取。这一结论提示需要同时改进防御机制与相关政策设计。 / Explainability interfaces in graph-classification GMLaaS expose exploitable attack surfaces; even under strict black-box settings with only discrete labels and binary explanation masks, effective model extraction is still possible. This implies the need for stronger defenses and more careful policy design.

title: Speculative Decoding Across Languages
comment: 10 pages, 11 figures, submitted to ACL ARR May 2026
summary:
Speculative decoding has become a crucial component of large language model (LLM) inference, enabling faster generation by drafting multiple tokens and verifying them in parallel. However, small draft models tend to suffer from disproportionately poor multilingual capabilities. Thus, when generating text in a non-English language, speculative decoding is far less effective.
  We compare three strategies to improve speculative decoding efficiency for eleven languages: finetuning the draft model on task-specific data (translation); finetuning the draft model on unlabeled monolingual corpora; and training simple n-gram draft models on the same monolingual corpora. We evaluate efficiency on translation (from English into the target language) and the held-out task of story generation. We find that while task-specific distillation can significantly improve efficiency, distilled models generalize poorly to a new task. Meanwhile, n-gram draft models, despite lower acceptance rates, consistently provide large speed-ups due to much faster draft generation.

AI.tldr: For multilingual speculative decoding, specialized distilled draft models help on the training task, but n-gram drafters are the most robust practical choice because they stay fast and generalize better across tasks.
AI.motivation: Speculative decoding speeds up LLM inference, but small draft models have weak multilingual ability, making the method much less effective for non-English text generation. The work aims to identify simple and effective ways to recover decoding efficiency across languages.
AI.method: The paper compares three approaches for improving speculative decoding in 11 target languages: (1) finetuning the draft model on translation data, (2) finetuning the draft model on unlabeled monolingual corpora, and (3) training n-gram draft models on the same monolingual corpora. Efficiency is evaluated on English-to-target translation and held-out story generation.
AI.result: Task-specific distilled draft models can significantly raise efficiency on translation, but their gains do not generalize well to story generation. In contrast, n-gram draft models consistently yield large speedups across settings because they are extremely cheap to run, even with lower acceptance rates.
AI.conclusion: Task-specific distillation improves speculative decoding efficiency for multilingual generation but transfers poorly across tasks, while simple n-gram draft models offer robust speedups across languages because their draft generation is much faster despite lower token acceptance.

title: UniScale: Adaptive Unified Inference Scaling via Online Joint Optimization of Model Routing and Test-Time Scaling
comment: Accepted at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2026)
summary: In real-world deployments of large language models (LLMs), balancing inference quality and computational cost has become a central challenge. Existing approaches tackle this trade-off along two largely independent dimensions: model routing, which switches among models of different scales to match request complexity, and test-time scaling (TTS), which adjusts inference-time compute within a fixed model for fine-grained control. However, this decoupled design introduces inherent limitations. Model routing yields coarse-grained, discrete performance changes due to the sparse set of model scales, while single-model TTS often encounters capacity ceilings and exhibits diminishing returns as compute increases. Moreover, treating the two mechanisms separately restricts adaptability in dynamic inference environments. To overcome these limitations, we introduce Unified Inference Scaling (UIS), which unifies model routing and TTS in a single optimization space. Building on this formulation, we propose UniScale, an online framework that models adaptive UIS as a contextual multi-armed bandit problem and learns inference policies via LinUCB. The framework incorporates efficiency-aware learning and cost modeling to ensure stable and scalable optimization over high-dimensional action spaces. Evaluation shows that UniScale effectively exploits the synergy in the UIS space to deliver a fine-grained and consistently better quality-cost trade-off across diverse, dynamic inference scenarios.

AI.tldr: The paper unifies model selection and inference-time compute control for LLMs. Its UniScale bandit-based online framework learns when to switch models and how much compute to spend, yielding better and more flexible quality-cost trade-offs than handling the two separately.
AI.motivation: Existing methods manage the quality-cost trade-off in LLM inference through either model routing or test-time scaling, but these are usually designed independently. This separation causes coarse-grained control, capacity ceilings, diminishing returns, and weak adaptability in dynamic inference environments. The paper is motivated by the need for a unified, more flexible inference optimization framework.
AI.method: The paper formulates inference adaptation as Unified Inference Scaling (UIS), which jointly optimizes model routing and test-time scaling in one action space. It then proposes UniScale, an online framework that casts adaptive UIS as a contextual multi-armed bandit problem and learns policies using LinUCB, with efficiency-aware learning and explicit cost modeling for high-dimensional action spaces.
AI.result: According to the abstract, experiments show that UniScale effectively leverages the synergy between routing and test-time scaling, providing finer-grained control and consistently better quality-cost trade-offs across diverse and dynamic inference scenarios.
AI.conclusion: Unified Inference Scaling (UIS) is a more effective formulation for balancing LLM inference quality and cost than treating model routing and test-time scaling separately. The proposed UniScale framework can stably learn adaptive inference policies and achieves a finer-grained, consistently better quality-cost trade-off in dynamic scenarios.

title: Universal Multiclass Transductive Online Learning
summary: We consider the problem of universal transductive online classification with a possibly unbounded label space. This setting considers online learning, with the sequence of instances (without labels) known to the learner in advance. We say a concept class $\mathcal{H}$ is learnable if there is a learning algorithm $\mathcal{A}$, such that for every realizable sequence, the number of mistakes made by $\mathcal{A}$ grows at most sublinearly with the number of predictions. We characterize the learnability of this setting and show that there are only two possible optimal rates for the learnable classes: either bounded or increasing logarithmically. We introduce a new combinatorial structure, called ``Level-Constrained-Littlestone-Littlestone (LCLL) tree'', which, along with the indifference property, characterizes the learnability. We also extend the learnability result to the agnostic case and the case where only the stochastic process that generates the instance sequence is known.

AI.tldr: The paper gives a full learnability characterization for transductive online classification with potentially unlimited labels, using a new LCLL tree plus an indifference condition, and shows learnable classes admit only bounded or O(log n) optimal mistake rates.
AI.motivation: Existing online learning theory does not fully characterize learnability in the transductive setting when the label space may be unbounded. The authors aim to determine when universal transductive online classification is possible and what optimal mistake rates can be achieved.
AI.method: The paper studies realizable universal transductive online classification where the unlabeled instance sequence is known in advance. It introduces the Level-Constrained-Littlestone-Littlestone (LCLL) tree as a new combinatorial object, combines it with the indifference property to characterize learnability, and extends the analysis to agnostic and stochastic-sequence settings.
AI.result: The main results are a necessary and sufficient characterization of learnability, a dichotomy showing that every learnable class has either bounded mistakes or logarithmic mistake growth, and extensions of these guarantees to the agnostic case and to settings where only the stochastic process over instances is known.
AI.conclusion: Universal transductive online classification with possibly unbounded labels is learnable exactly under a structural characterization based on the new LCLL tree and the indifference property. For learnable classes, the optimal mistake rate has only two forms: bounded or logarithmic growth.

title: AI for Monitoring and Classifying Data Used in Research Literature
summary: While platforms like Google Scholar and Semantic Scholar track citations for academic papers, no comparable infrastructure exists for monitoring dataset usage in research literature, leaving the landscape of data use largely opaque. Addressing this gap is critical for transparency, reproducibility, and monitoring of impact, yet progress is hindered by inconsistent citation practices, scarce labeled data, and ambiguous references to datasets in the wild. Traditional NLP approaches struggle with these challenges, motivating the shift toward more adaptive, semantically rich models. Building on prior work using LLMs for data mention detection and synthetic data for bootstrapping training, this paper presents an updated methodology for scalable dataset monitoring. We introduce a multitask GLiNER-based framework that jointly performs dataset mention extraction, relation identification, and usage-context classification. To address label scarcity, the pipeline leverages synthetic data generation to produce training examples and LLM-based revalidation to filter incorrect mentions and enforce labeling consistency, together improving reliability, coverage, and output consistency across the training pipeline. This work advances the development of open-source tools for monitoring data use in research literature, contributing to the broader goal of generalizable, unconstrained dataset citation tracking.

AI.tldr: 论文提出一个多任务GLiNER数据集监测框架，并结合合成数据与LLM重验证，来更可靠地追踪论文中的数据集提及、关系和使用方式。 / A multitask GLiNER framework plus synthetic data and LLM revalidation enables more reliable tracking of dataset mentions, relations, and usage context in research papers.
AI.motivation: 研究动机在于：当前学术界缺乏类似论文引用追踪那样的数据集使用监测基础设施，导致数据使用情况不透明；而不一致的数据集引用、标注数据稀缺以及真实场景中的模糊指代，使传统NLP方法难以有效解决该问题。 / The motivation is that, unlike paper citation tracking, there is no comparable infrastructure for monitoring dataset usage in the literature, making data use opaque; inconsistent citation practices, scarce labeled data, and ambiguous dataset references also limit traditional NLP approaches.
AI.method: 方法上，论文构建了一个多任务GLiNER框架，联合执行数据集提及抽取、关系识别和使用语境分类；同时使用合成数据生成扩充训练样本，并通过LLM重验证过滤错误提及、统一标注标准。 / Methodologically, it builds a multitask GLiNER-based framework that jointly performs dataset mention extraction, relation identification, and usage-context classification, while using synthetic data generation for training expansion and LLM-based revalidation for error filtering and label consistency.
AI.result: 结果表明，该流程通过合成数据和LLM重验证增强了训练管线的可靠性、覆盖率和输出一致性，并推动了面向通用、开放场景的数据集引用追踪工具发展。 / The results indicate that the pipeline improves training reliability, coverage, and output consistency via synthetic data and LLM-based revalidation, advancing generalizable open-source tools for unconstrained dataset citation tracking.
AI.conclusion: 该论文提出了一种可扩展的开放源代码数据集监测方法，通过多任务GLiNER框架、合成数据生成与基于LLM的重验证，提高了数据集提及检测、关系识别和使用语境分类的一致性、覆盖率与可靠性。 / The paper concludes with a scalable open-source methodology for dataset monitoring that improves consistency, coverage, and reliability in dataset mention detection, relation identification, and usage-context classification through a multitask GLiNER framework, synthetic data generation, and LLM-based revalidation.

title: Seeing Before Agreeing: Aligning Multi-Agent Consensus with Visual Evidence
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance on visual question answering (VQA). To mitigate individual hallucinations and blind spots, aggregating diverse perspectives via multi-agent collaboration has emerged as a promising paradigm. While this approach has shown great success in textual QA, its potential in the multimodal domain remains under-explored. Existing multi-agent VQA methods predominantly adapt text-centric protocols, focusing on textual discussions while ignoring the alignment of visual information. In this work, we reveal a key insight: answer-level agreement is insufficient for reliable multi-agent VQA; \textit{aligned visual evidence} -- shared support from the image regions agents rely on -- is essential for trustworthy consensus. To leverage this insight, we propose EAGLE (\textbf{E}vidence-\textbf{A}ligned \textbf{G}rounded mu\textbf{L}ti-agent r\textbf{E}asoning), a training-free evidence-centered framework for coordinating multiple VLM agents. EAGLE explicitly exposes each agent's grounding regions as visual evidence, enables mutual verification over the evidence, and uses evidence consistency to guide final decision-making. Experiments on six VQA benchmarks show that EAGLE achieves best average performance across domains while remaining lightweight, interpretable, and practical for deployment.

AI.tldr: Multi-agent VQA should agree on both the answer and the image evidence. EAGLE enforces evidence-aligned collaboration among VLM agents without training and improves benchmark performance.
AI.motivation: Existing multi-agent VQA methods mainly borrow text-only collaboration protocols and overlook whether agents rely on the same image evidence. The authors aim to improve reliability and trustworthiness in multimodal reasoning by incorporating aligned visual grounding into agent collaboration.
AI.method: The paper proposes EAGLE, a training-free evidence-centered multi-agent VQA framework that makes each VLM agent expose its grounding regions, lets agents mutually verify those visual evidences, and uses evidence consistency to guide the final consensus answer.
AI.result: On six VQA benchmarks, EAGLE achieves the best average cross-domain performance while remaining lightweight, interpretable, and practical for deployment.
AI.conclusion: EAGLE demonstrates that trustworthy multi-agent VQA requires not only answer agreement but also alignment of visual evidence, and it achieves strong, lightweight, interpretable performance across six benchmarks.

title: BilliardPhys-Bench: Benchmarking Physical Reasoning and Visual Dynamics of Multimodal LLMs
summary: Current multimodal models handle static image recognition well, but intuitive physical reasoning remains a weakness. Predicting how objects will move and interact from a single image is still difficult for these systems. We present BilliardPhys-Bench, a benchmark for physical reasoning in synthetic billiards environments. Its procedural engine generates randomized scenarios with friction and elastic collisions. The benchmark tests three abilities: (1) predicting ball-to-ball collisions, (2) reasoning about wall bounces, and (3) estimating final ball positions after motion stops. We evaluate recent MLLMs from the GPT, Claude, Gemini, and Qwen families. Performance drops as simulation time increases and scene geometry grows more complex. We also observe a consistent failure mode we call "stasis bias": when the correct physical outcome is harder to infer, models tend to predict no interaction. These findings show where current MLLMs break down on visual dynamics and point toward the need for better physical inductive biases in multimodal architectures.

AI.tldr: A new synthetic billiards benchmark shows that leading multimodal models still struggle to predict physical dynamics from a single image, especially in longer and more complex scenarios, often defaulting to incorrect no-interaction predictions.
AI.motivation: Although modern multimodal models perform strongly on static image understanding, they remain weak at intuitive physical reasoning. The work is motivated by the need to systematically measure how well such models can infer future object dynamics and interactions from a single image.
AI.method: The paper introduces BilliardPhys-Bench, a synthetic benchmark built with a procedural billiards simulation engine that randomizes scenarios with friction and elastic collisions. It evaluates models on three tasks: predicting ball-to-ball collisions, reasoning about wall bounces, and estimating final resting positions of balls. Recent MLLMs from GPT, Claude, Gemini, and Qwen families are tested on these tasks.
AI.result: Across tested MLLMs, performance declines as physical scenarios become temporally longer and spatially more complex. A recurring error pattern, termed 'stasis bias,' shows that models often default to predicting no movement or no interaction when reasoning becomes harder.
AI.conclusion: Current multimodal large language models show clear weaknesses in intuitive physical reasoning from single images. Their performance degrades with longer simulation horizons and more complex geometry, and they exhibit a systematic 'stasis bias' by predicting no interaction when the correct outcome is difficult to infer.

title: Discovering a Zeta Map Algorithm on Dyck Paths via Mechanistic Interpretability
summary: Machine learning is increasingly used in mathematical discovery, but in mathematics the desired output is often not a prediction itself, but an explicit construction that can be checked independently. We study this setting through the zeta map on Dyck paths, a classical bijection in the combinatorics of the q,t-Catalan numbers. We train a deliberately small one-layer, one-head encoder-decoder transformer on this map and analyze its learned computation using mechanistic interpretability tools, including decoder cross-attention analysis, linear probing, and causal intervention. The analysis reveals a level-based mechanism: encoder representations make path levels linearly accessible, while the decoder selects and traverses input positions in a structured way. Translating these signals into combinatorics leads to the scaffolding map, an explicit peak-centered traversal algorithm for Dyck paths. We prove that this algorithm agrees with the zeta map, modulo a reversal convention in the labeling. This gives a controlled example of AI-assisted mathematical discovery in which mechanistic interpretability turns model behavior into a precise, human-verifiable combinatorial algorithm.

AI.tldr: A tiny transformer learns the zeta map on Dyck paths; interpretability reveals how it works, and that insight is converted into a provably correct new explicit algorithm called the scaffolding map.
AI.motivation: In mathematical discovery, useful AI outputs are often explicit constructions or algorithms that can be independently checked, not just accurate predictions. The paper investigates whether mechanistic interpretability can turn a model's learned behavior into such a verifiable mathematical construction.
AI.method: The paper trains a deliberately small one-layer, one-head encoder-decoder transformer to learn the zeta map on Dyck paths, then studies its internal computation using decoder cross-attention analysis, linear probing, and causal intervention, and translates the discovered mechanism into an explicit combinatorial algorithm.
AI.result: The analysis uncovers a level-based mechanism: encoder states encode Dyck path levels in a linearly accessible way, and the decoder performs a structured traversal of input positions. From this, the authors formulate the scaffolding map and prove it is equivalent to the zeta map modulo a reversal convention.
AI.conclusion: Mechanistic interpretability can extract a precise, human-verifiable combinatorial algorithm from a small transformer: the derived scaffolding map matches the zeta map on Dyck paths up to a reversal convention.

title: ImmigrationQA: A Source-Grounded Dataset and Small-Model Adaptation for U.S. Immigration Law
comment: 12 pages, 4 tables. Dataset (17,058 QA pairs), fine-tuned model, and code are publicly released
summary: U.S. immigration law spans thousands of pages of official policy, federal regulations, and procedural guidance that change frequently and carry high stakes for petitioners who lack legal representation. We describe the construction of ImmigrationQA, a source-grounded question-answering dataset of 17,058 pairs across 13 immigration subdomains, and the fine-tuning of a Llama 3.2 3B Instruct model on that dataset using parameter-efficient LoRA. The corpus was assembled from 11 primary and secondary sources -- including the USCIS Policy Manual, 8 CFR, BIA precedent decisions, and community Q&A -- yielding 10,056 validated canonical documents and 18,308 text chunks. Structured QA pairs were generated from these chunks using Claude Sonnet 4.6 via five mode-specific prompts, with 22 pairs rejected for insufficient source-span overlap. The fine-tuned model was evaluated against a held-out split of 993 pairs using LLM-as-judge scoring on a 101-example stratified sample. The fine-tuned model scored a mean of 1.08/3.0 (16.8% fully correct; 101-example stratified eval) versus the Llama 3 8B base model at 0.85/3.0 (4% fully correct), a relative improvement of 27% in mean score; a zero-shot Claude Sonnet baseline scored 1.52/3.0 (25% fully correct). The fine-tuned model shows concentrated improvement in procedural subdomains (travel documents, adjustment of status, nonimmigrant visas) while remaining weak on complex legal reasoning and time-sensitive statistics. The full pipeline ran for approximately $29 in cloud compute. All artifacts -- dataset, model, code, and prompt templates -- are publicly released. The system is not a substitute for legal counsel and does not reflect regulatory changes after the corpus crawl date.

AI.tldr: The paper releases ImmigrationQA, an open immigration-law QA dataset and a cheap LoRA-tuned Llama 3.2 3B model. Fine-tuning helps noticeably versus the base model, but the system is still limited and not suitable as a replacement for legal advice.
AI.motivation: U.S. immigration guidance is large, fast-changing, high-stakes, and difficult for unrepresented petitioners to navigate. The work aims to create an open, source-grounded QA dataset and affordable baseline model to improve access to procedural immigration information.
AI.method: The paper builds ImmigrationQA, a 17,058-pair dataset across 13 immigration subdomains, from 10,056 validated documents and 18,308 text chunks collected from 11 legal and community sources. QA pairs are generated with Claude Sonnet 4.6 using five prompt modes, then a Llama 3.2 3B Instruct model is fine-tuned with LoRA and evaluated on a held-out set using LLM-as-judge scoring over a stratified sample.
AI.result: The fine-tuned model achieved 1.08/3.0 mean score with 16.8% fully correct answers, compared with 0.85/3.0 and 4% fully correct for the Llama 3 8B base model, a 27% relative gain in mean score. However, Claude Sonnet zero-shot still performed better at 1.52/3.0 and 25% fully correct. Gains were strongest in procedural areas, while weaknesses remained in complex legal reasoning and time-sensitive statistics.
AI.conclusion: A low-cost, publicly released, source-grounded immigration QA pipeline can improve a small instruction model over its base baseline, especially for procedural questions, but it still substantially underperforms a stronger zero-shot model and remains unreliable for complex legal reasoning or time-sensitive facts.

title: Mathematical Morphology in Machine Learning
summary: This work introduces mathematical morphology-an established visual computing theory-into machine learning to exploit shape and density aspects often overlooked by standard techniques. We propose a fast clustering algorithm based on morphological reconstruction that accurately preserves cluster shapes and density. This scheme offers unique features: an intrinsic sense of maximal clusters, cost-free noise removal, and diverse growth patterns controlled by structuring elements.Additionally, we propose a novel distance metric combining Minkowski and Chebyshev distances, highly efficient for morphological dilations. In $Z^2$ discrete neighbourhood iterations, it is roughly 1.3 times faster than Manhattan and 329.5 times faster than Euclidean distances. When evaluated using a k-Nearest Neighbours (k-NN) classifier across 33 UCI datasets against 14 other distances, our metric achieved above-average accuracies most frequently (26 of 33 cases) and the best overall accuracy in 9 cases.Finally, we introduce novel morphological classifiers. Unlike current literature, this proposal uniquely models shape, density, and fractal information in datasets.

AI.tldr: This paper brings mathematical morphology into machine learning by proposing a shape-preserving clustering method, a very fast hybrid distance metric, and new classifiers that explicitly model shape, density, and fractal structure.
AI.motivation: Standard machine learning methods often overlook structural properties such as shape and density. The paper is motivated by bringing mathematical morphology into machine learning to exploit these neglected geometric and topological aspects.
AI.method: The authors introduce a clustering algorithm based on morphological reconstruction, design a new distance metric that combines Minkowski and Chebyshev distances for efficient morphological dilation, and develop novel morphological classifiers that model shape, density, and fractal information.
AI.result: The proposed distance metric is about 1.3 times faster than Manhattan distance and 329.5 times faster than Euclidean distance in Z^2 discrete neighbourhood iterations. In k-NN experiments on 33 UCI datasets against 14 competing distances, it produced above-average accuracy in 26 datasets and the best overall accuracy in 9 datasets. The clustering method also preserves cluster shape and density while enabling intrinsic maximal cluster detection and noise removal.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that mathematical morphology can be effectively integrated into machine learning to better capture shape, density, and fractal characteristics, yielding fast and accurate clustering, a highly efficient distance metric, and new morphology-based classifiers.

title: A Persona-Based Evaluation Framework for Pluralistic Alignment in Generative AI
summary: Current alignment paradigms for generative artificial intelligence rely predominantly on monolithic benchmarking frameworks that reduce the plurality of human judgment to aggregated statistical baselines, thereby obscuring cultural, demographic, and contextual variability in evaluation. We introduce a state-space constrained emulation framework for AI evaluation that replaces singular assessment functions with a structured manifold of synthetic cognitive profiles representing diverse human perspectives. We show that modern generative architectures can instantiate and maintain these evaluative personas with high consistency, enabling a form of pluralistic, perspective-dependent benchmarking that more closely reflects real-world consensus variability. However, we further analyze the stability of these simulated evaluators under sequential inference and stochastic prompt perturbations, revealing systematic degradation in persona coherence that manifests as state-space drift and semantic inconsistency. These findings suggest that static alignment constraints are insufficient for sustaining robust evaluative behavior over time. Instead, we argue for the necessity of embedding dynamic, viability-driven regulatory mechanisms within generative systems to preserve coherent cognitive emulation. By framing persona-based evaluation as a structured dynamical system over latent representation manifolds, this study provides a foundation for more adaptive, human-aligned, and context-sensitive approaches to AI evaluation.

AI.tldr: 提出一种用多个可模拟不同人类视角的 synthetic personas 来替代单一 benchmark 的 AI 评估框架；模型能较一致地扮演这些评估者，但在连续推理和随机扰动下会发生 persona drift，因此需要动态调节机制而不是静态对齐约束。
AI.motivation: 动机是 current alignment and benchmarking methods collapse diverse human judgments into statistical averages, which hides cultural, demographic, and contextual variation. The paper aims to build a more pluralistic and context-sensitive evaluation framework that better reflects real-world disagreement and consensus variability.
AI.method: 该论文 proposes a state-space constrained emulation framework. Instead of one monolithic evaluation function, it constructs a structured manifold of synthetic cognitive profiles that emulate diverse human perspectives, and studies their consistency and stability as a dynamical system over latent representation manifolds under sequential inference and stochastic prompt perturbations.
AI.result: 结果表明 modern generative models can instantiate and maintain evaluative personas with high short-term consistency, enabling perspective-dependent benchmarking. However, these simulated evaluators show systematic degradation over time, including state-space drift and semantic inconsistency, especially under sequential inference and stochastic prompt changes.
AI.conclusion: 该论文 concludes that single aggregated benchmarks are insufficient for generative AI alignment evaluation. Persona-based evaluation can better capture human judgment diversity, but evaluator personas drift over time under sequential inference and prompt perturbations. Therefore, dynamic viability-based regulatory mechanisms are needed to preserve coherent evaluative behavior.

title: Graph-Conditioned Mixture of Graph Neural Network Experts for Traffic Forecasting
comment: An accepted paper at the 27th IEEE International Conference on Mobile Data Management (MDM 2026)
summary: Spatio-temporal forecasting on sensor graphs is commonly tackled with a single backbone architecture applied uniformly across all nodes, although graph regions can exhibit different dynamics. Road segments differ in functional class, structure, and traffic behavior, suggesting that node-wise expert specialization can be useful. We propose GC-MoE, a graph-conditioned mixture of experts framework that assigns each node a personalized combination of frozen forecasting experts based on graph topology and the recent traffic input window. GC-MoE combines frozen pretrained spatio-temporal GNN experts with an input-aware, spatially contextualized router while training only a lightweight routing module. We also study a bounded graph-conditioned output refinement layer as an optional extension and include node-adaptive ST-LoRA adapters only as an ablation diagnostic. Across four standard benchmarks (PEMS04, PEMS07, METR-LA, and PEMS-BAY), GC-MoE improves MAE over a zero-parameter ensemble baseline, with competitive RMSE and MAPE, while training only ~17K parameters on top of 1.5M frozen expert weights. The implementation is available at https://github.com/Ahghaffari/gc_moe.

AI.tldr: GC-MoE routes each sensor node to a custom mix of frozen traffic-forecasting experts using graph structure and recent inputs, improving efficiency and MAE with very few trainable parameters.
AI.motivation: Existing spatio-temporal forecasting methods usually apply one shared backbone to all nodes, but different graph regions and road segments have heterogeneous structures and traffic dynamics. This motivates node-wise expert specialization instead of uniform modeling.
AI.method: The paper proposes GC-MoE, a graph-conditioned mixture-of-experts framework. It uses multiple frozen pretrained spatio-temporal GNN experts, and a lightweight router that assigns each node a personalized mixture of experts based on graph topology and recent traffic observations. The authors also evaluate an optional bounded graph-conditioned output refinement layer and node-adaptive ST-LoRA adapters as ablations.
AI.result: On PEMS04, PEMS07, METR-LA, and PEMS-BAY, GC-MoE outperforms a zero-parameter ensemble baseline in MAE and remains competitive on RMSE and MAPE, while adding only about 17K trainable parameters on top of roughly 1.5M frozen expert parameters.
AI.conclusion: GC-MoE demonstrates that node-specific expert routing over frozen spatio-temporal GNN experts can improve traffic forecasting efficiency and accuracy, achieving better MAE than a zero-parameter ensemble while training only a very small routing module.

title: Semantic Motion Anchors: Bridging Motion and Meaning in Co-Speech Gestures
summary: Learning a shared representation between spoken text and gesture is central to co-speech gesture retrieval, synthesis, and understanding, but remains challenging for semantically meaningful gestures whose communicative intent is not captured by motion alone. Direct contrastive alignment between transcripts and continuous motion embeddings often overemphasizes low-level kinematics and misses the symbolic content of semantic gestures. We propose semantic motion anchors, natural-language abstractions of gesture motion capturing physical form and communicative intent. Our method discretizes 3D gestures into body-hand motion primitives, verbalizes them into structured descriptions, and grounds them in the transcript to provide auxiliary contrastive supervision. On BEAT2, our method improves text-to-gesture R@1 by 8.2% over a direct text-motion baseline and outperforms prior retrieval approaches on text to gesture and gesture to text retrieval directions. Beyond aggregate retrieval metrics, semantic motion anchor supervision helps retrieve gestures that are semantically meaningful for the spoken query, rather than defaulting to generic motion patterns. A downstream retrieval-augmented gesture generation study showed that users significantly preferred gestures retrieved by our approach over a retrieval-augmented generation baseline, demonstrating that semantically grounded retrieval translates to gestures that better convey communicative intent in downstream generation.

AI.tldr: Use language-based semantic motion anchors to describe gesture form and intent, then train text-gesture alignment with this extra supervision; it retrieves more meaningful gestures and improves downstream generation.
AI.motivation: Direct contrastive learning between transcripts and continuous motion embeddings tends to focus on low-level kinematics and fails to capture the symbolic, communicative intent of semantic gestures. The authors aim to bridge this gap with language-based abstractions of gesture meaning.
AI.method: The paper discretizes 3D gesture motion into body-hand motion primitives, verbalizes these primitives into structured natural-language descriptions called semantic motion anchors, grounds them in transcripts, and uses them as auxiliary contrastive supervision for text-gesture representation learning.
AI.result: On the BEAT2 dataset, the method improves text-to-gesture retrieval R@1 by 8.2% over a direct text-motion baseline and outperforms prior methods in both text-to-gesture and gesture-to-text retrieval. User studies in retrieval-augmented gesture generation also show significant preference for gestures retrieved by this method.
AI.conclusion: Semantic motion anchors improve cross-modal alignment between speech text and gesture by injecting natural-language abstractions of gesture meaning, leading to better retrieval of semantically meaningful gestures and improved downstream gesture generation preference.

title: Equivariant Latent Alignment via Flow Matching under Group Symmetries
summary: Geometry-aware generative models and novel view synthesis approaches have shown strong potential in visual fidelity and consistency. In parallel, equivariant representation learning has emerged as a powerful framework for constructing latent spaces where analytically known group transformations could act directly, capturing geometric structure in data and enhancing both interpretability and generalization in novel view synthesis. However, we identify that existing approaches often suffer from latent misalignment, a discrepancy between the intended group action and the actually required transformations in the latent space. Consequently, the learned latents often fail to consistently preserve the equivariant relations imposed by the underlying group symmetry. To address this, we propose Residual Latent Flow, a flow-based framework that corrects the misaligned latents, thereby improving compliance with the underlying equivariance relation. Our comprehensive experiments show that our method significantly reduces latent misalignment and improves novel view synthesis quality, under rotation groups SO(n).

AI.tldr: A flow-based residual correction is applied to equivariant latent spaces to fix latent misalignment, yielding better symmetry preservation and higher-quality novel view synthesis.
AI.motivation: Existing geometry-aware generative models and equivariant representation learning methods often exhibit latent misalignment, where the intended group action does not match the true latent transformation needed, weakening preservation of equivariant structure and hurting novel view synthesis consistency.
AI.method: The paper proposes Residual Latent Flow, a flow-based latent correction framework that adjusts misaligned latent representations so that analytically defined group actions better match the transformations actually required in latent space.
AI.result: Experiments show that the method significantly reduces latent misalignment and improves novel view synthesis quality for rotation groups SO(n).
AI.conclusion: Residual Latent Flow corrects latent misalignment in equivariant latent spaces and improves compliance with group equivariance, leading to better novel view synthesis under rotation groups SO(n).

title: HADT: A Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Differential Transformer for Autonomous Earth Observation Satellite Cluster
comment: Accepted in ECML-PKDD 2026. arXiv admin note: text overlap with arXiv:2511.12792
summary: This work addresses the problem of autonomous resource management in heterogeneous satellite cluster conducting Earth Observation (EO) missions including optical and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellites. In autonomous operation mode, satellites are equipped with intelligent capabilities enabling real-time decision-making based on the latest conditions, while requiring minimal interaction with ground operators. Traditional scheduling approaches typically rely on mathematical models to represent satellite mission and resource management. Then, this problem is solved by using optimization algorithms. However, such solutions become less effective when the underlying models are not available, over complex, and inaccurate due to dynamic changes and uncertainties inherent in the space mission environment. A promising alternative is to reformulate the problem as a sequential decision-making process and apply model-free reinforcement learning techniques to enable adaptive and real-time resource management. To this end, we propose a novel transformer-based architecture tailored for heterogeneous satellite cluster autonomous EO Mission with relational observations-actions tokenization and differential attention mechanism. Our experimental results demonstrate significant performance improvements compared to the available baselines. Moreover, the proposed architecture exhibits strong adaptability and transferability with respect to varying numbers of satellite clusters.

AI.tldr: 论文用无模型强化学习+定制Transformer解决异构卫星集群EO任务的自主资源管理，比传统基线更强，且能适应不同规模的卫星集群。/ TL;DR: The paper uses model-free RL plus a customized Transformer for autonomous EO resource management in heterogeneous satellite clusters, outperforming baselines and generalizing across different cluster sizes.
AI.motivation: 动机在于传统基于数学建模和优化的调度方法在模型缺失、系统过于复杂或环境动态不确定时效果下降，因此需要一种无需精确模型、可自适应实时决策的方法。/ The motivation is that traditional model-based scheduling and optimization become unreliable when models are unavailable, overly complex, or inaccurate under dynamic and uncertain space environments, motivating a model-free adaptive real-time approach.
AI.method: 方法上，作者将卫星任务与资源管理重构为序列决策问题，并采用无模型强化学习；核心模型是专为异构卫星集群设计的Transformer，包含关系化观测-动作tokenization和differential attention机制。/ Methodologically, the authors reformulate mission and resource management as a sequential decision-making problem, apply model-free reinforcement learning, and introduce a Transformer tailored to heterogeneous satellite clusters with relational observation-action tokenization and a differential attention mechanism.
AI.result: 实验结果表明，该方法相较现有基线取得了显著性能提升，并且在卫星集群规模变化时表现出较强的适应性与可迁移性。/ Experimental results show significant improvements over available baselines, along with strong adaptability and transferability across varying satellite cluster sizes.
AI.conclusion: 该论文提出了一种面向异构地球观测卫星集群自主资源管理的Transformer架构，通过关系化观测-动作标记与差分注意力机制，实现了更高效、更具适应性的实时决策。/ The paper concludes that a novel Transformer architecture for autonomous resource management in heterogeneous EO satellite clusters delivers more effective and adaptive real-time decision-making through relational observation-action tokenization and differential attention.

title: MAAT: Multi-phase Adapter-Aware Targeted Unlearning
summary: Machine unlearning evaluation is structurally skewed: Why-type questions, which probe causal and relational knowledge, comprise less than 0.06% of CounterFact, 0.6% of ZSRE, and less than 1.3% of TOFU, MUSE, and WMDP-Cyber. This near-zero representation means that methods that fail on causal knowledge can score highly in aggregate, and this failure is undetectable without balanced evaluation. We present 5WBENCH, a balanced 5,000-sample benchmark with 1,000 examples per 5W category (Who, What, When, Where, Why), making causal unlearning failures quantifiable for the first time. Using 5WBENCH, we show that no existing baseline simultaneously achieves high forgetting and high retention on Why-type questions: aggressive forgetting degrades retained knowledge, while conservative methods fail to forget causal facts. Why-type difficulty stems from multi-hop reasoning chains (44% of Why entries vs. less than or equal to 2% for others) and gradient dilution over 40.1-token answer spans. We present MAAT (Multi-phase Adapter-Aware Targeted Unlearning), a three-phase framework operating on LoRA adapter weights, combining gradient-projected ascent, SVD rank-dimension pruning, task vector negation, and hybrid KL-hidden-state retain repair. MAAT is the first method to simultaneously achieve high forgetting and high retention on Why-type causal knowledge, reaching a new operating point on the forget-retain Pareto frontier. We make our code publicly available.

AI.tldr: 论文指出机器遗忘评测对 Why 问题严重失衡，提出平衡基准 5WBENCH 和针对 LoRA 的三阶段遗忘方法 MAAT；结果显示只有 MAAT 能在因果 Why 知识上同时做好“忘掉该忘的”和“保留该留的”。 / The paper shows that machine unlearning evaluation is badly skewed against Why questions, introduces the balanced 5WBENCH benchmark and the LoRA-based three-phase MAAT method, and finds that only MAAT can both forget the target causal Why knowledge and preserve non-target knowledge well.
AI.motivation: 作者发现主流机器遗忘评测几乎不包含 Why 类问题，因此模型即使无法遗忘因果与关系知识，也可能在总体分数上表现良好。这使关键失效模式不可见，因此需要一个平衡评测集，并设计更适合因果知识遗忘的方法。 / The motivation is that existing machine unlearning evaluations contain almost no Why-type questions, so models can score well overall while still failing to forget causal and relational knowledge. This hides a critical failure mode, motivating a balanced benchmark and a method tailored to causal unlearning.
AI.method: 方法包括两部分：一是构建 5WBENCH，一个包含 5000 个样本、每个 5W 类别各 1000 条的平衡基准；二是提出 MAAT（Multi-phase Adapter-Aware Targeted Unlearning），一个作用于 LoRA adapter 权重的三阶段框架，结合 gradient-projected ascent、SVD rank-dimension pruning、task vector negation，以及混合 KL-hidden-state retain repair。 / The method has two parts: (1) 5WBENCH, a balanced 5,000-sample benchmark with 1,000 examples for each 5W category; and (2) MAAT, a three-phase framework operating on LoRA adapter weights that combines gradient-projected ascent, SVD rank-dimension pruning, task vector negation, and hybrid KL-hidden-state retain repair.
AI.result: 实验表明，现有基线在 Why 类问题上无法同时兼顾高遗忘与高保留：激进遗忘会损伤保留知识，保守方法又无法真正忘掉因果事实。5WBENCH 还揭示 Why 类问题更难，原因在于更多多跳推理链（44%）和更长答案跨度（40.1 tokens）。MAAT 在 Why 型因果知识上首次同时达到高遗忘和高保留。 / Experiments show that existing baselines cannot simultaneously achieve high forgetting and high retention on Why-type questions: aggressive forgetting harms retained knowledge, while conservative methods fail to erase causal facts. 5WBENCH also reveals that Why questions are harder due to more multi-hop reasoning chains (44%) and longer answer spans (40.1 tokens). MAAT is the first to achieve both strong forgetting and strong retention on Why-type causal knowledge.
AI.conclusion: 现有机器遗忘评测在 Why 类问题上严重失衡，导致因果知识遗忘失败长期被掩盖。论文提出 5WBENCH 与 MAAT，并表明 MAAT 首次能够在 Why 型因果知识上同时实现较高遗忘与较高保留，推进 forget-retain Pareto frontier。 / Existing machine unlearning benchmarks are severely imbalanced on Why-type questions, masking failures on causal knowledge. The paper introduces 5WBENCH and MAAT, and shows that MAAT is the first method to achieve both strong forgetting and strong retention on Why-type causal knowledge, advancing the forget-retain Pareto frontier.

title: The Architecture of Errors: From Universal Impossibility to Patch-Local LLM Reliability
summary: Universal LLM reliability is not a finite-library problem: across all possible tasks, tools, schemas, knowledge sources, and evaluator expectations, new intervention-distinguishable failure modes can appear without bound, so no finite intervention dictionary can guarantee bounded residual error for every such mode. But deployed systems do not operate over the whole universe. They operate inside operationally bounded patches (legal review, medical RAG, code repair, customer-support agents, contract extraction) with recurring tasks, schemas, tools, and evaluator expectations. Within such patches, empirical evidence suggests failures are sparse, repetitive, and concentrated in a small recurring catalogue, so reliability becomes a local catalogue-discovery and intervention-coverage problem rather than an exponential token-length problem. We formalize this transition with two propositions and one corollary. Proposition 1 is the worst-case-mode-wise negative result: no finite intervention dictionary covers every distinguishable failure mode of an unbounded domain. Corollary 1 is the inverse-discovery implication: the logarithmic upper bound on mode discovery cannot accommodate linearly more distinct tail modes without exponentially more observed hard-failure events. Proposition 2 is the positive patch-local result: under log active-mode exposure and head-heavy coverage, a sufficient per-hard-decision intervention budget grows polylogarithmically in sequence length and becomes domain-constant once the patch catalogue saturates. The framework relocates rather than dissolves long-context difficulty: where the number of hard decisions itself grows with task length, reliability remains hard; the contribution is to identify the on-axis intervention rather than to make those regimes easy.

AI.tldr: Global LLM reliability is impossible with a finite set of fixes, but local reliability in bounded real-world domains may be practical because failures repeat and can be covered by a small discovered catalogue.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to resolve the mismatch between pessimistic worst-case views of LLM reliability and the practical observation that many deployed systems improve reliably within narrow domains. The paper asks when reliability is fundamentally impossible and when it becomes manageable.
AI.method: The paper develops a theoretical framework with two propositions and one corollary. It contrasts worst-case unbounded domains with bounded deployment patches, analyzes failure-mode discovery and intervention coverage, and derives scaling claims under assumptions such as logarithmic active-mode exposure and head-heavy failure distributions.
