AI.result: Proposition 1 shows no finite intervention dictionary can cover all distinguishable failure modes in an unbounded domain. Corollary 1 states that discovering linearly more tail modes would require exponentially more hard-failure observations under a logarithmic discovery bound. Proposition 2 shows that in bounded patches, if active modes grow logarithmically and common modes dominate, the intervention budget per hard decision grows only polylogarithmically with sequence length and eventually becomes constant after catalogue saturation.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that universal LLM reliability cannot be guaranteed by any finite library of interventions over an unbounded task universe, but in operationally bounded deployment patches, reliability can become tractable because failures are sparse, repetitive, and coverable by a small recurring catalogue.

title: Vision-Based Localization in Dense Urban Environments: A Case Study of an Urban Village in China
summary: Urban villages, the widespread informal settlements which have emerged as a result of rapid urbanization, are now major residential hubs for migrant workers in large cities in China. The dense arrangement of buildings in these areas often leads to unreliable GPS signals, while incomplete mapping data further impairs accurate route planning and navigation. These issues not only hinder everyday mobility but also pose significant challenges for emergency response, as confusing road layouts and GPS inaccuracies can complicate evacuation efforts. To address these challenges, we propose a practical vision-based geo-localization solution tailored for dense urban environments. Our approach features a low-cost data collection pipeline utilizing a dual-camera system, comprising a panoramic camera and a smartphone camera, to capture synchronized 360-degree panoramas and query images. Using Shipai Village, a well-known densely populated urban village in Guangzhou, as a case study, we develop a specialized image geo-localization dataset. We then assess and compare the performance of existing models across various scene types to identify their strengths and weaknesses. The findings demonstrate both the potential and limitations of visual-based localization in dense urban-village environments. Our framework aims to enhance pedestrian navigation, last-mile delivery, and emergency management in areas with poor GPS coverage, ultimately supporting the vulnerable populations living within these informal settlements.

AI.tldr: They create a low-cost visual geo-localization pipeline and dataset for a dense urban village in Guangzhou, then test existing models and find that camera-based localization can help where GPS fails, though current methods are not yet fully reliable.
AI.motivation: Rapid urbanization has produced dense urban villages in China where migrant workers live. In these areas, unreliable GPS signals and incomplete maps make navigation, route planning, and emergency evacuation difficult, creating a need for a practical localization solution that works under poor GPS coverage.
AI.method: The authors build a low-cost dual-camera data collection pipeline using a panoramic camera and a smartphone camera to capture synchronized 360-degree panoramas and query images. Using Shipai Village in Guangzhou as a case study, they construct a specialized image geo-localization dataset and evaluate existing geo-localization models across different scene types.
AI.result: The study develops a dedicated dataset for dense urban-village geo-localization and shows that existing visual localization models have measurable potential in such environments, while also revealing important weaknesses and performance differences across scene categories.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that vision-based geo-localization is a practical and promising supplement to GPS for dense urban-village environments, but current models still show clear limitations depending on scene type and mapping complexity.

title: GraphARC: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Graph-Based Abstract Reasoning
comment: Accepted at KDD 2026 Datasets and Benchmarks Track
summary: Relational reasoning lies at the heart of intelligence, but existing benchmarks are typically confined to formats such as grids or text. We introduce GraphARC, a benchmark for abstract reasoning on graph-structured data. GraphARC generalizes the few-shot transformation learning paradigm of the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC). Each task requires inferring a transformation rule from a few input-output pairs and applying it to a new test graph, covering local, global, and hierarchical graph transformations. Unlike grid-based ARC, GraphARC instances can be generated at scale across diverse graph families and sizes, enabling systematic evaluation of generalization abilities. We evaluate state-of-the-art language models on GraphARC and observe clear limitations. Models can answer questions about graph properties but often fail to solve the full graph transformation task, revealing a comprehension-execution gap. Performance further degrades on larger instances, exposing scaling barriers. More broadly, by combining aspects of node classification, link prediction, and graph generation within a single framework, GraphARC provides a promising testbed for future graph foundation models.

AI.tldr: GraphARC is a new scalable benchmark for few-shot abstract reasoning on graphs. It tests whether models can infer graph transformation rules from examples and generalize them. Current language models struggle, particularly on full execution and larger instances.
AI.motivation: Existing reasoning benchmarks are mostly restricted to grids or text and do not adequately test abstract reasoning over graph-structured data. The authors aim to provide a systematic, scalable benchmark for evaluating relational reasoning and generalization on graphs.
AI.method: The paper introduces GraphARC, a graph-based extension of the ARC few-shot transformation learning paradigm. Each task provides several input-output graph pairs from which a model must infer a transformation rule and apply it to a new test graph, spanning local, global, and hierarchical transformations across diverse graph families and sizes.
AI.result: State-of-the-art language models can answer isolated questions about graph properties but often fail on the complete graph transformation task. Their performance declines further on larger graphs, indicating both a comprehension-execution gap and scaling limitations.
AI.conclusion: GraphARC is a scalable benchmark for abstract relational reasoning on graph-structured data, and current state-of-the-art language models show significant limitations on full graph transformation tasks, especially as instance size grows.

title: Revisiting Padded Transformer Expressivity: Which Architectural Choices Matter and Which Don't
summary: Recent work describes what transformers can and cannot compute through connections to boolean circuits, but existing results lack exact characterizations and are sensitive to modeling choices. Padded transformers -- to whose input filler symbols such as ``...'' are appended -- emerge as a useful gadget for establishing equivalences to circuit classes by providing polynomial space for adaptive parallel computation. However, only a limited set of padded transformer idealizations has been studied, leaving open how robustly these equivalences hold under changes to attention type, model width, and uniformity. We find that, under practical assumptions, padded transformers are surprisingly robust to all of these, and identify numeric precision and model depth as the main factors affecting expressivity. Concretely, we prove that polynomially padded $\text{L-uniform}$ constant-precision transformers are equivalent to $\text{L-uniform AC}^0$, while growing-precision ones achieve $\text{L-uniform TC}^0$ regardless of width. Furthermore, looping enables sequential processing analogous to circuits: $\log^d N$-looped constant-precision transformers reach $\text{FO-uniform AC}^d$, and growing-precision ones reach $\text{FO-uniform TC}^d$. Interestingly, growing width or precision beyond logarithmic does not increase expressivity, and all our results hold for both softmax and average hard attention transformers.

AI.tldr: The paper shows padded transformers have stable, exact circuit-class characterizations: precision and depth matter most, while width and attention type matter much less.
AI.motivation: Prior transformer-to-circuit results were incomplete and brittle with respect to modeling assumptions. The paper aims to determine whether padded-transformer expressivity results are exact and robust across practical design choices such as attention type, width, precision, depth, and uniformity.
AI.method: The paper proves equivalence theorems between several padded transformer variants and standard Boolean circuit classes, varying precision, width, attention type, padding, looping depth, and uniformity assumptions. It analyzes both softmax and average hard attention under L-uniform and FO-uniform settings.
AI.result: Polynomially padded L-uniform constant-precision transformers are equivalent to L-uniform AC^0; growing-precision variants are equivalent to L-uniform TC^0 regardless of width. With looping, log^d N-looped constant-precision transformers capture FO-uniform AC^d, while growing-precision ones capture FO-uniform TC^d. Increasing width or precision beyond logarithmic yields no further expressivity gain, and the results hold for both softmax and average hard attention.
AI.conclusion: Padded transformers have robust circuit-theoretic characterizations under practical modeling choices. Their expressivity is governed mainly by numeric precision and depth/looping, not by attention variant, width, or super-logarithmic precision/width growth.

title: COFT: Counterfactual-Conformal Decoding for Fair Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Large Language Models
summary: Large language models (LLMs) can reveal and amplify societal biases during chain-of-thought (CoT) generation. We present COFT (Chain of Fair Thought), a training-free decoding method that applies token-level fairness control at decode time, with distribution-free marginal validity guarantees (under exchangeability) for any frozen causal language model. COFT operates in three stages. First, it creates a masked counterfactual prompt by replacing sensitive spans with neutral tokens. Second, it compares the factual and masked logit distributions through lightweight logit fusion to attenuate attribute-driven biases. Third, it uses dual-branch split-conformal calibration to certify per-step candidate token sets at a user-chosen risk level. We evaluate COFT across six models and multiple bias benchmarks. Our method reduces standard bias metrics by 30-55% (median 38%) while preserving task utility and language quality. Reasoning accuracies remain unchanged within run-to-run noise margins. The computational overhead is modest, equivalent to one additional cached forward pass (<=11%). COFT offers a clear, auditable path to safer CoT generation with significant bias reduction, negligible utility loss, and no requirement for retraining, auxiliary classifiers, or weight access.

AI.tldr: COFT is a training-free, decode-time fairness control method for LLM chain-of-thought. It masks sensitive attributes, fuses logits from factual and counterfactual prompts, and uses conformal calibration to guarantee controlled token selection. It cuts bias substantially with minimal utility loss and low overhead.
AI.motivation: Large language models can expose and amplify societal bias during chain-of-thought generation. Existing mitigation methods often require retraining, auxiliary classifiers, or access to model weights. The paper aims to provide a practical, auditable, training-free bias-control method that works at decoding time for frozen models while offering statistical guarantees.
AI.method: The paper proposes COFT (Chain of Fair Thought), a three-stage decode-time method for frozen causal language models. First, it builds a masked counterfactual prompt by replacing sensitive spans with neutral tokens. Second, it performs lightweight logit fusion between factual and masked logit distributions to reduce attribute-driven bias. Third, it applies dual-branch split-conformal calibration to produce per-step candidate token sets with marginal validity guarantees under exchangeability.
AI.result: Across six models and multiple bias benchmarks, COFT reduces standard bias metrics by 30-55% with a median reduction of 38%. Reasoning accuracy remains effectively unchanged within run-to-run noise, task utility and language quality are preserved, and the extra cost is small, roughly one additional cached forward pass with overhead of up to 11%.
AI.conclusion: COFT is an effective training-free decoding framework for reducing bias in chain-of-thought generation. It substantially lowers bias while preserving reasoning accuracy, language quality, and utility, with only modest computational overhead and without requiring retraining or model weight access.

title: Simple Token-Efficient Vision-Language Model for Case-level Pathology Synoptic Report Generation
summary: Generating clinically useful pathology reports for pathology cases from whole-slide images (WSIs) is challenging due to gigapixel resolution, long visual-token sequences, and the complexity of case-level reasoning, where a single case may contain multiple WSIs with heterogeneous tissues and ambiguous findings. We present a simple token-efficient vision--language model for case-level synoptic report generation that remains practical under constrained GPU memory. Our architecture follows a minimal three-component design: a frozen pathology patch encoder, a lightweight two-layer MLP vision-language aligner, and a large language model decoder, with an explicit WSI marker token to separate slides within a case. Training proceeds in two supervised stages: (1) aligner-only WSI captioning using heterogeneous WSI-text pairs, and (2) case-level supervised fine-tuning on case-report pairs for structured report generation. To reduce sequence length, we represent each slide using $512 \times 512$ patches at $5\times$ magnification, which reduces the average sequence length by up to $64\times$ times compared to the commonly used $20\times$ patches. Combined with efficient training techniques, we enable practical training with only half a NVIDIA H100 GPU. Across both training stages, our approach achieves high ROUGE-L/METEOR/BLEU-4 scores while being substantially more efficient in memory and runtime. In AI-based evaluations, our model is consistently preferred over strong baselines. Extensive ablations characterize performance-efficiency trade-offs and identify simple choices that improve robustness in multi-WSI settings. Overall, this work provides a strong, reproducible baseline for efficient pathology report generation, lowering the barrier to multi-WSI VLM research under limited compute.

AI.tldr: A lightweight multi-WSI pathology VLM uses coarse 5x patches and two-stage supervised training to generate synoptic reports efficiently, matching strong quality metrics while greatly lowering memory and compute requirements.
AI.motivation: Existing pathology report generation is difficult because WSIs are gigapixel-scale, produce very long token sequences, and require case-level reasoning across multiple heterogeneous slides. The work is motivated by the need for a practical and efficient approach that works under limited compute and GPU memory.
AI.method: The method uses a three-part architecture: a frozen pathology patch encoder, a lightweight two-layer MLP aligner, and an LLM decoder, with explicit WSI marker tokens between slides. Training has two supervised stages: WSI captioning for aligner-only training on heterogeneous WSI-text pairs, then case-level fine-tuning on case-report pairs. Sequence length is reduced by using 512x512 patches at 5x magnification.
AI.result: The model achieves strong ROUGE-L, METEOR, and BLEU-4 across both training stages, is consistently preferred over strong baselines in AI-based evaluation, and substantially reduces memory/runtime costs. It can be trained with only half of an NVIDIA H100 GPU and includes ablation findings for performance-efficiency trade-offs and robustness in multi-WSI scenarios.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that a simple, token-efficient case-level vision-language architecture can generate structured pathology synoptic reports effectively under strict GPU-memory limits, while serving as a strong and reproducible multi-WSI baseline.

title: Vector Linking via Cross-Model Local Isometric Consistency
summary: We study Vector Linking: given two embedding clouds produced by different black-box encoders over partially overlapping datasets, recover cross-model object correspondences using only vectors. Empirically and theoretically, we show that independently trained contrastive encoders exhibit local geometric consistency: short-range distances are approximately preserved up to a scale factor, while long-range distances are not due to model-specific distortion. Building on this, we propose an iterative, reference-based geometric embedding hashing that recovers vector links from a tiny seed set of paired anchors. It represents each vector by distances to sampled paired anchors, proposes candidate links via hash-space matching, and aggregates evidence across views in a Beta-Bernoulli posterior to bootstrap high-confidence links as new anchors. Experiments across multiple benchmarks and embedding model pairs demonstrate accurate and robust linking under varying overlap, seed budgets, and out-of-domain anchors, with applications to vector database integration and cross-model clustering. Code is available at https://github.com/DBgroup-Edinburgh/VecLinking.

AI.tldr: TL;DR: The paper shows that different contrastive embedding models preserve nearby geometry similarly enough to match objects across embedding spaces. Using a few paired anchors, their iterative geometric hashing method finds candidate matches from anchor-distance signatures and bootstraps more links with Bayesian confidence aggregation, performing well across diverse linking settings.
AI.motivation: Different vector databases or models often encode overlapping objects with different black-box embedding models, but raw vectors are not directly aligned. The authors aim to recover cross-model object correspondences using vectors alone, without access to model internals, by exploiting geometric properties shared across independently trained contrastive encoders.
AI.method: The paper proposes iterative, reference-based geometric embedding hashing. Starting from a small seed set of paired anchors, each vector is represented by its distances to sampled paired anchors. Candidate correspondences are generated by matching in this hash/reference space. Multiple views are aggregated with a Beta-Bernoulli posterior, and high-confidence predicted links are added back as new anchors for iterative bootstrapping.
AI.result: Empirically and theoretically, the paper finds local geometric consistency across independently trained contrastive encoders: short-range distances are roughly preserved up to scale, while long-range distances are distorted. Experiments on multiple benchmarks and model pairs show accurate and robust linking under varying dataset overlap, limited seed anchors, and out-of-domain anchors, supporting applications such as vector database integration and cross-model clustering.
AI.conclusion: Vector links between partially overlapping embedding spaces from different black-box encoders can be recovered using only vectors, because independently trained contrastive encoders preserve local geometry approximately up to a scale factor. The proposed iterative reference-based geometric embedding hashing method uses a tiny seed set and progressively bootstraps new reliable links, achieving robust performance across benchmarks and settings.

title: Representation Collapse in Sequential Post-Training of Large Language Models
summary: Large language models are now adapted through chains of post-training stages rather than through a single instruction-tuning pass. This paper studies whether such sequential post-training gradually compresses internal representations into low-rank, anisotropic, and homogeneous feature spaces. We define a measurement suite for hidden states, logits, token trajectories, and LoRA updates, and we use it to analyze supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, safety/refusal tuning, math and code specialization, and long chain-of-thought tuning under controlled stage orderings. The central hypothesis is that excessive representation concentration is not merely a geometric curiosity: it predicts reduced plasticity during later adaptation, weaker out-of-domain generalization, and poorer calibration. We further evaluate lightweight interventions, including mixed-domain replay, feature refresh, representation diversity regularization, and LoRA update decorrelation, as ways to preserve future learnability without giving up the behavioral gains of post-training.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how multi-stage post-training may make LLM representations overly concentrated, which could reduce future learnability and robustness, and it tests simple methods to preserve adaptability without losing behavioral improvements.
AI.motivation: Modern LLMs are adapted through multiple sequential post-training stages rather than a single instruction-tuning pass, so the paper investigates whether this process progressively concentrates representations and whether that geometric change has practical negative consequences.
AI.method: The paper proposes a measurement suite covering hidden states, logits, token trajectories, and LoRA updates, then applies it across multiple post-training stages under controlled ordering: supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, safety/refusal tuning, math/code specialization, and long chain-of-thought tuning. It also evaluates interventions such as mixed-domain replay, feature refresh, representation diversity regularization, and LoRA update decorrelation.
AI.result: The abstract states the central hypothesis and evaluation setup rather than final quantified outcomes, but it indicates that excessive representation concentration is expected to predict reduced plasticity, weaker out-of-domain generalization, and poorer calibration, and that lightweight interventions are assessed as possible remedies.
AI.conclusion: Sequential post-training in large language models tends to compress internal representations into low-rank, anisotropic, and homogeneous spaces, and this concentration likely harms later adaptability, out-of-domain generalization, and calibration; lightweight interventions may mitigate these effects while retaining post-training benefits.

title: Same Patient, Different Words, Different Diagnosis? Evaluating Semantic Stability in Clinical LLMs
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in clinical applications. However, their behavior remains highly sensitive to subtle linguistic variations, such as rephrasing or syntactic variation. This sensitivity poses risks in safety-critical healthcare settings, where semantically equivalent inputs should produce consistent predictions. However, a key challenge is to ensure that prompt variations truly preserve clinical meaning, as embedding-based similarity metrics often fail to capture distinctions involving negation, temporality, or severity. To address this limitation, we propose a semantic verification framework based on Natural Language Inference (NLI) to filter meaning-preserving prompt variations, which are further refined using an LLM-as-a-judge and audited by a clinical expert. In addition, we introduce three metrics to quantify model sensitivity: MeaningPreserving Variation Sensitivity (MVS), confidence variation (ΔC), and Worst-Case Instability (WCI). We evaluate 16 open-source general-purpose (GP) and medical LLMs within the same model families and parameter scales, using reformulated prompts derived from the DiagnosisQA and MedQA datasets. Our results demonstrate that robustness differences between domain-specific (DS) models are mixed and highly model-dependent, i.e., domain specialization does not consistently improve or reduce robustness to meaning-preserving prompt reformulations. Several DS models rank among the most robust (when compared with GP counterparts), and strong GP baselines remain competitive as well.

AI.tldr: 中文：这篇论文研究医疗LLM是否会因等义改写而改变答案，并提出一种基于NLI的严格语义筛选方法和三项鲁棒性指标。结论是：医疗专用模型不一定比通用模型更稳，鲁棒性主要取决于具体模型。 English: This paper studies whether medical LLMs change their answers under semantically equivalent prompt reformulations, proposes an NLI-based filtering pipeline plus three robustness metrics, and finds that medical specialization does not consistently make models more robust than general-purpose ones.
AI.motivation: 中文：LLM已被广泛用于临床场景，但其输出对细微措辞变化非常敏感。在医疗这种安全关键环境中，语义等价输入应当产生一致预测；而现有基于嵌入的相似度方法难以可靠识别否定、时序、严重程度等临床关键语义差异。 English: LLMs are increasingly used in clinical applications, but their outputs are highly sensitive to subtle wording changes. In safety-critical healthcare settings, semantically equivalent inputs should yield consistent predictions, yet embedding-based similarity metrics often fail to preserve clinically crucial distinctions such as negation, temporality, and severity.
AI.method: 中文：论文提出基于自然语言推断（NLI）的语义验证框架，用于筛选真正保持临床语义不变的提示改写；随后结合LLM-as-a-judge进一步精炼，并由临床专家审计。作者还设计了三项敏感性指标：MVS、置信度变化ΔC和最坏情况不稳定性WCI，并在DiagnosisQA和MedQA生成的改写提示上评估16个开源通用与医疗LLM。 English: The paper proposes an NLI-based semantic verification framework to filter prompt reformulations that truly preserve clinical meaning, then refines them with an LLM-as-a-judge and audits them with a clinical expert. It also introduces three sensitivity metrics: MVS, confidence variation (ΔC), and Worst-Case Instability (WCI), and evaluates 16 open-source GP and medical LLMs on reformulated prompts from DiagnosisQA and MedQA.
AI.result: 中文：实验表明，不同模型在面对语义保持型提示改写时的鲁棒性差异显著，且领域专用化的影响并不一致：它既不会稳定提升，也不会稳定削弱鲁棒性。部分DS模型在与同家族、同规模GP模型比较时排名靠前，但一些强GP模型仍表现出相当竞争力。 English: Results show substantial robustness differences across models under meaning-preserving prompt reformulations, and the effect of domain specialization is inconsistent: it neither reliably improves nor degrades robustness. Some DS models rank among the most robust relative to same-family, same-scale GP counterparts, while strong GP models remain highly competitive.
AI.conclusion: 中文：在临床问答场景中，领域专用LLM对语义等价提示改写的鲁棒性并不稳定提升，表现出明显的模型依赖性；部分DS模型更稳健，但强GP基线同样具有竞争力。 English: In clinical QA settings, domain-specific LLMs do not consistently gain robustness to meaning-preserving prompt reformulations; robustness is strongly model-dependent. Some DS models are more robust, but strong GP baselines remain competitive.

title: Annotations Are Not All You Need: A Cross-modal Knowledge Transfer Network for Unsupervised Temporal Sentence Grounding
summary: This paper addresses the task of temporal sentence grounding (TSG). Although many respectable works have made decent achievements in this important topic, they severely rely on massive expensive video-query paired annotations, which require a tremendous amount of human effort to collect in real-world applications. To this end, in this paper, we target a more practical but challenging TSG setting: unsupervised temporal sentence grounding, where both paired video-query and segment boundary annotations are unavailable during the network training. Considering that some other cross-modal tasks provide many easily available yet cheap labels, we tend to collect and transfer their simple cross-modal alignment knowledge into our complex scenarios: 1) We first explore the entity-aware object-guided appearance knowledge from the paired Image-Noun task, and adapt them into each independent video frame; 2) Then, we extract the event-aware action representation from the paired Video-Verb task, and further refine the action representation into more practical but complicated real-world cases by a newly proposed copy-paste approach; 3) By modulating and transferring both appearance and action knowledge into our challenging unsupervised task, our model can directly utilize this general knowledge to correlate videos and queries, and accurately retrieve the relevant segment without training. Extensive experiments on two challenging datasets (ActivityNet Captions and Charades-STA) show our effectiveness, outperforming existing unsupervised methods and even competitively beating supervised works.

AI.tldr: Use cheap image-noun and video-verb supervision to transfer appearance and action knowledge into unsupervised temporal sentence grounding, enabling accurate segment retrieval without paired training annotations.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that existing temporal sentence grounding methods depend heavily on expensive video-query pair and temporal boundary annotations, which are difficult to collect at scale. The authors therefore seek a more practical unsupervised setting and leverage cheaper, more accessible cross-modal supervision from related tasks.
AI.method: The method targets unsupervised temporal sentence grounding by transferring two kinds of external knowledge: entity-aware appearance knowledge from paired Image-Noun data to video frames, and event-aware action knowledge from paired Video-Verb data. It further refines action representation with a copy-paste strategy, then combines both appearance and action cues to match videos and queries and retrieve relevant temporal segments without task-specific training.
AI.result: On ActivityNet Captions and Charades-STA, the proposed approach outperforms existing unsupervised methods and even achieves competitive performance compared with supervised approaches.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that transferring cheap cross-modal alignment knowledge from image-noun and video-verb tasks enables effective unsupervised temporal sentence grounding, achieving state-of-the-art unsupervised results and even competitive performance against supervised methods.

title: LLM-FACETS: A Privacy-Preserving Framework for Evaluating LLM Transparency and Accountability
comment: Submitted to ACM Journal on Responsible Computing, Special Section: Collaborative Methods and Tools for Engineering and Evaluating Transparency in AI. 28 pages 9 figures, 7 tables, 1 algorithm. Source code: https://github.com/Scriptor-Group/AIMVi
summary: Assessing whether Large Language Models outputs are factually grounded, epistemically calibrated, and methodologically reproducible is a prerequisite for responsible AI deployment. Yet auditing LLMs remains inaccessible to non-technical practitioners: existing tools require programming expertise and non-trivial environment setup, and cloud-hosted platforms transmit evaluation data to external services, creating barriers for domain experts and compliance officers legally responsible for AI oversight. We introduce LLM-FACETS (LLM FActuality Cross-EvaluaTion System): an open-source framework with a browser-accessible interface and a plugin architecture, structured around three practitioner profiles (technical experts, domain experts, compliance officers) that mirror the stakeholder categories identified in the EU AI Act and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework. The architecture makes data flows explicit: deterministic metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore) run entirely within the self-hosted server with no outbound transmission; LLM-judge metrics contact external APIs explicitly, with users retaining full credential control. The framework operationalizes transparency through three mechanisms: token-level log-probability visualization for epistemic uncertainty, multi-judge consensus to mitigate judge bias, and RAG Triad metrics (Faithfulness, Answer Relevance, Context Relevance) to detect and localize hallucinations. A plugin architecture allows any new metric or dataset to be integrated without modifying the evaluation pipeline. The open-source implementation enables cross-checking across multiple metrics targeting the same property, ensuring reproducibility and decoupling AI accountability from the teams building the systems assessed. We verify the framework through cross-validation of 18 metric implementations against canonical reference libraries.

AI.tldr: A self-hosted, open-source LLM auditing framework that lets practitioners evaluate factuality, calibration, and hallucinations with transparent data flows, extensible plugins, and validated metric implementations.
AI.motivation: Current LLM auditing tools are difficult for non-technical practitioners to use because they require programming skills, complex setup, and often send evaluation data to cloud services, which creates usability, governance, and compliance barriers.
AI.method: The paper proposes LLM-FACETS, an open-source browser-based evaluation framework with a plugin architecture. It separates deterministic local metrics from optional external LLM-judge metrics, provides token-level log-probability visualization, multi-judge consensus, and RAG Triad metrics, and validates 18 metric implementations against canonical libraries.
AI.result: The framework provides a self-hostable interface tailored to technical experts, domain experts, and compliance officers, supports extensible metric and dataset plugins, makes data-flow boundaries explicit, and achieves verification through cross-validation of 18 implemented metrics against reference libraries.
AI.conclusion: LLM-FACETS demonstrates that practical, self-hosted, and role-oriented auditing of LLMs can be made accessible to non-technical stakeholders while preserving transparency, reproducibility, and explicit control over external API usage.

title: Measuring, Localizing, and Ablating Alignment Signatures in LLMs
summary: Aligned language models often exhibit a recognizable AI-like style, yet its connection to post-training and internal representations remains poorly understood. In this work, we study whether post-training introduces or amplifies AI-like stylistic regularities and whether these regularities have a localized internal signature. To this end, we compare human text, base-model generations, and aligned-model generations under matched human-source prefixes. Aligned generations show lower human-corpus affinity and higher AI-detection rates than base generations, suggesting that post-training shifts generated text away from human-corpus style and toward detector-visible AI-like text. We then introduce PASTA (Post-training Alignment Signature Targeted Ablation), a training-free method that estimates a post-training alignment signature from aligned-base residual contrasts and ablates the corresponding direction during decoding. Across 11 aligned models and 6 AI detectors, PASTA lowers the detection rate for most aligned models; this effect transfers well across detectors and is not reproduced by random directions. Qualitative analysis suggests that PASTA generations remain relevant and coherent while exhibiting greater stylistic variation. Together, these results show that AI-like stylistic effects of post-training can be measured, localized, and causally tested through activation ablation.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that alignment post-training makes LMs write in a more detector-visible, AI-like style. It identifies an internal direction associated with this effect and introduces PASTA, a training-free ablation method that suppresses the signature during decoding, reducing AI-detection rates without obviously harming coherence.
AI.motivation: Aligned models often sound recognizably AI-like, but it is unclear whether this comes from post-training and whether the effect corresponds to a specific internal representation. The work aims to measure that stylistic shift and test whether it can be causally manipulated inside the model.
AI.method: The paper compares human text, base-model generations, and aligned-model generations under matched human-source prefixes. It then proposes PASTA, a training-free decoding-time intervention that estimates a post-training alignment signature from aligned-versus-base residual activation contrasts and ablates that direction during generation. The method is evaluated across 11 aligned models and 6 AI detectors.
AI.result: Aligned generations have lower affinity to human corpora and higher AI-detection rates than base-model generations. PASTA reduces detection rates for most aligned models, generalizes across multiple detectors, and outperforms random-direction ablations. Qualitative results indicate that generations remain relevant and coherent while showing greater stylistic diversity.
AI.conclusion: Post-training in aligned language models introduces measurable AI-like stylistic regularities that move outputs away from human-corpus style. These regularities have a localized internal activation signature, and targeted ablation of that signature can reduce AI-detector visibility while preserving coherence and relevance.

title: Counterfactual Graph for Multi-Agent LLM Calibration
summary: Multi-agent LLM systems often treat agreement as evidence: when many agents in a panel give the same answer, that answer is assumed to be more reliable. We show that this assumption can fail after agents communicate. Communication can induce correlated failures and false consensus, so the same vote share may reflect reliable agreement in one topology but over-confidence in another. We propose CAGE-CAL, a counterfactual agent-graph calibration framework for multi-agent LLMs. For each query, CAGE-CAL compares an observed post-communication agent graph with a matched counterfactual no-communication graph, capturing both pairwise failure correlations and group-level dependencies. Rather than simply counting how many agents agree, CAGE-CAL estimates the counterfactual shift between observed and no-communication dependence, and calibrates confidence accordingly. Across five benchmarks, CAGE-CAL improves reliability discrimination with competitive ECE, and its calibrated confidence further improves topology selection over the best fixed-topology strategy.

AI.tldr: TL;DR: In multi-agent LLMs, post-communication consensus can be falsely reassuring because agents may share the same error. CAGE-CAL fixes this by comparing the real communicating agent graph to a matched no-communication counterfactual and calibrating confidence based on the communication-induced dependency shift. It improves confidence reliability and topology choice on five benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing multi-agent LLM systems often assume that if many agents agree, the answer is more reliable. The paper is motivated by the observation that after inter-agent communication, agreement can be misleading because communication can induce correlated failures and overconfident false consensus.
AI.method: The paper proposes CAGE-CAL, a counterfactual agent-graph calibration framework. For each query, it compares the observed post-communication agent graph with a matched counterfactual no-communication graph, modeling pairwise failure correlations and group-level dependencies. It then estimates the dependence shift caused by communication and uses that shift to calibrate confidence instead of relying only on vote share.
AI.result: Across five benchmarks, CAGE-CAL improves reliability discrimination while maintaining competitive expected calibration error (ECE). Its calibrated confidence also improves topology selection compared with the best fixed-topology strategy.
AI.conclusion: CAGE-CAL shows that agreement among communicating LLM agents is not inherently reliable because communication can create correlated errors and false consensus. By calibrating confidence against a matched no-communication counterfactual graph, the method produces more trustworthy confidence estimates and improves topology selection.

title: Immuno-VLM: Immunizing Large Vision-Language Models via Generative Semantic Antibodies for Open-World Trustworthiness
summary: Large Vision-Language Models have achieved unprecedented success in zero-shot recognition by aligning visual features with broad semantic concepts. However, this semantic abstraction creates a critical vulnerability in open-world deployment: the ``Hubris of Semantics'', where models force-fit unknown anomalies into known categories with high confidence due to the lack of explicit negative knowledge. To address this \textit{Open-World Trustworthiness Paradox}, we propose \textbf{Immuno-VLM}, a bio-inspired framework that adapts the biological principle of \textbf{Immunological Negative Selection} to high-dimensional latent spaces. Departing from traditional Open-Set Recognition methods that rely on passive density estimation or inefficient pixel-space outlier generation, Immuno-VLM leverages the generative reasoning of Large Language Models to actively hallucinate ``Semantic Antibodies'', textual descriptions of near-distribution outliers (e.g., look-alikes, contextual anomalies) that effectively bound the decision space of known classes.Extensive experiments on ImageNet-1K and four challenging OOD benchmarks reveal that Immuno-VLM establishes a new state-of-the-art.

AI.tldr: Immuno-VLM makes VLMs safer in open-world settings by using LLM-generated negative class descriptions ('semantic antibodies') to teach the model what near-known anomalies look like, leading to SOTA OOD detection.
AI.motivation: Current large vision-language models excel at zero-shot recognition through semantic abstraction, but this same abstraction causes a failure mode in open-world settings: they confidently map unknown anomalies to known categories because they lack explicit negative knowledge. Existing OSR approaches based on density estimation or pixel-space outlier synthesis are insufficient or inefficient.
AI.method: The paper proposes Immuno-VLM, a bio-inspired framework based on immunological negative selection. It uses large language models to generate 'semantic antibodies'—text descriptions of near-distribution outliers such as look-alikes and contextual anomalies—which are mapped into the latent space to constrain class decision boundaries for vision-language models.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on ImageNet-1K and four challenging out-of-distribution benchmarks show that Immuno-VLM outperforms prior methods and sets a new state-of-the-art for open-world/OOD recognition.
AI.conclusion: Immuno-VLM shows that adding explicit, language-generated negative knowledge to LVLMs can substantially improve open-world trustworthiness and open-set/OOD detection, achieving new state-of-the-art performance on ImageNet-1K and four OOD benchmarks.

title: Formalizing and falsifying causal pathways of rare events
summary: Building on recent formalizations of root cause analysis for rare events (``outliers'') in structural equation models, we propose a formal definition of a causal pathway and discuss its testable implications. We identify conditions under which these implications depend only on a causal abstraction defined by the pathway of rare events, rather than on the full causal graph of the underlying system. Accordingly, we introduce an abstraction of causal structure to pathways of rare events that bridges simple verbal causal explanations and detailed causal modeling.

AI.tldr: Defines formal causal pathways for rare events in structural equation models and shows when their predictions can be analyzed using a simpler pathway abstraction instead of the full causal graph.
AI.motivation: The work is motivated by the gap between simple verbal explanations of rare events and full, detailed causal models. The authors aim to provide a principled intermediate abstraction for explaining outliers causally.
AI.method: The authors extend prior formal work on root cause analysis in structural equation models by introducing a formal definition of a causal pathway, deriving its testable implications, and identifying conditions under which these implications are preserved under abstraction to rare-event pathways.
AI.result: The main result is a pathway-based abstraction of causal structure for rare events that can support testable implications while avoiding dependence on the entire causal graph, provided specific conditions hold.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that causal pathways for rare events can be formally defined, and that under certain conditions their testable implications depend only on a pathway-level causal abstraction rather than the full underlying causal graph.

title: The Long-Term Effects of Data Selection in LLM Fine-Tuning
summary: Data selection is increasingly used to reduce the cost of large language model (LLM) fine-tuning, with recent methods prioritizing samples by current utility, diversity, quality, or influence. This paper studies a different question: when fine-tuning occurs over multiple stages, can selection strategies that look optimal now make the model less adaptable later? We introduce a long-horizon view of LLM data selection in which a selector is evaluated not only by immediate task performance, but also by future adaptation speed, forgetting, capability imbalance, and out-of-distribution robustness. We compare representative random, loss-based, gradient-based, diversity-based, quality-based, and utility-diversity selection families under a unified multi-stage protocol. Through controlled experiments designed to instantiate this protocol, we show how short-term selectors can exhibit rank reversal: they improve the current stage while slowing subsequent learning and increasing forgetting. We formalize this behavior as \emph{myopic selection}, provide a simple local analysis of why it can occur, and propose a diagnostic Long-Horizon Aware Selection (LHAS) objective that augments immediate utility with coverage, future-proxy transfer, and anti-concentration terms. The study argues that data selection should be evaluated as a training intervention that shapes the model's learning trajectory, rather than only as a local data-efficiency mechanism.

AI.tldr: This paper argues that the best data for the current fine-tuning stage may be bad for later stages. It studies multi-stage LLM training, identifies myopic selection as a key problem, and proposes a long-horizon objective (LHAS) to evaluate and guide data selection using both immediate and future-oriented criteria.
AI.motivation: Existing data selection methods mainly optimize short-term fine-tuning efficiency, focusing on immediate utility, diversity, quality, or influence. The paper is motivated by the concern that in multi-stage fine-tuning, such myopic choices may improve current performance while making the model less adaptable in future stages.
AI.method: The paper defines a unified multi-stage fine-tuning protocol and compares several representative data selection families: random, loss-based, gradient-based, diversity-based, quality-based, and utility-diversity methods. It then analyzes their behavior under long-horizon metrics and introduces Long-Horizon Aware Selection (LHAS), which combines immediate utility with coverage, future-proxy transfer, and anti-concentration terms.
AI.result: Controlled experiments show rank reversal among selectors: methods that look best in the current stage can slow subsequent learning and increase forgetting later. The paper formalizes this phenomenon as myopic selection, gives a local explanation for why it occurs, and presents LHAS as a diagnostic objective aligned with long-horizon behavior.
AI.conclusion: Data selection for multi-stage LLM fine-tuning should be evaluated from a long-horizon perspective, because strategies that maximize immediate gains can harm later adaptability, increase forgetting, worsen capability imbalance, and reduce out-of-distribution robustness. The paper concludes that selection is a trajectory-shaping training intervention rather than only a local efficiency tool.

title: EUDAIMONIA: Evaluating Undesirable Dynamics in AI
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as conversational partners for companionship, emotional disclosure, and interpersonal advice, but the social dynamics of these interactions can create harms that are not captured by capability-oriented or traditional safety evaluations. We introduce the Social AI Design Code, a framework for evaluating whether LLMs align with user welfare in social interactions, including whether they encourage harmful intimacy, dependence, or prolonged engagement. To evaluate these risks in natural and diverse user-LLM interactions, we operationalize the code with EUDAIMONIA, a benchmark of 969 user inputs and 3,147 design-requirement violation checks built from WildChat through weak-to-strong filtration, multi-model relabeling, and controlled rewriting. Evaluating 22 recent LLMs, we find that even the strongest models, Claude-Opus-4.7 and GPT-5.5, violate 30.7% and 27.2% of checks, respectively. Extended thinking does not reduce violation rates, suggesting that these failures are persistent social-alignment problems rather than deficits solvable through test-time reasoning alone.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a new benchmark and design framework to test whether chat-oriented LLMs support user welfare in social interactions, and shows that even top models still frequently encourage problematic social behaviors.
AI.motivation: As LLMs are increasingly used for companionship, emotional disclosure, and advice, harmful social dynamics such as unhealthy intimacy, dependence, or engagement-maximizing behavior may arise. Existing evaluations focused on capability or traditional safety do not adequately capture these user-welfare risks in social interaction.
AI.method: The paper proposes the Social AI Design Code as an evaluation framework for user-welfare alignment in social interactions, then operationalizes it through EUDAIMONIA, a benchmark constructed from WildChat using weak-to-strong filtration, multi-model relabeling, and controlled rewriting. The authors evaluate 22 recent LLMs against 3,147 design-requirement violation checks derived from 969 user inputs.
AI.result: Across 22 recent LLMs, even the strongest models perform poorly on the benchmark: Claude-Opus-4.7 violates 30.7% of checks and GPT-5.5 violates 27.2%. Extended thinking does not significantly lower violation rates, indicating persistent social-alignment weaknesses.
AI.conclusion: Current leading LLMs still show substantial social-alignment failures in conversational settings, and these failures are not meaningfully reduced by extended reasoning. A dedicated social-interaction evaluation framework is therefore necessary beyond standard capability or safety benchmarks.

title: SLAP: The Semantic Least Action Principle for Variational Video-Language Modeling
summary: In the era of Large Video-Language Models (LVLMs), the computational necessity of sparse frame sampling creates a fundamental ``temporal gap'', rendering models blind to critical causal transitions. Existing solutions relying on generative hallucination (e.g., latent diffusion) or autoregressive extrapolation often fail to maintain semantic consistency over long horizons, suffering from object vanishing and energetic instability. We propose a paradigm shift from probabilistic generation to variational mechanics with the \textbf{Semantic Least Action Principle (SLAP)}. Drawing a rigorous isomorphism between classical mechanics and semantic dynamics, we model the latent video trajectory as a path on a Riemannian manifold governed by a Semantic Lagrangian. By formulating the interpolation task as a Boundary Value Problem (BVP) solved via the discrete Euler-Lagrange equations, SLAP naturally enforces object persistence without pixel-level rendering. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our proposed SLAP.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes SLAP, a physics-inspired latent video interpolation framework that treats semantic evolution like motion governed by least action, aiming to bridge sparse-frame temporal gaps more stably than generative methods.
AI.motivation: Sparse frame sampling in Large Video-Language Models creates a temporal gap that prevents models from capturing crucial causal transitions. Existing generative or autoregressive interpolation approaches often lose semantic consistency over long horizons, leading to object disappearance and instability.
AI.method: The paper introduces the Semantic Least Action Principle (SLAP), defining a Semantic Lagrangian over latent video trajectories on a Riemannian manifold. Interpolation is solved through discrete Euler-Lagrange equations as a boundary value problem instead of diffusion-based or autoregressive generation.
AI.result: According to the abstract, extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of SLAP, suggesting improved semantic consistency and object persistence compared with prior interpolation approaches.
AI.conclusion: SLAP replaces probabilistic frame generation with a variational mechanics formulation, modeling latent video interpolation as a boundary value problem on a Riemannian manifold to better preserve semantic continuity and object persistence across sparse temporal gaps.

title: DisasterLex: An Expert Concept-to-Schema Knowledge Graph for Geospatial Reasoning in Disaster Analytics
summary: Disasters are inevitable and increasingly costly, and effective response depends on querying structured tabular data: precise, information-dense records of hazard, exposure, vulnerability, and lifeline infrastructure that underpin disaster management. Current text-to-SQL methods enable natural-language access to such tables but transfer poorly to the disaster domain, where queries span heterogeneous geospatial schemas and require reasoning over causal relations. We introduce DisasterLex, a knowledge-graph-mediated framework that inserts an Expert Knowledge Graph (EKG) of curated concepts and typed causal edges between the user query and the database, bridged to schema by concept-to-table links. The orchestration runs four stages (identifying query entities, routing to the operational domain, planning over causal edges, and grounding the SQL), restricting the schema passed to the model at each step. We instantiate it on a disaster-analytics database (36 geospatial tables, 150 columns) with an EKG of 107 concepts, 117 causal edges, and 52 concept-to-schema links, evaluated on a 75-query test set. On all seven base models spanning proprietary and open-weight families, DisasterLex beats four state-of-the-art baselines (LightRAG, HippoRAG 2, ReFoRCE, CHESS) by 1.4x to 2.75x, with absolute scores of 1.65 to 3.56 (of 5.0). Error analysis shows baseline failures cluster in routing and multi-table SQL composition, the operations our orchestration explicitly addresses. Code, data, and the EKG artifact are available at https://github.com/YimingXiao98/DisasterLex and on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20388029.

AI.tldr: DisasterLex uses an expert knowledge graph to guide text-to-SQL generation for disaster databases, narrowing schema choices step by step and improving performance over existing methods on complex geospatial, causal disaster queries.
AI.motivation: Existing text-to-SQL systems transfer poorly to disaster analytics because disaster queries require domain-specific causal reasoning and must operate over heterogeneous geospatial schemas with structured records on hazards, exposure, vulnerability, and infrastructure.
AI.method: The paper proposes DisasterLex, a four-stage knowledge-graph-mediated text-to-SQL framework: identify query entities, route the query to the operational domain, plan over typed causal edges in an Expert Knowledge Graph, and ground the result to SQL using concept-to-schema links while progressively restricting the candidate schema.
AI.result: On a disaster-analytics database with 36 geospatial tables and a 75-query benchmark, DisasterLex outperforms four strong baselines across seven base models by 1.4x to 2.75x, reaching absolute scores from 1.65 to 3.56 out of 5.0.
AI.conclusion: DisasterLex shows that inserting an expert knowledge graph between natural-language queries and disaster-management databases substantially improves text-to-SQL performance in the disaster domain, especially for routing and multi-table reasoning over heterogeneous geospatial schemas.

title: CobSeg: Coherence Boundary Modeling for Dialogue Topic Segmentation
summary: Dialogue topic segmentation is critical in many human-AI collaborative applications which requires identifying heterogeneous boundary cues, including lexical transitions near utterance edges and semantic discontinuities across utterances. Existing utterance models often dilute these local lexical signals. We propose CobSeg, a novel multi-branch architecture that separates coherence-level semantic continuity from lexical boundary transitions and recovers both through directional boundary prediction. CobSeg further uses boundary informativeness weighting to emphasize high-utility utterance positions, and incorporates a corpus-derived topic coherence cue with learned combination weights. While CobSeg is evaluated as a compact trainable segmenter under supervised gold-boundary training and a pseudo-label setting with automatically induced boundaries, it performs enhanced boundary prediction without LLM calls during inference. Across five benchmarks, it improves $P_k$ and $W_d$ particularly when local lexical cues are prominent: under gold supervision, it reduces $P_k$ by 0.7 points and $W_d$ by 0.6 points on VHF, and reaches $P_k$ of 1.0 on DialSeg711; with induced boundaries, it reduces $P_k$ by 14.8 points on VHF, by 1.5 points on DialSeg711, and by 1.1 points on TIAGE, outperforming prior non-LLM approaches.

AI.tldr: 中文：CobSeg 是一种轻量级对话主题分割模型，专门把“语义连贯性”和“局部词汇边界信号”分开建模，因此比传统话语模型更擅长找出主题切换点，并且不依赖 LLM 推理。 English: CobSeg is a compact dialogue topic segmenter that separately models semantic coherence and local lexical boundary cues, making it better at detecting topic shifts without relying on LLM inference.
AI.motivation: 中文：现有话语级模型往往会稀释主题切换时局部而关键的词汇边界信号，难以同时捕捉边界附近的词汇变化和跨话语的语义不连续，因此需要一种能够显式分离并重建这两类线索的分割方法。 English: Existing utterance models tend to blur local lexical boundary signals that are crucial for topic shifts, making it hard to jointly capture edge-level lexical transitions and cross-utterance semantic discontinuities.
AI.method: 中文：方法提出了一个多分支架构 CobSeg，一支建模跨话语的语义连续性，另一支建模话语边界附近的词汇转移；同时通过方向性边界预测恢复两类线索，并对高信息量边界位置赋予更高权重，最后融合语料统计得到的主题连贯性特征与学习到的组合权重。 English: The paper introduces CobSeg, a multi-branch model with one branch for inter-utterance semantic continuity and another for lexical transitions near utterance boundaries; it uses directional boundary prediction, boundary informativeness weighting, and a corpus-derived topic coherence cue with learned fusion weights.
AI.result: 中文：在五个基准数据集上，CobSeg 在 gold-boundary 监督和伪标签设置下都优于以往非 LLM 方法；在 gold 监督下，VHF 上 P_k 降低 0.7、W_d 降低 0.6，DialSeg711 上达到 P_k=1.0；在自动诱导边界下，VHF 上 P_k 降低 14.8，DialSeg711 降低 1.5，TIAGE 降低 1.1。 English: Across five benchmarks, CobSeg outperforms prior non-LLM approaches in both gold-boundary supervision and pseudo-label settings; under gold supervision it lowers P_k by 0.7 and W_d by 0.6 on VHF and reaches P_k=1.0 on DialSeg711, while with induced boundaries it reduces P_k by 14.8 on VHF, 1.5 on DialSeg711, and 1.1 on TIAGE.
AI.conclusion: 中文：CobSeg 通过分离语义连贯性与词汇边界线索，并结合方向性边界预测、边界信息量加权和语料级主题连贯性信号，在多个基准上稳定提升对话主题分割性能，且推理时无需调用 LLM。 English: CobSeg improves dialogue topic segmentation by disentangling semantic coherence from lexical boundary cues and combining directional boundary prediction, boundary informativeness weighting, and corpus-derived topic coherence, achieving consistent gains across benchmarks without LLM inference.

title: DisPlace: Discriminative Place Projections for Multi-Reference Visual Place Recognition
summary: A key challenge in Visual Place Recognition (VPR) is matching query images against reference maps captured under diverse environmental conditions and viewpoints. While multiple reference traversals improve robustness, existing fusion strategies either aggregate references uniformly or rely on heuristic selection, without distinguishing descriptor variations that preserve stable place identity from those caused by changing conditions or viewpoints. In this paper, we propose DisPlace, a multi-reference VPR framework that fuses multiple reference descriptors into a single compact and discriminative place representation. DisPlace formulates descriptor fusion as a generalized eigenvalue problem that maximizes between-place separability while suppressing within-place variation across references, rather than preserving overall descriptor variance. Unlike existing multi-reference fusion methods, DisPlace exploits variation across reference traversals to identify which linear combinations of descriptor dimensions preserve place identity and which capture condition- or viewpoint-specific variation. We evaluate DisPlace on Oxford RobotCar, Nordland, Pittsburgh30k, and Google Landmarks v2 across six state-of-the-art VPR descriptors. DisPlace outperforms seven multi-reference baselines in 49 out of 54 appearance-varying conditions, consistently improves descriptor-level fusion performance under viewpoint and unstructured settings, and requires less storage during inference than all compared fusion methods.

AI.tldr: TL;DR：DisPlace利用多次参考遍历中的“有用变化”和“干扰变化”做可判别融合，生成单一紧凑场所描述子，在精度和存储效率上都优于现有多参考VPR方法。 / TL;DR: DisPlace uses discriminative fusion to separate useful identity-preserving variation from nuisance variation across multiple reference traversals, producing a single compact place descriptor that improves both accuracy and storage efficiency over prior multi-reference VPR methods.
AI.motivation: 动机是：现有多参考VPR虽然能提升鲁棒性，但常见融合策略要么对所有参考一视同仁，要么依赖启发式选择，无法显式区分“有助于保持地点身份的描述子变化”和“由天气、光照、季节或视角变化造成的无关变化”。 / The motivation is that while multiple references improve VPR robustness, existing fusion strategies either treat references uniformly or use heuristic selection, and cannot explicitly distinguish descriptor variations that preserve place identity from irrelevant changes caused by weather, lighting, season, or viewpoint.
AI.method: 方法上，论文提出DisPlace，一个多参考VPR框架。它不再保留总体方差，而是通过最大化地点间可分性、最小化同一地点在不同参考遍历下的类内变化来进行线性融合，从而区分稳定的地点身份信息与由环境/视角变化引入的扰动。 / Methodologically, the paper proposes DisPlace, a multi-reference VPR framework. Instead of preserving overall variance, it performs linear fusion by maximizing between-place separability and minimizing within-place variation of the same place across traversals, separating stable place-identity information from condition/viewpoint-induced variation.
AI.result: 实验在Oxford RobotCar、Nordland、Pittsburgh30k和Google Landmarks v2上，结合6种SOTA VPR描述子进行评估。DisPlace在54种外观变化设置中的49种优于7个多参考基线，在视角变化和非结构化场景下也稳定提升描述子级融合效果，并且推理时存储需求低于所有对比融合方法。 / Experiments on Oxford RobotCar, Nordland, Pittsburgh30k, and Google Landmarks v2 with six state-of-the-art VPR descriptors show that DisPlace beats seven multi-reference baselines in 49 of 54 appearance-varying conditions, consistently improves descriptor-level fusion under viewpoint and unstructured settings, and requires less storage at inference than all compared fusion methods.
AI.conclusion: DisPlace通过将多参考描述子融合建模为广义特征值问题，学习到既紧凑又有判别性的场所表示；它在多种数据集、条件变化和描述子上整体优于现有多参考融合方法，同时推理存储开销更低。 / DisPlace learns a compact, discriminative place representation by formulating multi-reference descriptor fusion as a generalized eigenvalue problem; across datasets, condition changes, and descriptors, it generally outperforms existing multi-reference fusion methods while using less inference-time storage.

title: Industrializing Prediction-Powered Inference: The GLIDE Library for Reliable GenAI and Agentic Systems Evaluation
comment: 8 pages, accepted at the ICML 2026 workshop Agentic Uncertainty
summary: Reliable evaluation of agentic systems requires unbiased estimates with valid uncertainty, but standard practice navigates between costly human annotation and biased LLM-as-judge proxies. Prediction-powered inference (PPI) combines both into debiased estimates with valid confidence intervals, yet its various methods remain scattered across papers under partial implementations. We introduce GLIDE, an open-source Python library that unifies state-of-the-art PPI estimators (PPI++, Stratified PPI, Predict-Then-Debias and its stratified variants, Active Statistical Inference) and samplers (uniform, stratified, active, cost-optimal) under a scipy-style API specialized to mean estimation. GLIDE ships with a reproducible Monte Carlo validation suite, an empirically grounded decision tree for method selection, and an agentic evaluation case study showing substantial annotation savings at equivalent precision. The GLIDE package is available at this URL: https://github.com/EmertonData/glide

AI.tldr: GLIDE is an open-source Python toolkit that consolidates modern prediction-powered inference methods for unbiased, uncertainty-aware evaluation of agentic systems, helping cut annotation cost without sacrificing statistical validity.
AI.motivation: Standard evaluation of agentic systems faces a tradeoff between expensive human annotation and biased LLM-as-judge proxies. Existing PPI methods can address this, but implementations are fragmented across papers and tools.
AI.method: The paper introduces GLIDE, a scipy-style API that integrates multiple state-of-the-art PPI estimators and sampling strategies for mean estimation, along with a reproducible Monte Carlo validation suite, a method-selection decision tree, and an agentic evaluation case study.
AI.result: GLIDE unifies PPI++ , Stratified PPI, Predict-Then-Debias and variants, and Active Statistical Inference, and demonstrates substantial annotation savings at equivalent precision in an agentic evaluation case study.
AI.conclusion: GLIDE provides a unified open-source Python library for prediction-powered inference in agentic system evaluation, delivering debiased mean estimates with valid confidence intervals and reducing human annotation cost while maintaining precision.

title: TeachObs: A Human-Validated Benchmark for Multimodal Teaching Observation and Model Evaluation
summary: Classroom videos contain observable teaching practices, but their pedagogical and visual signals are rarely organized in forms suitable for model evaluation. We present \textit{TeachObs}, a human-validated benchmark for multimodal teaching observation in classroom videos. \textit{TeachObs} includes 30 public lesson videos from eight countries divided into 5,158 fixed 15-second scenes. Seven researchers annotated each scene with 39 binary observation codes, covering 20 visual codes, such as gesture, board work, pointing, and visual materials, and 19 nonvisual codes, such as instruction, monitoring, questioning, feedback, and reflection. Gold segment labels are constructed using reliability- and prevalence-aware rules based on Krippendorff's alpha. In addition to segment-level labels, three expert raters produced lesson-level ratings and qualitative evaluations of instructional design, instructional delivery, learner response, learning materials, and lesson closure across the 30 lessons, with rater coverage detailed in the body. Using these two human reference layers, we evaluate five vision-capable frontier LLMs across three tracks - text-only segment coding, text + frame segment coding, and lesson-level coverage scored under an LLM-as-judge protocol - and find that no single model consistently outperforms others across all three tracks, that adding a mid-frame inflates both true and false attributions per scene, and that model evaluations over-rate procedurally clear lessons relative to expert raters. \textit{TeachObs} therefore supports both fine-grained annotation benchmarking and whole-lesson evaluation, showing where AI systems can assist classroom video analysis and where expert judgment remains necessary across varied subjects, classroom formats, and annotation difficulty levels.

AI.tldr: 中文：本文提出TeachObs，一个面向课堂视频的多模态教学观察基准，用双层人工标注评测前沿视觉LLM。结果显示现有模型能力不稳定，图像帧会放大正确与错误判断，整课评价仍明显依赖专家。 English: This paper introduces TeachObs, a multimodal benchmark for classroom-video teaching observation with both segment- and lesson-level human references. Frontier vision LLMs show uneven performance, image frames amplify both correct and incorrect attributions, and whole-lesson evaluation still depends heavily on experts.
AI.motivation: 中文：课堂视频包含丰富的可观察教学行为，但这些教学学与视觉信号通常没有被系统组织成适合模型评测的标准数据形式，因此缺少一个能衡量AI在课堂视频分析中能力与局限的可靠基准。 English: Classroom videos contain rich observable teaching practices, but their pedagogical and visual signals are rarely organized into benchmark-ready formats for model evaluation, creating a need for a reliable benchmark to assess AI capabilities and limitations in classroom video analysis.
AI.method: 中文：作者将30节来自8个国家的公开课堂视频切分为5,158个固定15秒片段，由7位研究者依据39个二元观察码进行标注，其中包括20个视觉码和19个非视觉码；再基于Krippendorff's alpha并结合一致性与流行率规则构建金标准标签。同时，3位专家对30节课进行整课层面的评分与定性评价。随后用两层人工参考，对5个具视觉能力的前沿LLM在三条评测轨道上进行测试：仅文本片段编码、文本+帧片段编码，以及LLM-as-judge的整课覆盖评分。 English: The authors segmented 30 public lesson videos from eight countries into 5,158 fixed 15-second scenes. Seven researchers annotated each scene with 39 binary observation codes (20 visual, 19 nonvisual), and gold labels were derived using reliability- and prevalence-aware rules based on Krippendorff’s alpha. In parallel, three experts provided lesson-level ratings and qualitative evaluations. Using these two human reference layers, five vision-capable frontier LLMs were evaluated on three tracks: text-only segment coding, text+frame segment coding, and lesson-level coverage scoring under an LLM-as-judge protocol.
AI.result: 中文：实验发现，没有任何单一模型能在三条评测轨道上持续优于其他模型；加入中间视频帧会同时增加每个片段的真阳性和假阳性归因；此外，相较于专家评分，模型更容易高估程序清晰、流程规范的课程。 English: The study finds that no single model consistently outperforms others across all three evaluation tracks; adding a mid-frame increases both true and false attributions per scene; and model-based evaluations tend to overrate procedurally clear lessons relative to expert raters.
AI.conclusion: 中文：TeachObs 提供了一个经人工验证的课堂视频多模态教学观察基准，可同时支持细粒度片段标注评测和整节课评估；结果表明，当前前沿多模态/视觉LLM尚无单一模型能在所有任务上稳定领先，且专家判断在课堂分析中仍不可替代。 English: TeachObs is a human-validated benchmark for multimodal teaching observation in classroom videos that supports both fine-grained segment benchmarking and whole-lesson evaluation; results show that no single frontier vision-capable LLM consistently leads across all tasks, and expert judgment remains essential.

title: TraceGraph: Shared Decision Landscapes for Diagnosing and Improving Agent Trajectories
summary: Agent benchmarks increasingly record rich interaction trajectories, yet evaluation often reduces each rollout to a pass rate or reward score. We introduce TraceGraph, a graph-based framework that turns released multi-model agent trajectories into shared decision landscapes. For each task, TraceGraph builds a graph over observable action-observation states from pooled rollouts before model identity is introduced. It then overlays outcome-informed productive cores and trap regions, and summarizes each rollout with three events: Access, Trap exposure, and Repair. Across trajectories spanning five benchmark splits, TraceGraph profiles reveal navigation differences hidden by aggregate scores and show that splits differ in whether they reward avoiding traps or recovering from them. The same TraceGraph landscape also motivates a trap-aware recovery pipeline for SWE-bench: aruntime detector fires on states matching historical trap regions, then lightweight continuation policies are evaluated from the same prefix. On fired states, the best pooled single-factor policy raises official resolved rate from 40.4% to 43.5% on the per-provider fired subset and from 41.0% to 44.8% on common-fired instances, with provider-specific active components. Overall, TraceGraph provides a process vocabulary for asking what agent benchmarks test, where models diverge on a shared landscape, and how failure regions can guide downstream improvement.

AI.tldr: TraceGraph converts agent trajectories into a shared state graph, labels useful and failure-prone regions, and measures whether agents reach good states, enter traps, and recover. This exposes benchmark-specific navigation patterns and enables a trap-aware recovery pipeline that improves SWE-bench resolved rates.
AI.motivation: Standard agent benchmark evaluation compresses rich interaction trajectories into pass rate or reward, hiding how models navigate, fail, and recover. The paper aims to provide a shared process-level framework for comparing behaviors across models and understanding what benchmarks actually reward.
AI.method: The paper builds a graph over observable action-observation states from multi-model trajectories for each task before attaching model identity. It annotates the graph with outcome-informed productive cores and trap regions, then summarizes each rollout using three events: Access, Trap exposure, and Repair. The same landscape is used to trigger a runtime trap detector and evaluate lightweight continuation policies from identical prefixes on SWE-bench.
AI.result: Across five benchmark splits, TraceGraph reveals behavioral differences that aggregate scores hide and shows that some splits favor trap avoidance while others favor recovery. In the SWE-bench recovery setting, the best pooled single-factor continuation policy improves official resolved rate from 40.4% to 43.5% on the per-provider fired subset and from 41.0% to 44.8% on common-fired instances, with provider-specific active components.
AI.conclusion: TraceGraph turns pooled agent trajectories into a shared decision landscape, exposing productive cores, trap regions, and recovery behavior that aggregate metrics miss; these process-level signals can also improve downstream agent performance through trap-aware intervention.

title: Early Prediction of Future Behavioral Strategy from Process Traces
summary: Adaptive systems often need to make task-specific decisions about people from limited evidence: a tutor may need to anticipate how a learner will approach a new problem, a game may need to adapt when a player enters a new level, and a human-AI system may need to infer whether a partner will persist with a plan or switch goals. These decisions depend on person-level tendencies that shape how people solve related tasks, but such tendencies are difficult to infer from standard behavioral evidence. One approach is to use aggregate outcome summaries, such as scores, completion rates, or productivity; these summaries are compact and available across tasks, but can collapse distinct behavioral processes into similar outcomes. Another approach is to use process-level traces, which record how behavior unfolds; however, process modeling within one task can entangle stable person-level tendencies with task-specific layout and affordances. In this work, we study early cross-task behavioral inference: whether partial source-task process traces can reveal transferable person-level structure that predicts strategy in a held-out target task. We introduce a Process-Level Latent Variable Model (PLVM), which encodes task-specific traces and fuses them into a shared person-level latent representation for cross-task prediction. In PowerWash Simulator, a naturalistic telemetry dataset of human gameplay, PLVM uses partial traces from two cleaning tasks to predict locally persistent Zone Planner behavior versus frequent Zone Hopper behavior in the held-out Fire Station level. Controlled simulations with known latent types show that cross-task fusion helps when source tasks reveal complementary dimensions of a shared latent process. These results suggest that process-level cross-task modeling can support early prediction of target-task strategy when observing sufficient target-task behavior is impractical.

AI.tldr: Use partial behavior traces from multiple related tasks, map them into one shared latent person model, and predict how someone will act in a new task earlier and better than relying on simple outcomes or single-task process signals.
AI.motivation: Adaptive systems need to make task-specific decisions about people from limited evidence. Aggregate outcome summaries are compact but lose behavioral detail, while single-task process modeling can confound stable person-level tendencies with task-specific structure. The paper is motivated by the need to infer transferable person-level tendencies from early, partial behavior across tasks.
AI.method: The authors propose a Process-Level Latent Variable Model (PLVM) that encodes task-specific behavioral process traces, fuses them into a shared person-level latent representation, and uses that representation for cross-task prediction of strategy in a held-out target task. They evaluate it on PowerWash Simulator telemetry and in controlled simulations with known latent types.
AI.result: On PowerWash Simulator data, PLVM uses partial traces from two cleaning tasks to predict whether a player will behave as a locally persistent Zone Planner or a frequent Zone Hopper in the held-out Fire Station level. Simulations further show that cross-task fusion is especially beneficial when source tasks reveal complementary dimensions of the same latent process.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that process-level cross-task modeling can infer transferable person-level tendencies early, and that fusing partial traces from multiple source tasks improves prediction of held-out target-task strategy when the tasks expose complementary aspects of a shared latent process.

title: Human-Alignment, Calibration, and Activation Patterns in Large Language Model Uncertainty
summary: Uncertainty Quantification is a large and growing subfield of large language model behavioral analysis. Primarily to recognize and combat hallucination, the field has largely focused on measuring and improving calibration, the accuracy of uncertainty judgments to task efficacy. In this work, we investigate the relatively underexplored question of how similar large language model uncertainty is to human uncertainty. We investigate the presence and strength of human-similar uncertainty signals, deemed uncertainty alignment, in large language model overt behavior and internal activation patterns. We identify whether the models show evidence of simultaneous alignment and calibration on a variety of datasets covering both multiple choice and open ended factual recall. And we characterize the effect of instruct fine-tuning on each of these facets.

AI.tldr: This paper asks whether LLMs are uncertain in ways similar to humans, not just whether they are well calibrated. It measures that alignment in outputs and hidden states across factual tasks, and studies how instruction tuning changes the relationship between human-like uncertainty and calibration.
AI.motivation: Prior uncertainty quantification work in LLMs has focused mainly on calibration for reducing hallucinations, while the question of whether model uncertainty resembles human uncertainty remains underexplored.
AI.method: The paper studies uncertainty alignment by comparing LLM uncertainty with human uncertainty across multiple-choice and open-ended factual recall datasets, examining both observable behavior and internal activation patterns, and evaluating simultaneous alignment and calibration before and after instruction fine-tuning.
