AI.method: The paper proposes Canopy Entropy (CE*), a tree-based measure of the generation space that models all possible rollouts ('the canopy'). CE* jointly accounts for uncertainty in output length N and generated sequence Y_{1:N}, and the authors show it is equivalent to the total Shannon entropy H(N, Y_{1:N}|X). They further derive interpretable components such as the correlation term rho(N, r_N), where r_N is the entropy rate, to analyze how informativeness per token changes with output length.
AI.result: Across different tasks and model families, the experiments show that fine-tuned models consistently have a stronger positive rho(N, r_N), even when total entropy decreases. After controlling for model family, task, prompt, and output-length effects, fine-tuning nearly triples the correlation strength between entropy rate and semantic diversity. This indicates that aligned or fine-tuned models use uncertainty more efficiently to produce semantically diverse outputs.
AI.conclusion: Fine-tuning does not merely reduce uncertainty in large language models; it reorganizes uncertainty so that generations become more informative and semantically meaningful. In particular, fine-tuned models show stronger positive correlation between output length and entropy rate, and they convert token-level uncertainty into semantic diversity more efficiently.

title: IAF-Net: Illumination-Adaptive Fusion for Low-Light Urban Road Segmentation
summary: Semantic road segmentation is important for autonomous driving, but existing methods suffer severe performance degradation under low-light conditions. Many existing multi-modal fusion methods do not explicitly adapt to illumination-dependent changes in modality reliability, which can propagate degraded RGB features into the fused representation at night. We propose IAF-Net (Illumination-Adaptive Fusion Network), an end-to-end framework with illumination-adaptive fusion for robust road segmentation across different lighting conditions. It dynamically adjusts fusion weights of RGB and geometric features via the core Illumination-Adaptive Fusion (IAF) module, and enhances low-light feature selection with a brightness-modulated attention decoder. We also construct two dedicated datasets: nuScenes Nighttime Road Segmentation (nuScenes-NRS) and CARLA Multi-Weather Road Segmentation (CARLA-MWRS). Experiments on nuScenes-NRS show state-of-the-art overall performance among the compared methods, while CARLA-MWRS further validates robustness across adverse weather conditions. Ablation studies on a 40% training subset further highlight the importance of the IAF module, which provides the largest individual gain of 0.70% in MaxF.

AI.tldr: IAF-Net is a lighting-aware multi-modal road segmentation model that learns to trust RGB less in the dark and rely more on geometric cues, leading to stronger nighttime and bad-weather performance.
AI.motivation: Existing road segmentation methods for autonomous driving degrade significantly at night. Prior multi-modal fusion approaches often ignore illumination-dependent modality reliability, allowing poor RGB features in low light to harm the fused representation. The paper aims to make fusion explicitly adaptive to lighting changes.
AI.method: The paper proposes IAF-Net, an end-to-end semantic road segmentation framework. Its core Illumination-Adaptive Fusion (IAF) module dynamically adjusts fusion weights between RGB and geometric modalities based on lighting conditions, and a brightness-modulated attention decoder further enhances low-light feature selection.
AI.result: On nuScenes-NRS, IAF-Net achieves state-of-the-art overall performance among compared methods. On CARLA-MWRS, it demonstrates robustness across adverse weather conditions. Ablation on a 40% training subset shows the IAF module contributes the largest individual gain, improving MaxF by 0.70%.
AI.conclusion: IAF-Net improves road segmentation robustness under low-light and adverse-weather conditions by adaptively weighting RGB and geometric features according to illumination, achieving state-of-the-art overall results on nuScenes-NRS and strong generalization on CARLA-MWRS.

title: CellBRIDGE: Learning Cellular Trajectories via Interaction-Aware Alignment
summary: Inferring dynamics from population snapshots is a fundamental challenge in machine learning and biology. In scRNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq), destructive measurements preclude direct tracking of individual cells across time, making trajectory inference underdetermined. Optimal Transport (OT) provides a principled framework for snapshot alignment, but a long-standing modeling question is which cost functions yield biologically meaningful couplings. Standard OT approaches rely on gene-expression distances, implicitly treating cells as independent points and neglecting structured cell-cell communication mediated by ligand-receptor signaling. We introduce CellBRIDGE (Cell-Based Regularized Interaction-Driven Gene Expression), which augments feature-based OT with a directed, typed interaction cost derived from ligand-receptor activity. By explicitly modeling cell-cell communication, CellBRIDGE improves cross-snapshot couplings and downstream trajectory estimates across synthetic and real scRNA-seq datasets relative to feature-only baselines. Notably, CellBRIDGE enables mechanistically interpretable in silico perturbations: on lung cancer data, silencing specific ligand-receptor pairs induces trajectory shifts that recapitulate expected effects of targeted pathway inhibition.

AI.tldr: CellBRIDGE adds ligand-receptor communication structure to optimal transport for scRNA-seq time-snapshot alignment, improving trajectory inference and enabling interpretable in silico perturbation analysis.
AI.motivation: Trajectory inference from scRNA-seq snapshots is underdetermined because cells are destructively measured and cannot be tracked over time. Existing OT methods mainly use expression-distance costs and ignore structured cell-cell communication, which may limit biological fidelity.
AI.method: The paper proposes CellBRIDGE, an optimal transport framework that combines conventional gene-expression feature costs with a directed, typed interaction regularizer derived from ligand-receptor signaling activity to align cell population snapshots.
AI.result: Across synthetic and real scRNA-seq datasets, CellBRIDGE outperforms feature-only OT baselines in snapshot coupling and downstream trajectory estimation. On lung cancer data, perturbing selected ligand-receptor pairs causes trajectory shifts consistent with expected pathway inhibition effects.
AI.conclusion: CellBRIDGE demonstrates that incorporating directed ligand-receptor interaction costs into optimal transport yields more biologically meaningful cross-time cell couplings, improves trajectory inference, and supports mechanistically interpretable perturbation analysis.

title: Speculative Pipeline Decoding: Higher-Accruacy and Zero-Bubble Speculation via Pipeline Parallelism
summary: Speculative Decoding (SD) accelerates low-concurrency LLM inference by employing a draft-then-verify paradigm. However, mainstream methods typically rely on multi-token prediction, which introduces escalating prediction difficulty and serial drafting latency. To address these, we propose Speculative Pipeline Decoding (SPD), a groundbreaking framework that unlocks the true potential of pipeline parallelism. By partitioning the target LLM into $n$ pipeline stages, SPD allows LLM to process $n$ tokens in parallel to accelerate decoding. To continuous fill the pipeline in single sequence decoding, a speculation module aggregates intermediate features across different pipeline depths to predict the next token, executing strictly in parallel with the target model's pipeline step, to realize bounded difficulty, higher acceptance rates, and zero latency bubbles. Our experiments demonstrate that SPD achieves a significantly higher theoretical speedup compared to mainstream baselines, offering a highly scalable solution for LLM decoding acceleration. Our code is available at https://github.com/yuyijiong/speculative_pipeline_decoding

AI.tldr: SPD用“流水线并行 + 并行推测”替代传统串行draft-then-verify中的多token草稿生成，让LLM在解码时并行处理多个token，同时保持更低预测难度和更高接受率，从而获得更好的理论加速。 / SPD replaces the serial multi-token drafting in conventional draft-then-verify decoding with pipeline parallelism plus parallel speculation, enabling the LLM to process multiple tokens concurrently while keeping prediction easier and acceptance higher, yielding better theoretical speedup.
AI.motivation: 现有SD方法主要依赖multi-token prediction，但随着预测token数增加，预测难度会不断上升，而且草稿生成仍带来串行延迟，限制了低并发LLM推理加速效果。 / Existing speculative decoding methods mainly rely on multi-token prediction, but prediction becomes harder as the token horizon grows, and draft generation still incurs serial latency, limiting acceleration in low-concurrency LLM inference.
AI.method: 方法上，SPD把目标大模型划分为n个流水线阶段，使模型能够并行处理n个token；同时利用一个推测模块聚合不同流水线深度的中间特征来预测下一个token，并与目标模型流水线步骤严格并行执行，以降低预测难度、提升接受率并消除额外串行草稿延迟。 / Methodologically, SPD partitions the target LLM into n pipeline stages so the model can process n tokens in parallel. A speculation module aggregates intermediate features from different pipeline depths to predict the next token, executing strictly in parallel with the target model’s pipeline step to bound prediction difficulty, improve acceptance rate, and remove extra serial drafting latency.
AI.result: 实验结果表明，SPD相比主流基线具有显著更高的理论加速比，并表现出较强的可扩展性，适合作为LLM解码加速方案。 / Experimental results indicate that SPD achieves a significantly higher theoretical speedup than mainstream baselines and offers strong scalability as a decoding acceleration framework for LLMs.
AI.conclusion: SPD通过将目标LLM切分为多个流水线阶段，并结合与流水线并行执行的推测模块，实现了更高可扩展性的解码加速；实验表明其理论加速上限显著优于主流Speculative Decoding基线。 / SPD accelerates decoding by partitioning the target LLM into pipeline stages and pairing it with a speculation module that runs in parallel with the pipeline; experiments show a significantly higher theoretical speedup ceiling than mainstream speculative decoding baselines.

title: Score Broadcast and Decorrelation: A General Framework for Broadcast-Based Credit Assignment
summary: We introduce Score Broadcast and Decorrelation (SBD), a principled framework for broadcast-based credit assignment for general families of differentiable losses. Error broadcast is a biologically plausible alternative to backpropagation that sends output information to hidden layers without weight transport. The Error Broadcast and Decorrelation (EBD) framework, recently introduced for the mean-squared-error (MSE) setting, grounded this mechanism in the stochastic orthogonality of optimal estimators, under which the optimal residual is orthogonal to functions of the input. We generalize that foundation by introducing an orthogonality principle between the output score (the gradient of loss with respect to the final-layer output) and hidden-layer activations, which holds whenever the optimal score has conditional mean zero. This single principle unifies broadcast-based credit assignment across the standard differentiable-loss families, including cross-entropy, Bregman divergences, proper scoring rules, and exponential-family negative log-likelihoods. The framework supplies a theoretical grounding for the three-factor learning rule under general losses, with the neuromodulatory factor derived as the broadcast loss score. We derive the cross-entropy case explicitly, characterize the admissible loss class, and introduce a score vector expansion technique that enriches the broadcast signal while preserving the orthogonality framework. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and Tiny ImageNet show that SBD substantially improves over existing broadcast approaches, with score vector expansion delivering further gains. Overall, this work identifies the loss score as the signal to broadcast, supplies the orthogonality theory and theoretical grounding for the three-factor learning rule from neuroscience, and shows how score vector expansion enriches the decorrelation directions of the resulting objective.

AI.tldr: SBD says hidden layers should receive the loss score, not just raw errors: this gives a unified theory for biologically plausible broadcast learning under many common losses, and empirically improves performance on image benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Prior broadcast-based learning methods had a solid theoretical basis mainly for MSE via EBD, leaving a gap for more general and practically important losses like cross-entropy. The authors aim to build a unified, biologically plausible credit-assignment framework that avoids backpropagation weight transport while extending to standard differentiable losses.
AI.method: The paper generalizes Error Broadcast and Decorrelation by proving an orthogonality principle between the output score (loss gradient w.r.t. final-layer output) and hidden activations when the optimal score has conditional mean zero. It applies this principle to broad differentiable loss families, derives the cross-entropy case, characterizes admissible losses, and proposes score vector expansion to enrich broadcast signals.
AI.result: The framework unifies broadcast-based credit assignment across cross-entropy, Bregman divergences, proper scoring rules, and exponential-family negative log-likelihoods. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and Tiny ImageNet show substantial gains over prior broadcast approaches, with additional improvements from score vector expansion.
AI.conclusion: SBD provides a general theoretical foundation for broadcast-based credit assignment beyond MSE by identifying the loss score as the correct broadcast signal, and score vector expansion can further improve learning performance while preserving the theory.

title: MADS: Model-Aware Diverse Core Set Selection for Instruction Tuning
summary: Instruction fine-tuning is employed to enhance the instruction-following ability of large language models (LLMs). As the amount of instruction fine-tuning data increases, selecting the optimal core set becomes particularly important. However, ensuring the diversity of the core set remains a significant challenge. Existing methods predominantly distinguish different training data based on the text features themselves, decoupled from LLMs' own understanding and representation of the data. To address this issue, we propose a Model-Aware Diverse Core Set Selection method, which distinguishes data features based on the neural activation states during LLM inference. This approach serves as an efficient instantiation of coverage-based selection using model-intrinsic activation features to ensure the diversity in the core set. We extensively evaluate our method on six benchmarks that cover five distinct tasks. In our method, the core set selected by the 3B-parameter LLM performs effectively when utilized to fine-tune larger models with 7B, 8B, and 13B parameters. Experimental results on the Alpaca-GPT4 dataset, which comprises 52K instruction-response pairs, show that the core set, sized at 15\% of the original dataset and selected by Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, achieves an average improvement of 2.5\% when fine-tuning four larger base models compared with training on the full dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that our method enhances model performance on multiple downstream tasks while reducing data requirements.

AI.tldr: Use the LLM’s own activation patterns, not just text features, to pick a diverse 15% instruction-tuning subset; this subset can outperform full-data fine-tuning by 2.5% on average across multiple downstream tasks.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that as instruction tuning datasets grow, it becomes increasingly important to select a compact but high-quality subset. Existing selection methods mainly rely on surface text features and are decoupled from how LLMs internally represent and understand the data, which limits diversity-aware selection.
AI.method: The method is a Model-Aware Diverse Core Set Selection approach. It uses neural activation states generated during LLM inference as intrinsic data representations, then applies a coverage-based core set selection strategy to choose a diverse subset for instruction fine-tuning.
AI.result: The method is evaluated on six benchmarks spanning five tasks. On the 52K Alpaca-GPT4 dataset, a 15% core set selected by Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct yields an average 2.5% improvement over using the full dataset when fine-tuning four larger base models, including 7B, 8B, and 13B models.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that selecting instruction fine-tuning data using model-aware neural activation features produces a more diverse and effective core set than using the full dataset or text-feature-only selection. A small 15% subset can improve downstream performance while reducing data requirements.

title: Variational Adapter for Cross-modal Similarity Representation
comment: Accepted by the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2026)
summary: The core of vision-language models lies in measuring cross-modal similarity within a unified representation space. However, most image-text matching or multi-class image classification datasets lack fine-grained cross-modal matching annotations, forcing the continuous similarity space into binary classification boundaries. This compression induces false negative samples and significantly impairs the generalization performance of cross-modal tasks. While prior research has attempted to mitigate this by modeling intra-modal ambiguity, it often overlooks inherent annotation flaws, leading to suboptimal uncertainty allocation. To address these challenges, we propose a Variational Adapter for Cross-modal Similarity Representation (VACSR). This approach reformulates image-text matching with fine-grained semantic scarcity as a variational inference problem. It constructs a latent space for cross-modal similarity and uses regularization techniques to mitigate overfitting to binary annotations. Experiments on image-text retrieval, domain generalization, and base-to-novel generalization demonstrate the proposed method's effectiveness and robust generalization ability.

AI.tldr: VACSR learns image-text similarity as a latent probabilistic variable instead of a strict binary label, which reduces annotation-induced errors and improves retrieval and generalization.
AI.motivation: Existing vision-language datasets usually provide only coarse binary matching labels rather than fine-grained semantic alignment. This compresses a naturally continuous similarity space, creates false negatives, and hurts generalization. Prior work models intra-modal ambiguity but often ignores annotation defects themselves.
AI.method: The paper proposes a Variational Adapter for Cross-modal Similarity Representation (VACSR). It builds a latent space for cross-modal similarity, reformulates image-text matching under fine-grained annotation scarcity as variational inference, and applies regularization to prevent the model from collapsing continuous similarity into binary decision boundaries.
AI.result: Experiments show gains on image-text retrieval, domain generalization, and base-to-novel generalization, indicating that VACSR is effective and more robust than prior approaches under limited fine-grained annotations.
AI.conclusion: VACSR improves cross-modal similarity learning by treating scarce fine-grained image-text supervision as a variational inference problem, reducing overfitting to binary labels and yielding stronger generalization across retrieval and transfer settings.

title: CSULoRA: Closest Safe Update Low-Rank Adaptation
summary: Low-rank adaptation has become a standard method for parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large language models, but even small amounts of unsafe or adversarial fine-tuning data can substantially weaken the safety behavior of aligned models. Existing safety-preserving LoRA methods often rely on hard interventions such as projection, pruning, thresholding, or additional training objectives. While these methods can suppress unsafe update directions, they may also remove task-relevant information or require extra tuning. We introduce CSULoRA, a post-hoc method for correcting trained LoRA adapters through closest safe update estimation. CSULoRA estimates a safety-aligned subspace from the weight displacement between a safety-aligned model and its corresponding base checkpoint. It then decomposes each LoRA update into fully aligned, partially aligned, and off-subspace components. Instead of discarding components outside the estimated safety subspace, CSULoRA solves a closed-form penalized minimum-change problem that preserves the fully aligned component while smoothly attenuating potentially unsafe directions according to their relative energy. In adversarial fine-tuning experiments, CSULoRA substantially reduces attack success rate while preserving most of the utility gains obtained from standard LoRA fine-tuning.

AI.tldr: CSULoRA is a post-hoc safety correction for LoRA that softly suppresses unsafe update directions via a safety-aligned subspace, improving robustness with minimal loss of task utility.
AI.motivation: Existing safety-preserving LoRA methods often use hard interventions such as projection, pruning, thresholding, or extra objectives, which can damage task-relevant information or require additional tuning. The paper aims to preserve safety without sacrificing utility or adding costly retraining.
AI.method: The paper proposes CSULoRA, a post-hoc correction method for trained LoRA adapters. It estimates a safety-aligned subspace from the weight displacement between a safety-aligned model and its base checkpoint, decomposes LoRA updates into fully aligned, partially aligned, and off-subspace components, and then applies a closed-form penalized minimum-change solution to smoothly attenuate potentially unsafe directions instead of hard-removing them.
AI.result: In adversarial fine-tuning experiments, CSULoRA substantially lowers attack success rate and preserves most of the performance gains achieved by standard LoRA fine-tuning.
AI.conclusion: CSULoRA can significantly reduce the attack success rate caused by adversarial or unsafe fine-tuning while retaining most of the downstream utility gained from standard LoRA fine-tuning.

title: dMoE: dLLMs with Learnable Block Experts
comment: Working in progress. Code is available at: \url{https://github.com/fscdc/dMoE}
summary: Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs) have recently emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive models, offering competitive performance while naturally supporting parallel decoding. However, as dLLMs are increasingly integrated with Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures to scale model capacity, a fundamental mismatch arises between block parallel decoding and token-level expert selection. Specifically, each dLLM forward pass processes multiple tokens with bidirectional dependencies, whereas conventional MoE layers route each token independently. This mismatch substantially increases the number of uniquely activated experts, making inference increasingly memory-bound. To address this, we propose dMoE, a simple yet effective block-level MoE framework. The central idea of dMoE is to aggregate token-level expert distributions within each block into a unified block-level expert distribution, which is then used to guide expert routing in a more coherent manner. In this way, dMoE substantially reduces the number of uniquely activated experts during inference without sacrificing performance, thereby mitigating the memory-bound bottleneck. Extensive experiments across a variety of benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of dMoE. On average, dMoE reduces the number of uniquely activated experts from 69.5 to 14.6 while retaining 99.11% of the original performance. Meanwhile, it reduces memory usage by 76.64% to 79.84% and achieves 1.14$\times$ to 1.66$\times$ end-to-end latency speedup. Code is available at: https://github.com/fscdc/dMoE

AI.tldr: dMoE introduces block-level expert routing for diffusion LLMs with MoE, greatly reducing active experts and memory cost while keeping nearly the same accuracy and speeding up inference.
AI.motivation: In diffusion LLMs combined with MoE, each forward pass processes multiple tokens with bidirectional dependencies, but conventional MoE routes each token independently. This mismatch activates too many unique experts, making inference memory-bound and inefficient.
AI.method: The paper proposes dMoE, which aggregates token-level expert distributions within each decoding block into a unified block-level expert distribution. This block-level distribution is then used for more coherent expert routing across the block, reducing the number of uniquely activated experts during inference.
AI.result: Across multiple benchmarks, dMoE reduces uniquely activated experts from 69.5 to 14.6 on average while retaining 99.11% of original performance. It also cuts memory usage by 76.64% to 79.84% and improves end-to-end latency by 1.14x to 1.66x.
AI.conclusion: dMoE is an effective block-level MoE framework for diffusion LLMs that resolves the mismatch between block parallel decoding and token-level expert routing. It significantly reduces activated experts and memory usage while preserving almost all model performance, leading to faster inference.

title: Omni-Supervised Motion Editing: Balancing Change and Invariance through Positive-Negative Learning
summary: Text-based human motion editing aims to modify existing motion sequences according to natural language instructions while maintaining the consistency of the original motion. Existing diffusion-based approaches often rely on heuristic similarity cues or coarse global conditioning, leading to motion distortion and suboptimal semantic alignment. The key challenge lies in balancing change (i.e. precisely editing target regions) and invariance (i.e. preserving unedited parts). To handle such challenge, we propose an Omni-Supervised Positive-Negative Learning framework, named OmniME. Our method integrates three complementary components: (1) retrospective feature supervision that enforces coarse-to-fine consistency across transformer layers,(2) motion preservation mechanism that focuses on subtle variations according to the source-target similarity, and (3) triplet-based semantic alignment that strengthens text-motion correspondence. Together, these components form a unified supervision paradigm that balances change and invariance. Extensive experiments on the MotionFix and STANCE Adjustment datasets demonstrate that OmniME achieves state-of-the-art performance in editing alignment, validating the effectiveness of our unified learning framework. Our source codes and models have been released at: https://github.com/rocket-ycyer/OmniME.git

AI.tldr: OmniME是一个用于文本驱动人体动作编辑的统一监督框架，通过层间一致性监督、动作保持和三元组语义对齐三种机制，同时提高编辑精度与原动作保真度，并取得SOTA表现。 / OmniME is a unified framework for text-based human motion editing that combines inter-layer consistency supervision, motion preservation, and triplet semantic alignment to improve both edit accuracy and motion fidelity, reaching state-of-the-art results.
AI.motivation: 现有基于扩散的文本动作编辑方法依赖启发式相似性线索或粗粒度全局条件，容易造成动作失真和语义对齐不足。核心难点是同时实现‘变化’与‘不变性’：精确编辑目标区域，同时保持未编辑部分的原始一致性。 / Existing diffusion-based text-driven motion editing methods rely on heuristic similarity cues or coarse global conditioning, which often causes motion distortion and weak semantic alignment. The main motivation is to address the tradeoff between change and invariance: accurately edit target regions while preserving the rest of the motion.
AI.method: 该方法提出OmniME框架，包含三部分：1）回溯式特征监督，在Transformer不同层之间施加由粗到细的一致性约束；2）动作保持机制，基于源动作与目标动作相似性关注细微变化；3）基于三元组的语义对齐，增强文本与动作之间的对应关系。三者共同构成统一监督机制。 / The method proposes OmniME with three components: (1) retrospective feature supervision for coarse-to-fine consistency across Transformer layers, (2) a motion preservation mechanism guided by source-target similarity to preserve subtle unchanged content, and (3) triplet-based semantic alignment to strengthen text-motion correspondence, forming a unified supervision scheme.
AI.result: 在MotionFix和STANCE Adjustment数据集上的大量实验表明，OmniME在编辑对齐方面达到了SOTA，验证了统一学习框架的有效性。 / Extensive experiments on MotionFix and STANCE Adjustment show that OmniME achieves state-of-the-art performance in editing alignment, validating the effectiveness of the unified learning framework.
AI.conclusion: OmniME通过统一的全监督正负学习范式，在文本驱动的人体动作编辑任务中更好地平衡了目标区域编辑与未编辑区域保持，并在MotionFix和STANCE Adjustment数据集上取得了最先进结果。 / OmniME shows that a unified omni-supervised positive-negative learning framework can better balance precise target-region edits and preservation of unedited motion, achieving state-of-the-art results on MotionFix and STANCE Adjustment.

title: Diffusion Models Preferentially Memorize Prototypical Examples or: Why Does My Diffusion Model Love Slop?
summary: Generative models have a persistent limitation: their tendency to memorize training data can create legal liabilities and erode creative diversity. Understanding which samples are memorized in whole or in part, and under what conditions, therefore remains an important open problem. Here we answer the question "Are atypical or rare samples memorized first?" in the negative. We train diffusion models on strings generated according to the production rules of the Random Hierarchy Model (RHM), and find that samples composed of common substrings are preferentially memorized. This holds true even if the training data consists of entirely unique samples, indicating that deduplication at the data point level does not provide a meaningful privacy guarantee. Correspondingly we predict, then observe, delayed memorization for fat-tailed datasets (i.e., those with more atypical samples). This effect is amplified when fat-tails are introduced into high-level production rules. These together suggest that dataset diversity, particularly at higher levels of abstraction, plays an important role in staving off memorization. Finally, we identify an intermediate regime of partial memorization in which common substrings are learned first and subsequently overproduced during generation. If training is stopped in this regime, models will exhibit the reversion-to-the-mean blandness often derided as "slop".

AI.tldr: Diffusion models do not memorize rare examples first; they memorize common underlying parts first. More abstract dataset diversity helps resist this, while partial learning of common patterns can produce generic 'slop' outputs.
AI.motivation: Generative models may memorize training data, creating privacy/legal risks and reducing creative diversity. A key open question is whether atypical or rare samples are memorized first, and what dataset properties govern memorization.
AI.method: The paper trains diffusion models on synthetic string datasets generated by the Random Hierarchy Model (RHM). By controlling substring frequency, sample uniqueness, and fat-tailedness across different production-rule levels, the authors measure when and how full or partial memorization emerges during training and generation.
AI.result: Samples built from common substrings are memorized preferentially, even when every full sample in the training set is unique, showing that record-level deduplication is not a strong privacy safeguard. Fat-tailed datasets delay memorization, especially when diversity is introduced at higher-level generative rules. The authors also observe an intermediate partial-memorization phase where common substrings are learned and overgenerated before full memorization.
AI.conclusion: Memorization in diffusion models is driven more by the frequency of shared substructures than by the rarity of whole samples. Increasing dataset diversity, especially at higher abstraction levels, can delay or reduce memorization; stopping training in a partial-memorization regime leads to overproduction of common patterns and bland outputs ('slop').

title: PatchWorld: Gradient-Free Optimization of Executable World Models
summary: Text-agent environments are typically modeled as partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs), assuming that the simulator's latent state and transition dynamics are hidden from the agent. Yet little work has examined whether executable code can be induced to serve as a world model for prediction and planning under partial observability. We introduce PatchWorld, a gradient-free framework that turns offline trajectories into executable Python world models through counterexample-guided code repair. Instead of predicting the next observation with a black-box model, PatchWorld induces symbolic belief-state programs whose action updates can be inspected, replayed, and locally patched. Across seven AgentGym environments, PatchWorld-Simple achieves the highest code-based planning score among evaluated methods, reaching 76.4\% macro success in live one-step lookahead while invoking no LLM calls inside the world-model prediction module itself. We further find that a human-specified residual-memory bias improves surface observation fidelity but weakens decision utility. This exposes a tradeoff in executable world models, since improving observation fidelity can come at the expense of action-discriminative dynamics, and vice versa. Code is available at https://github.com/HKBU-KnowComp/PatchWorld.

AI.tldr: 中文：PatchWorld 用离线轨迹+反例修复自动生成可执行 Python 世界模型，在 7 个文本环境中实现了强规划表现，并揭示了“观测更准”与“决策更好”之间并不一致。 English: PatchWorld turns offline trajectories into executable Python world models via counterexample-guided repair, performs strongly on seven text-agent environments, and reveals that better observation fidelity can conflict with better decision-making.
AI.motivation: 中文：现有文本智能体环境通常被建模为 POMDP，默认潜在状态与转移动态对智能体不可见，但很少有工作研究能否直接归纳出“可执行代码”作为世界模型，以支持部分可观测条件下的预测与规划。 English: Text-agent environments are usually modeled as POMDPs with hidden latent states and dynamics, yet little prior work studies whether executable code can be induced as a world model for prediction and planning under partial observability.
AI.method: 中文：作者提出 PatchWorld，一个无梯度框架，从离线轨迹中归纳可执行的 Python 世界模型；核心做法是通过反例引导的代码修复，把轨迹转化为可检查、可回放、可局部修补的符号化 belief-state 程序，而不是训练黑盒下一观测预测器。 English: The paper proposes PatchWorld, a gradient-free framework that induces executable Python world models from offline trajectories via counterexample-guided code repair, producing symbolic belief-state programs that are inspectable, replayable, and locally patchable instead of black-box next-observation predictors.
AI.result: 中文：在 7 个 AgentGym 环境中，PatchWorld-Simple 在代码型规划方法里取得最佳结果，在实时一步前瞻设置下达到 76.4% 的宏平均成功率，且世界模型预测模块内部不需要调用 LLM；另外，人工指定的 residual-memory bias 虽提高了表层观测拟合，但削弱了决策效用。 English: Across seven AgentGym environments, PatchWorld-Simple achieves the best code-based planning performance, reaching 76.4% macro success in live one-step lookahead without any LLM calls inside the world-model prediction module; a human-specified residual-memory bias improves surface observation fidelity but hurts decision utility.
AI.conclusion: 中文：PatchWorld 证明了可执行的 Python 代码世界模型可以在部分可观测文本智能体环境中用于预测与规划，并且“更高的观测拟合度”不一定带来“更好的决策效用”，两者之间存在权衡。 English: PatchWorld shows that executable Python world models can support prediction and planning in partially observable text-agent environments, and that higher observation fidelity does not necessarily yield better decision utility; there is a tradeoff between the two.

title: The Flip Side of RLHF: On-Policy Feedback for Reward Model Self-Supervised Improvement
summary: Building strong reward models (RMs) for language model alignment is bottlenecked by the cost and difficulty of acquiring diverse and reliable preference data from human annotation or judge models. It is dramatically worse as the policy evolves beyond the static RM training. Therefore, we propose SAVE (Self-supervised reward model improvement via Value-Anchored On-policy feedback), a framework that grades on-policy responses as feedback by using the value function for on-policy RM training. SAVE naturally converts the reward-graded on-policy responses into supervision with a prompt-specific value head as an adaptive anchor. It computes RM advantages and filters ambiguous samples to update the RM via a contrastive objective. The effectiveness of SAVE for enhancing RM training is strongly validated through rigorous empirical evaluation across six diverse benchmarks. It achieves outperforming results across all datasets while maintaining consistent improvements across three RL algorithms (GRPO, RLOO, GSPO) and different policy backbones.

AI.tldr: 中文：这篇论文提出 SAVE，用价值函数给 on-policy 回答自动打分，生成自监督信号来持续改进奖励模型，减少对昂贵人工偏好数据的依赖，并在多基准和多种 RL 设置下显著优于现有方法。 English: This paper proposes SAVE, which uses value functions to automatically score on-policy responses and create self-supervised signals for continual reward model improvement, reducing reliance on costly preference data and outperforming prior approaches across benchmarks and RL settings.
AI.motivation: 中文：高质量、多样化偏好数据昂贵且难以获取，而静态奖励模型难以跟上不断演化的策略，因此奖励模型成为语言模型对齐的瓶颈。 English: Acquiring diverse, reliable preference data is costly and difficult, and static reward models lag behind evolving policies, making reward model improvement a key bottleneck in alignment.
AI.method: 中文：方法核心是 SAVE：利用策略在训练过程中的 value function 对 on-policy 响应进行打分；以 prompt-specific value head 作为自适应锚点，将这些带分数的响应转成监督信号；计算奖励模型 advantage，过滤模糊样本，并用对比学习目标更新奖励模型。 English: The method, SAVE, grades on-policy responses with the policy’s value function, uses a prompt-specific value head as an adaptive anchor to convert graded responses into supervision, computes RM advantages, filters ambiguous pairs, and updates the reward model with a contrastive objective.
AI.result: 中文：论文在六个不同基准上验证了 SAVE 的有效性；其结果在所有数据集上都优于对比方法，并且在 GRPO、RLOO、GSPO 三种 RL 算法及不同策略骨干上保持稳定提升。 English: Across six diverse benchmarks, SAVE outperforms baselines on all datasets and shows consistent improvements under GRPO, RLOO, and GSPO with different policy backbones.
AI.conclusion: 中文：SAVE 通过基于价值函数的 on-policy 自监督反馈，能够稳定提升奖励模型训练质量，并在多基准、多个强化学习算法和不同策略骨干上取得一致更优表现。 English: SAVE uses value-function-anchored on-policy self-supervised feedback to reliably improve reward model training, delivering consistent gains across benchmarks, RL algorithms, and policy backbones.

title: Can BEV Perception Gracefully Degrade under Sensor Failures?
summary: Despite the remarkable success of multi-modal bird's-eye view (BEV) perception in autonomous driving, current systems exhibit a critical vulnerability: existing fusion mechanisms are highly brittle to sensor corruptions, often causing catastrophic performance degradation. This vulnerability largely stems from the fact that standard fusion frameworks typically integrate multi-modal representations in a static manner, leading to a precipitous performance collapse under missing or corrupted modalities. In contrast, we show that graceful degradation is achievable through active modality reliability assessment. To this end, we present Grace-BEV, a lightweight and plug-and-play framework that enforces active reliability awareness during multi-modal fusion. Instead of relying on computationally expensive cross-modal interactions, Grace-BEV leverages the aligned BEV space to explicitly assess modality trustworthiness via a TrustGate Router and dynamically recalibrate feature integration using the FailSafe Fusion Block. Furthermore, we devise a Three-Phase Training strategy with Modality Dropout to prevent modality dominance and encourage balanced cross-modal learning under unreliable inputs. Extensive experiments on nuScenes-R and nuScenes-C show that Grace-BEV maintains robust performance across diverse corruption settings. Notably, under catastrophic LiDAR failures where standard baselines collapse to 0.0% mean Average Precision (mAP), Grace-BEV restores performance to as high as 34.7% mAP. Moreover, it improves clean accuracy by up to 1.4%, achieving a strong trade-off between robustness and efficiency.

AI.tldr: Grace-BEV is a lightweight reliability-aware BEV fusion method for autonomous driving that detects which sensor modality is trustworthy and adapts fusion accordingly, greatly improving robustness to corruption and missing sensors while slightly boosting clean accuracy.
AI.motivation: Existing multimodal BEV perception systems for autonomous driving are brittle when sensors are missing or corrupted because they fuse modalities statically. The paper is motivated by the need for robust fusion that can adapt to unreliable sensor inputs and avoid catastrophic performance collapse.
AI.method: The paper proposes Grace-BEV, a lightweight plug-and-play multimodal BEV fusion framework. It uses a TrustGate Router to estimate modality trustworthiness in aligned BEV space, a FailSafe Fusion Block to dynamically recalibrate fusion, and a Three-Phase Training strategy with Modality Dropout to avoid modality dominance and improve learning under unreliable inputs.
AI.result: Experiments on nuScenes-R and nuScenes-C show that Grace-BEV maintains robust performance across diverse corruption settings. Under catastrophic LiDAR failure, where standard baselines drop to 0.0% mAP, Grace-BEV recovers performance up to 34.7% mAP. It also improves clean accuracy by up to 1.4%, indicating a strong robustness-efficiency trade-off.
AI.conclusion: Grace-BEV demonstrates that actively estimating modality reliability in aligned BEV space enables graceful degradation under sensor corruption, substantially improving robustness while preserving efficiency and even slightly improving clean performance.

title: LARK: Learnability-Grounded Trajectory Selection for Efficient Reasoning Distillation
summary: We study trajectory selection for reasoning distillation, where teacher-generated reasoning trajectories are selectively used as supervision for a student model. Existing methods rely on heuristics such as trajectory quality or model confidence, but they often overlook whether a trajectory is learnable by the student. In this paper, we present LARK, a learnability-grounded method for reasoning trajectory selection. LARK selects trajectories that the student can learn efficiently while preserving the generalization of the full training distribution. At the core of LARK is a learnability factor $ρ$, which characterizes the rate at which the student's training loss decreases. To estimate this rate efficiently and maintain generalization, we introduce a learnability proxy and a $χ^2$-regularized selection policy that balances learnability and distributional coverage, both with strong theoretical guarantees on their estimation error. Empirically, LARK consistently outperforms data selection baselines across multiple base models and reasoning tasks. Diagnostic analyses show that the LARK score predicts downstream training utility and that LARK-selected trajectories induce faster supervised fine-tuning loss reduction. Our code is available at https://github.com/Tianrun-Yu/LARK.

AI.tldr: LARK picks reasoning traces that are not just high-quality, but actually learnable for the student model, while still matching the full data distribution. This improves reasoning distillation performance and speeds up student training.
AI.motivation: Prior trajectory selection methods for reasoning distillation mainly use heuristic signals such as trajectory quality or model confidence, but they neglect whether a given reasoning trajectory is actually easy and useful for the student to learn from. The paper aims to select trajectories that improve student learning efficiency without sacrificing generalization.
AI.method: The paper proposes LARK, a learnability-grounded trajectory selection method. It defines a learnability factor rho to capture how quickly the student’s training loss decreases on a trajectory, uses an efficient learnability proxy to estimate this factor, and applies a chi-squared-regularized selection policy to balance learnability with coverage of the original training distribution. The method is supported by theoretical estimation error guarantees.
AI.result: Across multiple base models and reasoning tasks, LARK consistently outperforms existing data selection baselines. Additional diagnostics show that the LARK score correlates with downstream training utility and that selected trajectories lead to faster supervised fine-tuning loss reduction.
AI.conclusion: LARK demonstrates that selecting teacher reasoning trajectories based on student learnability, rather than only quality or confidence heuristics, yields better reasoning distillation performance while preserving distributional generalization.

title: Generating Reports or Repeating Templates? Measuring and Mitigating Template Collapse in 3D CT Report Generation
summary: Modern 3D medical vision-language models (VLMs) can generate fluent radiology-style text while exhibit critically low pathology detection and output diversity, collapsing to generic templates that under-report rare yet critical findings. We identify this failure mode as Template Collapse. This failure stems from the unique constraints of 3D medical imaging, e.g., limited data, severe label imbalance, and weak signals from volumetric encoders. Under these constraints, text-generation objectives encourage shortcut learning and fluent but weakly grounded reports. We systematically diagnose the Template Collapse through clinical fidelity, output diversity, normal-template bias, and rare-finding survival. To mitigate it, we propose CLarGen, a decoupled framework that separates what to say (clinical detection) from how to say it (language synthesis). CLarGen uses (i) a Latent Query Transformer for multi-label pathology detection, (ii) pathology-guided retrieval for clinically matched exemplars, and (iii) a medical language model to synthesize the final report from detected findings and retrieved context. Across state-of-the-art 3D CT report generation baselines, CLarGen mitigates Template Collapse and substantially improves clinical accuracy (macro-F1 0.487 vs. 0.189; CRG 0.472 vs. 0.368) while maintaining fluent reporting. Our results suggest that explicit, measurable clinical grounding is essential for template-collapse-resistant 3D CT report generation. Code will be released upon acceptance.

AI.tldr: 3D CT report generators often produce safe, generic reports and miss important abnormalities. CLarGen fixes this by separating pathology detection from text writing, then using retrieval plus a medical language model to generate reports. It significantly improves clinically grounded accuracy over prior methods.
AI.motivation: Current 3D medical vision-language models generate fluent but weakly grounded radiology reports, often collapsing into generic normal templates that miss rare but critical findings. This failure mode, called Template Collapse, is driven by limited data, strong label imbalance, and weak volumetric visual signals in 3D imaging.
AI.method: The paper proposes CLarGen, a decoupled framework that separates clinical content determination from language realization. It combines a Latent Query Transformer for multi-label pathology detection, pathology-guided retrieval of clinically matched exemplars, and a medical language model that synthesizes reports from detected findings and retrieved context.
AI.result: Across state-of-the-art 3D CT report generation baselines, CLarGen mitigates Template Collapse and improves clinical accuracy, achieving macro-F1 0.487 versus 0.189 and CRG 0.472 versus 0.368, while maintaining fluent report generation.
AI.conclusion: Explicit, measurable clinical grounding is essential to resist template collapse in 3D CT report generation, and the proposed CLarGen framework substantially improves clinical accuracy while preserving fluency.

title: Bridging the Gap Between Natural Language and Market Dynamics via High-Dimensional Representation Learning
summary: Traditional multi-modal financial forecasting often relies on scalar sentiment scores, which fail to capture the nuances of financial news. To address this information loss, this paper explores high-dimensional representation learning by replacing discrete polarity ratings with dense FinBERT embeddings within a Transformer-based forecasting architecture. We benchmarked various embedding strategies on the FNSPID dataset, including raw embeddings, attention-weighted aggregation, and a custom Siamese network. While the attention-based mechanism struggled with the low signal-to-noise ratio typical of financial data, the integration of Siamese-optimized embeddings outperformed both the scalar baseline and raw embedding approaches, demonstrating that preserving high-dimensional narrative context yields improved predictive accuracy for short-term stock price movements.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that using richer FinBERT news embeddings, particularly after Siamese optimization, beats traditional sentiment-score inputs for short-term stock prediction.
AI.motivation: Scalar sentiment scores compress financial news into overly simple polarity values, causing loss of nuanced narrative information that may be useful for predicting market movements.
AI.method: The paper replaces scalar sentiment labels with high-dimensional FinBERT embeddings and evaluates multiple embedding integration strategies in a Transformer-based multi-modal forecasting model on the FNSPID dataset, including raw embeddings, attention-weighted aggregation, and a custom Siamese network.
AI.result: Attention-based aggregation underperformed in noisy financial settings, while Siamese-optimized embeddings outperformed both scalar sentiment baselines and raw embedding variants in predictive accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Using dense FinBERT embeddings, especially Siamese-optimized embeddings, preserves richer semantic context than scalar sentiment scores and improves short-term stock movement forecasting in a Transformer framework.

title: EMBGuard: Constructing Hazard-Aware Guardrails for Safe Planning in Embodied Agents
summary: MLLM-powered embodied agents deployed in real-world environments encounter physical hazards. However, existing approaches lack explicit mechanisms for identifying hazards and reasoning about action-conditioned risks, leading agents to either miss risky interactions or over-identify risks. To address this, we propose EMBGuard, the first MLLM-based safety guardrail for embodied agents designed to decouple physical risk reasoning from agent policy. By evaluating a (visual observation, action) pair, EMBGuard identifies hazardous configurations and provides natural language explanations of potential risks. Alongside EMBGuard, we contribute EMBHazard, a training dataset of 15.1K action-conditioned pairs, and EMBGuardTest, a benchmark of 329 manually curated real-world scenarios spanning seven physical risk categories. Through compositional variation of hazards and actions, we generate diverse risky and benign scenarios that agents may encounter during planning. Despite its compact size (2B, 4B), EMBGuard achieves performance competitive with proprietary MLLMs (e.g., GPT-5.1, Gemini-2.5-Pro) while significantly reducing the false-positive rates that hinder real-time deployment. We make the code, data, and models publicly available at https://github.com/dongwxxkchoi/EMBGuard

AI.tldr: EMBGuard is a compact MLLM safety guardrail for embodied agents that checks image-action pairs for physical hazards, explains risks, and matches strong proprietary models with fewer false alarms using a new dataset and benchmark.
AI.motivation: Existing MLLM-powered embodied agents in real environments lack explicit mechanisms for hazard identification and action-conditioned risk reasoning, which causes them either to overlook dangerous interactions or to over-predict risks. The work aims to provide a dedicated safety layer that improves physical risk assessment without entangling it with the agent policy.
AI.method: The paper proposes EMBGuard, an MLLM-based safety guardrail that evaluates visual observation and action pairs to detect hazardous configurations and explain risks in natural language. It is trained with EMBHazard, a 15.1K action-conditioned dataset, and evaluated on EMBGuardTest, a benchmark of 329 curated real-world scenarios across seven physical risk categories.
AI.result: Despite being compact (2B and 4B models), EMBGuard reaches performance competitive with proprietary MLLMs such as GPT-5.1 and Gemini-2.5-Pro, while significantly lowering false-positive rates that are critical for real-time deployment.
AI.conclusion: EMBGuard demonstrates that explicit, action-conditioned physical risk reasoning can be separated from embodied agent policy, achieving strong safety performance with low false-positive rates and competitive results against larger proprietary MLLMs.

title: Benchmarking Single-Step Inpainting Methods for Multi-Object 3D Gaussian Splatting Scenes
comment: Accepted as an extended abstract to the CVEU Workshop at CVPR 2026
summary: The tasks of object removal and inpainting 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) scenes face challenges such as 3D consistency across camera views. In comparing 2D inpainters and their suitability for the 3D domain, we find that reconstruction-based inpainters outperform generative diffusion models in 3D consistency. Integrating these 2D inpainters into different single-step methods for creating and finetuning 3DGS scenes, our results indicate that initializing the scene from scratch produces higher quality results than finetuning the existing scene. Using a state-of-the-art generative 2D inpainter, we create a straightforward baseline to underline the importance of object removal before inpainting in the 3D setting. Since 360° datasets rarely include real-world ground truths, and challenging occlusion scenarios are equally sparse, we introduce a novel multi-object scene with recorded ground truth data and many views with object occlusions.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how to remove and inpaint objects in 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes without breaking multi-view consistency. It finds that reconstruction-based 2D inpainters work better than diffusion models for 3D-consistent results, and that rebuilding the 3DGS scene from scratch is better than finetuning. It also introduces a new occlusion-heavy 360-degree dataset with ground truth for evaluation.
AI.motivation: Object removal and inpainting in 3DGS scenes are difficult because edits must remain consistent across multiple camera views, while existing 360-degree datasets rarely provide real-world ground truth or difficult occlusion cases. The paper aims to understand which 2D inpainting approaches transfer best to 3DGS editing and how to build more reliable evaluation data.
AI.method: The paper compares different 2D inpainters for their 3D consistency when applied to object removal and inpainting in 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes. It integrates these inpainters into multiple single-step pipelines for either initializing a new 3DGS scene from scratch or finetuning an existing one, and builds a baseline using a state-of-the-art generative 2D inpainter. It also constructs a new multi-object 360-degree scene dataset with recorded ground truth and significant occlusions for evaluation.
AI.result: Experiments show that reconstruction-based inpainters outperform diffusion-based generative inpainters in 3D consistency. Among the tested 3DGS editing strategies, initializing the scene from scratch produces higher-quality results than finetuning an existing scene. The proposed baseline further highlights the necessity of removing objects before inpainting in the 3D setting, and the new dataset provides a more realistic benchmark for evaluation.
AI.conclusion: Reconstruction-based 2D inpainters are more suitable than generative diffusion models for maintaining 3D consistency in 3DGS object removal/inpainting, and rebuilding a 3DGS scene from scratch yields better quality than finetuning an existing scene. The work also shows that explicit object removal before inpainting is important in 3D scene editing and introduces a new benchmark dataset with ground truth and occlusion-heavy views.

title: Learning to Perceive the World Through Control: Empowerment-Based Representation Learning
summary: In many practical reinforcement learning environments, observations are far higher-dimensional than the variables that matter for control. In this work, we ask: can we learn representations that capture only control-relevant features of the environment? We study this question through the empowerment objective, which maximizes an agent's influence over the environment and is widely used for unsupervised skill learning. We show that empowerment agents induce two distinct representations -- forward and backward -- that capture complementary aspects of the state, and both of which are invariant to control-irrelevant features. Thus, empowerment maximization leads agents to learn an implicit, control-centric model of the world. Our analysis highlights the importance of learning representations through interaction rather than from passive datasets: interaction aimed at maximizing control is essential for learning useful invariance properties, a perspective that aligns closely with the causal learning literature.

AI.tldr: The paper argues that maximizing empowerment in RL makes an agent learn compact state representations centered on what it can control, not on irrelevant observation details, and that this requires active interaction with the environment.
AI.motivation: In many RL problems, observations contain many high-dimensional details that do not matter for control. The paper aims to determine whether an unsupervised objective can learn representations that keep only control-relevant information.
AI.method: The paper studies representation learning in high-dimensional reinforcement learning through the empowerment objective. It analyzes the representations induced by empowerment-based agents and characterizes them as forward and backward representations that encode complementary control-relevant aspects of state while discarding irrelevant variation.
AI.result: The analysis shows that empowerment agents learn two distinct but complementary invariant representations, both focused on control-relevant state information. It also argues that passive datasets are insufficient for learning these invariances, while interactive control-seeking behavior is crucial, connecting the findings to causal learning.
AI.conclusion: Empowerment maximization implicitly learns control-centric state representations. It induces two complementary representations, called forward and backward representations, and both are invariant to control-irrelevant features. Interaction that seeks control is essential for acquiring these useful invariances.

title: MineExplorer: Evaluating Open-World Exploration of MLLM Agents in Minecraft
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have shown strong capabilities in perception, reasoning, and action generation. However, their ability to sustain exploration in dynamic open worlds remains unclear. Existing embodied and game-based benchmarks often compress interaction into short-horizon tasks or entangle success with domain-specific game mechanics. In this paper, we introduce MineExplorer benchmark for evaluating open-world exploration capabilities of MLLM agents in Minecraft. We first filter atomic tasks whose solutions rely heavily on Minecraft-specific knowledge to better reflect general open-world reasoning. Then we organize the benchmark around a ReAct-style capability formulation and compose atomic tasks into implicit multi-hop tasks. To further construct reliable instances, MineExplorer uses a multi-agent synthesis workflow that jointly designs task graphs, sandbox scenes, and rule-based milestone evaluators. Human evaluation shows that the multi-agent synthesis workflow produces significantly more reliable instances than a single-agent baseline. Experiments with advanced MLLM agents show that open-world exploration remains challenging, as strong models can handle many single-hop tasks but degrade sharply when hidden prerequisites must be coordinated over longer trajectories. Further analysis finds that task difficulty tracks agent completion, and larger models or thinking modes do not consistently translate into better performance. Code and dataset are available at https://github.com/Jometeorie/MineExplorer.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces MineExplorer, a Minecraft benchmark designed to measure general open-world exploration in MLLM agents. It removes overly game-specific tasks, builds multi-hop exploration challenges with a multi-agent generation pipeline, and shows that even strong models still fail badly when exploration requires long-horizon coordination and hidden prerequisite reasoning.
AI.motivation: Existing embodied and game-based benchmarks usually focus on short-horizon tasks or mix general exploration ability with domain-specific game mechanics, making it unclear how well MLLM agents can sustain exploration in dynamic open worlds.
AI.method: The paper builds MineExplorer, a Minecraft-based benchmark for open-world exploration. It filters out atomic tasks that depend too much on Minecraft-specific knowledge, organizes tasks with a ReAct-style capability formulation, composes them into implicit multi-hop tasks, and constructs benchmark instances through a multi-agent synthesis workflow that jointly creates task graphs, sandbox scenes, and rule-based milestone evaluators.
AI.result: Human evaluation shows the multi-agent synthesis workflow generates more reliable benchmark instances than a single-agent baseline. Experiments with strong MLLM agents show they perform reasonably on many single-hop tasks but struggle significantly on multi-hop exploration tasks requiring coordination of hidden prerequisites. Task difficulty correlates with completion rate, and larger models or thinking modes do not consistently yield better performance.
AI.conclusion: MineExplorer reveals that open-world exploration remains difficult for multimodal large language model agents: performance drops sharply on longer-horizon tasks with hidden prerequisites, and neither larger model scale nor explicit thinking modes reliably improve results.

title: Iterative Framework For Data Augmentation Of Segmented Fingerprints
summary: Infant biometrics presents unique challenges due to the physiological differences between infants and adults, compounded by the scarcity of available data for research that limits the development of robust matching systems. This paper proposes a novel data augmentation method that uses iterative techniques to generate diverse variants of segmented fingerprints by inducing errors in a convolutional neural network trained to extract fingerprint ridges and valleys. Experiments on real infant fingerprints demonstrate the method's effectiveness in expanding fingerprint variability, with augmentations exhibiting significant fluctuations in minutiae counts while still retaining visual similarity to the originals. The study also highlights the method's customizable nature for applying varying levels of changes to fingerprint segmentations. Future research includes training segmentation and matching neural networks using datasets augmented by the proposed framework.

AI.tldr: A new CNN-based iterative augmentation method creates realistic variations of infant fingerprint segmentations, addressing data scarcity and helping future infant biometric matching systems.
AI.motivation: The work is motivated by two main issues in infant biometrics: physiological differences between infants and adults that make matching difficult, and the scarcity of infant fingerprint data, which limits the development of robust recognition systems.
AI.method: The method augments infant fingerprint data by iteratively inducing controlled errors in a convolutional neural network trained to extract fingerprint ridges and valleys, generating diverse variants of segmented fingerprints.
AI.result: Experiments on real infant fingerprints show that the generated augmentations increase fingerprint variability, including significant changes in minutiae counts, while still remaining visually similar to the original images. The method is also customizable in terms of augmentation strength.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that the proposed iterative augmentation framework can effectively expand the variability of infant fingerprint segmentations while preserving visual similarity to the original fingerprints, making it a promising tool for improving infant biometric datasets.

title: BOKBO (Best of K Bad Options): Calibrated Abstention for VLA Policies
summary:
Test-time scaling for vision-language-action (VLA) policies, methods such as RoboMonkey, SEAL, MG-Select, and V-GPS, samples K candidate action chunks at inference and executes the verifier-best. When all K candidates are unsafe, the system executes a violating action with no warning. We propose BOKBO, the first conformal abstention layer for K-sample VLA inference, providing finite-sample distribution-free guarantees on executed-violation rate. We provide both global and per-task (Mondrian) variants, with the per-task variant closing the conditional gap on the hardest tasks.
  Our analysis exposes a structural failure of policy-internal nonconformity scores under perturbation-based K-sampling: the base-policy confidence proxy and K-sample disagreement correlate at 0.98 with the action-noise hyperparameter $σ$, while correlating at the noise floor with actual safety violations. We test the failure's scope by replicating the analysis under token-level temperature sampling and find the failure is mechanism-specific and partially mitigated under policy-stochasticity-based sampling. A learned violation predictor conditioned on semantic visual features and task identity supports tight calibration: at $ε$ = 0.05 on libero_object_temp_x0.1 with OpenVLA-OFT, the conditional CRC bound holds on 86% of bootstrap splits with 78% coverage and 70% net task success. Mondrian-BOKBO raises the minimum per-task conditional hold fraction from 0.71 to 0.93. Results are stable across 5 training seeds, replicate within bootstrap noise on $π_0$-FAST, hold on libero_spatial_temp_x0.1 as a co-equal benchmark, and survive four within-suite distribution shifts. We additionally identify and correct a methodological pitfall: globally-set force thresholds well below expert-typical manipulation forces conflate unsafe behavior with normal manipulation, inflating violation rates by $5\times$.

AI.tldr: BOKBO adds a conformal abstention layer to K-sample VLA inference so the robot can refuse execution when sampled actions look unsafe, instead of always choosing a bad option. It shows standard internal safety/confidence scores fail under perturbation-based sampling, while a learned violation predictor with global or Mondrian conformal calibration yields stronger safety guarantees and better per-task reliability.
AI.motivation: Existing test-time scaling approaches for VLA policies pick the best action among K sampled candidates, but if every sampled candidate is unsafe, the system still executes one without warning. The work is motivated by the need for a principled abstention layer that can reject unsafe execution while providing formal guarantees, and by the observation that common internal confidence/disagreement signals may be badly misaligned with actual safety risk.
AI.method: The paper adds a conformal abstention mechanism on top of test-time K-candidate action sampling for VLA policies. It studies failure modes of policy-internal nonconformity scores under perturbation-based sampling, compares this with token-temperature sampling, and instead calibrates a learned violation predictor using semantic visual features and task identity, with both global and per-task (Mondrian) conformal variants.
AI.result: The authors report that internal nonconformity signals are strongly correlated with the action-noise hyperparameter (0.98) but near the noise floor with true safety violations, showing a structural failure for perturbation-based K-sampling. Their learned predictor plus conformal calibration achieves, at epsilon=0.05 on libero_object_temp_x0.1 with OpenVLA-OFT, 86% conditional CRC hold over bootstrap splits, 78% coverage, and 70% net task success; Mondrian-BOKBO improves the minimum per-task conditional hold fraction from 0.71 to 0.93. Findings are stable across 5 seeds, reproduce on another policy and benchmark, survive four within-suite shifts, and they also correct an evaluation pitfall where overly low global force thresholds inflated violation rates by 5x.
AI.conclusion: BOKBO is presented as the first conformal abstention layer for K-sample VLA inference, giving finite-sample, distribution-free guarantees on executed safety violations. The Mondrian per-task variant improves conditional reliability on difficult tasks, and the method remains robust across seeds, benchmarks, and moderate distribution shifts.

title: Do Large Language Models Encode Institutional Experience? Evidence from Cross-Linguistic Moral Reasoning Under Ambiguity
summary: Large language models (LLMs) exhibit systematic differences in moral reasoning across languages, yet the source of this variation remains unclear. We test the hypothesis that languages encode aspects of the institutional environments in which they are spoken, allowing LLMs to inherit institution-specific moral priors through training. Across nine languages spanning a broad gradient of institutional quality, six frontier LLMs, and two preregistered studies, we examine moral dilemmas whose acceptability depends on institutional functioning. In Study 1, explicit institutional framing produced uniformly null results: cross-linguistic moral divergence did not increase in institutionally contingent scenarios, nor did it track institutional differences between language communities. In Study 2, we introduced institutionally ambiguous scenarios in which institutional stakes were present but not explicitly stated. Under these conditions, cross-linguistic moral divergence increased relative to institutionally inert controls and, with one theoretically informative exception, was associated with real-world institutional differences between language communities. Explicit framing again attenuated these effects. These findings suggest that institutional experience may leave detectable traces in language that shape LLM moral reasoning, while also indicating that explicit institutional cues can suppress the expression of those differences.

AI.tldr: 论文表明：LLM的跨语言道德差异可能来自语言中隐含的制度经验，但这种影响主要在“制度存在却未明说”的情境中显现；一旦把制度线索说得太明确，差异反而会被压制。 / LLM cross-linguistic moral differences may stem from institutional experience embedded in language, but this effect shows up mainly when institutional stakes are implicit; making those cues explicit tends to suppress the differences.
AI.motivation: 动机是解释为什么LLM在不同语言中的道德推理会系统性不同。作者提出一个机制性假设：语言可能编码了其使用社群所处制度环境的经验，因此LLM在训练中会继承带有制度特征的道德先验。 / The motivation is to explain why LLMs show systematic cross-linguistic differences in moral reasoning. The paper tests a mechanistic hypothesis that languages encode experiences of the institutional environments of their speaker communities, allowing LLMs to inherit institution-specific moral priors during training.
AI.method: 作者在两个预注册研究中，使用9种语言、6个前沿LLM，测试一组道德困境。研究1操纵显性制度框架，检验跨语言差异是否在制度依赖情境中扩大并与制度质量梯度一致。研究2改用制度上模糊的情境，其中制度利害存在但未明确说明，并与制度无关的对照情境比较。 / The authors ran two preregistered studies across 9 languages and 6 frontier LLMs using moral dilemmas. Study 1 manipulated explicit institutional framing to test whether divergence increased in institution-dependent scenarios and tracked institutional-quality gradients. Study 2 used institutionally ambiguous scenarios, where institutional stakes were implicit rather than explicit, and compared them with institutionally inert controls.
AI.result: 研究1结果基本为零：显性制度框架没有放大跨语言道德分歧，分歧也不随语言社群间的制度差异而增强。研究2发现，在制度模糊情境下，跨语言分歧相对制度无关对照显著增加，并且除一个理论上重要的例外外，这种分歧与现实制度差异相关；一旦重新加入显性框架，这些效应又被削弱。 / Study 1 found null effects: explicit institutional framing did not amplify cross-linguistic moral divergence, nor did divergence track institutional differences between language communities. Study 2 found that in institutionally ambiguous scenarios, divergence increased relative to institutionally inert controls and, with one theoretically informative exception, correlated with real-world institutional differences; explicit framing again attenuated these effects.
AI.conclusion: LLMs的跨语言道德推理差异并不主要在显性制度框架下表现出来；相反，这些差异更容易在制度相关但未被明说的模糊情境中显现，且通常与现实世界中的制度差异相对应。这表明语言可能携带制度经验的痕迹，并影响LLM的道德先验。 / Cross-linguistic moral differences in LLMs do not primarily emerge under explicit institutional framing. Instead, they become more visible in institutionally relevant but unstated scenarios, and usually align with real-world institutional differences, suggesting that language carries traces of institutional experience that shape LLM moral priors.

title: PEEK: Picking Essential frames via Efficient Knowledge distillation
summary: Video-language models can process only a limited number of frames, making frame selection a key bottleneck for efficient video captioning. Most captioning pipelines still rely on uniform sampling, which is computationally cheap but agnostic to visual content. Adaptive frame sampling has recently emerged as a promising approach for selecting the most informative frames from a video; however, existing methods remain computationally expensive. We introduce PEEK, an efficient dynamic frame sampling method that distills caption-conditioned frame relevance rankings from a stronger teacher model into a lightweight temporal model that operates only on visual content. We find that, overall, on ActivityNet Captions and MSR-VTT, our method outperforms state-of-the-art methods across all evaluated downstream vision language models, especially when only one or two frames are selected for captioning, obtaining the best CIDEr for most frame budgets. On ActivityNet Captions, PEEK is particularly strong, winning 14 out of 16 configurations. Zero-shot evaluation on MSR-VTT shows that our model transfers best at low frame budgets, while results at four and eight frames are more mixed as temporal coverage and visual diversity become increasingly competitive. Compared with recent adaptive baselines, PEEK is both more accurate in the low-budget regime and more efficient: it adds only $5.2\%$ to the captioning time, compared with $65.4\%$ for CSTA and $211.9\%$ for MaxInfo. We release our code and pre-trained checkpoint at https://github.com/momentslab/peek.

AI.tldr: PEEK learns from a strong teacher to pick the most useful video frames cheaply, beating prior adaptive frame samplers for captioning at low frame budgets while being far more efficient.
AI.motivation: Video-language models can process only a limited number of frames, so frame selection is a critical bottleneck. Uniform sampling is cheap but ignores content, while existing adaptive methods are promising yet too computationally expensive. The work aims to deliver adaptive sampling that is both accurate and efficient.
AI.method: The paper proposes PEEK, a lightweight temporal model that predicts frame relevance from visual content only. It is trained by distilling caption-conditioned frame relevance rankings from a stronger teacher model, enabling dynamic selection of informative frames for downstream video-language captioning.
AI.result: On ActivityNet Captions and MSR-VTT, PEEK outperforms recent state-of-the-art adaptive sampling methods across evaluated downstream vision-language models, particularly when selecting only one or two frames. It wins 14 of 16 configurations on ActivityNet Captions, transfers best in zero-shot low-frame settings on MSR-VTT, and incurs only 5.2% extra captioning time versus 65.4% for CSTA and 211.9% for MaxInfo.
AI.conclusion: PEEK is an efficient adaptive frame sampling method for video captioning that achieves state-of-the-art or better captioning performance, especially at very low frame budgets, while adding only minimal inference overhead compared with prior adaptive samplers.

title: Spatio-temporal stochastic graph-based learning for infectious disease forecasting
summary: Spatio-temporal graph-based models have typically been used to forecast new cases of infectious diseases such as COVID-19 and chickenpox outbreaks. However, the use of stochastic modelling into their learning process has been surprisingly under-investigated and rarely considered entire data sets of large countries. As a result, it is unknown whether these models would provide accurate forecasts in real-world disease spread scenarios. In this work, we propose a spatio-temporal stochastic graph-based architecture that integrates a stochastic formulation and uncertainty approximation process to forecast new infectious disease cases. We find that our approach can adapt to encode large and small population geographical networks within a single model architecture. Using two real-world data sets, COVID-19 in the US and chickenpox in Hungary, we report an enhanced effect of the proposed architecture across predictions of the 2022 first wave for COVID-19 in the US and comparative results of chickenpox waves during 2012-2014 in Hungary. By benchmarking with four spatio-temporal graph-based models, quantitative results show competitive overall weekly performance of the proposed approach on forecasting new cases for all 3,218 US counties and all 20 Hungary counties. The proposed approach can represent overall epidemic progression relative to baselines, though with a one-step delay; while exhibiting a reduced sensitivity to high-frequency and low-amplitude variability.

AI.tldr: A stochastic spatio-temporal graph model improves infectious-disease forecasting across both very large and small regional networks, achieving competitive weekly accuracy on US COVID-19 and Hungary chickenpox data, though it tends to lag by one step and smooth out small rapid changes.
AI.motivation: Existing spatio-temporal graph models are widely used for infectious-disease forecasting, but they rarely integrate stochasticity into learning and are seldom evaluated on complete large-country datasets. This leaves uncertainty about whether such models can forecast accurately in realistic, large-scale epidemic spread scenarios.
AI.method: The authors propose a spatio-temporal stochastic graph-based architecture that explicitly incorporates stochastic modeling and an uncertainty approximation process into the learning pipeline for forecasting new infectious disease cases across geographic regions represented as graphs.
AI.result: On real-world datasets for COVID-19 in all 3,218 US counties and chickenpox in all 20 Hungary counties, the proposed model shows competitive overall weekly forecasting performance against four spatio-temporal graph baselines. It performs especially well for the 2022 first COVID-19 wave in the US and yields comparative results for Hungarian chickenpox waves from 2012 to 2014.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that a spatio-temporal stochastic graph-based model can deliver competitive weekly infectious-disease forecasting on both large-scale and small-scale geographic networks, while better capturing overall epidemic progression than several baselines. Its main limitations are a one-step delay in tracking epidemic dynamics and lower sensitivity to high-frequency, low-amplitude fluctuations.

title: Extending AI for Research to the Humanities: A Multi-Agent Framework for Evidence-Grounded Scholarship
