comment: 28 pages, 3 figures. Code, data catalogues, and reproduction scripts: https://github.com/YatingPan/SPIRE. Lead corresponding author: Jun Wang; corresponding author: Qi Su
summary: LLM-based research agents have advanced rapidly in science and engineering, where research is organized around executable experiments, code, and quantitative signals. Humanities scholarship, however, requires a different mode of reasoning: interpretive, evidence-grounded argument over primary sources, where scholarly value depends on faithful quotation, verifiable provenance, and close reading. Existing research agents remain largely optimized for execution and retrieval, not evidence-grounded interpretive reasoning. To address this gap, we introduce SPIRE (Scholarly-Primitives-Inspired Research Engine), a multi-agent framework for evidence-grounded humanities scholarship. Drawing on Scholarly Primitives theory, SPIRE casts recurring humanities operations as cooperating agent roles (source discovery, evidence annotation, comparison, provenance checking, sampling, citation binding, and argumentative synthesis) over a multi-scale close-reading substrate of passages, intra-context graph communities, and cross-context semantic clusters. On a peer-reviewed-paper benchmark over classical Chinese and Greco-Roman Latin scholarship, SPIRE recovers cited primary-source evidence more reliably than Naive LLM, Text RAG, and GraphRAG, and receives higher blind-judge scores on answer accuracy, depth, coverage, and evidence quality. Ablations show that both the scholarly-operation agents and close-reading retrieval contribute to evidence-grounded essays. Code, data catalogues, and reproduction scripts are released at https://github.com/YatingPan/SPIRE.

AI.tldr: SPIRE is a humanities-focused multi-agent research system that organizes LLM reasoning around scholarly operations and close reading, leading to better evidence recovery and stronger evidence-grounded essays than common LLM and RAG baselines.
AI.motivation: Existing LLM-based research agents are optimized for executable, retrieval-heavy scientific workflows, but humanities scholarship requires interpretive reasoning grounded in faithfully quoted primary sources, verifiable provenance, and close reading. The work is motivated by this mismatch and aims to build an agent system better aligned with humanities research practices.
AI.method: The paper proposes SPIRE, a multi-agent framework inspired by Scholarly Primitives theory. It decomposes humanities research into cooperating roles such as source discovery, evidence annotation, comparison, provenance checking, sampling, citation binding, and argumentative synthesis, operating over a multi-scale close-reading substrate that includes passages, intra-context graph communities, and cross-context semantic clusters.
AI.result: On a peer-reviewed benchmark spanning classical Chinese and Greco-Roman Latin scholarship, SPIRE more reliably recovers cited primary-source evidence than Naive LLM, Text RAG, and GraphRAG, and earns higher blind-judge scores for accuracy, depth, coverage, and evidence quality. Ablation studies further show that both the scholarly-operation agents and the close-reading retrieval substrate are important.
AI.conclusion: SPIRE demonstrates that evidence-grounded, multi-agent workflows tailored to humanities scholarship outperform standard LLM, Text RAG, and GraphRAG baselines on primary-source recovery and judged essay quality, with both agentized scholarly operations and close-reading retrieval contributing materially to performance.

title: SlotMemory: Object-Centric KV Memory for Streaming Long-Video Generation
summary: Streaming video generation models typically rely on temporal-centric memory, which organizes historical context as raw frames, chunk segments, or unclustered tokens. This organization frequently leads to identity drift and semantic inconsistency when entities exit the frame or during interactive prompt transitions. To address these limitations, we propose SlotMemory, an object-centric Key-Value memory mechanism for streaming video diffusion. Our approach shifts the memory abstraction from "when" an event occurred to "what" is being represented by decomposing the transformer's key-value manifold into discrete, reusable semantic slots. By utilizing these slots as routing addresses to index and store high-fidelity key-value tokens, we enable entity-level persistence and prompt-aware retrieval across long horizons. Evaluated on 60-second interactive narratives using the Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B backbone, SlotMemory achieves a state-of-the-art quality score of 81.61 and a 22.8 percent relative improvement in dynamic consistency over the strongest existing streaming baseline. Our results demonstrate that structured semantic representation, rather than raw temporal capacity, is the essential primitive for persistent long-form video synthesis. Our codes and checkpoints are available at https://tj12323.github.io/SlotMemory/.

AI.tldr: SlotMemory replaces raw time-based memory with object-centric semantic slots, improving long-form streaming video diffusion by better preserving entity identity and prompt consistency over time.
AI.motivation: Existing streaming video generation methods mostly use temporal-centric memory organized as frames, chunks, or unclustered tokens. This causes identity drift and semantic inconsistency, especially when objects leave the frame or prompts change interactively. The work is motivated by the need for more stable long-term entity persistence and semantic coherence.
AI.method: The paper proposes SlotMemory, an object-centric Key-Value memory mechanism for streaming video diffusion. It decomposes the transformer's key-value space into discrete semantic slots that act as routing addresses, allowing high-fidelity key-value tokens to be stored and retrieved at the entity level in a prompt-aware manner across long time horizons.
AI.result: On 60-second interactive narrative generation with the Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B backbone, SlotMemory achieves a state-of-the-art quality score of 81.61 and improves dynamic consistency by 22.8% relative to the strongest streaming baseline.
AI.conclusion: Structured semantic memory built around reusable object-centric slots is more effective than raw temporal memory capacity for maintaining persistent, coherent long-form streaming video generation.

title: Universal Decision Learners
summary: Many theories of decision making -- planning, reinforcement learning, causal intervention, online learning, and game-theoretic equilibrium -- turn local information into globally coherent behavior. This paper proposes a common categorical formulation: a Universal Decision Learner (UDL) extends a partially specified decision functor from observed contexts to new contexts by a pair of universal constructions. Left Kan extensions express rollout, aggregation, and candidate generation; right Kan extensions express consistency, constraint satisfaction, and fixed-point semantics. The central claim is not that every decision problem has the same algorithm, but that many decision formalisms instantiate the same universal problem: extend local behavioral data canonically, then characterize the globally coherent extensions. We give the abstract UDL construction, prove its universal comparison property, define Kan-invariant behavioral equivalence and minimal abstractions, and show how Bellman equations, planning recursions, causal interventions, online regret, and equilibria arise as special cases. The supplementary material develops the reinforcement-learning specialization in more detail.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a category-theoretic meta-framework for decision making: extend local decision rules with left Kan extensions, then identify globally coherent solutions with right Kan extensions. Many classical formalisms in planning, RL, causality, online learning, and game theory fit this same abstract template.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that multiple decision-making theories such as planning, reinforcement learning, causal intervention, online learning, and game theory all transform local information into globally coherent behavior, but lack a shared high-level mathematical formulation. The paper aims to expose that common structure without claiming a single algorithm for all domains.
AI.method: The method introduces an abstract categorical framework called the Universal Decision Learner. It models observed behavior as a partially specified decision functor over contexts, then uses left Kan extensions for rollout/aggregation/candidate generation and right Kan extensions for consistency/constraint satisfaction/fixed-point characterization. The paper proves a universal comparison property and defines Kan-invariant behavioral equivalence and minimal abstractions.
AI.result: The paper shows that Bellman equations, planning recursions, causal interventions, online regret, and equilibria can all be recovered as special cases of the UDL framework. It also establishes theoretical concepts including universal comparison, behavioral equivalence under Kan invariance, and minimal abstraction.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that many decision-making frameworks can be unified under a categorical Universal Decision Learner (UDL), where local decision information is canonically extended to globally coherent behavior using paired universal constructions, with left and right Kan extensions capturing complementary aspects of decision semantics.

title: EvoGens: A Population-Based Heuristic Search Framework for Scientific Idea Generation
summary: Generating novel research ideas is fundamental to scientific progress. While Large Language Models (LLMs) show promise in assisting this process, existing approaches often exhibit semantic convergence, resulting in limited diversity and novelty. To address this, we introduce EvoGens, an evolution-inspired framework that recasts scientific idea generation as an evolutionary search over a population of ideas. EvoGens iteratively applies rank-based mutation with differentiated retrieval planning to incorporate external knowledge, and semantic-aware crossover to fuse complementary concepts for conceptual reorganization. A lightweight evaluation signal guides the selection process, encouraging sustained exploration while mitigating premature convergence. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EvoGens substantially enhances exploration capabilities compared to state-of-the-art baselines. Specifically, it improves the Novelty from 0.1 to 0.4 and the Diversity from 0.24 to 0.55, while maintaining comparable idea quality under the current automatic evaluation protocol. These findings suggest that evolutionary mechanisms can serve as a useful framework for exploration-oriented research ideation, especially for broadening the novelty and diversity of candidate ideas under a shared automatic evaluation setting.

AI.tldr: EvoGens uses evolutionary operations over idea populations to help LLMs generate more novel and diverse research ideas without hurting overall quality.
AI.motivation: Existing LLM-based research idea generation methods tend to semantically converge, which limits diversity and novelty. The work aims to improve exploration in idea generation.
AI.method: The paper proposes EvoGens, an evolution-inspired framework for scientific idea generation that maintains a population of ideas and iteratively performs rank-based mutation with differentiated retrieval planning, semantic-aware crossover, and lightweight evaluation-guided selection.
AI.result: In extensive experiments, EvoGens outperformed state-of-the-art baselines in exploration metrics, improving Novelty from 0.1 to 0.4 and Diversity from 0.24 to 0.55, while keeping idea quality comparable under the current automatic evaluation protocol.
AI.conclusion: EvoGens shows that framing scientific idea generation as an evolutionary search process can significantly improve novelty and diversity while preserving comparable idea quality under automatic evaluation.

title: GGT-100K: Generative Ground Truth for Generalizable Real-World Image Restoration
summary: Real-world image restoration (IR) is bottlenecked by the scarcity of high-quality paired training data. Synthetic datasets are abundant but often fail to model real-world degradations, while real-world paired datasets are expensive and difficult to capture. As a result, IR models trained on these datasets show limited generalization in real-world scenarios. In this work, we propose Generative Ground Truth (GGT) by using generative multimodal foundation models (MFMs) to produce high-quality (HQ) targets from real-world low-quality (LQ) images. We first conduct a systematic evaluation of nine state-of-the-art MFMs, including Nano-Banana-2 and GPT-Image-2, on images of various scenes and degradation types. The results demonstrate that Nano-Banana-2 with VLM-based adaptive prompting shows the highest capability to synthesize perceptually realistic and content-faithful HQ targets, which can serve as the GGT for the LQ input. We then employ Nano-Banana-2 to build a GGT synthesis pipeline, which involves multi-stage quality control to ensure data reliability, and construct GGT-100K, an LQ-HQ paired dataset comprising 103,707 training pairs and covering diverse scenes and complex real-world degradations. A test set of 500 image pairs is also established. Extensive experiments show that GGT-100K consistently improves the real-world generalization of a wide range of IR models, with particularly strong benefits for finetuning generative models for IR tasks. Our results suggest that MFMs can serve as practical tools for restoration-oriented data generation, and GGT-100K is a useful resource to expand the generalization boundaries of real-world IR models.

AI.tldr: Use a strong multimodal generative model to turn real degraded images into paired training data with generated clean targets; this yields a 100K-scale dataset that materially improves real-world image restoration generalization.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that real-world image restoration suffers from a lack of high-quality paired training data: synthetic data does not adequately reflect real degradations, while real paired data is costly and hard to collect, limiting model generalization.
AI.method: The method systematically evaluates nine state-of-the-art multimodal foundation models for generating high-quality targets from real low-quality images, selects Nano-Banana-2 with VLM-based adaptive prompting as the best performer, and uses it in a multi-stage quality-controlled pipeline to build the GGT-100K paired dataset for training image restoration models.
AI.result: The results show that Nano-Banana-2 produces the most perceptually realistic and content-faithful targets among the tested models, and training or fine-tuning image restoration models on GGT-100K consistently improves their real-world generalization, with especially strong gains for generative restoration models.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that multimodal foundation models, especially Nano-Banana-2 with VLM-based adaptive prompting, can generate reliable high-quality targets from real low-quality images, enabling construction of the GGT-100K dataset and significantly improving real-world generalization of image restoration models.

title: A Context-Aware Middleware for Medical Image Based Reports: An approach based on image feature extraction and association rules
summary: This work proposes a context-aware middleware for medical workflow organization and efficiency improvement. In hospitals, laboratories and teleradiology companies, each physician or technician is specialized in a specific kind of diagnosis or analysis. Therefore, certain types of medical images are often forwarded to a certain physician or a certain group. This forwarding is time consuming. That is, repeatedly deciding who would be the best physician, whether he is available at a certain moment given a certain context is exhaustive and may be very inefficient. Thus, the proposed middleware has the ability to process and collect data from images analyzed by each medical staff. Based on the collected data and current clinical context, the middleware is able to infer who would be the best fit staff to receive a certain incoming medical image.

AI.tldr: Build a context-aware routing system for medical images: it learns from prior case handling and current staff context to automatically send each image to the most suitable available specialist.
AI.motivation: Manual forwarding of medical images to the appropriate specialist in hospitals, laboratories, and teleradiology settings is time consuming, repetitive, and inefficient because staff expertise and moment-to-moment availability must be considered for each case.
AI.method: The paper proposes a context-aware middleware that collects and processes data from medical images previously analyzed by medical staff, models staff specialization and availability, and uses the current clinical context to infer the best-fit recipient for each incoming medical image.
AI.result: The abstract claims that the middleware can infer which physician or technician is the best fit to receive a given incoming medical image, thereby reducing exhaustive manual decision making and improving workflow efficiency.
AI.conclusion: A context-aware middleware can improve the organization and efficiency of medical image workflow by automatically routing incoming cases to the most suitable available physician or technician based on historical performance data and current clinical context.

title: Cognitive Fatigue in Autoregressive Transformers: Formalization and Measurement
comment: 9 pages, 7 figures. Accepted at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2026)
summary: Autoregressive language models frequently degrade during long-horizon generation, producing repetitive text, losing instruction adherence, and exhibiting unstable entropy. Despite the prevalence of these failures, practitioners lack online diagnostics to detect them in real-time as they occur. We formalize this degradation as cognitive fatigue, a measurable generation-time state characterized by decay in attention to the original prompt, representational drift, and entropy miscalibration. We introduce the Fatigue Index (FI), a lightweight, model-agnostic diagnostic that aggregates these three signals under explicit axioms (monotonicity, boundedness, interpretability) enabling reliable runtime monitoring. Across nine models (1B-13B parameters), FI trajectories exhibit structured temporal dynamics, predict task degradation (AUROC = 0.95) and repetition (Spearman rho = 0.94), and reveal non-monotonic scaling behavior: instruction-tuned models below 3B exhibit faster collapse than base models, with this trend reversing at 7B. Stress analyses further show that FI onset accelerates under longer contexts, middle-positioned evidence, and reduced numerical precision. These results establish cognitive fatigue as a coherent and measurable phenomenon, and position FI as a principled tool for runtime reliability monitoring in production LLM systems.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the Fatigue Index (FI), a lightweight runtime metric for detecting long-generation failure in language models. FI combines prompt-attention decay, representational drift, and entropy miscalibration, and strongly predicts degradation and repetition across models.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that autoregressive language models often fail during long-horizon generation by becoming repetitive, drifting away from instructions, and showing unstable entropy, yet practitioners lack online diagnostics that can detect these failures in real time as generation unfolds.
AI.method: The authors define cognitive fatigue using three generation-time signals: decay in attention to the original prompt, representational drift, and entropy miscalibration. They then design the Fatigue Index (FI) to aggregate these signals under explicit axioms such as monotonicity, boundedness, and interpretability, and evaluate FI across nine language models ranging from 1B to 13B parameters under multiple stress conditions.
AI.result: FI shows strong predictive power for generation failures: it predicts task degradation with AUROC = 0.95 and repetition with Spearman rho = 0.94. The experiments also uncover non-monotonic scaling behavior, where instruction-tuned models below 3B collapse faster than base models, while the trend reverses at 7B. In addition, fatigue emerges faster with longer contexts, middle-positioned evidence, and reduced numerical precision.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that long-horizon generation degradation in autoregressive language models can be formalized as a measurable runtime state called cognitive fatigue, and that the proposed Fatigue Index (FI) provides a principled, lightweight, and model-agnostic way to monitor this degradation reliably in production.

title: Does Visual Information Play a Decisive Role in Vision-Language-Action Model Driving Behavior?
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated promising capability in autonomous driving, highlighting the potential of unified multimodal architectures for jointly modeling perception and planning. However, how current VLA-based driving behavior is grounded in visual information remains poorly understood. Existing evaluation protocols mainly focus on aggregate performance metrics, lacking structured and practical diagnostics to quantify visual-behavior dependency. In this work, we introduce a structured multi-level visual perturbation framework to analyze visual-behavior dependency in VLA-based driving models systematically. The framework organizes controlled visual perturbations along three complementary dimensions: channellevel degradation, information-level disruption, and structurelevel modification. We apply it to VLA-based driving systems and evaluate behavioral responses under both open-loop trajectory prediction and interactive closed-loop safety evaluation. Experimental results reveal evaluation-dependent dependency patterns and uneven visual grounding across abstraction levels. These findings call for more structured analyses and principled design of VLA driving models to better understand how visual information shapes behavior and develop safer, more robust systems.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a structured perturbation-based evaluation framework to test how much VLA driving models depend on visual input. By perturbing visuals at channel, information, and structural levels and testing in open- and closed-loop settings, it finds that visual grounding is uneven and evaluation-dependent, motivating safer and more principled VLA model design.
AI.motivation: Current VLA models for autonomous driving show strong multimodal capability, but it remains unclear how their behavior is actually grounded in visual input. Existing evaluations focus mostly on aggregate metrics and do not provide practical, structured diagnostics for measuring how much behavior depends on visual information.
AI.method: The authors propose a structured multi-level visual perturbation framework to systematically probe visual-behavior dependency in VLA driving models. The framework applies controlled perturbations along three dimensions: channel-level degradation, information-level disruption, and structure-level modification, and evaluates model responses in both open-loop trajectory prediction and closed-loop interactive safety settings.
AI.result: Experiments show that visual-behavior dependency patterns vary across evaluation settings and are not uniform across different levels of visual abstraction. This indicates that current VLA driving systems may rely on visual cues in inconsistent ways, exposing gaps in our understanding of their perception-planning integration.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that VLA-based driving models exhibit uneven and evaluation-dependent visual grounding: their driving behavior relies on visual information differently across perturbation types and abstraction levels. Therefore, structured diagnostics are necessary to better understand, design, and improve the safety and robustness of VLA driving systems.

title: Diversity Matters: Revisiting Test-Time Compute in Vision-Language Models
summary: Test-time compute (TTC) strategies have emerged as a lightweight approach to boost reasoning in large language models (LLMs). However, their application and benefits for vision-language models (VLMs) remain underexplored. We present a systematic study of TTC across seven VLMs and six benchmarks, specifically analyzing feature-based scoring and majority voting methods. We find that feature heuristics fail and voting yields only modest gains in single-model settings. We theoretically show that this limitation stems from a lack of prediction diversity: when outputs are highly correlated, voting provides little benefit. In contrast, multi-model ensembles offer richer diversity, yet standard majority voting fails to account for varying model capabilities. To address this, we propose Entropy-based TTC (ETTC), which selects the most confident prediction based on predictive entropy. Our method reduces to majority voting in the single-model case, but in model ensembles, it leverages confidence disparities to prioritize stronger models. We prove that ETTC outperforms majority voting under mild assumptions and empirically demonstrate that it consistently surpasses both voting and the best individual model. Crucially, our results show that smaller models can synergistically enhance larger ones, unlocking ensembling gains not achievable with standard strategies.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that standard test-time compute methods bring limited benefits to single vision-language models because their outputs lack diversity. It introduces ETTC, an entropy-based ensemble strategy that uses model confidence to choose better predictions and consistently beats majority voting and the strongest individual model.
AI.motivation: Although test-time compute has improved reasoning in large language models, its utility for vision-language models is unclear. The paper aims to understand why existing TTC methods provide limited gains for VLMs and to design a better strategy for multi-model settings.
AI.method: The paper conducts a systematic evaluation of test-time compute strategies across seven vision-language models and six benchmarks, focusing on feature-based scoring and majority voting. It then proposes Entropy-based TTC (ETTC), which selects predictions using predictive entropy, and provides theoretical and empirical comparisons against majority voting and individual models.
AI.result: Feature-based heuristics do not work well, and majority voting gives only limited improvements for single VLMs because correlated outputs reduce the benefit of voting. ETTC consistently outperforms standard voting and the best single model in ensemble settings under mild assumptions and in experiments.
AI.conclusion: ETTC is a more effective test-time compute strategy for vision-language models than standard majority voting, especially in multi-model ensembles where prediction diversity and confidence differences can be exploited. Smaller models can also complement stronger models and improve ensemble performance.

title: MoG: Mixture of Experts for Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: Retrieval-augmented generation is intensively studied to ground large language models on external evidence. However, retrieving from a unified knowledge base could inevitably introduce irrelevant information that may mislead generation for complex reasoning. Inspired by the conditional computation of mixture of experts (MoE), where a router sparsely selects specialized experts alongside shared ones for each input, we propose \textbf{M}ixture \textbf{o}f experts for \textbf{G}raph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation, i.e., \textbf{MoG}. It organizes knowledge into two core components: (i) diverse, always-accessible hub graphs that encode semantically and structurally central knowledge and provide contextual clues for expert activation, and (ii) sparsely activated expert graphs that contain domain-specific evidence. MoG first accesses hub graphs to identify general evidence and derive contextual clues. Then, a topology-aware router dynamically activates a limited set of expert graphs conditioned on the query, thereby confining retrieval to a focused evidence subspace. Extensive experiments on challenging benchmarks show that MoG consistently outperforms strong baselines, with over 20\% relative improvement on MuSiQue. Our code is available in https://github.com/DEEP-PolyU/MoG.

AI.tldr: MoG is a graph-based MoE-style RAG system that uses hub graphs plus selectively activated expert graphs to reduce noisy retrieval and substantially improve multi-hop reasoning.
AI.motivation: Standard RAG over a unified knowledge base often retrieves irrelevant information, which can mislead generation in complex reasoning tasks. The work aims to make retrieval more selective and context-aware.
AI.method: The paper proposes MoG, a graph-based RAG framework inspired by mixture-of-experts. It first retrieves from always-accessible hub graphs to gather general evidence and routing clues, then uses a topology-aware router to activate a small set of domain-specific expert graphs for focused retrieval.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on challenging benchmarks show consistent gains over strong baselines, including more than 20% relative improvement on MuSiQue.
AI.conclusion: MoG improves retrieval-augmented generation by organizing knowledge into hub graphs and sparsely activated expert graphs, reducing irrelevant evidence and improving complex reasoning performance.

title: Rethinking Efficient Crack Segmentation with Task-Aligned Structural-Directional Modeling
summary: Recent crack segmentation methods often follow generic semantic segmentation designs, using stronger backbones, hybrid CNN-Transformer-Mamba encoders, and auxiliary enhancement branches. Although effective, this raises whether stronger generic feature mixing is the most suitable direction for crack segmentation. We instead formulate crack segmentation as sparse structural recovery. Cracks have limited category-level semantics but strong morphological regularities, being thin, sparse, anisotropic, locally fragmented, and easily confused with textures or shadows. Thus, the key bottleneck lies in preserving weak structural evidence, recovering directional continuity, and suppressing background coupling. We propose RIFT, a compact family of morphology-aligned crack segmentation models. Rather than compressing a complex generic architecture, RIFT is simple by design, preserving local evidence, aggregating cooperative directional continuity, and restoring crack structures through lightweight multi-scale fusion. Experiments on four public benchmarks show that RIFT achieves the best or tied-best results across the 16 main metrics against reproduced representative baselines. RIFT-B gives the strongest overall accuracy, while RIFT-T provides the best deployment efficiency with only 0.47M parameters and high inference speed. Topology-aware evaluation, ablations, transfer experiments, and visualizations further verify that task-aligned simplicity can match or surpass complex hybrid architectures when its inductive bias fits crack morphology. Code: https://github.com/xauat-liushipeng/RIFT

AI.tldr: RIFT reframes crack segmentation as morphology-driven sparse structural recovery and uses a simple, lightweight architecture to preserve local crack evidence and directional continuity. It achieves state-of-the-art or tied state-of-the-art results on four benchmarks, with both strong accuracy and very high efficiency.
AI.motivation: Existing crack segmentation methods largely inherit generic semantic segmentation designs with stronger backbones and hybrid encoders, but cracks have limited semantic content and strong morphological structure. The authors argue the main challenge is recovering thin, sparse, anisotropic, fragmented crack structures while suppressing confusing background textures and shadows.
AI.method: The paper proposes RIFT, a lightweight family of crack segmentation models that treats crack segmentation as sparse structural recovery. It preserves weak local evidence, aggregates cooperative directional continuity, and restores crack structures through lightweight multi-scale fusion instead of relying on heavy generic feature-mixing backbones.
AI.result: Across four public benchmarks, RIFT achieves the best or tied-best performance on the 16 main metrics versus reproduced representative baselines. RIFT-B delivers the strongest overall accuracy, while RIFT-T offers the best deployment efficiency with only 0.47M parameters and high inference speed. Additional topology-aware evaluation, ablations, transfer experiments, and visualizations support the approach.
AI.conclusion: RIFT demonstrates that a compact, morphology-aligned design can match or outperform more complex generic/hybrid segmentation architectures for crack segmentation when the inductive bias is tailored to crack morphology.

title: When are LLMs Sufficient Policy Optimizers for Sequential RL Tasks?
summary: We study when large language models (LLMs) can serve as effective black-box policy optimizers for reinforcement learning (RL) tasks, i.e., when can we replace classical RL algorithms with an LLM? We explore this question by introducing Prompted Policy Optimization (PromptPO), an iterative method that prompts an LLM with Python descriptions of the state space, action space, and reward function, then has it generate and refine executable policies based on rollout feedback. Across hard exploration environments, Meta-World robotics tasks, and several real-world control problems, PromptPO often matches or exceeds the performance of standard RL baselines while using substantially fewer environment interactions. To maximize expected return, and without further explicit prompting, the policies PromptPO outputs range from tuned proportional controllers or rule-based plans to policies that run planning algorithms like value iteration. Our results demonstrate that LLM-based policy optimization is sufficient when the LLM can leverage prior knowledge about the environment or optimization strategy. PromptPO underperforms standard RL baselines in MuJoCo domains. This demonstrates possible limitations of LLM-based policy optimization to settings that requiring fine-grained continuous control.

AI.tldr: PromptPO uses an LLM to iteratively write and improve executable RL policies from environment descriptions and rollout feedback. It is sample-efficient and competitive in several discrete or structured control settings, but struggles on fine-grained continuous-control benchmarks like MuJoCo.
AI.motivation: The paper investigates when classical RL algorithms can be replaced by an LLM used as a black-box policy optimizer, aiming to understand whether LLM priors and code-generation abilities can improve policy search with fewer environment interactions.
AI.method: The paper proposes Prompted Policy Optimization (PromptPO), an iterative framework that prompts an LLM with Python-form descriptions of state space, action space, and reward function, then repeatedly asks it to generate and refine executable policies using rollout feedback from the environment.
AI.result: PromptPO often matches or outperforms standard RL baselines in hard exploration tasks, Meta-World robotics, and several real-world control problems while using substantially fewer interactions. The generated policies include proportional controllers, rule-based strategies, and even planning procedures like value iteration. However, it underperforms standard RL methods in MuJoCo continuous-control tasks.
AI.conclusion: LLMs can function as effective black-box policy optimizers in some RL settings when they can exploit prior knowledge or optimization heuristics, but they are limited in domains requiring fine-grained continuous control such as MuJoCo.

title: TRACE: Discovering Task-Specific Parameter via Adaptation-Aware Probing for Continual Fine-Tuning
summary: In real-world deployment, LLMs are often adapted continually across tasks to keep LLMs up-to-date in production, where new fine-tuning should preserve previously learned skills. However, indiscriminately mixing tasks can dilute task specialization, while sequential fine-tuning (full-parameter or low rank adaptation) often causes catastrophic forgetting due to destructive overwriting. Replay-based continual tuning and maintaining separate task-specific adapters can mitigate forgetting, but introduce additional compute, storage, and management overhead. Recognizing the redundancy of LLM parameters for any single task, we reframe continual task adaptation as task-specific parameter discovery via adaptation-aware probing: a short warm-start probe exposes a task's adaptation trace, enabling us to identify and isolate the small subset of parameters essential for each task to mitigate catastrophic forgetting. Building on this view, we introduce TRACE, a novel approach for discovering Task-specific paRameters via Adaptation-aware probing for Continual finE-tuning. We perform a short warm-start fine-tune to derive task-specific core parameters by comparing the warm-started and pre-trained models. Core parameters are identified via two strategies: importance scoring (L$_2$ norm and Fisher Information) and specificity analysis (cosine similarity of parameter updates). In continual fine-tuning settings, only the active task's core parameters are updated while others remain frozen, preserving prior knowledge. We conduct extensive experiments across multiple standard benchmarks to demonstrate the superior performance of our proposed method. Additionally, we validate the generalization of our method through a cross-model and scale transferability study, demonstrating a "small-to-large" paradigm that guides the fine-tuning of large-scale models under resource constraints.

AI.tldr: TRACE先用短暂探测找出每个任务真正需要更新的小部分参数，随后在持续微调中只改这些参数，以更低开销减轻灾难性遗忘，并且这种参数发现还能迁移到更大模型。 / TRACE briefly probes each task to find the small subset of parameters that really matter, then updates only those during continual fine-tuning to reduce forgetting with lower overhead; the discovered adaptation pattern also transfers to larger models.
AI.motivation: 现实部署中的LLM需要持续适配新任务，但混合训练会削弱任务专门化，顺序微调又容易因参数覆盖导致灾难性遗忘；重放方法和独立适配器虽能缓解，但带来额外计算、存储和管理成本。作者因此将持续任务适配重构为任务特定参数发现问题。 / In real-world deployment, LLMs must be continually adapted to new tasks, but mixed-task tuning dilutes specialization and sequential fine-tuning causes catastrophic forgetting through destructive overwriting; replay and separate adapters help but add compute, storage, and management overhead. The paper therefore reframes continual adaptation as task-specific parameter discovery.
AI.method: 方法先进行一次短暂的warm-start微调，将warm-start后的模型与预训练模型对比以发现任务核心参数；核心参数通过两类策略识别：重要性评分（L2范数、Fisher Information）与特异性分析（参数更新的余弦相似度）。在持续微调时，仅更新当前任务的核心参数，其余参数冻结。 / The method performs a short warm-start fine-tuning phase, compares the warm-started model against the pretrained model to discover task-core parameters, identifies them using importance scoring (L2 norm, Fisher Information) and specificity analysis (cosine similarity of parameter updates), and then updates only the active task's core parameters while freezing the rest.
AI.result: 在多个标准基准上的大量实验表明，该方法优于对比方法；同时，跨模型与跨尺度实验验证了其泛化能力，并展示了可由小模型发现参数模式来指导大模型微调的‘small-to-large’范式。 / Extensive experiments on multiple standard benchmarks show superior performance over baselines. Cross-model and cross-scale studies further validate generalization and demonstrate a small-to-large paradigm for guiding large-model fine-tuning.
AI.conclusion: TRACE通过适应感知探测识别并隔离每个任务的核心参数，在持续微调中只更新当前任务的核心参数，从而有效缓解灾难性遗忘，并在资源受限场景下具备跨模型、跨尺度迁移潜力。 / TRACE identifies and isolates task-specific core parameters via adaptation-aware probing, updates only those parameters during continual fine-tuning, effectively mitigates catastrophic forgetting, and shows transferability across models and scales under resource constraints.

title: LVSA: Training-Free Sparse Attention for Long Video Diffusion
summary: Dense self-attention is the compute and quality bottleneck of long-video diffusion inference: cost grows quadratically with the sequence length, and beyond the training horizon the model converges to near-static output, that is, "frozen" repetitive video. State of the art approaches are either too costly, e.g., they require retraining, or fail to satisfy both performance and quality objectives in a scalable manner. To this end, we introduce Long Video Sparse Attention (LVSA), a training-free model-agnostic block-sparse attention for video diffusion transformers that combines a structured window pattern with rotating global anchors, thus removing the fixed-grid bias which causes long-range temporal artifacts. LVSA, combined with a FlashInfer kernel, reduces compute up to 3.17x on Wan 2.1 1.3B at a 6x horizon, 2.98x on Wan 2.1 14B at a 6x horizon, and 3.33x on HunyuanVideo 1.5 at a 1.5x horizon, compared to dense attention. Beyond reducing compute, LVSA enables HunyuanVideo 1.5 generation at a 2x horizon, which is otherwise out-of-memory on a single GPU. Moreover, LVSA provides speedups up to 2.41x compared to RIFLEx and 3.27x compared to UltraViCo on Wan 2.1 1.3B. To demonstrate applicability across diverse platforms, we apply LVSA on NPUs and achieve speedups up to 2.71x on Wan 2.2 A14B and 3.24x on Wan 2.1 1.3B compared to dense attention. To evaluate quality in a fair way, we introduce VQeval, a tool properly scoring loopy video failures, which instead are rewarded in state of the art evaluators like VBench-Long. LVSA is quality-neutral for generation at training horizon length and quality-positive at extended lengths.

AI.tldr: LVSA replaces dense attention in long-video diffusion with a training-free sparse pattern using local windows plus rotating global anchors, cutting compute and memory substantially while avoiding long-range artifacts and preserving or improving video quality at extended lengths.
AI.motivation: Dense self-attention is the main compute and quality bottleneck for long-video diffusion: its quadratic cost is expensive, and extending beyond the training horizon often produces frozen, repetitive videos. Existing methods are either too costly or do not balance scalability, speed, and quality well.
AI.method: The paper proposes Long Video Sparse Attention (LVSA), a block-sparse attention pattern combining structured local windows with rotating global anchors, implemented with a FlashInfer kernel and applied without retraining to video diffusion transformers.
AI.result: LVSA achieves up to 3.17x speedup on Wan 2.1 1.3B at 6x horizon, 2.98x on Wan 2.1 14B at 6x horizon, and 3.33x on HunyuanVideo 1.5 at 1.5x horizon versus dense attention; it also enables 2x-horizon HunyuanVideo generation on a single GPU where dense attention runs out of memory, outperforms RIFLEx and UltraViCo in speed, works on NPUs, and is quality-neutral at training horizon and quality-positive at longer horizons.
AI.conclusion: LVSA is a training-free, model-agnostic sparse attention method that reduces long-video diffusion inference cost while maintaining or improving quality, especially beyond the training horizon.

title: Kalimati Vegetable Price Index Forecasting with a Momentum Corrected Online Stacking Ensemble
summary: Forecasting agricultural commodity prices in emerging economies is difficult due to high volatility, frequent supply disruptions, and strong cultural influences on demand. This study introduces the Kalimati Vegetable Price Index (KVPI), a new inverse-volatility weighted composite index that aggregates 135 daily wholesale commodities from Kathmandu over ten years (2013-2023). By creating a stable macro-level signal, the KVPI reduces the noise inherent in modelling individual crops. A rich set of 64 causally valid features was developed, including festival lead-lag effects, rolling statistics, and calendar variables. Fourteen forecasting models spanning statistical, tree-based, deep learning, hybrid, and transformer architectures were rigorously evaluated across short (7-day), medium (14- and 30-day), and long-term (90-day) horizons. Tree-based ensembles proved notably robust, while classical statistical models and complex transformers struggled with the noisy dataset. The proposed Momentum-Corrected Online Stacking Ensemble achieved the strongest performance, yielding a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 1.771, an exceptionally low Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 0.68%, and explaining 84.5% of the variance (R-squared = 0.845) at the 90-day horizon. This open-source pipeline provides policymakers and supply chain actors in Nepal and similar markets with a practical, reliable tool for anticipating price movements and strengthening food security.

AI.tldr: The paper creates a stable vegetable price index for Kathmandu and shows that a momentum-corrected online stacking ensemble forecasts it better than 14 competing models, especially at 90 days, making it a practical open-source tool for price planning in emerging markets.
AI.motivation: Agricultural commodity price forecasting in emerging economies is difficult because prices are highly volatile, supply disruptions are frequent, and culturally driven demand patterns add noise. Modeling individual crops is especially unstable, so the paper is motivated by the need for a more robust aggregate signal and a practical forecasting tool for Nepal-like markets.
AI.method: The study builds the Kalimati Vegetable Price Index (KVPI), an inverse-volatility weighted composite index from 135 daily wholesale vegetable commodity series in Kathmandu from 2013 to 2023. It engineers 64 causally valid features, including festival lead-lag variables, rolling statistics, and calendar effects, then evaluates 14 forecasting models across 7-, 14-, 30-, and 90-day horizons, covering statistical, tree-based, deep learning, hybrid, and transformer approaches. A Momentum-Corrected Online Stacking Ensemble is proposed as the final model.
AI.result: The main results are that tree-based ensemble models are robust on this noisy dataset, while classical statistical models and transformer-based models underperform. The proposed Momentum-Corrected Online Stacking Ensemble achieves the strongest 90-day forecast with RMSE 1.771, MAPE 0.68%, and R-squared 0.845, explaining 84.5% of the variance.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that constructing a macro-level vegetable price index and forecasting it with an online stacking ensemble is more reliable than modeling individual commodity prices in a noisy emerging-market setting. The proposed Momentum-Corrected Online Stacking Ensemble delivers the best long-horizon performance and offers practical value for policy and supply-chain planning.

title: How Much Do LLMs Know About Chinese Zero Pronouns?
summary: Zero Pronouns (ZPs) are a pervasive linguistic phenomenon in pro-drop languages such as Chinese and have long posed a challenge for natural language processing systems. Although Large Language Models (LLMs) perform well on many Chinese language tasks, their ability to process ZPs remains poorly understood. We conduct a systematic investigation of LLMs' handling of Chinese ZPs through a sequence of linguistically motivated tasks, including identification, referentiality classification, referential type classification, resolution, and translation. A diverse set of LLMs is evaluated across all tasks. Our results show that Chinese ZPs remain highly challenging for current LLMs, particularly for upstream tasks such as identification and referentiality classification. Performance on downstream tasks, such as ZP translation, is also consistently low: even state-of-the-art reasoning-oriented LLMs correctly translate fewer than half of Chinese ZPs into English.

AI.tldr: 这篇论文系统测试了大语言模型处理中文零代词的能力，结论是：从识别到翻译，各环节都难，最先进模型也远未解决问题。 This paper systematically tests LLMs on Chinese zero pronouns and finds that the problem remains unsolved across the pipeline, from identification to translation, even for top models.
AI.motivation: 中文等省略主语语言中的零代词普遍存在，并长期给自然语言处理带来挑战；尽管大语言模型在许多中文任务上表现良好，但其对零代词的处理能力仍缺乏系统认识，因此需要专门研究。 Zero pronouns are pervasive in pro-drop languages like Chinese and have long challenged NLP; although LLMs perform well on many Chinese tasks, their capability on zero pronouns remains insufficiently understood, motivating a focused study.
AI.method: 论文设计了一组具有语言学动机的连续任务来系统评估多种大语言模型对中文零代词的处理能力，这些任务包括零代词识别、指代性分类、指代类型分类、消解和翻译。 The paper systematically evaluates a diverse set of LLMs on a sequence of linguistically motivated tasks for Chinese zero pronouns, including identification, referentiality classification, referential type classification, resolution, and translation.
AI.result: 实验发现，中文零代词对现有大语言模型仍然是高度困难的问题。上游任务表现尤其薄弱，下游任务如零代词翻译也持续低迷，整体显示模型尚未可靠掌握该现象。 The experiments show that Chinese zero pronouns remain highly challenging for current LLMs. Upstream tasks are particularly weak, and downstream tasks such as translation also remain poor, indicating that models have not yet mastered this phenomenon reliably.
AI.conclusion: 当前大语言模型对中文零代词的处理能力仍然明显不足，尤其在识别与指代性判断等上游任务上表现较弱；即使是面向推理的先进模型，在将中文零代词正确翻译为英文时，准确率也不到一半。 Current LLMs still perform poorly on Chinese zero pronouns, especially on upstream tasks such as identification and referentiality classification; even advanced reasoning-oriented models correctly translate fewer than half of Chinese zero pronouns into English.

title: HQ-JEPA: Hybrid Quantum Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Cross-Modal Remote Sensing Representation Learning
summary: We introduce HQ-JEPA, a hybrid quantum-classical joint-embedding predictive architecture for cross-modal remote sensing representation learning. The proposed framework extends JEPA-style masked latent prediction to paired Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery by predicting masked target representations from visible context regions while aligning heterogeneous modality features in a shared embedding space. To improve representation quality, HQ-JEPA combines four complementary objectives: latent token prediction, cross-modal token alignment, SIGReg-based Gaussian regularization in the fused latent space, and a differentiable SWAP-test-based Fidelity Quantum Similarity (FQS) loss. Unlike pixel reconstruction methods, HQ-JEPA learns semantic representations directly in latent space and uses quantum state-overlap-based similarity as an additional regularization signal. We evaluate the pretrained encoder on GeoBench classification and segmentation tasks under linear probing and fine-tuning settings. Results show that HQ-JEPA achieves competitive and often superior performance over strong self-supervised and remote sensing foundation-model baselines, demonstrating the benefit of integrating predictive self-supervision, cross-modal geometric regularization, and quantum fidelity-based representation learning for remote sensing applications.

AI.tldr: HQ-JEPA is a hybrid quantum-classical JEPA for Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 representation learning. It predicts masked latent features instead of reconstructing pixels, aligns the two modalities in a shared space, and adds SIGReg plus a quantum fidelity similarity loss. This combination improves downstream remote sensing classification and segmentation performance on GeoBench.
AI.motivation: The work is motivated by the need for better cross-modal remote sensing representations that capture semantic structure without relying on pixel-level reconstruction. Existing methods may underutilize complementary information across heterogeneous modalities or lack effective regularization of latent geometry. The authors aim to improve semantic representation learning by integrating predictive self-supervision, cross-modal alignment, and quantum-inspired similarity regularization.
AI.method: The paper proposes HQ-JEPA, a hybrid quantum-classical joint-embedding predictive architecture for cross-modal remote sensing. It predicts masked latent target tokens from visible context regions in paired Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery, while learning a shared embedding space across modalities. Training uses four objectives: latent token prediction, cross-modal token alignment, SIGReg-based Gaussian regularization on fused latent features, and a differentiable SWAP-test-based Fidelity Quantum Similarity loss.
AI.result: On GeoBench classification and segmentation benchmarks, using both linear probing and fine-tuning evaluations, HQ-JEPA achieves competitive and often superior performance relative to strong self-supervised learning methods and remote sensing foundation-model baselines.
AI.conclusion: HQ-JEPA demonstrates that combining JEPA-style latent prediction, cross-modal alignment, SIGReg Gaussian regularization, and a quantum fidelity-based similarity loss can produce strong semantic representations for paired Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 remote sensing data, achieving competitive or better downstream performance on GeoBench classification and segmentation tasks.

title: Self-Certifying Transport MCMC via Dual Spectral-Gap Certificates
comment: 35 pages, 3 figures, 9 tables. Submitted to JASA
summary: We propose CerT-MCMC, a framework that equips learned-transport Markov chain Monte Carlo with automatic, rigorous convergence certificates. A normalising flow maps a Gaussian reference to an approximation of the target posterior; the same flow then serves as both the independence Metropolis-Hastings proposal and the basis for a computable spectral-gap bound. We develop two complementary certificates. The covering certificate bounds the weight-ratio oscillation over the full proposal support via finite-sample covering arguments, yielding full-support spectral-gap bounds when a conservative gradient bound is available; its correction term scales as O(n^{-1/D}), making it rapidly weak and eventually vacuous as dimension increases. We prove a matching Omega(n^{-1/D}) lower bound, establishing that this barrier is intrinsic to pointwise Lipschitz certification. The quantile-core certificate restricts attention to a high-probability residual core on which the oscillation is controlled by one-dimensional empirical quantiles, with a finite-sample probability slack of O(n^{-1/2}), independent of the ambient dimension. On synthetic targets (D=2-20), structural-engineering posteriors (D=6,8), real-data logistic regression on the Heart Disease data set (D=13), and synthetic Bayesian logistic regression (D=20), the quantile-core certificate delivers non-vacuous spectral-gap bounds where the covering certificate is vacuous, and its spectral-gap proxy tracks empirical effective sample sizes within 7%. A negative control experiment confirms that the certificate discriminates flow quality by a factor exceeding 10x, whereas acceptance rates differ by only 1.15x. To our knowledge, the dual-certificate framework is the first to provide automatic, dimension-aware convergence certificates for learned-transport MCMC, distinguishing genuine transport failure from proof-technique limitations.

AI.tldr: CerT-MCMC turns a learned normalizing flow into both an MCMC proposal and a rigorous convergence certificate. It introduces a full-support certificate that suffers from the curse of dimensionality and a quantile-core certificate that avoids this dependence and works well in practice. The latter provides useful, non-vacuous spectral-gap bounds and better diagnoses transport quality than acceptance rate alone.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that learned-transport MCMC methods can be empirically effective, but they generally lack automatic and rigorous convergence guarantees. Existing certification based on pointwise global control becomes weak or vacuous in higher dimensions, so the paper seeks a dimension-aware certification framework that can separate true transport failure from limitations of the proof technique.
AI.method: The method uses a normalizing flow to approximate the target posterior from a Gaussian reference. The same flow is used both as an independence Metropolis-Hastings proposal and to derive computable spectral-gap bounds. Two certification strategies are introduced: (1) a covering certificate based on finite-sample covering arguments and gradient/Lipschitz control over the full support, and (2) a quantile-core certificate that restricts certification to a high-probability residual core using one-dimensional empirical quantiles.
AI.result: The main results are: the covering certificate has a correction term scaling as O(n^{-1/D}) and the paper proves a matching Omega(n^{-1/D}) lower bound, showing this dimensional barrier is intrinsic to pointwise Lipschitz certification. The quantile-core certificate achieves finite-sample probability slack of O(n^{-1/2}) independent of dimension. Empirically, on synthetic and real-data tasks up to D=20, the quantile-core certificate gives non-vacuous spectral-gap bounds where the covering certificate fails, and its proxy tracks empirical ESS within 7%. A negative-control experiment shows it distinguishes flow quality by more than 10x, while acceptance rates differ by only 1.15x.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that CerT-MCMC can provide automatic and rigorous convergence certificates for learned-transport MCMC through two complementary certificates: a full-support covering certificate and a dimension-robust quantile-core certificate. The quantile-core approach remains non-vacuous in moderate dimensions and better reflects practical sampler quality.

title: Combinatorial Synthesis: Scaling Code RLVR via Atomic Decomposition and Recombination
summary: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has recently emerged as the cornerstone for shaping the remarkable coding abilities of Large Language Models (LLMs). However, the scalability of RLVR is severely constrained by the scarcity of sufficiently challenging verifiable code tasks that target near the model's edge of competence. Prior studies often rely on heuristic seed expansions for data synthesis, which severely limits both novelty and difficulty. Consequently, the training value of such data fails to scale proportionally with the size of its synthesis. To this end, we propose Atomic Decomposition and Recombination (ADR), a novel framework that generates verifiable code tasks via decomposition into atomic elements and controlled recombination, thereby enabling the generation of genuinely novel and challenging verifiable code tasks. Experiments and analysis demonstrate that ADR achieves superior originality, difficulty, diversity, and test quality over existing baselines, and consistently delivers greater improvements in code ability across RLVR in diverse downstream domains, including algorithmic programming, tool usage, and data science. Our work sheds light on a new paradigm for novel code task synthesis and scalable RLVR training.

AI.tldr: ADR is a new framework for generating harder and more novel verifiable coding tasks for RLVR by decomposing tasks into atomic parts and recombining them, leading to better synthetic data and stronger LLM coding performance.
AI.motivation: Existing RLVR data synthesis depends heavily on heuristic seed expansion, which limits novelty and difficulty, making it hard to create tasks near the model’s competence boundary and constraining scalability.
AI.method: The paper proposes Atomic Decomposition and Recombination (ADR), which breaks code tasks into atomic elements and then recombines them in a controlled manner to generate new verifiable code tasks.
AI.result: Experiments show ADR outperforms prior baselines in originality, difficulty, diversity, and test quality, and yields stronger RLVR gains across algorithmic programming, tool use, and data science.
AI.conclusion: ADR offers a scalable way to synthesize novel, challenging, and verifiable code tasks, improving RLVR training effectiveness and downstream coding ability.

title: Towards Effective Long-Video Event Prediction via Multi-Level Event Semantics Mining
summary: Accurately predicting future events is fundamental to content understanding and decision-making across various domains. While prior research has primarily focused on text or short-video scenarios, long-video event prediction, characterized by vast multimodal context and more complex narratives, remains underexplored. Meanwhile, although recent Long-Video Language Models (LVLMs), built on Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs), have shown promise in long-video question answering and summarization, they struggle to generalize to event prediction, as they can neither precisely extract event-related details nor perform fine-grained analysis of event development. To address this gap, we propose VISTA, a multi-level event semantics mining framework for long-video event prediction. Initially, VISTA applies a character-centric visual prompt to precisely extract event-related visual details, enhancing detail-level semantics; subsequently, it employs a knowledge-enhanced iterative retrieval strategy, guiding the LLM to progressively construct logically coherent event chains, thereby improving event-level narratives; ultimately, VISTA adopts a human-like propose-then-retrieve strategy to generate diverse future-oriented proposals and integrate multi-level clues, producing robust and accurate predictions. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets validate the effectiveness of VISTA for long-video event prediction.

AI.tldr: VISTA is a new framework for predicting future events in long videos. It extracts fine visual details, builds coherent event chains with iterative retrieval, and combines future-oriented proposals with multi-level clues, leading to stronger prediction performance on real-world datasets.
AI.motivation: Existing work mainly studies event prediction in text or short videos, while long-video event prediction is harder due to richer multimodal context and more complex narratives. Current LVLMs perform well on QA and summarization but are not well suited for precise event detail extraction or fine-grained event development analysis.
AI.method: The paper proposes VISTA, a multi-level event semantics mining framework. It first uses a character-centric visual prompt to extract event-related visual details, then applies a knowledge-enhanced iterative retrieval strategy to build coherent event chains, and finally adopts a propose-then-retrieve strategy to generate future-oriented hypotheses and integrate multi-level clues for prediction.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on real-world datasets show that VISTA is effective for long-video event prediction and outperforms existing approaches in producing robust and accurate future event predictions.
AI.conclusion: VISTA effectively improves long-video event prediction by mining multi-level event semantics, combining precise visual detail extraction, iterative event-chain construction, and future-oriented proposal retrieval to produce more robust and accurate predictions.

title: AdaptR1: Reinforcement Learning Based Adaptive Interleaved Thinking in Multi-hop Question Answering
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable performance in complex reasoning tasks through Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting. However, this approach often leads to ``over-thinking,'' where models generate unnecessarily long reasoning traces for simple queries and incur avoidable inference cost. While recent work has explored adaptive reasoning, existing methods typically make a single query-level decision about whether to reason. This overlooks the dynamic nature of multi-step tasks, where the need for explicit reasoning varies across intermediate stages. To address this limitation, we introduce AdaptR1, a Reinforcement Learning (RL) based framework for adaptive interleaved thinking in multi-hop Question Answering (QA). Unlike previous approaches that require Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) for cold-start initialization, AdaptR1 uses a fully RL-based strategy with a quality-gated efficiency reward to dynamically allocate reasoning budgets at each step. Under the Graph-R1 setting, AdaptR1 reduces average think tokens by 69.71\%, with a 90.35\% reduction on HotpotQA, while maintaining performance comparable to or better than standard baselines. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that overthinking in multi-hop reasoning is not uniformly distributed but occurs predominantly during the initial planning stages, highlighting the effectiveness of step-wise adaptive budget allocation.

AI.tldr: AdaptR1 用纯 RL 在多跳问答的每一步动态控制是否“思考”，显著节省推理 token，同时不牺牲准确率。 / AdaptR1 uses pure RL to decide step by step when to “think” in multi-hop QA, greatly cutting reasoning tokens without sacrificing accuracy.
AI.motivation: 动机在于 CoT 虽然提升复杂推理能力，但会导致简单或局部不需要深推理的步骤出现 over-thinking，造成不必要的推理开销；现有方法多只在查询级别做一次性决策，无法适配多步任务中不断变化的推理需求。 / The motivation is that although CoT improves complex reasoning, it often causes over-thinking on simple or locally easy steps, leading to unnecessary inference cost; existing methods usually make only a single query-level reasoning decision and cannot capture the changing reasoning needs across multi-step tasks.
AI.method: 方法上，AdaptR1 采用完全基于强化学习的训练策略，不依赖冷启动 SFT；并设计了 quality-gated efficiency reward，在每个中间步骤动态决定是否以及分配多少显式推理预算。 / Methodologically, AdaptR1 uses a fully RL-based training strategy without SFT cold start, and introduces a quality-gated efficiency reward to decide at each intermediate step whether and how much explicit reasoning budget to allocate.
AI.result: 在 Graph-R1 设定下，AdaptR1 将平均 think tokens 降低 69.71%，在 HotpotQA 上降低 90.35%，同时性能与标准基线相当或更优；分析还表明，多跳推理中的过度思考主要集中在初始规划阶段。 / Under the Graph-R1 setting, AdaptR1 reduces average think tokens by 69.71%, including a 90.35% reduction on HotpotQA, while achieving comparable or better performance than standard baselines; the analysis further shows that overthinking is concentrated mainly in the early planning stages.
AI.conclusion: 该论文提出 AdaptR1，通过纯强化学习在多跳问答中进行分步自适应推理分配，在显著减少思维 token 的同时保持或提升性能。 / The paper concludes that AdaptR1 enables step-wise adaptive reasoning allocation for multi-hop QA via pure RL, substantially reducing thinking tokens while maintaining or improving task performance.

title: Task-Focused Memorization for Multimodal Agents
summary: Long-term memory is essential for multimodal agents to build coherent experience, accumulate world knowledge, and achieve continual learning. However, constructing effective memory goes beyond memory module design and basic requirements such as accuracy and fidelity; the key challenge lies in determining what to memorize. Multimodal agents, such as embodied agents, continuously perceive, reason, and act in real or virtual environments, receiving an unbounded stream of multimodal observations. From this combinatorial explosion of information, an agent must selectively retain content that is relevant to its role in the environment and valuable for future tasks. To bridge this gap, we frame memory generation as a learnable memorization policy and introduce TaskMem (Task-focused Memorization Policy Learning), a reinforcement-learning-based framework that enables the policy to dynamically adjust its focus to the demands of real tasks encountered in the environment. TaskMem adopts a two-phase training paradigm: Phase One learns how to memorize by optimizing memory quality under fundamental fidelity requirements; Phase Two occurs after deployment, where the agent learns what to memorize by tuning an adapter on its base MLLM, using recent environment tasks to define a reward model that guides the memorization policy toward task-relevant content. To evaluate our approach, we reformulate VideoMME, EgoLife, and EgoTempo into streaming benchmarks that simulate a realistic setting in which an agent processes streaming observations and handles tasks arriving online. To isolate memory assessment, the questions must be answered using only the agent's memory, without access to raw video. Built on Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B, TaskMem improves VQA accuracy by 6.3%, 7.0%, and 5.3% on these benchmarks, respectively.

AI.tldr: TaskMem uses reinforcement learning to teach a multimodal agent not just how to store memories accurately, but what task-relevant information to keep from continuous multimodal streams, yielding clear VQA gains on three streaming benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing multimodal agent memory work focuses on memory modules and fidelity, but the harder problem is deciding what information should be stored from an unbounded multimodal stream so that it remains useful for future tasks.
AI.method: The paper formulates memory generation as a learnable memorization policy and proposes TaskMem, a reinforcement-learning-based framework with two training phases: first, learning how to memorize under fidelity constraints; second, after deployment, learning what to memorize by tuning an adapter on the base MLLM using recent tasks as rewards for task relevance.
AI.result: Built on Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B, TaskMem improves VQA accuracy by 6.3% on VideoMME, 7.0% on EgoLife, and 5.3% on EgoTempo under streaming-memory-only evaluation settings.
AI.conclusion: TaskMem shows that learning a task-focused memorization policy can significantly improve long-term memory usefulness for multimodal agents in streaming environments, leading to better downstream question answering from memory alone.

title: ConsisGuard: Aligning Safety Deliberation with Policy Enforcement in LLM Guardrails
summary: Reasoning-based LLM guardrails improve safety moderation by generating explicit rationales before issuing final decisions. However, their rationales do not always lead to faithful enforcement: a model may recognize a harmful intent in its reasoning but still predict a safe label, or issue an unsafe decision without policy-grounded justification. We identify this safety-critical failure mode as the deliberation-to-enforcement gap. Unlike general chain-of-thought faithfulness, guardrail reliability requires policy execution consistency: the generated reasoning should be grounded in the safety policy, and the final decision should be entailed by that reasoning. We propose ConsisGuard, a consistency-aware framework for reasoning-based LLM guardrails. ConsisGuard performs Policy-to-Decision Trajectory Distillation and Functional Coupling Alignment, aligning the internal coupling between safety deliberation and decision enforcement. Experiments on prompt and response harmfulness detection benchmarks show that ConsisGuard improves detection performance while reducing policy execution failures. These results suggest that reliable reasoning-based guardrails require accurate faithful execution of safety policies.

AI.tldr: The paper identifies a key failure mode in reasoning-based LLM safety systems: the model's reasoning and final moderation decision can disagree. To fix this, it introduces ConsisGuard, which trains guardrails so policy-based reasoning and enforcement stay tightly coupled. Experiments show better harmful-content detection and fewer inconsistent safety decisions.
AI.motivation: Reasoning-based guardrails often generate explicit rationales, but these rationales are not always faithfully reflected in the final moderation label. This deliberation-to-enforcement gap creates a safety-critical reliability problem: the model may recognize harmful intent yet output a safe label, or flag content without policy-grounded justification.
AI.method: The paper proposes ConsisGuard, a consistency-aware framework with two main components: Policy-to-Decision Trajectory Distillation and Functional Coupling Alignment. Together they align safety-policy reasoning trajectories with final enforcement decisions so the decision is entailed by the deliberation.
AI.result: On prompt and response harmfulness detection benchmarks, ConsisGuard improves detection performance and reduces policy execution failures compared with prior reasoning-based guardrails.
AI.conclusion: ConsisGuard demonstrates that improving consistency between policy-grounded reasoning and final moderation decisions can both raise harmfulness detection performance and reduce safety-critical policy execution failures in reasoning-based LLM guardrails.

title: Beyond Accuracy: Evaluating Efficiency, Robustness and Explainability in Deep Learning for Malaria Diagnosis
summary: Malaria remains a leading cause of mortality in sub-Saharan Africa, where scarce diagnostic infrastructure makes timely, accurate diagnosis particularly challenging. While deep learning offers a compelling path toward automated malaria screening, clinical adoption is hindered by computational cost and opacity in decision-making. This work benchmarks four deep learning models spanning a wide range of designed design architectures and model capacities on the NLM-Malaria dataset, jointly evaluating predictive performance, robustness, and post-hoc explainability. We find that lightweight, efficient-by-design models match their heavier counterparts in predictive performance, and the Friedman test confirms no statistically significant performance differences. CAM-based XAI methods consistently localize diagnostically relevant regions, while fine-grained attribution methods produce less targeted explanations, particularly with heavier backbones. Robustness evaluation under three types of image corruption further reveals that model confidence degrades faster than accuracy, providing a practical signal for human review. However, no XAI method is robust to corruption, with explanation reliability degrading at noise levels plausible in clinical practice, even when predictions remain accurate. These findings support the deployment of lightweight architectures for malaria diagnosis in resource-constrained settings, while highlighting the vulnerability of post-hoc explanations as an important consideration for responsible clinical deployment.

AI.tldr: Efficient lightweight deep learning models work as well as larger ones for malaria image classification, but the explanations produced by current post-hoc XAI methods are not robust enough for dependable clinical deployment.
AI.motivation: Malaria diagnosis in sub-Saharan Africa is constrained by limited diagnostic infrastructure. The study is motivated by the need for automated deep-learning-based screening that is both computationally efficient and interpretable enough for clinical adoption.
AI.method: The paper benchmarks four deep learning models with different architectural designs and capacities on the NLM-Malaria dataset. It jointly evaluates predictive performance, robustness under three image corruption types, and post-hoc explainability using CAM-based and fine-grained attribution XAI methods, with statistical comparison via the Friedman test.
AI.result: The models show no statistically significant performance differences according to the Friedman test. CAM-based XAI methods better localize diagnostically relevant regions than fine-grained attribution methods, especially compared with heavier backbones. Under corruption, model confidence declines faster than accuracy, but all XAI methods lose reliability even at clinically plausible noise levels.
AI.conclusion: Lightweight malaria-screening models can achieve performance comparable to heavier architectures on the NLM-Malaria dataset, making them more suitable for resource-constrained deployment. However, post-hoc explainability methods are fragile under realistic image corruption, which limits their reliability for clinical use.

title: Beyond Static Dialogues: Benchmarking Realistic, Heterogeneous, and Evolving Long-Term Memory
summary: In existing memory benchmarks for Large Language Models (LLMs), the evaluated dialogue sessions often lack long-term semantic consistency, and the underlying personas tend to be flat and static. Furthermore, in real-world scenarios, interactions between users and assistants involve more diverse, heterogeneous data streams, such as documents and emails. These shortcomings significantly limit the realism and effectiveness of current evaluations. To address these limitations, we introduce RHELM (Realistic, Heterogeneous, and Evolving Long-term Memory). Driven by meticulously crafted user profiles and a novel LOOP (pLan-rOllout-evOlve-Prune) module, we construct realistic dialogues across diverse interaction scenarios that exhibit dynamic temporal evolution and long-term coherence. Crucially, these dialogues are deeply integrated with heterogeneous external sources synchronized with the user's temporal event trajectory. The resulting benchmark encompasses challenging question-answer pairs spanning seven inquiry types, with each question mapping to at least one of 27 critical memory characteristics that we identify as essential yet underexplored in current research. Comprehensive experiments across full-context models, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods, and representative memory frameworks reveal that contemporary approaches still expose critical weaknesses in complex, real-world settings, particularly in resolving multi-source aggregation and real-world contextual reasoning.

AI.tldr: RHELM is a more realistic long-term memory benchmark for LLMs that combines evolving personas, coherent dialogues, and heterogeneous data; tested systems still struggle badly on these harder real-world memory challenges.
AI.motivation: Existing LLM memory benchmarks are limited by weak long-term semantic consistency, static personas, and lack of heterogeneous real-world data streams, reducing evaluation realism and effectiveness.
AI.method: The paper introduces RHELM, a benchmark built with crafted user profiles and a LOOP module (pLan-rOllout-evOlve-Prune) to generate realistic, temporally evolving, semantically coherent dialogues aligned with heterogeneous external sources such as documents and emails.
AI.result: Experiments on full-context models, RAG methods, and representative memory frameworks show substantial weaknesses in realistic long-term memory tasks, particularly in cross-source aggregation and real-world contextual reasoning.
AI.conclusion: Current LLM memory methods remain inadequate for realistic long-term memory settings, especially for multi-source aggregation and contextual reasoning over evolving user histories.

title: Cross-Modal Clinical Knowledge Integration for Mammography Report Generation
summary: Breast cancer is a major global health concern, and mammography screening plays a central role in early detection. The large volume of screening examinations creates a substantial workload for radiologists, making accurate and consistent report generation a critical clinical challenge. Existing automated mammography report generation methods primarily focus on direct visual-to-text mapping, while overlooking the structured clinical reasoning process followed by radiologists in real-world practice. To address this limitation, we propose MammoRG, a mammography report generation framework that explicitly simulates the clinical reporting workflow by following the BI-RADS guideline and incorporating prior clinical knowledge to produce diagnostic reports. Specifically, MammoRG adopts a two-stage training framework. In the first stage, the model learns to integrate clinically relevant prior knowledge from a patient's four-view mammograms through classification-based supervision.
