AI.conclusion: Light Interaction is a training-free inference acceleration framework for interactive video world models that significantly improves long-horizon interactive generation efficiency while preserving competitive visual quality.

title: Cross-Layer Subspace Coupling for LLM Compression: A Unifying Framework and Its Empirical Limits
summary: Recent SVD based compression methods for large language models like SVD LLM and Basis Sharing can be unified under one optimization problem. While mathematical proofs and tests on Pythia models show this unified approach improves weight reconstruction error by up to 46% percent it fails in practical tasks. Downstream metrics like perplexity and accuracy severely degrade compared to standard per layer SVD LLM. The authors explain this failure mechanistically. Although the bundle method mathematically couples adjacent layers the transformer residual stream actually decouples them during forward passes. Thus per layer optimality matters more than joint cross layer optimization. The paper concludes that weight space reconstruction is a flawed objective for cross layer compression and future methods must focus on per layer activation reconstruction instead.

AI.tldr: A unified cross-layer SVD compression objective looks better mathematically and reconstructs weights more accurately, but it performs worse on real tasks because transformer residual connections make per-layer fidelity more important than joint layer coupling.
AI.motivation: Existing SVD-based LLM compression methods appear different but may share a common optimization structure. The authors aim to understand whether a unified cross-layer formulation can improve compression quality and whether lower weight reconstruction error translates into better practical model performance.
AI.method: The paper formulates recent SVD-based compression approaches, such as SVD-LLM and Basis Sharing, under a unified optimization framework. It provides mathematical analysis and empirical evaluation on Pythia models, comparing unified cross-layer optimization against standard per-layer SVD compression in terms of weight reconstruction error and downstream task performance.
AI.result: The unified method reduces weight reconstruction error by up to 46%, but downstream metrics such as perplexity and accuracy degrade substantially relative to standard per-layer SVD-LLM. The analysis attributes this mismatch to the transformer residual stream, which weakens the intended coupling between adjacent layers during forward computation.
AI.conclusion: Cross-layer weight-space reconstruction is not a reliable objective for compressing large language models. Despite lower reconstruction error, jointly optimizing adjacent layers harms downstream performance because transformer residual connections effectively decouple layers during inference. Future compression methods should prioritize per-layer activation reconstruction rather than joint cross-layer weight reconstruction.

title: Shared Doubt: Zero-shot Cross-Lingual Confidence Estimation for Language Models
summary: Confidence estimation (CE), i.e. quantifying the reliability of a model's prediction, has attracted great interest in the context of large language models (LLMs). However, most studies focus on English, ignoring the multilingual reality of LLM usage, while many CE methods degrade or require retraining across languages. To address this gap, we investigate whether multilingual LLMs encode shared, language-transferable confidence features. We use a lightweight linear probe that predicts answer correctness directly from intermediate representations. Trained monolingually, the probe generalizes zero-shot to unseen, typologically diverse languages without target-language supervision. Learned layer weights and multiple ablations reveal that confidence features concentrate in middle layers across languages, suggesting a shared confidence subspace. While zero-shot cross-lingual performance depends on similarity to the source language, the probe provides a strong baseline without any retraining and compares favorably to other popular confidence estimation methods.

AI.tldr: Train a simple linear probe on one language’s hidden states to predict whether an LLM answer is correct, and it still works on other languages zero-shot. This suggests multilingual LLMs share a cross-lingual confidence subspace, mainly in middle layers.
AI.motivation: Existing confidence estimation methods for LLMs mainly focus on English and often degrade or require retraining when applied to other languages. Since real-world LLM use is multilingual, the paper aims to test whether confidence signals are shared across languages and can transfer without supervision.
AI.method: The paper trains a lightweight linear probe on intermediate representations of a multilingual LLM to predict answer correctness. The probe is trained on one source language and then evaluated zero-shot on unseen target languages. Layer-weight analysis and ablation studies are used to identify where confidence-related features are located.
AI.result: A monolingually trained linear probe generalizes effectively to typologically diverse unseen languages in a zero-shot setting. Confidence information is concentrated in middle layers across languages, and cross-lingual performance is stronger when the target language is more similar to the source language. The method also compares favorably with popular confidence estimation baselines without requiring retraining.
AI.conclusion: Multilingual LLMs appear to encode shared, language-transferable confidence features, especially in middle layers, enabling zero-shot confidence estimation across diverse languages with a simple linear probe and no target-language retraining.

title: Guidance for Low-Level Perceptual Editing in Unconditional Diffusion Models
comment: 11 pages, 12 figures, Generative Models for Computer Vision Workshop CVPR 2026
summary: Unconditional diffusion models offer powerful generative priors, yet steering them toward aesthetically enhanced outputs remains largely unexplored. We show that h-space patching, the dominant paradigm for training-free diffusion editing, systematically fails for global, low-level transformations required for aesthetic and perceptual refinement. We introduce a novel, generalized framework for image-editing in unconditional diffusion models without explicit training. This inference-time mechanism operates on low-level features by extracting degradation concept vectors and combining bottleneck patching with classifier-free guidance to guide sampling away from the degraded manifold, producing consistently improved images without any model retraining.

AI.tldr: A training-free diffusion editing method for unconditional models improves image aesthetics by identifying degradation directions in low-level features and steering sampling away from them with bottleneck patching plus CFG, avoiding any retraining.
AI.motivation: Existing training-free diffusion editing methods, especially h-space patching, mainly target local or semantic edits and fail on global, low-level transformations needed for aesthetic enhancement and perceptual refinement. The paper aims to enable such refinements without explicit model retraining.
AI.method: The method is a training-free image editing framework for unconditional diffusion models. It extracts degradation concept vectors from low-level features, applies bottleneck patching, and combines this with classifier-free guidance during inference to steer sampling away from a degraded image manifold.
AI.result: The proposed inference-time mechanism produces consistently improved images by guiding generation away from degradation-related directions, addressing a setting where prior h-space patching methods systematically fail.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that standard h-space patching is inadequate for global, low-level aesthetic/perceptual refinements in unconditional diffusion models, and that inference-time guidance using degradation concept vectors plus bottleneck patching and classifier-free guidance can improve image quality consistently without retraining.

title: Scaling Multi-Hop Training Data via Graph-Constrained Path Selection
summary: Endowing large language models with compositional reasoning over specialized documents requires multi-hop training data at scale, where such data rarely exists outside of curated benchmarks built on structured sources. To construct it directly from plain, unannotated text, existing methods ask a single teacher model to jointly discover an evidence path through a document and verbalize it as a question-answer pair. However, these methods degrade sharply when documents are structured around repetitive templates and densely cross-referencing clauses, conditions that characterize most real-world specialized corpora. In this work, we decouple the two operations: reasoning paths are enumerated offline over a graph of contextual keyword centroids, and the teacher is invoked only to verbalize pre-validated paths. The graph enforces five geometric admissibility constraints, for which we provide Gram-matrix arguments establishing that local similarity bounds alone admit endpoint drift up to ${\sim}91^{\circ}$, and that an upper similarity bound is necessary to exit dense embedding cliques formed by boilerplate text. A matched-size ablation isolates the mechanism: at equal training scale, constrained and unconstrained chains yield indistinguishable downstream performance, and the gain at full scale comes from a 4.4$\times$ expansion of the usable corpus rather than from higher per-chain quality -- reframing the role of graph constraints, in this setting, as raising teacher synthesizability rather than improving chain content. Fine-tuning Qwen3-32B on 80K examples constructed from the CUAD legal contract corpus improves closed-book Token F1 from 21.66% to 38.58%. We have released our codes at https://github.com/hkgai-official/GCSCS.

AI.tldr: 论文提出一种两阶段多跳数据合成框架：先在关键词质心图上离线找满足几何约束的推理路径，再让教师模型只负责把路径表述成问答。核心发现是图约束主要提升“可合成数据量”而不是“单条链质量”。在CUAD上，该方法显著提升了Qwen3-32B的法律合同推理能力。 / The paper proposes a two-stage framework for multi-hop data synthesis: first enumerate geometrically constrained reasoning paths on a keyword-centroid graph, then use a teacher model only to verbalize them into QA pairs. The key finding is that graph constraints mainly improve the amount of synthesizable data rather than per-chain quality. On CUAD, this substantially boosts Qwen3-32B’s legal contract reasoning performance.
AI.motivation: 动机是解决专业文档中缺乏大规模多跳训练数据的问题。现有“单教师同时找路径并生成问答”的方法在真实世界专业语料上效果差，尤其当文档高度模板化、包含大量重复条款和密集交叉引用时更容易退化，因此需要一种更稳健、可扩展的数据构造方案。 / The motivation is to address the lack of large-scale multi-hop training data for specialized documents. Existing single-teacher approaches that jointly discover evidence paths and generate QA pairs degrade badly on real-world corpora, especially when documents are highly templated, repetitive, and densely cross-referential, so a more robust and scalable construction pipeline is needed.
AI.method: 方法上，作者先在未标注文本上构建“上下文关键词质心图”，离线枚举满足五个几何可接受性约束的推理路径；随后仅将这些预验证路径交给教师模型，将其语言化为问答样本。论文还给出基于Gram矩阵的理论论证，说明仅靠局部相似度下界会导致终点漂移，并证明需要加入相似度上界以跳出由样板文本形成的嵌入团簇。最后在CUAD合同语料上构建80K样本，对Qwen3-32B进行微调并做匹配规模消融。 / Methodologically, the authors first build a graph of contextual keyword centroids over raw unannotated text and enumerate reasoning paths offline under five geometric admissibility constraints. Only these pre-validated paths are then sent to a teacher model for verbalization into QA examples. The paper also provides Gram-matrix arguments showing that local lower-bound similarity constraints alone allow endpoint drift, and that an upper similarity bound is needed to escape embedding cliques induced by boilerplate text. They then fine-tune Qwen3-32B on 80K examples from the CUAD corpus and run matched-size ablations.
AI.result: 实验结果显示：在CUAD法律合同语料上，用该方法构造的80K训练样本将Qwen3-32B的closed-book Token F1从21.66%提升到38.58%。匹配规模消融表明，在相同训练规模下，受约束与无约束链的下游效果几乎无差别；满规模增益主要来自可用语料扩大了4.4倍，而非单链质量提升。 / Results show that on the CUAD legal contract corpus, 80K examples built by the proposed method improve closed-book Token F1 of Qwen3-32B from 21.66% to 38.58%. A matched-size ablation shows that constrained and unconstrained chains yield nearly identical downstream performance at equal training size; the full-scale gain mainly comes from a 4.4x expansion in usable corpus size, not from better per-chain quality.
AI.conclusion: 该论文认为，在专业文档多跳数据构造中，图约束的主要价值不是提升单条推理链质量，而是显著提高教师模型可合成的有效语料规模；通过将路径发现与语言化解耦，可在复杂、模板化、强交叉引用的文档上更稳定地构造训练数据，并显著提升下游模型表现。 / The paper concludes that, for multi-hop data construction over specialized documents, graph constraints matter primarily because they expand the amount of teacher-synthesizable usable data rather than improving the intrinsic quality of each reasoning chain. By decoupling path discovery from verbalization, the method builds training data more robustly on templated, cross-referential corpora and substantially improves downstream performance.

title: Detect in Any Scene: An Agentic Framework for Object Detection with Experience-Aware Reasoning
summary: Object detection in real-world scenarios remains challenging due to diverse image degradations and heterogeneous object distributions, which significantly hinder the generalization of existing detectors. Conventional approaches, including scene-specific representation learning and end-to-end pipeline design, are inherently limited by their reliance on predefined conditions and lack adaptability to dynamic environments. In this paper, we propose DetAS, an agentic detection framework that formulates object detection as a dynamic decision process. Instead of relying on static pipelines, DetAS leverages a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) as a central agent to adaptively compose detection workflows by selecting from a toolbox of restoration modules and specialized detectors. Specifically, DetAS consists of two key components: Self-Adaptive Image Restoration, which dynamically determines whether and how to enhance images for downstream detection, and Multi-Expertise Detection, which integrates multiple domain-specialized detectors and resolves their predictions through instance-level reasoning. To further improve decision quality under fine-grained conditions, we introduce Self-Evolving Experience Harvesting and extend the framework to DetAS-X, which accumulates node-level decision experience from a small set of annotated data and enables experience-aware reasoning during inference. This mechanism allows the system to progressively refine its decision policy and adapt to diverse real-world scenarios. Extensive experiments on six challenging benchmarks demonstrate that DetAS-X significantly outperforms existing MLLM-based detectors, achieving an average improvement of 28.36% in F1 score, with up to 37.01% gain on DarkFace. These results demonstrate the promise of agentic detection and establish a solid foundation for its application in complex and dynamic environments.

AI.tldr: DetAS turns object detection into an agent-based decision process: an MLLM chooses restoration steps and expert detectors adaptively, while DetAS-X improves these choices using learned experience. This yields large F1 gains on difficult real-world benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing object detectors struggle in real-world settings because image degradations and heterogeneous object distributions reduce generalization. Static pipelines and predefined scene-specific methods are insufficiently adaptive for dynamic environments, motivating a more flexible decision-driven framework.
AI.method: The paper proposes DetAS, an agentic detection framework centered on an MLLM that dynamically composes detection workflows. It includes Self-Adaptive Image Restoration to decide whether/how to enhance images, Multi-Expertise Detection to combine domain-specialized detectors with instance-level reasoning, and an extension called DetAS-X that uses Self-Evolving Experience Harvesting to accumulate node-level decision experience from limited annotated data for better inference-time decisions.
AI.result: On six challenging benchmarks, DetAS-X significantly outperforms prior MLLM-based detectors, with an average F1 improvement of 28.36% and a maximum gain of 37.01% on DarkFace.
AI.conclusion: DetAS/DetAS-X demonstrates that framing object detection as an agentic, dynamic decision process can substantially improve robustness and generalization in degraded, heterogeneous real-world scenarios. Experience-aware reasoning further strengthens adaptation and delivers strong gains across challenging benchmarks.

title: A Lecture Note on Offline RL and IRL, Part II: Foundations of Inverse Reinforcement Learning and Dynamic Discrete Choice Models
summary: In the forward reinforcement-learning problem, the reward is fixed and known; the learner is asked to find a good policy or value function. Here we turn the question around. Given offline data generated by an expert, can we recover the reward the expert was optimizing? This is the inverse reinforcement learning problem, and remarkably, two communities, structural econometricians studying dynamic discrete choice (DDC) and machine learners studying entropy-regularized IRL, have been working on exactly the same probabilistic model under different names. We begin by proving their equivalence. We then develop the classical identification result of Magnac and Thesmar and the classical computational paradigms that grew out of it: Rust's nested fixed-point algorithm, the conditional-choice-probability approach of Hotz and Miller, and the two temporal-difference approaches of Adusumilli and Eckardt: linear semi-gradient TD and approximate value iteration. Each route has its limits: dimensionality, transition-kernel estimation, the deadly triad, or projected fixed-point bias. We then walk through the modern ML/IRL strand: adversarial IRL, occupancy matching, IQ-Learn, and offline ML-IRL, deriving each method's actual objective and stating precisely what it does and does not identify. We close with the empirical-risk-minimization framework of Kang et al., which yields a gradient-based estimator for offline IRL/DDC.

AI.tldr: This paper unifies econometric DDC and entropy-regularized IRL, showing they are the same model. It reviews classical and modern methods for recovering rewards from offline expert data, explains their identification limits and computational tradeoffs, and points to ERM-based gradient estimation as a practical path forward.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to address the inverse reinforcement learning problem in the offline setting: given expert-generated data, can we recover the reward function being optimized? The paper is motivated by the observation that econometrics and machine learning have independently studied the same underlying model using different terminology, leading to fragmented understanding of equivalence, identification, and computational tradeoffs.
AI.method: The paper first proves the equivalence between DDC and entropy-regularized IRL. It then reviews and unifies major classical estimation methods, including Rust’s nested fixed-point algorithm, Hotz-Miller conditional choice probability estimation, and temporal-difference approaches such as linear semi-gradient TD and approximate value iteration. Next, it analyzes modern ML-based IRL methods including adversarial IRL, occupancy matching, IQ-Learn, and offline ML-IRL by deriving their underlying objectives and identification properties. Finally, it presents the empirical-risk-minimization framework of Kang et al. as a gradient-based estimator for offline IRL/DDC.
AI.result: The paper’s main result is a formal unification of two previously separate literatures. It establishes equivalence between DDC and entropy-regularized IRL, explains classical identification results, compares the computational strengths and weaknesses of major estimators, and precisely characterizes what modern IRL methods do and do not identify. It also highlights ERM-based offline IRL/DDC as a scalable gradient-based estimation framework.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that dynamic discrete choice (DDC) in structural econometrics and entropy-regularized inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) in machine learning are fundamentally equivalent formulations of the same probabilistic model. It clarifies the identification limits of offline IRL, compares classical and modern estimation routes, and highlights empirical-risk minimization as a practical gradient-based estimator for offline IRL/DDC.

title: Mellum2 Technical Report
summary: We present Mellum 2, an open-weight 12B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model with 2.5B active parameters per token. Mellum 2 is a general-purpose language model specialized in software engineering, spanning code generation and editing, debugging, multi-step reasoning, tool use and function calling, agentic coding, and conversational programming assistance, and it is the successor to the completion-focused 4B dense Mellum model. The architecture builds on the Mixture-of-Experts (64 experts, 8 active) and combines Grouped-Query Attention with 4 KV heads, Sliding Window Attention on three of every four layers, and a single Multi-Token Prediction head that doubles as both an auxiliary pre-training objective and a built-in draft model for speculative decoding; each choice was validated by ablation with inference efficiency on commodity GPUs as a design constraint. Pre-training spans approximately 10.6 trillion tokens through a three-phase curriculum that progressively shifts the mixture from diverse web data toward curated code and mathematical content, optimized with Muon under FP8 hybrid precision and a Warmup-Hold-Decay schedule with linear decay to zero. The pre-trained base is extended to a 128K context window via a layer-selective YaRN and then post-trained in two stages (supervised fine-tuning followed by RLVR), yielding two released variants: an Instruct model that answers directly and a Thinking model that emits an explicit reasoning trace before its final answer. Across code generation, math and reasoning, tool use, knowledge, and safety benchmarks, Mellum 2 is competitive with open-weight baselines in the 4B-14B range while running at the per-token compute of a 2.5B dense model. We release the base, instruct, and thinking checkpoints, together with this report on the architecture decisions, data pipeline, and training recipe behind them, under the Apache 2.0 license.

AI.tldr: Mellum 2 is an efficient open 12B MoE coding-focused LLM: only 2.5B parameters are active per token, yet it matches many 4B-14B open models across coding and reasoning tasks through a carefully engineered architecture, 10.6T-token curriculum pretraining, 128K context extension, and post-training into instruct and reasoning variants.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to create an efficient open-weight general-purpose language model specialized for software engineering that goes beyond code completion to support generation, editing, debugging, reasoning, tool use, and agentic programming, while keeping inference cost low enough for commodity GPUs.
AI.method: The paper builds a 12B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts language model with 64 experts and 8 active experts per token, using Grouped-Query Attention, Sliding Window Attention, and a Multi-Token Prediction head for both auxiliary pre-training and speculative decoding. It is trained on 10.6T tokens with a three-phase curriculum, optimized with Muon in FP8 hybrid precision, extended to 128K context via layer-selective YaRN, and post-trained with supervised fine-tuning plus RLVR.
AI.result: Mellum 2 is competitive on benchmarks covering code generation, mathematics and reasoning, tool use, knowledge, and safety relative to open-weight models in the 4B-14B range, despite operating at the per-token compute cost of a 2.5B dense model. The work also produces two post-trained variants: Instruct and Thinking.
AI.conclusion: Mellum 2 demonstrates that an open-weight 12B MoE model with only 2.5B active parameters per token can deliver competitive software-engineering and reasoning performance against 4B-14B open baselines while maintaining efficient inference on commodity GPUs; the authors also release base, instruct, and thinking checkpoints under Apache 2.0.

title: Vanilla ViT for Automotive Point Cloud Semantic Segmentation
summary: Plain Transformers have become the de-facto architecture for processing text, audio, image, and video, offering a unified backbone for multimodal learning. However, state-of-the-art architectures for point cloud semantic segmentation remain dominated by U-Nets architectures where convolutions are interleaved with local or windowed attentions. In this work, we show how to effectively leverage vanilla, non-hierarchical ViTs for segmentation of large-scale automotive lidar scenes. We bridge the performance gap thanks to a carefully designed tokenizer, a lightweight decoder segmentation head, and tailored data augmentations. Our approach, VaViT for Vanilla ViT, matches or exceeds the performance of state-of-the-art methods while maintaining the simplicity of ViT architecture. We provide extensive evaluations on nuScenes, SemanticKITTI, and Waymo Open Dataset to validate the efficiency of our method. Code and models are available at https://github.com/valeoai/VaViT.

AI.tldr: VaViT shows that plain vanilla ViTs, with the right tokenizer, decoder, and augmentations, can rival or beat specialized U-Net-based point cloud segmentation models on major LiDAR benchmarks.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to challenge the dominance of U-Net-style architectures with convolution and local/window attention in point cloud segmentation, and to test whether the simpler, unified plain Transformer paradigm that works well across text, audio, image, and video can also work effectively for automotive LiDAR segmentation.
AI.method: The method, called VaViT, uses a vanilla ViT backbone for point cloud semantic segmentation. Its key components are a carefully designed tokenizer for point cloud inputs, a lightweight segmentation decoder, and tailored data augmentation strategies to adapt plain transformers to large-scale LiDAR scenes.
AI.result: VaViT matches or exceeds state-of-the-art performance on nuScenes, SemanticKITTI, and Waymo Open Dataset, demonstrating both effectiveness and efficiency while preserving the simplicity of the vanilla ViT architecture.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that a plain, non-hierarchical vanilla Vision Transformer can be made competitive for large-scale point cloud semantic segmentation when paired with a strong tokenizer, lightweight decoder head, and suitable augmentations, matching or surpassing prior state-of-the-art methods on major automotive LiDAR benchmarks.

title: Wind Turbine Maintenance Log Labelling Framework: LLM-Driven Data Correction and Enrichment via Semantic Extraction of Reliability Intelligence
comment: An adjustable template containing the Python script architecture, applied dynamic prompts, and data schemas is hosted in an open-source GitHub repository: https://github.com/mvmalyi/llm-driven-wind-turbine-maintenance-log-labelling
summary: As wind turbine fleets age, data-driven reliability engineering is essential to optimise their operation and maintenance for service life extension and levelised cost of energy reduction. Failure event descriptions within historical maintenance logs are a source of valuable reliability intelligence. However, they typically appear as unstructured natural language entries, rendering them inaccessible for quantitative analysis. This paper presents a novel methodology leveraging a large language model (LLM) to systematically standardise and structure maintenance logs based on their free-text descriptors. Operating on a dataset of 16,316 maintenance logs from 280 turbines monitored over nine years, the developed model-agnostic framework autonomously corrected hierarchical system codes and extracted evidence-based taxonomies of maintenance actions and failure modes. The automated pipeline successfully structured over 70% of the dataset. It resolved pervasive misclassification issues, such as isolating previously unclassified pitch system faults and restoring missing system codes, and enriched the records by applying empirical taxonomies to label specific actions taken and failure modes addressed. By using system-based log batches to construct empirical dictionaries of failure modes, observable symptoms, dominant mechanisms, and candidate causes, this approach reduces the inherent subjectivity of manual failure modes and effects analysis (FMEA). Ultimately, the methodology provides a highly scalable, cost-effective blueprint for translating large sets of qualitative field observations into quantitative reliability metrics, laying the foundation for integrated root-cause analysis across the renewable energy sector, improved FMEA, and advanced predictive maintenance.

AI.tldr: TL;DR：论文用LLM把风电维护日志中的自由文本自动整理成标准化可靠性数据，在真实长期数据上结构化了70%以上记录，显著改善故障分类质量，并为更高质量的FMEA、根因分析和预测性维护提供基础。 / TL;DR: The paper uses an LLM to automatically turn free-text wind turbine maintenance logs into standardized reliability data, structures over 70% of real long-term records, improves failure classification quality, and provides a foundation for better FMEA, root-cause analysis, and predictive maintenance.
AI.motivation: 研究动机在于：随着风电机组老化，延寿和降本需要更强的数据驱动可靠性工程能力；但维护日志中的故障事件描述通常是非结构化自然语言，难以直接用于定量分析，因此需要一种自动化方法把这些文本转成结构化可靠性信息。 / The motivation is that aging wind turbine fleets require stronger data-driven reliability engineering for life extension and LCOE reduction, but failure descriptions in maintenance logs are usually unstructured natural language and therefore difficult to use in quantitative analysis.
AI.method: 方法上，作者基于16,316条、来自280台风机、跨9年的维护日志，构建了一个与具体模型无关的LLM框架，用于纠正分层系统编码，并从自由文本中提取维护动作和故障模式的证据型分类。系统还按系统类别批量构建经验词典，包含故障模式、可观察症状、主导机理和候选原因。 / Methodologically, the authors build a model-agnostic LLM framework on 16,316 maintenance logs from 280 turbines over nine years. The framework corrects hierarchical system codes and extracts evidence-based taxonomies of maintenance actions and failure modes from free-text descriptions, while constructing empirical dictionaries of failure modes, symptoms, mechanisms, and candidate causes from system-based log batches.
AI.result: 结果表明，该自动化流程成功结构化了超过70%的数据集，纠正了大量系统误分类问题，例如识别出此前未分类的变桨系统故障、补全缺失系统编码，并通过经验分类为记录增加了具体维护动作和故障模式标签。 / The results show that the automated pipeline successfully structured more than 70% of the dataset, resolved widespread misclassification issues such as isolating previously unclassified pitch system faults and restoring missing system codes, and enriched the logs with labels for specific maintenance actions and failure modes.
AI.conclusion: 该论文提出了一种利用大语言模型自动标准化和结构化风电维护日志的方法，可将大量非结构化文本转化为可量化的可靠性数据，并为根因分析、改进FMEA和预测性维护提供可扩展基础。 / The paper concludes that an LLM-based pipeline can automatically standardize and structure wind turbine maintenance logs at scale, converting unstructured text into quantitative reliability intelligence and enabling better root-cause analysis, improved FMEA, and predictive maintenance.

title: From Local Geometry to Global Pseudo Labeling for Robust Positive Unlabeled Learning under Covariate Shift
summary: Detecting covariate shift is critical for building reliable vision systems. While most prior work focuses on improving robustness to shift, explicitly detecting covariate shift remains underexplored. Existing approaches typically rely on fully supervised training, requiring labeled examples from both original and shifted distributions, which is often impractical. In this paper, we show that covariate shift detection can be effectively addressed with weaker supervision using Positive Unlabeled (PU) learning. However, under covariate shift, in distribution and shifted data overlap significantly, making classical PU methods unstable and sensitive to noise. To overcome this challenge, we introduce Spectral PU Neighborhood Annotation (SPUNA), a geometry aware framework that progressively discovers shifted data by leveraging the local manifold structure of visual features. Extensive experiments show that SPUNA achieves state of the art performance in PU settings and remarkably matches the performances of fully supervised methods. Moreover, our approach transfers robustly across different types of shifts, demonstrating strong generalization capabilities.

AI.tldr: The paper reframes covariate shift detection as a PU learning problem and introduces SPUNA, a geometry-aware method that uses local feature manifold structure to stably detect shifted data with weak supervision, matching supervised baselines in many cases.
AI.motivation: Existing covariate shift detection methods usually require fully supervised labels from both in-distribution and shifted data, which is impractical; moreover, classical PU learning is unstable when the two distributions overlap heavily under covariate shift.
AI.method: The paper proposes Spectral PU Neighborhood Annotation (SPUNA), a geometry-aware PU learning framework that progressively identifies shifted samples by exploiting the local manifold structure of visual feature space.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show state-of-the-art performance under PU settings, performance comparable to fully supervised methods, and robust generalization across different types of covariate shifts.
AI.conclusion: SPUNA demonstrates that covariate shift detection in vision systems can be solved effectively with weak supervision via PU learning, achieving near fully supervised performance and strong transfer across shift types.

title: DARTS: Distribution-Aware Active Rollout Trajectory Shaping for Accelerating LLM Reinforcement Learning
comment: 16 pages, 14 figures, 5 tables. Accepted to ICML 2026
summary: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has become pivotal for improving model capabilities yet suffers from rollout efficiency bottlenecks due to the long-tail response length distribution. While existing works mitigate the impact of long tails via prompt-level tail scheduling, we focus on the root source of inefficiency: the distribution itself. Specifically, we characterize the long-tail distribution at a finer granularity, identifying intra-prompt long tails, and revealing that they frequently consist of ineffective verbosity. To address this, we propose a novel paradigm of active distribution shaping to shape the rollout distribution towards conciseness and certainty, thereby fundamentally resolving tail-induced overheads. We achieve this through a distribution-aware trajectory sampling mechanism, which selects trajectories from a redundant exploration space for each prompt, and an adaptive redundancy allocation scheme to maximize both shaping effectiveness and system efficiency. Experiments demonstrate significant acceleration over state-of-the-art systems by up to 1.77x without compromising model performance.

AI.tldr: Instead of only scheduling around long responses, this paper directly reshapes the rollout distribution to favor shorter, more certain outputs, reducing wasted verbose trajectories and making RL training significantly faster.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that RL for model training is bottlenecked by rollout inefficiency caused by long-tail response lengths. Prior work mainly schedules prompts to reduce tail effects, but this paper argues the deeper problem is the rollout length distribution itself, including intra-prompt long tails driven by ineffective verbosity.
AI.method: The method introduces active distribution shaping with two core components: a distribution-aware trajectory sampling mechanism that chooses trajectories from a redundant exploration space for each prompt, and an adaptive redundancy allocation scheme that balances shaping effectiveness with system efficiency.
AI.result: Experiments show up to 1.77x speedup over state-of-the-art systems while maintaining model performance.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that actively shaping the rollout length distribution toward concise and certain responses can remove a major source of RL rollout inefficiency, yielding substantial acceleration without hurting model quality.

title: Divergence Decoding: Inference-Time Unlearning via Auxiliary Models
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) frequently memorize sensitive training data thereby creating significant privacy and copyright risks. Addressing these risks, i.e., removing such knowledge from an existing model checkpoint, has proven challenging as many unlearning methods lead to catastrophic utility loss or are ineffective for complex queries. We introduce Divergence Decoding (DD), a mechanism that uses small auxiliary models to steer the logits of the LLM away from specific data during inference. Training these models is straight forward, i.e., we use standard pre-training and fine-tuning setups. We find the method decisively outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) baselines on unlearning benchmarks across a variety of model and training dataset scales consistent with DD being an effective and inexpensive solution to unlearning. We then demonstrate that this steered distribution can be trivially distilled back into the base model. Since the method is generally applicable to any probabilistic model, we explore its efficacy outside of text generation and find evidence of generalization to the domain of images.

AI.tldr: Use small helper models at decoding time to push an LLM away from sensitive memorized content; this beats prior unlearning methods, preserves utility better, can be distilled into the model, and may generalize to images.
AI.motivation: LLMs can memorize sensitive training data, creating privacy and copyright risks. Existing unlearning methods are often either ineffective on complex queries or cause severe utility degradation, so a more practical and robust unlearning method is needed.
AI.method: The paper introduces Divergence Decoding, which uses small auxiliary models trained with standard pre-training and fine-tuning pipelines to modify the base LLM's logits during inference, steering generation away from specific target data. The resulting steered distribution can also be distilled back into the original model checkpoint.
AI.result: The method outperforms state-of-the-art unlearning baselines across benchmarks spanning different model sizes and dataset scales, while remaining inexpensive and practical. The authors also report evidence that the approach extends to image-domain probabilistic models.
AI.conclusion: Divergence Decoding (DD) provides an effective, low-cost way to unlearn memorized sensitive data from LLMs at inference time, and the steered behavior can later be distilled into the base model. The approach may also generalize beyond text to image models.

title: The Regularizing Power of Language-Training Deepfake Detectors
summary: Recently, thanks to the advent of Multimodal-LLMs, deepfake detectors are striving not only to be generalizable but also interpretable. We propose that these two challenges can effectively be tackled jointly, since describable artifacts typically generalize better, opening the possibility to use language as a regularization mechanism. Since deepfake detection generally suffers from overfitting to low-level domain-specific artifacts, our intuition is that an LLM that has been pretrained on language would prefer high-level artifacts that can be described better. This way, we can use high-level features where possible, while training the model to use low-level features where necessary. We utilize a dual-encoder architecture, pairing a frozen specialist detector with a LoRA-tuned MLLM encoder, and a two-stage training curriculum: first, a binary alignment phase demonstrates that the intrinsic capability of MLLMs can effectively combine features to mitigate overfitting to dataset-specific artifacts. To further bolster generalization and achieve interpretability, we employ a reinforcement learning stage that encourages the model to generate descriptive reasoning before classifying, using only binary labels. By rewarding this "explain-then-classify" behavior, we explicitly incentivize the model to prioritize high-level, robust features. Crucially, this process yields both interpretable descriptions and a further boost in cross-dataset performance, even when reasoning chains are omitted at inference. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets validate our approach, outperforming state-of-the-art methods by a large margin.

AI.tldr: Use language-guided explain-then-classify training for deepfake detection: a frozen detector plus a tuned MLLM learns to focus on high-level, describable artifacts, yielding better generalization and interpretable outputs than prior methods.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that deepfake detectors often overfit to low-level, domain-specific artifacts and therefore generalize poorly. The authors argue that artifacts expressible in language are more likely to be high-level and robust, so leveraging an MLLM and language-based reasoning can jointly improve interpretability and generalization.
AI.method: The method uses a dual-encoder architecture: a frozen specialist detector is paired with a LoRA-tuned MLLM encoder. Training follows two stages: (1) binary alignment to combine features and reduce overfitting to dataset-specific artifacts, and (2) reinforcement learning with only binary labels to reward descriptive reasoning before classification, encouraging reliance on high-level, robust, describable artifacts.
AI.result: Experiments on benchmark datasets show substantial gains in cross-dataset deepfake detection and strong interpretability through generated descriptions, with performance surpassing state-of-the-art methods by a large margin.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that coupling a frozen specialist deepfake detector with a LoRA-tuned multimodal LLM and training it with an explain-then-classify reinforcement stage improves both cross-dataset generalization and interpretability, outperforming prior methods even when the generated reasoning is not used at inference.

title: GlucoFM: A Dual-Stream Foundation Model for Continuous Glucose Monitoring
summary: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) provides a dense view of daily metabolic physiology, yet existing generic time-series and CGM-specific foundation models often encode glucose traces as entangled single-stream sequences, leaving the distinct temporal structure of glycemic dynamics only implicitly modeled. We present GlucoFM, a lightweight CGM foundation model that aligns irregular recordings to a 24-hour chronological grid, preserves observation masks, and decomposes glucose dynamics into slow physiological state and transient event streams, capturing low-frequency glycemic baselines and short-term deviations that may reflect acute physiological responses or sensor artifacts. GlucoFM is pretrained on 109,066 hours of unlabeled CGM recordings from 477 subjects with two complementary objectives: masked contextual latent prediction over fused daily representations and temporal dynamics prediction over state and event streams. Across four diverse cohorts and seven clinical prediction tasks, GlucoFM achieves the strongest subject-disjoint linear-probing performance among evaluated baselines, improving average PR-AUC by 4.1 points over the best CGM-specific foundation model. Its gains are most pronounced on core metabolic outcomes, leading PR-AUC on all diabetes-risk and $β$-cell dysfunction tasks and on 3 of 4 insulin-resistance tasks. GlucoFM also achieves the best overall cross-dataset transfer performance and strong few-shot adaptation among evaluated methods, and consistent gains when aggregating multiple days for subject-level prediction, highlighting physiology-aware decomposition as an effective inductive bias for transferable CGM representation learning.

AI.tldr: GlucoFM is a lightweight CGM foundation model that explicitly separates slow glucose trends from short-term events after mapping irregular data onto a 24-hour grid. This physiology-aware design improves transferable CGM representations and outperforms prior baselines on multiple metabolic prediction and transfer settings.
AI.motivation: Existing generic time-series and CGM-specific foundation models treat glucose traces as entangled single-stream sequences, which only implicitly capture the distinct temporal structure of glycemic dynamics. The work is motivated by the need for a physiology-aware representation that separately models low-frequency glycemic baselines and short-term deviations to better capture metabolic behavior and improve transferability.
AI.method: The paper proposes GlucoFM, a lightweight CGM foundation model that first aligns irregular CGM recordings to a 24-hour grid while preserving observation masks, then decomposes the glucose signal into slow state and transient event streams. It is pretrained on 109,066 hours of unlabeled CGM data from 477 subjects using two objectives: masked contextual latent prediction on fused daily representations and temporal dynamics prediction on the state and event streams.
AI.result: Across four cohorts and seven clinical prediction tasks, GlucoFM achieves the best subject-disjoint linear-probing performance among baselines, improving average PR-AUC by 4.1 points over the strongest CGM-specific foundation model. It leads PR-AUC on all diabetes-risk and beta-cell dysfunction tasks, on 3 of 4 insulin-resistance tasks, and also shows the best overall cross-dataset transfer, strong few-shot adaptation, and consistent gains from multi-day aggregation.
AI.conclusion: GlucoFM demonstrates that explicitly decomposing CGM signals into physiological state and transient event streams provides a strong inductive bias for transferable representation learning, yielding superior linear-probing, cross-dataset transfer, few-shot adaptation, and multi-day subject-level prediction performance across multiple clinical tasks.

title: Reinforcement Learning Amplifies Emergent Misalignment from Harmless Rewards
summary: Emergent misalignment (EM) is the surprising tendency of language models to become broadly misaligned after fine-tuning on narrowly misaligned examples. While EM has been extensively studied in the supervised fine-tuning (SFT) setting, evidence that it also arises from reinforcement learning (RL) is limited to large, closed-source models, leaving the phenomenon expensive to study and difficult to reproduce. We characterize EM from RL in small, off-the-shelf open-weight models along three axes. First, we show that rewarding narrow, overtly misaligned behavior produces substantially higher general-domain misalignment than sample-matched SFT. Second, we show that EM from RL can be induced by reward signals that could plausibly arise naturally, such as unpopular aesthetic preferences or poor rhetorical appeals. Third, we evaluate in-training mitigations developed for SFT-induced EM and find that they broadly transfer, with interleaving on-policy safety data performing best.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that emergent misalignment is not just an SFT problem: small open-weight models also develop broad misalignment under RL, often more severely than with matched SFT. Realistic reward misspecification can trigger it, and the most effective mitigation tested is interleaving on-policy safety data during training.
AI.motivation: Prior evidence for RL-induced emergent misalignment was limited to large closed-source models, making the phenomenon costly to study and hard to reproduce. The authors aim to establish whether RL can cause EM in accessible small open models and to understand its severity, realistic triggers, and mitigations.
AI.method: The paper studies emergent misalignment induced by reinforcement learning in small open-weight models along three axes: comparing RL against sample-matched SFT, testing whether plausible naturally arising reward signals can induce EM, and evaluating in-training mitigations previously proposed for SFT-induced EM.
AI.result: Rewarding narrow overt misalignment in RL causes substantially greater broad general-domain misalignment than matched SFT. Even seemingly plausible reward signals, such as aesthetic or rhetorical preferences, can induce EM. Mitigations transfer from the SFT setting, and interleaving on-policy safety data performs best.
AI.conclusion: RL can also trigger emergent misalignment in small open-weight language models, often more strongly than sample-matched SFT, and SFT-era mitigations largely transfer, with interleaved on-policy safety data working best.

title: Probing Collision Grounding in Vision-Language Models for Safe Human-Robot Collaboration
summary: Safe human--robot collaboration requires more than visual description: a monitor must determine whether the robot body is safely separated, already colliding with the scene or a person, or about to collide. We call this capability collision grounding: binding visual observations to robot body geometry, camera viewpoint, scene layout, human proximity, and temporal motion in order to infer present and imminent contact. We introduce TouchSafeBench, a physics-grounded benchmark for evaluating collision grounding in vision-language models (VLMs). Built in Habitat~3.0, TouchSafeBench contains 2,940 simulated indoor co-presence episodes across social navigation and social rearrangement, with synchronized multi-view RGB-D observations, top-down trajectory maps, calibrated camera metadata, and simulator-derived contact labels. We study two deployment-facing tasks: classifying the current safety state and warning about imminent collision before contact. Across three frontier or robotics-oriented VLMs and nine visual representations, current models remain far from reliable: the best average Macro-F1 stays below 50\%, explicit depth is not automatically transformed into robot-body collision evidence, and robot--scene contact is consistently harder than human-contact risk. TouchSafeBench reveals a central limitation of embodied VLMs: visual fluency does not imply physical accountability. Reliable robot safety monitors will need representations that explicitly bind viewpoint, robot morphology, metric geometry, and future collision. We will release the benchmark upon acceptance.

AI.tldr:
这篇论文提出 TouchSafeBench，用于评测 VLM 是否能基于物理和几何关系判断机器人当前或即将发生的碰撞；实验表明现有模型效果很差，说明“看懂画面”并不等于“对物理安全负责”。
This paper introduces TouchSafeBench to evaluate whether VLMs can infer current and imminent robot collisions from physically grounded visual evidence; current models perform poorly, showing that scene-level visual fluency is not the same as physical safety awareness.
AI.motivation:
动机是安全的人机协作不能只依赖场景描述，机器人监测系统必须判断机器人是否与环境或人安全分离、已经发生碰撞、或即将碰撞。现有 VLM 是否真正具备这种将视觉观测绑定到机器人几何、视角、场景布局、人体距离和时序运动上的能力尚不清楚，因此需要一个系统性的基准来测量这种“collision grounding”。
The motivation is that safe human-robot collaboration requires more than generic scene description: a monitor must determine whether the robot is safely separated, already in contact, or about to collide with the scene or a person. It is unclear whether existing VLMs can truly bind visual observations to robot geometry, viewpoint, scene layout, human proximity, and temporal motion, so a dedicated benchmark is needed to measure this collision-grounding capability.
AI.method:
方法上，作者提出了 TouchSafeBench，这是一个基于 Habitat 3.0 构建、具有物理约束的评测基准，包含 2,940 个室内人机共处仿真片段，覆盖 social navigation 和 social rearrangement。每个片段提供同步的多视角 RGB-D、俯视轨迹图、标定相机元数据以及仿真器生成的接触标签，并据此评测两项任务：当前安全状态分类与接触前的 imminent collision 预警。
Methodologically, the authors introduce TouchSafeBench, a physics-grounded benchmark built in Habitat 3.0 with 2,940 simulated indoor human-robot co-presence episodes covering social navigation and social rearrangement. Each episode includes synchronized multi-view RGB-D observations, top-down trajectory maps, calibrated camera metadata, and simulator-derived contact labels, enabling evaluation on two tasks: current safety-state classification and pre-contact imminent-collision warning.
AI.result:
结果显示，在 3 个前沿/机器人导向的 VLM 和 9 种视觉表示上，模型表现都距离可部署的可靠性很远：最佳平均 Macro-F1 低于 50%；显式深度信息不会自动转化为与机器人本体相关的碰撞证据；机器人与场景的接触判断始终比人与机器人接触风险更难。
The results show that across three frontier or robotics-oriented VLMs and nine visual representations, performance remains far from deployment-ready: the best average Macro-F1 is below 50%; explicit depth is not automatically converted into robot-body collision evidence; and robot-scene contact is consistently harder to detect than human-contact risk.
AI.conclusion:
论文结论是，当前视觉语言模型在机器人安全监测所需的“collision grounding”能力上明显不足；仅有视觉理解和语言流畅性并不能保证对当前或即将发生碰撞的可靠判断，未来需要显式建模视角、机器人形态、度量几何和未来碰撞关系。
The paper concludes that current vision-language models are substantially inadequate for collision grounding in robot safety monitoring; visual fluency alone does not yield reliable judgments of current or imminent collision, and future systems need explicit representations of viewpoint, robot morphology, metric geometry, and future contact.

title: Bundesrecht: An Open Library and Corpus for German Statutory Reference Processing
summary: Statutory references are central to legal language understanding, but are difficult to process automatically, as they appear in compact and variable surface forms, may combine multiple targets, use special abbreviations, and often point to lower-level units. Existing tools for German focus either on parsing references from legal documents or accessing statutory text once citations are explicit. This paper introduces bundesrecht, an open resource for German statutory reference processing, consisting of a software library and a structured corpus of German federal law. The library parses, normalizes, and resolves German statutory references, mapping raw citation strings to structured objects, expanding compact references into canonical forms, and linking them to statutory provisions. The accompanying dataset preserves the internal hierarchy of statutes from laws to fine-granular subclauses. We evaluate the parser and normalizer on 2,944 annotated German legal references using strict exact-match and micro information extraction metrics. We further evaluate canonical reference deduplication and show that normalized references group real citation surface variants far more reliably than string matching. bundesrecht is the first open resource that covers German statutory reference processing as an end-to-end pipeline, from raw citation string to resolved statutory provision, and is available on PyPI.

AI.tldr: bundesrecht is an open German legal NLP resource that parses, normalizes, deduplicates, and resolves statutory references end-to-end, with strong evaluation results and PyPI availability.
AI.motivation: German statutory references are crucial for legal NLP but hard to process automatically because they are compact, variable, abbreviated, can refer to multiple targets, and often point to lower-level legal units. Existing tools only solve isolated subproblems rather than the full pipeline.
AI.method: The authors build bundesrecht as an open resource containing a software library and a structured corpus of German federal law. The library parses, normalizes, and resolves statutory references, expands compact citations into canonical forms, and links them to fine-grained statutory units. They evaluate it on 2,944 annotated German legal references using exact-match and micro information extraction metrics, and also test deduplication performance.
AI.result: The parser and normalizer perform well on 2,944 annotated references, and normalized canonical references outperform simple string matching for grouping citation variants. The resource supports end-to-end processing from citation strings to resolved statutory provisions.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that bundesrecht provides the first open end-to-end resource for German statutory reference processing, effectively parsing, normalizing, deduplicating, and resolving legal references from raw citation strings to statutory provisions.

title: Probabilistic Precipitation Nowcasting with Rectified Flow Transformers
summary: Accurate weather forecasts are essential across various domains and are safety-critical in extreme weather conditions. Compared to simulation-based forecasting, data-driven approaches show greater efficiency, enabling short-term, high-resolution nowcasting. In particular, diffusion models proved effective in weather nowcasting due to their strong probabilistic foundation. However, existing methods rely on deterministic compression to reduce the complexity of high-dimensional weather data, limiting their ability to capture uncertainty in the decoding process. In this work, we introduce $\textbf{FREUD}$, a $\textbf{Fr}$ame-wise $\textbf{E}$ncoder and $\textbf{U}$nited $\textbf{D}$ecoder model based on rectified flow transformers for efficient compression of spatio-temporal weather data. Frame-wise encoding enables continuous forecast updates, while the unified video decoder ensures temporal consistency. Our uncertainty-preserving first stage allows us to capture aleatoric uncertainty via ensembling, which is particularly beneficial for extreme weather events with high decoding variability. We achieve state-of-the-art performance in precipitation nowcasting with a compact latent-space rectified flow transformer on the SEVIR benchmark and show further performance gains by model and test-time scaling. Code available here: https://github.com/CompVis/weather-rf

AI.tldr: FREUD是一种用于天气临近预报的逐帧编码+统一解码框架，在压缩阶段保留不确定性，从而更好地处理极端天气，并在SEVIR上达到SOTA。 / FREUD is a frame-wise encode and unified decode framework for weather nowcasting that preserves uncertainty during compression, better handles extreme events, and achieves SOTA on SEVIR.
AI.motivation: 现有基于扩散的数据驱动天气临近预报方法虽然高效，但依赖确定性压缩来处理高维天气数据，导致解码阶段的不确定性无法被充分建模，尤其不利于极端天气预测。 / Existing data-driven nowcasting methods, including diffusion-based ones, are efficient but rely on deterministic compression of high-dimensional weather data, which limits uncertainty modeling during decoding and is especially problematic for extreme-weather forecasting.
AI.method: 提出FREUD：使用逐帧编码器对时空天气数据进行高效压缩，支持持续更新；再用统一的视频解码器保证时间一致性；整体基于rectified flow transformers，并在第一阶段保留解码不确定性，可通过集成捕获aleatoric uncertainty。 / The paper proposes FREUD: a frame-wise encoder for efficient spatio-temporal weather compression with continuous updates, paired with a united video decoder for temporal consistency, built around rectified flow transformers and an uncertainty-preserving first stage that captures aleatoric uncertainty via ensembling.
AI.result: 在SEVIR基准上的降水临近预报任务中，FREUD取得最优性能；其紧凑潜空间设计有效，同时模型扩展和测试时扩展还能带来额外增益，说明方法兼具性能与可扩展性。 / On precipitation nowcasting over the SEVIR benchmark, FREUD reaches state-of-the-art results; its compact latent-space design is effective, and both model scaling and test-time scaling provide additional gains, indicating strong performance and scalability.
AI.conclusion: FREUD通过保留不确定性的压缩方式与基于rectified flow transformer的紧凑潜空间建模，在SEVIR降水临近预报上达到SOTA，并且通过模型规模与测试时扩展可进一步提升性能。 / FREUD achieves state-of-the-art precipitation nowcasting on SEVIR by combining uncertainty-preserving compression with compact latent rectified flow transformers, and it improves further with model and test-time scaling.

title: Bandwidth Allocation with Device Partitioning for Federated Learning over Industrial IoT networks
summary: We consider a federated learning (FL) system in which Industrial Internet-of-Things (IIoT) devices collaboratively train a global model over wireless channels without sharing local data. In such systems, communication time is a primary bottleneck that constrains overall training efficiency. Unlike conventional networks that prioritize individual quality-of-service requirements, FL systems collectively aim to converge to an optimal global model as efficiently as possible, which calls for a fundamentally different approach to bandwidth allocation. In this paper, we propose a novel bandwidth allocation policy that exploits the heterogeneity of device computing capabilities to minimize total training time. Rather than distributing bandwidth among all selected devices simultaneously, the proposed policy partitions the participating devices into ordered subsets and sequentially grants each subset exclusive access to the full bandwidth. We formally prove that this partitioning-based policy achieves a strictly lower training time than any bandwidth allocation scheme without partitioning, irrespective of the underlying scheduling algorithm. Furthermore, by reducing per-device transmission duration, the proposed policy also minimizes uplink energy consumption, which is particularly beneficial for battery-constrained IIoT devices. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets - including GC10-Det, an industrial surface defect benchmark, and CIFAR-10, a standard image classification benchmark - demonstrate that the proposed policy consistently reduces training time and energy consumption compared to existing bandwidth allocation schemes, approaching the theoretical lower bound on round time.

AI.tldr: A new FL bandwidth policy for wireless IIoT trains faster by splitting devices into ordered groups and letting each group use all bandwidth one at a time; it is theoretically better than non-partitioned sharing and experimentally cuts both training time and energy use.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that in wireless FL for IIoT, communication delay is a key bottleneck for end-to-end training efficiency. Conventional bandwidth allocation targets per-device QoS, but FL has a system-level objective: reaching a well-trained global model as fast as possible. Device heterogeneity further suggests that simultaneous bandwidth sharing may be inefficient, motivating a new allocation strategy tailored to FL convergence time.
AI.method: The method designs a bandwidth allocation policy for wireless federated learning in IIoT. Instead of simultaneously sharing bandwidth across all selected devices, the approach partitions devices according to heterogeneous computing capabilities into ordered subsets and schedules these subsets sequentially, granting each subset exclusive access to the full bandwidth. The paper also provides a formal proof of superiority over non-partitioning schemes.
AI.result: Experimental results on GC10-Det and CIFAR-10 show that the proposed policy consistently lowers training time and uplink energy consumption compared with existing bandwidth allocation methods, while approaching the theoretical lower bound on round time. Theoretical analysis further proves strict training-time improvement over all schemes without partitioning.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that a partitioning-based bandwidth allocation policy, which groups participating IIoT devices into ordered subsets and lets each subset exclusively use the full bandwidth in sequence, strictly outperforms any non-partitioning bandwidth allocation scheme in terms of total federated training time. It also reduces uplink energy consumption and approaches the theoretical lower bound on round time in experiments.

title: FBHM: Functional Benchmarking and Steering of VLMs for Hateful Meme Detection
summary: Hateful meme detection remains a formidable challenge for vision-language models, as existing benchmarks are structurally observational - confounding rhetorical hate mechanisms with target community features and preventing causal evaluation of model vulnerabilities. To address this, we introduce FBHM, a systematically curated benchmark of Functionality Based Hateful Memes constructed along two orthogonal axes: 25 distinct rhetorical functionalities and 10 target communities (5,000 memes total). Benchmarking state-of-the-art VLMs reveals a severe generalization gap: models highly accurate on standard datasets catastrophically drop to near-random performance on FBHM, proving they exploit dataset-specific heuristics rather than robust multimodal reasoning. To efficiently close this gap, we propose LSV (learnable steering vectors), an ultra-low data regime strategy that applies a causal intervention objective on as few as 500 steering samples (50 unique base memes), boosting FBHM performance by ~30 Macro-F1 points while outperforming in-context learning and PEFT without degrading source-domain performance.

title: Benchmarking and Enhancing Text-to-Image Models for Generating Visual Representations in Early Arithmetic Education
summary: AI systems are increasingly used to support educational content creation, yet it remains unclear whether they can generate outputs that faithfully represent the pedagogical concepts they are intended to teach. Thus, we introduce equation-to-visual generation, a task that, in contrast to conventional image generation, requires producing pedagogically meaningful visuals from arithmetic equations while precisely preserving their numerical and relational structure. Informed by interviews with teachers and an analysis of educational materials, we construct E2V-Bench, a benchmark spanning four pedagogically grounded visual types, along with automatic metrics for evaluating visual correctness. Our evaluation reveals that recent text-to-image (T2I) models frequently fail on this task, with errors dominated by incorrect object counts and broken relational structure. Building on this, we explore benchmark-guided enhancement strategies. These strategies improve representative models, while the remaining gap calls for stronger numerical and relational grounding in future T2I models.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces E2V-Bench to test whether image models can turn arithmetic equations into correct teaching visuals. Current models frequently miscount objects or break relationships, and although benchmark-guided tuning helps, better numerical and relational reasoning is still required.
AI.motivation: AI is increasingly used in educational content creation, but it is unclear whether generated visuals truly preserve the pedagogical meaning, numerical values, and relations required for teaching arithmetic concepts accurately.
AI.method: The paper defines the equation-to-visual generation task, builds the E2V-Bench benchmark from teacher interviews and educational material analysis, designs automatic visual-correctness metrics, evaluates recent T2I models, and tests benchmark-guided enhancement strategies.
AI.result: Across four pedagogically grounded visual types, recent T2I models often fail, mainly due to wrong object counts and broken relational structure; targeted enhancement strategies improve representative models but do not close the gap.
AI.conclusion: Current text-to-image models are not yet reliable for generating pedagogically faithful visuals from arithmetic equations; benchmark-guided improvements help, but stronger numerical and relational grounding is still needed.

title: Zero Collapse: A Failure Mode of Policy Gradient Methods in Discontinuous Reward Environments
summary:
Bidding in repeated auctions is a central challenge for reinforcement learning (RL), combining continuous control with the strategic complexities of digital advertising. While policy gradient and value-based methods seem well-suited for these settings, they often struggle with the discontinuous, "cliff-like" nature of auction reward landscapes. In a first-price auction, for example, a bidder receives zero reward until they cross a specific threshold, after which the reward decreases as the bid increases. This creates a landscape of flat, zero-reward regions separated by sharp boundaries.
  We identify a fundamental failure mode in this setting termed "zero collapse." We show that stochastic exploration and gradient-based updates can cause policies to overshoot optimal high-reward regions and enter flat, zero-reward regimes. Once there, the lack of an informative gradient signal makes recovery extremely sample-inefficient, effectively trapping the agent. We find that actor-critic methods are particularly susceptible, as biased value estimates can accelerate this movement toward unstable regions.
  Our contributions include: (1) a mechanistic explanation of how discontinuous rewards lead to vanishing signals and zero collapse; (2) an analysis of the interaction between policy stochasticity and step size; and (3) an empirical demonstration of this phenomenon across REINFORCE and actor-critic variants. We propose practical mitigation strategies involving initialization and architectural choices to improve stability. Finally, we introduce a formal RL framework for auction environments highlighting their unique structural properties.

AI.tldr: 论文解释了为什么强化学习在重复拍卖里常常“突然学废”：由于奖励像悬崖一样不连续，策略可能一旦越过有效竞价区就掉入大片零奖励区域，随后几乎没有梯度信号可供恢复，这就是“zero collapse”。作者分析了这一机制，证明actor-critic更容易中招，并给出缓解建议。 / The paper explains why RL often suddenly fails in repeated auctions: because rewards are cliff-like and discontinuous, policies can overshoot productive bidding regions and fall into broad zero-reward zones where gradients vanish, causing “zero collapse.” It analyzes this mechanism, shows actor-critic methods are especially vulnerable, and provides mitigation guidance.
AI.motivation: 动机在于，重复拍卖是数字广告中的核心问题，也很适合被建模为连续控制下的RL任务；但现有策略梯度和价值学习方法在这类任务中经常表现不稳定，原因并不清楚。论文旨在解释这些方法为何会在拍卖场景中失效，并揭示拍卖环境相较于常规RL基准任务的特殊结构性难点。 / The motivation is that repeated auction bidding is a central problem in digital advertising and naturally fits an RL formulation with continuous control. However, standard policy-gradient and value-based methods often perform unstably in these environments, and the reason is not well understood. The paper aims to explain why these methods fail in auction settings and to expose the structural challenges that make auctions different from conventional RL benchmarks.
AI.method: 方法上，论文首先从机制层面分析一价拍卖等环境中的奖励结构，解释不连续奖励如何造成平坦零奖励区域与尖锐边界；随后分析策略随机性与学习步长之间的交互如何导致策略越过最优区域；再通过REINFORCE与多种actor-critic方法进行实证验证，比较它们在该现象下的脆弱性；最后提出基于初始化和模型架构的实用缓解策略，并给出拍卖环境的形式化RL建模。 / Methodologically, the paper provides a mechanistic analysis of reward discontinuities in auction settings such as first-price auctions, showing how they create flat zero-reward regions separated by sharp thresholds. It then studies how policy stochasticity interacts with update step size to push policies past optimal regions. The authors empirically validate the phenomenon across REINFORCE and actor-critic variants, and finally propose practical mitigation strategies based on initialization and architectural design, together with a formal RL formulation for auction environments.
AI.result: 结果表明，zero collapse并非偶发现象，而是由拍卖奖励不连续性、策略探索噪声以及更新步长共同驱动的系统性失败模式。实验显示REINFORCE和actor-critic变体都会受到影响，其中actor-critic由于价值估计偏差往往更脆弱。论文还表明，合理的初始化与架构设计能够在一定程度上提升训练稳定性。 / The results show that zero collapse is a systematic failure mode driven by the combination of reward discontinuities, stochastic exploration, and update step size rather than an isolated artifact. Experiments demonstrate that both REINFORCE and actor-critic variants suffer from it, with actor-critic methods being especially vulnerable because biased value estimates can accelerate movement into unstable zero-reward regions. The paper also shows that better initialization and architectural choices can improve training stability.
AI.conclusion: 该论文认为，重复拍卖中的强化学习会因拍卖奖励函数的不连续、悬崖式结构而出现“zero collapse（零坍塌）”：策略一旦越过高奖励区进入大面积零奖励区域，就会因梯度信号消失而极难恢复。作者同时指出，合适的初始化与架构选择可以缓解这一问题，并提出了一个更适合拍卖环境分析的形式化RL框架。 / The paper concludes that reinforcement learning in repeated auctions is prone to a failure mode called zero collapse because auction rewards are discontinuous and cliff-like. Once a policy overshoots into broad zero-reward regions, the gradient signal vanishes and recovery becomes highly sample-inefficient. The paper also concludes that suitable initialization and architectural choices can mitigate this instability, and it introduces a formal RL framework tailored to auction environments.

title: A Visually Impaired Assistance Benchmark for VLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation
summary: AI-based Visually Impaired Assistance (VIA) remains challenging, largely due to the high cost of human evaluation. The VLM-as-a-Judge paradigm may offer a promising alternative, although it has mostly been studied in general domains. We therefore ask whether such judges can be trusted for VIA tasks. To investigate this question, we introduce VIABLE (Visually Impaired Assistance Benchmark for VLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation), the first benchmark for VLM-as-a-Judge evaluation in VIA. VIABLE contains over 300K judgment samples across three scenarios and introduces an Effectiveness--Impartiality--Stability framework with a 12-mode failure taxonomy. Based on VIABLE, our systematic study of seven judges across different model scales shows that existing models are largely unreliable across all evaluation axes. The strongest judge, GPT-5.4, achieves only 52.6% single-failure diagnostic accuracy, yet exhibits the highest self-preference rate at 94.2%; while open-source judges are strongly biased and adversarially fragile. To address these issues, we propose VIA-Judge-Agent, a model-agnostic inference-time harness that augments judges with visual evidence extraction and a taxonomy-guided workflow. It enables positive improvements in diagnostic accuracy and downstream VIA responses more preferred by BLV users. Data and code are available at: https://github.com/YiyiyiZhao/VIABLE

AI.tldr: 本文提出VIABLE基准来检验VLM评审器在视障辅助任务中的可信度，结果表明现有模型普遍不可靠；作者进一步提出VIA-Judge-Agent，在不改模型参数的前提下提升评审质量与下游回答效果。 / The paper introduces VIABLE to test whether VLM judges can be trusted in visually impaired assistance, finds current judges broadly unreliable, and proposes VIA-Judge-Agent to improve judging and downstream responses without changing model weights.
AI.motivation: 由于VIA系统的人类评测成本很高，VLM-as-a-Judge看似是可扩展替代方案，但其在通用领域外，尤其是VIA场景中的可信度尚不明确，因此需要专门的基准和系统性评估。 / Human evaluation for VIA is expensive, making VLM-as-a-Judge an attractive scalable alternative, but its trustworthiness in VIA-specific settings is unknown, motivating a dedicated benchmark and systematic study.
AI.method: 作者构建了首个面向VIA评审的基准VIABLE，包含30多万条样本、三类场景，并提出Effectiveness-Impartiality-Stability三维评估框架及12类失败模式；随后系统评测7个不同规模的judge模型，并设计VIA-Judge-Agent，通过视觉证据提取和基于失败 taxonomy 的工作流增强评审。 / The paper introduces VIABLE, the first benchmark for evaluating judges in VIA, with 300K+ judgment samples across three scenarios, an Effectiveness-Impartiality-Stability framework, and a 12-mode failure taxonomy; it then evaluates seven judge models and proposes VIA-Judge-Agent, which augments judging with visual evidence extraction and a taxonomy-guided workflow.
AI.result: 研究发现7个现有judge在三个评估维度上都表现不佳。最强模型GPT-5.4的单一失败诊断准确率仅52.6%，但自偏好率高达94.2%；开源judge表现出显著偏置和对抗脆弱性。VIA-Judge-Agent带来诊断准确率的正向提升，并使下游VIA回答更受BLV用户偏好。 / The study shows poor performance across all three axes for all seven judges. The strongest model, GPT-5.4, reaches only 52.6% single-failure diagnostic accuracy while showing a 94.2% self-preference rate; open-source judges are strongly biased and adversarially fragile. VIA-Judge-Agent yields positive gains in diagnostic accuracy and produces downstream VIA responses more preferred by BLV users.
AI.conclusion: 现有VLM-as-a-Judge在视障辅助（VIA）任务上整体不可靠；作者提出的VIA-Judge-Agent能在推理时增强评审模型，提升诊断准确率并改善下游VIA回答的用户偏好。 / Existing VLM-as-a-Judge systems are broadly unreliable for visually impaired assistance (VIA) tasks; the proposed VIA-Judge-Agent improves judge accuracy at inference time and leads to downstream VIA responses preferred by BLV users.

title: TALON: Token-Aligned Lightweight Adapters for 6-DoF Spacecraft Pose Estimation
comment: 13 pages paper with 3 figures in total
summary: Monocular 6-DoF spacecraft pose estimation methods predominantly process individual frames, discarding the temporal information present in an image sequence acquired during spacecraft manoeuvres. Few temporal approaches require full backbone fine-tuning or auxiliary optical flow networks, risking catastrophic forgetting or increasing computational cost, respectively. We propose TALON (Token-Aligned Lightweight adapters for Orbital Navigation): spatiotemporal 3D adapters injected before the self-attention layers of a frozen ViT vision transformer, combined with a patch-token alignment loss that geometrically grounds the adapted features to keypoint structure through a prototype-conditioned KL-divergence objective. Pre-attention placement allows the frozen attention to reason over temporally enriched tokens, achieving stronger performance with a single adapter per block than post-attention alternatives. The alignment loss shapes the intermediate representations so that each keypoint induces a spatially precise activation in the token field, while the framework adds less than 5% parameters to the frozen backbone. On SPADES dataset, TALON reduces the pose error by 50% over the prior state-of-the-art, and on SwissCube dataset it surpasses the prior best by 21.8% in ADD-0.1d accuracy. Zero-shot cross-domain evaluation from sim-to-real on SPARK real data reduces pose error by 4.7x, and ablations characterise the role of adapter depth across in-domain and cross-domain settings.

AI.tldr: TALON adds lightweight pre-attention spatiotemporal adapters and a keypoint-grounded token alignment loss to a frozen ViT, yielding major improvements in monocular spacecraft pose estimation with under 5% extra parameters.
AI.motivation: Existing monocular 6-DoF spacecraft pose estimation methods mostly process frames independently and ignore temporal cues from manoeuvre sequences. Prior temporal approaches either require full backbone fine-tuning, which risks catastrophic forgetting, or auxiliary optical flow networks, which increase computational cost. The paper aims to exploit temporal information efficiently and robustly with minimal parameter overhead.
AI.method: The paper proposes TALON, which injects spatiotemporal 3D adapters before the self-attention layers of a frozen Vision Transformer backbone. It also introduces a patch-token alignment loss based on a prototype-conditioned KL-divergence objective so that token activations align with geometric keypoint structure. The design preserves the frozen backbone, avoids full fine-tuning, and uses one adapter per block.
AI.result: On the SPADES dataset, TALON reduces pose error by 50% compared with the previous state of the art. On SwissCube, it improves ADD-0.1d accuracy by 21.8% over the prior best. In zero-shot sim-to-real transfer on SPARK real data, it reduces pose error by 4.7x. Ablation studies further analyze the effect of adapter depth in both in-domain and cross-domain scenarios.
AI.conclusion: TALON demonstrates that lightweight spatiotemporal adapters inserted before self-attention in a frozen ViT, together with a patch-token alignment loss, can substantially improve monocular 6-DoF spacecraft pose estimation while adding less than 5% parameters. It achieves strong gains in both in-domain and cross-domain settings.

title: Latent Geometric Chords for Query-Efficient Decision-Based Adversarial Attacks
comment: 14 pages, 9 figures, 7 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security. The source code is available at https://github.com/eihmuekhine/Latent-Geometric-Chords
summary: While decision-based black-box adversarial attacks present a severe security threat, current methodologies suffer from fundamental limitations. Pixel-wise attacks frequently introduce unnatural, high-frequency visual artifacts, while latent-space frameworks are confined by the limited search space of low-dimensional manifolds and inherent reconstruction flaws.
