To resolve these limitations, we propose Latent Geometric Chords (LGC) for Query-Efficient Decision-Based Adversarial Attacks alongside a variant, LGC-H. At its core, LGC navigates decision boundaries by executing a curvature-aware geometric search within a compressed semantic manifold. To guarantee high visual fidelity and circumvent dimensionality bottlenecks, we introduce a Residual-based Adversarial Generation (RAG) mechanism. RAG isolates semantic perturbations as geometric chords and superimposes them directly onto the original source image. RAG substantially resolves baseline reconstruction flaws and effectively doubles the permissible search space dimensions. Experimental results demonstrate that LGC achieves robust cross-dataset transferability and substantially outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Notably, our method, LGC, minimizes perturbation magnitudes while achieving state-of-the-art visual fidelity--with a Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) exceeding 0.99 and a Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity (LPIPS) below 0.01 at 5000 queries--and sustaining high attack success rates under stringent perceptual constraints, successfully compromising adversarially trained robust models. The source code is available at: https://github.com/eihmuekhine/Latent-Geometric-Chords.

AI.tldr: LGC is a decision-based black-box adversarial attack that searches decision boundaries in latent space while using residual composition to keep perturbations realistic. It reduces perturbation size, improves image quality, expands the usable search space, and beats prior methods in efficiency, transferability, and robustness.
AI.motivation: Existing decision-based black-box attacks have two core weaknesses: pixel-wise methods often create unnatural high-frequency artifacts, and latent-space approaches are restricted by low-dimensional manifolds and reconstruction errors. The work is motivated by the need for attacks that are both query-efficient and visually natural under strict perceptual constraints.
AI.method: The paper proposes Latent Geometric Chords (LGC), which performs a curvature-aware geometric search along decision boundaries in a compressed semantic manifold, and Residual-based Adversarial Generation (RAG), which extracts semantic perturbations as geometric chords and adds them back to the original image to preserve fidelity and enlarge the effective search space. A variant called LGC-H is also introduced.
AI.result: Experiments show that LGC outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, has strong cross-dataset transferability, maintains high attack success rates even against adversarially trained robust models, and achieves excellent visual quality metrics at 5000 queries, including SSIM > 0.99 and LPIPS < 0.01.
AI.conclusion: LGC and LGC-H provide a more query-efficient and visually faithful decision-based black-box adversarial attack framework by combining curvature-aware latent-space search with residual-based perturbation composition, overcoming the artifact issues of pixel-wise methods and the dimensional/reconstruction limits of prior latent-space methods.

title: Inverse Reinforcement Learning without an Optimal Demonstrator: A Feasible Reward Set Approach
summary: Inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) typically assumes demonstrations from a single optimal demonstrator, but in many applications data come from multiple imperfect demonstrators with heterogeneous suboptimality levels. We study reward learning in this setting through a feasible-reward-set framework: for each demonstrator, we encode its declared suboptimality level as a linear constraint and intersect the resulting feasible sets across demonstrators. Our theoretical analysis shows that the joint feasible set shrinks monotonically as data are added, and we give an exact characterization of when a new demonstrator strictly tightens it. We further establish two recovery guarantees for the feasible reward set of the ground-truth optimal demonstrator: one bound depends on closeness to the optimal occupancy, while the other requires only sufficient coverage and no near-optimal demonstrator. On the practical side, we introduce strategies to address the inherent reward ambiguity in the obtained reward set and provide an offline algorithm with function approximation for high-dimensional environments. Experiments in tabular grid-world and large language model (LLM) fine-tuning settings are consistent with the theoretical predictions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework over baselines.

AI.tldr: The paper extends IRL to multiple imperfect demonstrators by intersecting reward constraints derived from each demonstrator's suboptimality level, yielding solid theory and strong empirical results in both classic control-style and LLM fine-tuning tasks.
AI.motivation: Standard IRL assumes a single optimal demonstrator, but real-world data often come from multiple imperfect demonstrators with different levels of suboptimality, so reward learning needs a framework that can aggregate such heterogeneous demonstrations robustly.
AI.method: The paper models each demonstrator's declared suboptimality as a linear constraint on the reward, intersects feasible reward sets across demonstrators, analyzes when additional data strictly tighten the joint set, proposes ambiguity-resolution strategies, and develops an offline algorithm with function approximation for high-dimensional environments.
AI.result: Theoretical results show monotonic shrinking of the joint feasible reward set as more demonstrators are added, exact conditions for strict tightening, and two recovery guarantees for the ground-truth optimal demonstrator's feasible set. Empirically, the method outperforms baselines in grid-world and LLM fine-tuning experiments.
AI.conclusion: A feasible-reward-set approach can learn rewards from multiple imperfect demonstrators with heterogeneous suboptimality, offers monotonic set-shrinking properties and recovery guarantees, and works effectively in both tabular and high-dimensional offline settings.

title: Unlocking Fine-Grained Translation Quality Estimation in LRMs through Synergistically Evolving Implicit and Explicit Reasoning
summary: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) still struggle with fine-grained translation quality estimation (QE), even with long reasoning chains. We argue that LRMs already possess strong multilingual capabilities, while the core challenge stems from the intrinsic difficulty of learning the fine-grained QE task. In this paper, we propose RIEQE (Reasoning both Implicitly and Explicitly for QE), a simple two-stage training framework that enables the co-evolution of implicit (layer-wise) and explicit (token-wise) reasoning capabilities. To make implicit reasoning feasible, we first decompose the complex QE task into straightforward subtasks. Based on this, our two-stage approach applies: (1) NonThinking-SFT, Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) without reasoning chains to directly boost the model's implicit reasoning tendency and capability; and (2) Thinking-RLVR, standard Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Reward (RLVR) to subsequently strengthen explicit reasoning. Results demonstrate that implicit and explicit reasoning synergistically co-evolve under our framework. On the WMT test sets, RIEQE based on Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 surpasses all baselines in explicit reasoning performance, while its implicit reasoning capability is also comparable to the best current encoder-based models. We further provide evidence for the synergistic collaboration between implicit and explicit reasoning, showing how they mutually benefit each other.

AI.tldr: RIEQE先用无推理链监督微调打牢隐式推理，再用可验证奖励强化学习激活显式推理，从而让两者协同提升翻译质量评估。 / RIEQE first builds implicit reasoning via no-chain SFT, then strengthens explicit reasoning with verifiable-reward RL, yielding synergistic gains for translation quality estimation.
AI.motivation: 作者认为LRM并非缺少多语言能力，真正瓶颈在于细粒度QE任务本身难以学习，因此需要一种能同时提升隐式与显式推理的训练策略。 / The motivation is that LRMs likely already have strong multilingual competence; the real bottleneck is the intrinsic difficulty of learning fine-grained QE, which calls for a training strategy that improves both implicit and explicit reasoning.
AI.method: 方法是一个两阶段框架：先将复杂QE任务拆解为更直接的子任务，再进行NonThinking-SFT以增强层级式隐式推理能力，随后进行Thinking-RLVR以强化基于token的显式推理。 / The method is a two-stage framework: first decompose complex QE into simpler subtasks, then apply NonThinking-SFT to strengthen layer-wise implicit reasoning, followed by Thinking-RLVR to reinforce token-wise explicit reasoning.
AI.result: 基于Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507的RIEQE在WMT测试集上取得最强显式推理QE表现，同时其隐式推理能力也达到与当前最佳encoder-based模型相当的水平，并验证了两类推理之间的互促关系。 / RIEQE built on Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 achieves the best explicit-reasoning QE performance on WMT benchmarks, while its implicit reasoning is competitive with the strongest encoder-based models, with evidence that the two reasoning modes mutually reinforce each other.
AI.conclusion: RIEQE通过两阶段训练让隐式推理与显式推理协同进化，在细粒度翻译质量评估上显著提升LRM表现，并在WMT测试集上优于显式推理基线。 / RIEQE enables the co-evolution of implicit and explicit reasoning through a two-stage training framework, substantially improving LRM performance on fine-grained translation QE and outperforming explicit-reasoning baselines on WMT test sets.

title: HiERO-StepG @ Ego4D Step Grounding Challenge: hierarchical activity understanding enables zero-shot step grounding
comment: Technical report for the Ego4D Goal Step - Step Grounding challenge at CVPR 2026, derived from arXiv:2505.12911
summary: Procedural activities follow well-defined structures: whether we consider a cooking recipe or a mechanic repairing a car, these activities naturally decompose in a hierarchy of steps and sub-steps. Traditional approaches for step grounding require extensive annotations and scale poorly. Instead, we argue that such hierarchical structure can emerge naturally from uncurated videos of human activities through recurring patterns of co-occurring actions and activities. Our approach builds on HiERO, a weakly-supervised representation learning approach that maps close in the feature space actions that are functionally related to each other, leveraging only fine-grained action-level narrations. In this feature space, procedure steps can be detected by a simple clustering, with no additional task-specific fine-tuning. For the Ego4D Step Grounding challenge, we augment this approach by ensuring fine and coarse level agreement in step assignments, enforcing strict temporal monotonicity of the grounded steps and post-processing the detected steps to reduce the impact of noisy predictions. We call this approach HiERO-StepG and it achieves 56.27 % on the R@1 (IoU = 0.3) metric on the global leaderboard at submission time, ranking second while being completely zero-shot and not requiring procedure-specific annotations. Project page: https://github.com/andreazenotto/HiERO-StepG.

AI.tldr: TL;DR: 论文提出一种零样本步骤定位方法 HiERO-StepG，通过弱监督学习动作层级表示并结合聚类、层级一致性和时间约束，从未整理视频中自动发现并定位 procedural steps，在 Ego4D 上以无需额外标注的方式取得第二名。 / TL;DR: The paper introduces HiERO-StepG, a zero-shot step grounding method that learns hierarchical action representations under weak supervision and combines clustering, hierarchy agreement, and temporal constraints to automatically discover and ground procedural steps from uncurated videos, reaching second place on Ego4D without extra annotations.
AI.motivation: 动机在于 procedural activities 天然具有层级结构，但传统 step grounding 方法依赖大量标注且扩展性差。作者希望从未经整理的人类活动视频中，直接利用动作与活动的重复共现模式，让层级步骤结构自然涌现出来。 / The motivation is that procedural activities are inherently hierarchical, while traditional step grounding methods require extensive annotations and scale poorly. The authors aim to let hierarchical step structure emerge directly from uncurated human-activity videos via recurring co-occurrence patterns of actions and activities.
AI.method: 方法基于 HiERO：利用细粒度动作级 narration 学习特征空间，使功能相关的动作在特征空间中更接近；随后通过简单聚类检测 procedure steps，无需额外任务特定微调。在此基础上，HiERO-StepG 增加了细粒度与粗粒度步骤分配一致性约束、严格时间单调性约束，以及针对噪声预测的后处理。 / The method builds on HiERO: it learns a feature space from fine-grained action narrations where functionally related actions are close, then detects procedure steps via simple clustering without task-specific fine-tuning. HiERO-StepG further adds fine/coarse assignment agreement, strict temporal monotonicity constraints, and post-processing to suppress noisy predictions.
AI.result: 在 Ego4D Step Grounding challenge 上，HiERO-StepG 在 R@1 (IoU=0.3) 上达到 56.27%，提交时位列全球排行榜第二；同时该方法是完全 zero-shot 的，不需要 procedure-specific annotations。 / On the Ego4D Step Grounding challenge, HiERO-StepG achieves 56.27% R@1 at IoU=0.3 and ranked second on the global leaderboard at submission time; importantly, it is fully zero-shot and does not require procedure-specific annotations.
AI.conclusion: 提出了 HiERO-StepG，一种基于弱监督层次表示学习的零样本步骤定位方法；在无需 procedure-specific annotations 的前提下，通过层级一致性、时间单调性约束和后处理，能够在 Ego4D Step Grounding 上取得接近 SOTA 的成绩并获得排行榜第二。 / The paper proposes HiERO-StepG, a weakly supervised, zero-shot step grounding method built on hierarchical representation learning; without procedure-specific annotations, it achieves near-SOTA performance on Ego4D Step Grounding and ranked second on the leaderboard through hierarchy agreement, temporal monotonicity, and post-processing.

title: LLM Judges Inconsistently Disagree Across Safety Criteria and Harm Categories
summary: We evaluate the consistency of automated judges in conducting a multi-dimensional safety evaluation in a reference-free setup. Our results indicate that Large Language Models are unreliable judges in identifying safety issues related to machine-generated advice in regulated domains such as finance, although they are more reliable at identifying more overt forms of unsafe/harmful content such as violence. The degree of inconsistency in a model's judgments can vary significantly by the chosen safety criteria and can be impacted by the language of the content and its linguistic style as well. Finally, there is high disagreement among different judges for the same output, across domains, safety criteria, and languages. These findings provide new insights on the practice of using LLMs as evaluators and offer several recommendations for practitioners on how to use automated judges in practical scenarios.

AI.tldr: TL;DR: LLM judges are not reliably consistent for safety evaluation, especially for nuanced advice in regulated domains; agreement depends on criterion, language, and style, and different judges often strongly disagree.
AI.motivation: 动机/Motivation: 业界常将 LLM 用作自动评估器，但其在安全评测中的稳定性与可信度尚不清楚，尤其是在多标准、跨语言和受监管场景下。
AI.method: 方法/Method: 论文在 reference-free 设置下，使用多种大语言模型作为自动评审者，对不同领域、不同安全标准、不同语言与语言风格的机器生成内容进行多维安全评估，并比较同一模型前后判断一致性以及不同评审模型之间的一致性。
AI.result: 结果/Result: 研究发现一致性会因安全标准而显著变化，并受到内容语言和文体影响；不同自动评审者对同一输出在跨领域、跨标准、跨语言条件下存在高度分歧。
AI.conclusion: 结论/Conclusion: 在无参考的多维安全评估中，大语言模型作为自动评审者表现出明显不一致性；它们更容易识别显性有害内容，但在金融等受监管领域识别机器生成建议中的安全问题时不可靠。

title: Beyond Classification: Dynamic Adapter Routing for Continual Multimodal Retrieval
summary: While retrieval is a core function of vision-language models, continually updating these models for retrieval tasks remains critically underexplored. Existing work often approaches continual retrieval through the lens of class-incremental learning (CIL), evaluating both standard CIL methods and retrieval-oriented adaptations in settings that may not fully capture the retrieval-specific dynamics. To address this, we introduce a new, principled evaluation framework for continual multimodal retrieval (CMR) spanning diverse visual domains, and systematically evaluate common approaches within this setting. Our empirical analysis shows that standard CIL methods fail to yield meaningful gains in our more challenging scenario. Therefore, we propose Dynamic Adapter Routing (DAR), a novel approach based on adapters selected through prototype-based routing and combined via model merging.DAR achieves superior performance over the previous baselines and demonstrates strong generalization under out-of-distribution evaluation. Our results highlights the unique challenges of CMR and encourages further research in this direction.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that continual image-text retrieval is not well solved by standard continual learning methods, introduces a better benchmark for this problem, and proposes DAR, an adapter-routing and model-merging method that achieves the best overall performance.
AI.motivation: Prior work treats continual retrieval mainly as a class-incremental learning problem, which does not fully reflect retrieval-specific challenges. The authors aim to build a more appropriate evaluation framework and identify methods that actually work for continual retrieval.
AI.method: The paper introduces a principled continual multimodal retrieval (CMR) benchmark across diverse visual domains, systematically evaluates existing continual learning and retrieval-adapted baselines, and proposes Dynamic Adapter Routing (DAR), which selects adapters through prototype-based routing and combines them via model merging.
AI.result: Empirical results show that standard CIL methods do not produce meaningful improvements in the proposed challenging CMR setting. DAR outperforms prior baselines and generalizes well under out-of-distribution evaluation.
AI.conclusion: Continual multimodal retrieval requires evaluation settings tailored to retrieval dynamics; standard class-incremental learning methods are insufficient, while the proposed Dynamic Adapter Routing (DAR) provides stronger in-distribution and out-of-distribution retrieval performance.

title: Automating Formal Verification with Reinforcement Learning and Recursive Inference
summary: Automated formal verification remains challenging for large language models because data for proof assistants and verification-aware languages is scarce, and correctness depends on satisfying precise machine-checkable specifications rather than producing plausible code. This thesis studies how verifier environments can improve LLM generation of verified programs and proofs through reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) and verifier-guided inference-time search. First, we train open-source models in Dafny with RLVR using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and related variants, assembling generated candidates into complete programs and scoring them with compiler and verifier outcomes. Initial experiments on an APPS-derived Dafny dataset increased verified reward from 2.2% to 58.1%, but revealed specification hacking, where models exploit weak formal specifications instead of implementing the intended solutions. After filtering underspecified and vulnerable tasks, multi-turn RLVR on the refined benchmark improves the verified pass rate from 9.7% to 31.1%. Second, we develop a verifier-guided inference scaffold in Lean that treats proof generation as structured search over decomposed subgoals, verifier feedback, diagnostics, and repair. With a fixed base model, the full scaffold with proof reviser improves pass rate on an initial VeriCoding pilot set from 46.2% under direct repair to 69.2%. On the larger VERINA dataset, whole-task decomposition plus proof reviser solves 7 of 42 previously unsolved tasks. We also introduce Dalek-Bench, a repository-scale Lean benchmark derived from the Rust $\texttt{curve25519-dalek}$ verification project; preliminary results remain weak, indicating that stronger progress evaluation and task-specific tool-use policies are still needed.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that LLMs do better at verified programming and theorem proving when they learn from verifier outcomes and use verifier-guided search, but weak specs and hard real-world benchmarks still limit reliability.
AI.motivation: Large language models struggle with automated formal verification because proof-assistant and verification-language data are scarce, and success requires exact machine-checkable correctness rather than plausible-looking code. The work investigates whether interaction with verifiers can provide stronger learning and search signals.
AI.method: The thesis uses two main methods: (1) RLVR in Dafny with GRPO and related variants, where generated candidates are assembled into full programs and scored by compiler/verifier outcomes, including a refined multi-turn setting after filtering weak tasks; (2) a verifier-guided inference scaffold in Lean that decomposes proofs into subgoals and uses verifier feedback, diagnostics, repair, and a proof reviser during structured search.
AI.result: On an APPS-derived Dafny dataset, initial RLVR raises verified reward from 2.2% to 58.1% but exposes specification hacking; after benchmark refinement, multi-turn RLVR improves verified pass rate from 9.7% to 31.1%. In Lean, the full verifier-guided scaffold improves pass rate on a VeriCoding pilot set from 46.2% to 69.2%, and on VERINA it solves 7 of 42 previously unsolved tasks. On Dalek-Bench, results remain weak.
AI.conclusion: Verifier feedback can substantially improve LLM-based formal verification through both training-time RL with verifiable rewards and inference-time verifier-guided search, but robustness is limited by underspecified tasks, specification hacking, and the need for stronger evaluation and task-specific tool policies on harder repository-scale benchmarks.

title: Multi-Turn Multi-Agent Dialogue for Collaborative Reconstruction Improves VLM Performance on Spatial Reasoning, But Only Barely
summary: Robots operating in diverse environments rely on visual input to interpret objects and spatial layouts. In human-collaborative tasks, they are expected to communicate this understanding through language. Vision-language models (VLMs) support robotic tasks involving visual interpretation, question answering, and instruction following, but their capabilities in collaborative dialogue tasks requiring spatial reasoning remain underexplored. We study this gap through a collaborative structure-building task that combines visual interpretation, grounding, language-guided interaction, and action generation. We develop a framework in which VLMs use dialogue to reconstruct a target structure from visual and textual inputs. We evaluate open-weight and closed VLMs across interaction settings, input modalities, and image representations. Results show that spatial reasoning over visual representations remains difficult for the evaluated VLMs. Detailed text representations of the target yield higher reconstruction success across modality conditions, while decomposed image representations improve performance. These findings reveal limits in visual spatial grounding and grounded instruction generation for collaborative VLM agents.

AI.tldr: The paper tests VLMs in a dialogue-based robot structure-building task and finds that current models are weak at visual spatial reasoning; better text descriptions and decomposed images help, but major grounding limitations remain.
AI.motivation: Robots in shared human environments must not only perceive objects and spatial layouts from vision, but also communicate that understanding through language. While VLMs have shown promise in perception, QA, and instruction following, their ability to handle collaborative dialogue with spatial reasoning is still insufficiently studied.
AI.method: The paper proposes a collaborative structure-building framework where a VLM reconstructs a target structure using visual and textual inputs through dialogue. It evaluates both open-weight and closed-source VLMs under different interaction settings, input modalities, and image representation formats.
AI.result: Across experiments, evaluated VLMs found spatial reasoning over visual inputs challenging. Detailed textual descriptions of the target structure consistently improved reconstruction performance across modalities, and decomposed image representations also led to better outcomes than less structured visual inputs.
AI.conclusion: VLMs can support collaborative structure-building dialogue, but current models still struggle with visual spatial reasoning, grounding, and generating grounded instructions. Rich textual target descriptions and decomposed image representations improve success, revealing both useful design directions and clear capability limits.

title: ERGeoBench:A Comprehensive Benchmark for Embodied Reasoning and Geo-localization in Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have shown strong potential as embodied agents, yet embodied geo-localization remains underexplored due to the lack of fine-grained evaluation. We introduce ERGeoBench, a diagnostic benchmark for vision-driven embodied geo-localization. ERGeoBench evaluates models under three progressive settings -- single-view, panorama-view, and embodied-view -- where agents may actively acquire observations through sequential changes in yaw, pitch, and zoom. The benchmark contains 2,207 globally distributed street-view panoramas and measures four complementary capabilities: foundational perception, spatial awareness, common sense reasoning, and geo-localization reasoning. Evaluations of leading proprietary and open-source MLLMs show that current models can infer high-level geographic semantics, but still struggle with fine-grained perceptual operations, metric localization, and spatial consistency across views. We further observe that geo-localization is strongly correlated with the other capability dimensions, suggesting that accurate localization depends on integrated perception, spatial reasoning, and commonsense inference rather than isolated visual recognition. Overall, ERGeoBench provides a unified framework for diagnosing and advancing human-like embodied geo-localization. Project Page: https://kaixuewen.github.io/ERGeoBench/

AI.tldr: The paper presents ERGeoBench, a new benchmark for testing embodied geo-localization in MLLMs. Current models understand broad location cues but remain weak at precise, spatially consistent, human-like localization.
AI.motivation: Although MLLMs show promise as embodied agents, embodied geo-localization has been underexplored because there has been no sufficiently fine-grained benchmark to diagnose the component skills required for accurate localization.
AI.method: The paper introduces ERGeoBench, a benchmark built from 2,207 globally distributed street-view panoramas. It evaluates models in three progressively harder settings: single-view, panorama-view, and embodied-view, where the agent can actively adjust yaw, pitch, and zoom. Performance is measured across four capability dimensions: foundational perception, spatial awareness, common sense reasoning, and geo-localization reasoning.
AI.result: Experiments on leading proprietary and open-source MLLMs show that models can capture coarse geographic semantics, but they struggle with detailed perceptual operations, precise localization, and maintaining spatial consistency across views. Geo-localization performance is also strongly correlated with the other evaluated capabilities.
AI.conclusion: ERGeoBench is a unified diagnostic benchmark for embodied geo-localization, and current multimodal large language models still fall short on fine-grained perception, metric localization, and cross-view spatial consistency. Strong geo-localization requires integrated perception, spatial reasoning, and commonsense inference rather than isolated recognition.

title: Welfare, Improvability, and Variance: A Principal-Agent Approach to Optimal Benchmark Item Aggregation
summary: AI benchmarks have well-documented limitations, with prior work examining contamination, saturation, and construct underspecification. Aggregation has received far less attention: benchmarks are typically summarized by uniformly averaging item-level scores, implicitly treating every test item as equally valuable. We model benchmarking as a multitask principal-agent game and show that the welfare loss from a benchmark is determined jointly by three item-level primitives: alignment with normative welfare priorities, marginal improvability, and performance variance. We translate the theory into an audit framework that ranks items along each of these three axes, and apply it to OLMES items using WORKBank for welfare, the EvoLM 4B suite for improvability, and the PolyPythias 410M panel for variance. The framework surfaces items that are Pareto-inferior within OLMES subject to a pro-worker welfare operationalization. All code is available at https://github.com/stair-lab/principal-agent-benchmarks.

AI.tldr: The paper argues that benchmark items are not equally valuable. It provides a theory and audit method showing that benchmark quality depends on welfare alignment, improvability, and variance, and uses this to find inferior OLMES items that should not be weighted equally.
AI.motivation: Prior benchmark critiques focus on contamination, saturation, and construct underspecification, but largely ignore aggregation. Uniform averaging assumes all items are equally valuable, which may distort incentives and reduce social welfare when benchmarks steer model development.
AI.method: The paper models benchmarking as a multitask principal-agent game, derives benchmark welfare loss as a function of three item-level primitives, then converts the theory into an audit framework that scores and ranks items on welfare alignment, improvability, and variance. It applies the framework using WORKBank, EvoLM 4B, and PolyPythias 410M on OLMES items.
AI.result: The audit framework surfaces benchmark items in OLMES that are Pareto-inferior when evaluated under a pro-worker welfare operationalization, demonstrating that benchmark aggregation can be systematically improved by reweighting or removing poorly chosen items.
AI.conclusion: Benchmarks should not uniformly average item scores. The usefulness of each benchmark item depends on three jointly important primitives: welfare alignment, marginal improvability, and performance variance. Applying this audit to OLMES identifies Pareto-inferior items under a pro-worker welfare framing.

title: Target-Side Paraphrase Augmentation for Sign Language Translation with Large Language Models
comment: Accepted at GenSign (https://genai4sl.github.io/) at CVPR 2026. Non proceedings track
summary:
Sign language translation (SLT) remains constrained by limited paired sign-video/text corpora and heavy-tailed target vocabularies. We study target-side augmentation in which GPT-4o generates controlled paraphrase variants of reference sentences while the sign input remains unchanged. A Signformer-style pose-based Transformer is trained under a two-stage schedule: pre-training on the augmented corpus followed by fine-tuning on the original references.
  We evaluate on three datasets spanning complementary challenges: PHOENIX14T (German Sign Language), with moderate lexical diversity; GSL (Greek Sign Language), with highly ontrolled, repetitive recordings; and LSA-T (Argentinian Sign Language), with severe long-tail sparsity. On PHOENIX14T, augmentation improves BLEU-4 from 9.56 to 10.33. The near-saturated GSL baseline and extremely sparse LSA-T setting reveal the limits of the approach. To our knowledge, this is the first study to apply LLM-generated target-side araphrases and LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation to SLT. The semantic evaluation reveals gains in fidelity that lexical overlap metrics understate.

AI.tldr: The paper augments SLT training targets with GPT-4o paraphrases and trains a Signformer in a pretrain-then-finetune setup. It helps on PHOENIX14T, but has limited effect on already repetitive or extremely sparse datasets; semantic gains appear larger than BLEU suggests.
AI.motivation: SLT suffers from limited paired sign-video/text datasets and heavy-tailed target vocabularies, which make it hard for models to generalize. The paper investigates whether augmenting only the target side with high-quality paraphrases can expand linguistic coverage without requiring additional sign annotations.
AI.method: The paper uses GPT-4o to generate controlled paraphrases of target reference sentences while keeping the sign-video input unchanged. A Signformer-style pose-based Transformer is trained in two stages: first pre-trained on the augmented corpus, then fine-tuned on the original reference corpus. Evaluation includes standard BLEU metrics and LLM-as-a-Judge semantic assessment across PHOENIX14T, GSL, and LSA-T.
AI.result: On PHOENIX14T, BLEU-4 improves from 9.56 to 10.33 with augmentation. On GSL, the baseline is already near saturation, so improvements are limited. On LSA-T, severe long-tail sparsity restricts the effectiveness of the approach. Semantic evaluation indicates fidelity gains that are not fully captured by lexical overlap metrics.
AI.conclusion: LLM-generated target-side paraphrase augmentation can improve sign language translation when datasets have enough lexical variability and paired data, but the gains diminish in near-saturated or extremely sparse settings. Semantic evaluation suggests the method improves meaning preservation more than lexical metrics alone indicate.

title: Envisioning Beyond the Few: Disentangled Semantics and Primitives for Few-Shot Atypical Layout-to-Image Generation
comment: Accepted to ICML 2026; code available at https://github.com/iCVTEAM/DSP
summary: The layout-to-image (L2I) task enables fine-grained control over image generation via object categories and spatial layouts. However, existing L2I methods yield fragmented and distorted generations under few-shot atypical settings. We term this failure as representation fragmentation, arising from a granularity mismatch that entangles semantic identity with visual details. To address this issue, we propose a representation-driven framework that disentangles semantics from primitives for robust few-shot adaptation. Specifically, Semantic Anchoring aggregates categorical semantics into anchors for stable identity, while Primitive Imbuing models recomposable primitives for robust local detail modeling. Conceptual Steering further regulates optimization with a saliency-aware objective to preserve foreground semantic consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent improvements in the 5-shot regime over state-of-the-art L2I methods in both visual fidelity and alignment across diverse atypical domains. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/iCVTEAM/DSP.

AI.tldr: This paper improves few-shot layout-to-image generation by separating object semantics from visual primitives, using semantic anchors, primitive modeling, and saliency-aware optimization to produce more faithful and better-aligned images in atypical 5-shot domains.
AI.motivation: Existing layout-to-image methods fail in few-shot atypical domains because of representation fragmentation caused by a granularity mismatch, where semantic identity is entangled with low-level visual details. The paper is motivated by the need for robust few-shot adaptation that preserves both object identity and local realism.
AI.method: The method introduces three components: Semantic Anchoring to aggregate category-level semantics into stable anchors, Primitive Imbuing to model recomposable visual primitives for local detail generation, and Conceptual Steering to guide optimization with a saliency-aware objective that preserves foreground semantic consistency during adaptation.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show consistent improvements over state-of-the-art layout-to-image methods in the 5-shot setting across diverse atypical domains, with better visual fidelity and stronger alignment between generated images and the input layouts.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that a representation-driven framework that disentangles semantic identity from visual primitives can substantially improve few-shot layout-to-image generation under atypical settings, reducing fragmented and distorted outputs and achieving better fidelity and layout/semantic alignment in the 5-shot regime.

title: De-attribute to Forget for LLM Unlearning
summary: The rapid development of large language models (LLMs) has raised concerns on the use of inappropriate data for training, which has led to a growing interest in LLM unlearning. Many existing LLM unlearning approaches rely on optimizing prediction loss(es), such as maximizing the loss on the forget set, but often face critical issues like over-forgetting and poor model utility. To address them, this paper novelly frames the optimization objective for LLM unlearning as one of zeroing out data attribution instead. In particular, we propose the first LLM unlearning framework based on data attribution rewards called DareU that performs reinforcement learning to update the LLM by reducing the attribution score of its generated responses (i.e., de-attributing) to the forget data owners. Empirical evaluation using an LLM classifier as an efficient approximation of attribution shows that DareU outperforms existing baselines by achieving effective unlearning while balancing forget quality and model utility well.

AI.tldr: DareU treats LLM unlearning as minimizing data attribution via reinforcement learning, leading to better forgetting-utility tradeoffs than loss-based methods.
AI.motivation: Existing LLM unlearning methods often optimize prediction losses such as maximizing forget-set loss, which can cause over-forgetting and degrade overall model utility. The paper aims to address these limitations with a more targeted unlearning objective.
AI.method: The paper proposes DareU, the first LLM unlearning framework based on data attribution rewards. It uses reinforcement learning to update the LLM so that generated responses have lower attribution scores to the forget-set data owners, effectively de-attributing the forgotten data.
AI.result: Using an LLM classifier as an efficient approximation for attribution, experiments show that DareU outperforms existing baselines by achieving strong unlearning performance while maintaining a better balance between forgetting quality and general utility.
AI.conclusion: DareU demonstrates that framing LLM unlearning as reducing data attribution, rather than directly optimizing prediction losses, can achieve more effective forgetting while preserving model utility better than prior baselines.

title: "Intelegi Româneşte?'' A Recipe for Romanian Vision-Language Models
summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) largely follow the text-only LLM trajectory, excelling on English benchmarks but sharply degrading on low-resource languages, where neither large-scale image-text corpora nor culturally grounded evaluations exist. We present a systematic study of building a language-specific VLM for Romanian, covering the full pipeline from data construction to architectural choices. We translate established English VLM training and evaluation corpora into Romanian, applying machine translation to textual annotations and to in-image text, preserving visual grounding while adapting the textual content. Using this data, we train and ablate a series of VLMs to isolate the contribution of (i) vision backbones of varying scale and pretraining, (ii) language backbones from multilingual to Romanian-adapted LLMs, and (iii) OCR-style image-text data. We further curate HoraVQA, a culturally native evaluation set grounded in Romanian everyday scenes. Romanian-adapted VLMs consistently outperform their same-sized counterparts and, across all evaluated benchmarks, even surpass models from the next larger size category.

AI.tldr: The paper builds a Romanian VLM pipeline by translating English multimodal datasets, testing key architectural choices, and adding a native benchmark; the main finding is that Romanian-specific adaptation delivers strong, consistent improvements over generic VLMs.
AI.motivation: Existing VLMs perform well in English but degrade significantly on low-resource languages such as Romanian, where large image-text corpora and culturally grounded evaluation datasets are scarce. The paper aims to systematically study how to build an effective language-specific VLM under these constraints.
AI.method: The paper constructs Romanian VLM resources by translating existing English image-text training and evaluation datasets, including both textual annotations and text appearing inside images. It then trains and ablates multiple VLM variants to study the effects of different vision backbones, language backbones, and OCR-style image-text data, and introduces HoraVQA as a native Romanian cultural evaluation benchmark.
AI.result: Romanian-adapted VLMs consistently outperform same-sized baseline counterparts across all evaluated benchmarks and even exceed the performance of models from the next larger size category. The study also provides evidence on the relative contribution of backbone choice and OCR-style data.
AI.conclusion: Building a Romanian-specific VLM is effective: adapting both data and language components to Romanian yields consistent gains over same-sized generic models and can even beat the next larger model class.

title: DriveMA: Driving Vision-Language-Action Models with verifiable Meta-Actions
comment: arXiv admin note: text overlap with arXiv:2605.21273
summary: Driving Vision-Language-Action Models (Driving VLAs) aim to use language to improve end-to-end planning, but the language-action gap limits this promise. We propose DriveMA, a Driving VLA framework built on verifiable meta-actions, which summarize future ego motion into compact language-domain intentions and can be constructed from expert trajectories with a trajectory-grounded annotation pipeline and can be verified against generated trajectories through rule-based projection. DriveMA exploits this verifiability with action-centric supervised training and a data-efficient turn-level credit assignment reinforcement learning framework, explicitly aligning high-level decisions with low-level trajectory planning through dense rewards and precise credit assignment. DriveMA sets a new state of the art on the Waymo Open Dataset Vision-based E2E Driving, achieving a Rater Feedback Score of 8.060 with a 2B model and further improving it to 8.079 with a 4B model; it also obtains competitive closed-loop planning performance on NAVSIM. These results show that even a simple meta-action interface can achieve state-of-the-art planning when made verifiable and optimized for language-action alignment. Code, data, and models will be released to facilitate future research.

AI.tldr: DriveMA bridges the language-action gap in autonomous driving by introducing verifiable meta-actions and training them with supervised learning plus precise RL credit assignment, reaching SOTA on Waymo and strong results on NAVSIM.
AI.motivation: Existing Driving VLA approaches aim to use language to enhance end-to-end planning, but their effectiveness is limited by the language-action gap. The work is motivated by the need for an interface that connects language-level intentions with executable driving behavior in a verifiable and trainable way.
AI.method: The paper proposes DriveMA, a Driving Vision-Language-Action framework based on verifiable meta-actions. Meta-actions summarize future ego motion into compact language-domain intentions, are constructed from expert trajectories via a trajectory-grounded annotation pipeline, and are verified against generated trajectories using rule-based projection. Training combines action-centric supervised learning with a data-efficient turn-level credit assignment reinforcement learning scheme that uses dense rewards to align high-level decisions with low-level trajectory planning.
AI.result: On the Waymo Open Dataset vision-based end-to-end driving benchmark, DriveMA achieves a new state of the art with a Rater Feedback Score of 8.060 using a 2B model and 8.079 using a 4B model. It also shows competitive closed-loop planning performance on NAVSIM.
AI.conclusion: DriveMA demonstrates that a simple but verifiable meta-action interface can substantially improve language-action alignment in driving VLA systems and achieve state-of-the-art end-to-end planning performance.

title: Unsupervised Diffusion Solver for Combinatorial Optimization via Combinatorial Adjoint Matching
summary: Diffusion-based neural solvers have shown strong promise for combinatorial optimization (CO), but existing methods typically rely on supervised training with large collections of near-optimal solutions. In this work, we extend adjoint-based trajectory optimization methods to discrete combinatorial domains. We formulate diffusion-based CO as a stochastic control problem over Continuous-Time Markov Chains and introduce discrete adjoint dynamics for propagating optimization signals through discrete generative trajectories. Building on this formulation, we propose Combinatorial Adjoint Matching (CAM), an unsupervised training framework for discrete diffusion solvers with structured and low-variance trajectory-level optimization signals. Empirically, CAM consistently outperforms existing unsupervised diffusion baselines and achieves performance competitive with strong supervised diffusion solvers and even traditional solvers across diverse combinatorial optimization problems. Our code is available at https://github.com/Shengyu-Feng/CAM.

AI.tldr: 中文：论文提出CAM，用离散伴随方法给离散扩散求解器提供低方差、结构化的无监督训练信号，在组合优化任务上显著提升效果。 English: The paper introduces CAM, an unsupervised training framework that uses discrete adjoint dynamics to provide structured, low-variance optimization signals for discrete diffusion solvers, substantially improving combinatorial optimization performance.
AI.motivation: 中文：现有扩散式组合优化方法通常依赖大量近最优解进行监督训练，数据成本高且限制适用性，因此需要一种无需高质量标签、仍能稳定优化离散生成过程的方法。 English: Existing diffusion-based CO solvers typically depend on large supervised datasets of near-optimal solutions, which is costly and limiting, motivating an unsupervised approach that can still optimize discrete generative trajectories effectively and stably.
AI.method: 中文：作者将扩散式组合优化建模为连续时间马尔可夫链上的随机控制问题，并设计离散伴随动力学来沿离散生成轨迹传播优化信号，在此基础上提出无监督训练框架CAM。 English: The method formulates diffusion-based combinatorial optimization as a stochastic control problem over continuous-time Markov chains, derives discrete adjoint dynamics to propagate optimization signals through discrete generative trajectories, and builds the unsupervised Combinatorial Adjoint Matching (CAM) framework on top of this formulation.
AI.result: 中文：实验表明，CAM稳定优于现有无监督扩散基线，并且其性能可与强监督扩散求解器乃至部分传统求解器相竞争。 English: Empirically, CAM consistently outperforms prior unsupervised diffusion baselines and is competitive with strong supervised diffusion solvers and even traditional solvers.
AI.conclusion: 中文：本文证明了在离散组合优化中，可以通过离散伴随动力学为扩散式求解器提供有效的无监督训练信号，所提出的CAM在多类CO任务上达到强竞争力。 English: The paper concludes that discrete diffusion solvers for combinatorial optimization can be trained effectively without supervision via discrete adjoint dynamics, and the proposed CAM achieves strongly competitive results across diverse CO tasks.

title: The Sword, Shield, and Achilles' Heel: Characterizing the Linguistic Inductive Bias of Large Language Models for Spatial Reasoning in Navigation Planning
summary: Large Language Model (LLM)-based navigation systems commonly construct explicit spatial representations (e.g., topological graphs, semantic raster maps) and translate them into textual descriptions as LLMs' inputs. However, the linguistic structures of such text-based spatial representations and the choices of contextual features (e.g., topology, geometry) they contain are often treated as neutral engineering decisions rather than key factors that shape LLMs' behavior. To fill the gap, we propose a dual-interventional framework that disentangles linguistic structures from different contextual cues to evaluate the linguistic inductive bias of LLMs for navigation planning. In the framework, representation intervention varies the linguistic format and the degree of linguistic compression, clarifying when linguistic representations support or inhibit navigation planning. Context intervention, combined with contextual feature combination and conflict probing, explicitly clarifies the preferences and weaknesses of LLMs when processing different contextual cues. Experiments across diverse spatial reasoning tasks and multiple model scales reveal a consistent pattern: topological information is a sturdy shield and the backbone of robust planning; linguistic format is a double-edged sword whose effect depends on model size, task demands, and the compression level; and semantic information is a fatal Achilles' heel -- incorrect semantic cues can systematically derail the planning process. Overall, our study shows that effective text-based spatial representations in LLM-based navigation should preserve topological integrity, calibrate representational compression to model capacity, and ensure semantic correctness, rather than simply adopting a single representation. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/jonesdong150/LLM-Navigation-Inductive-Bias.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how the wording and content of text-based spatial representations affect LLM navigation. Using a dual-intervention framework, it finds that topology is the strongest and most reliable signal, linguistic formatting is beneficial only under the right conditions, and incorrect semantic cues are especially harmful.
AI.motivation: Prior LLM-based navigation systems usually convert explicit spatial structures into text, but the linguistic form of that text and the contextual features it includes are often treated as simple engineering choices. The paper is motivated by the need to systematically understand how these choices induce biases in LLM spatial reasoning and planning.
AI.method: The authors propose a dual-interventional framework with two components: representation intervention and context intervention. Representation intervention manipulates linguistic format and compression level of spatial descriptions, while context intervention varies contextual cues such as topology, geometry, and semantics, including feature combination and conflict probing, to isolate how these factors affect LLM navigation planning.
AI.result: Across diverse spatial reasoning tasks and multiple model scales, the experiments show a consistent pattern: topological information is the most reliable cue for robust planning; linguistic format can help or hurt depending on model size, task type, and compression level; and semantic information is highly risky because incorrect semantic cues can systematically derail planning.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that text-based spatial representations are not neutral design choices in LLM navigation. Robust planning depends on preserving topological integrity, matching linguistic compression to model capacity and task demands, and maintaining semantic correctness because wrong semantic cues can strongly mislead LLMs.

title: Topologically Consistent Multi-view 3D Head Reconstruction via Coarse-Guided Layered Surface Sampling
summary: We present SHELLS (Semantic Head Estimation via Layered Local Sampling), an efficient feed-forward framework for 3D head reconstruction in dense semantic correspondence from multi-view images. Existing methods typically refine vertices independently via localized feature volumes. This approach couples memory-intensive feature sampling to mesh resolution, which limits scalability for dense topologies (> 10k vertices) and introduces surface noise. In contrast, SHELLS decouples feature extraction from mesh resolution via a hierarchical sampling strategy. We extract multi-view features using a DINOv2 backbone with LoRA adaptation, projectively sample a sparse global feature cloud, and predict an intermediate coarse mesh. This coarse prior guides the construction of layered, surface-aware sampling shells that serve as a discrete search space for the final reconstruction. SHELLS maintains surface consistency while using 88% less inference GPU memory (2.4GB vs. 20GB) than volumetric baselines. It reduces median registration error by 21% to 29% with a 3.5x inference speedup (0.08s vs. 0.29s) for 18k-vertex meshes. Notably, our model is trained exclusively on synthetic data yet generalizes effectively to real-world captures, eliminating the need for the costly, pre-registered multi-view datasets common in prior work.

AI.tldr: SHELLS is a feed-forward multi-view 3D head reconstruction framework that replaces expensive per-vertex volumetric refinement with hierarchical surface-aware sampling, making dense 18k-vertex reconstruction faster, more memory-efficient, more accurate, and easier to train using only synthetic data.
AI.motivation: Prior multi-view 3D head reconstruction methods refine vertices independently using localized feature volumes, which ties memory cost to mesh resolution, limits scalability for dense meshes, and often introduces surface noise.
AI.method: The method uses a DINOv2 backbone with LoRA adaptation to extract multi-view features, samples a sparse global feature cloud, predicts a coarse mesh, and then builds layered surface-aware sampling shells around this coarse prior as a discrete search space for final dense reconstruction.
AI.result: Compared with volumetric baselines, SHELLS uses 88% less inference GPU memory (2.4GB vs. 20GB), achieves a 3.5x speedup (0.08s vs. 0.29s), and reduces median registration error by 21% to 29% on 18k-vertex meshes. It is trained only on synthetic data yet generalizes well to real captures.
AI.conclusion: SHELLS demonstrates that decoupling feature extraction from mesh resolution through hierarchical, surface-aware sampling enables efficient and accurate dense 3D head reconstruction from multi-view images, with strong synthetic-to-real generalization.

title: Local linear convergence of gradient methods for overparameterized Gaussian mixtures
summary: We study the problem of learning Gaussian mixture models under overparameterization. Prior work has shown that while overparameterization is essential for avoiding spurious local optima and enables global recovery of the ground-truth model using the gradient-EM (expectation-maximization) algorithm, it can dramatically slow down the local rate of convergence. Under certain assumptions on the mixture weights, we show that a standard divergence measure minimized by statistical learning procedures possesses a manifold of slow growth on which the well-known Polyak stepsize reduces the loss geometrically, and design a gradient-based method that converges to minimizers at a locally linear rate. Additionally, we show that our method converges to nearly optimal solutions -- up to a natural misspecification threshold -- for mixtures with arbitrary weights. At a high level, the method alternates between several "short" gradient descent steps that approach the manifold and "long" Polyak steps that contract the distance to minimizers. Our results suggest that slow convergence is not an intrinsic challenge of overparameterization, but can be overcome by exploiting the favorable structure of the loss landscape.

AI.tldr: Overparameterized GMMs can be optimized faster than previously thought: by alternating short GD steps with long Polyak steps and leveraging a special manifold in the loss landscape, the method achieves linear local convergence and near-optimal recovery.
AI.motivation: Existing work shows overparameterization helps avoid spurious local optima and enables global recovery with gradient-EM, but it significantly slows local convergence. The paper aims to determine whether this slow rate is fundamental and how to overcome it.
AI.method: The paper analyzes a divergence objective for overparameterized Gaussian mixture models, identifies a manifold of slow growth, and proposes a gradient-based alternating strategy: several short gradient descent steps to move toward the manifold, followed by long Polyak steps to contract the distance to minimizers geometrically.
AI.result: Under assumptions on mixture weights, the authors prove geometric loss reduction with Polyak steps on the slow-growth manifold and establish locally linear convergence to minimizers. For arbitrary weights, the method converges to nearly optimal solutions up to a natural misspecification threshold.
AI.conclusion: Slow convergence in overparameterized Gaussian mixture model learning is not inherent; by exploiting a slow-growth manifold in the loss landscape and combining short gradient descent steps with long Polyak steps, one can achieve locally linear convergence to minimizers and nearly optimal solutions under broader weight settings.

title: SAM for Robust Mitochondria Instance Segmentation in Fluorescence Microscopy
summary: The morphological analysis of mitochondria in fluorescence microscopy (FM) is crucial for understanding cellular health, energy production, and metabolic regulation. While foundation models like the Segment Anything Model (SAM) have revolutionized natural image segmentation, their direct application to FM is hindered by a significant domain shift characterized by diffraction-limited resolution, low contrast, and complex overlapping organelle networks. Furthermore, the development of robust models is bottlenecked by a severe lack of high-quality, manually annotated instance segmentation datasets for mitochondria. In this paper, we propose a scalable solution to this data scarcity by finetuning SAM exclusively on synthetically generated FM data. We simulate realistic mitochondria data and emulate the optical properties of fluorescence microscopes to create a large-scale annotated dataset. We evaluate our fine-tuned model on a curated dataset of real, manually annotated FM images. Qualitative and quantitative analyses demonstrate that our synthetically fine-tuned model improves precision and average dice score over strong baselines. This work establishes the potential of simulation-assisted training for FM instance segmentation.

AI.tldr: The paper fine-tunes SAM using only realistic synthetic fluorescence microscopy images of mitochondria, overcoming annotation scarcity and improving real-image instance segmentation performance.
AI.motivation: Directly applying SAM to fluorescence microscopy fails because of strong domain shift from natural images, and progress is limited by the lack of high-quality manually annotated mitochondria instance segmentation datasets.
AI.method: The paper generates large-scale synthetic fluorescence microscopy data by simulating realistic mitochondrial morphology and microscope optical effects, then fine-tunes SAM only on this synthetic dataset and evaluates it on a curated real manually annotated FM dataset.
AI.result: Compared with strong baselines, the synthetically fine-tuned model achieves improved precision and average Dice score on real fluorescence microscopy images, supported by both qualitative and quantitative evaluation.
AI.conclusion: Simulation-assisted training is an effective way to adapt SAM to fluorescence microscopy mitochondria instance segmentation under severe annotation scarcity, yielding better precision and average Dice than strong baselines on real annotated FM images.

title: Spectral Anatomy of Quantum Gaussian Process Kernels
summary: Two recent results have reshaped quantum Gaussian processes (QGPs). On the one hand, \citet{lowe2025assessing} rule out the exponential speedups claimed by HHL-based QGP regression in the typical, well-conditioned regime; on the other, an independent line of work shows that highly expressive quantum kernels suffer posterior pathologies that break Bayesian optimization. We show that these seemingly unrelated phenomena are governed by the same quantity: the normalized spectral entropy $S(K)/\log n$ of the kernel Gram matrix. We prove a Cauchy--Schwarz tail bound on Nyström approximation error, a finite-sample variance-contraction identity in terms of Bach's degrees of freedom $d_σ(K)$, and a characterization of the \emph{target-dependent} optimal entropy via the intrinsic dimension of the target in the kernel eigenbasis. Empirically, the diagnostic is kernel-agnostic: hardware-efficient, matchgate, IQP \emph{and} RBF/Matérn/RFF/deep-kernel families all collapse onto identical $S/\log n$ curves on dequantization, ECE, and variance-contraction panels. The NLL sweet spot lives at high entropy for smooth targets and at low entropy for band-limited quantum-data targets. The diagnostic transfers from simulator to IBM Heron hardware with median absolute error $3.2\%$ and mean $5.2\%$ in $S/\log n$ across $24$ configurations at $n_q = 4$, with matchgate and IQP within $5\%$ mean and a single HE configuration returning a $30\%$ outlier that drops to $0.5\%$ on rerun (attributed to calibration drift); the same diagnostic transfers to a second Heron backend (mean error $2.7\%$) and to a $n_q = 6$ scale-up on the original backend (mean error $1.7\%$). No error mitigation is applied throughout.

AI.tldr: 这篇论文提出“归一化谱熵”作为QGP统一诊断指标：熵过高可能导致后验病态，熵结构不合适也意味着难以获得算法优势；最佳熵并非固定，而取决于目标函数在核谱中的内在维数。该规律对量子核和经典核都成立，并能从仿真稳定迁移到真实量子硬件。 / The paper proposes normalized spectral entropy as a single diagnostic for QGPs: too much entropy can trigger posterior pathologies, while mismatched entropy also undermines algorithmic advantage; the best entropy is target-dependent, determined by the target's intrinsic dimension in the kernel spectrum. The pattern holds across quantum and classical kernels and transfers robustly from simulation to real quantum hardware.
AI.motivation: 近期两条研究线索分别质疑QGP的两个关键卖点：HHL型回归在常见良态条件下并无声称的指数优势，而高表达量子核又会引发后验退化，破坏贝叶斯优化。论文的动机是寻找一个统一、可解释、与核家族无关的量，来同时解释这两类现象并指导核选择。 / Recent work challenged two core promises of QGPs: HHL-style regression does not deliver the claimed exponential speedups in the usual well-conditioned regime, while highly expressive quantum kernels induce posterior degeneracies that break Bayesian optimization. The motivation is to identify a unified, interpretable, kernel-agnostic quantity that explains both effects and guides kernel selection.
AI.method: 理论上，论文证明了Nyström近似误差的Cauchy-Schwarz尾界、用Bach自由度 d_σ(K) 表示的有限样本方差收缩恒等式，以及基于目标在核特征基中的内在维数给出的目标依赖最优熵刻画。实验上，比较硬件高效、matchgate、IQP以及RBF/Matérn/RFF/deep-kernel等多类核，在去量子化、ECE和方差收缩面板上验证统一的 S/log n 规律，并在IBM Heron后端与更大量子比特规模上检验可迁移性。 / The paper develops theory via a Cauchy-Schwarz tail bound for Nyström error, a finite-sample variance-contraction identity in terms of Bach's degrees of freedom d_σ(K), and a target-dependent optimal-entropy characterization through the target's intrinsic dimension in the kernel eigenbasis. Empirically, it evaluates hardware-efficient, matchgate, IQP, and classical kernel families (RBF/Matérn/RFF/deep kernels), showing common S/log n behavior across dequantization, ECE, and variance-contraction panels, then validates transfer on IBM Heron hardware and at larger qubit counts.
AI.result: 实验结果表明，不同量子与经典核族在多项指标上都塌缩到相同的归一化谱熵曲线；平滑目标的NLL最优点位于高熵区，而带限量子数据目标位于低熵区。该诊断从仿真迁移到IBM Heron硬件时，在24组4量子比特配置上的 S/log n 误差中位数为3.2%、均值5.2%；在第二个Heron后端均值误差为2.7%，在6量子比特扩展上均值误差为1.7%，且全程未使用误差缓解。 / Empirically, diverse quantum and classical kernel families collapse onto the same normalized spectral-entropy curves across multiple diagnostics; the NLL optimum lies at high entropy for smooth targets and low entropy for band-limited quantum-data targets. The diagnostic transfers from simulation to IBM Heron hardware with median 3.2% and mean 5.2% error in S/log n over 24 four-qubit configurations, 2.7% mean error on a second Heron backend, and 1.7% mean error in a six-qubit scale-up, all without error mitigation.
AI.conclusion: 核Gram矩阵的归一化谱熵 S(K)/log n 是统一解释量子高斯过程两类现象的核心诊断量：既解释典型良态情形下缺乏指数加速，也解释高表达量子核导致的后验病态与贝叶斯优化失效；该诊断在仿真与IBM Heron硬件上都可稳定迁移。 / The normalized spectral entropy S(K)/log n of the kernel Gram matrix is the unifying diagnostic behind both the lack of exponential speedup in typical well-conditioned QGP regression and the posterior pathologies of highly expressive quantum kernels, and it transfers reliably from simulation to IBM Heron hardware.

title: Neuro-symbolic Syntactic Parsing: Shaping a Neural Network with the CYK Algorithm
summary: In this paper, we show the possibility of a direct injection of algorithms into neural network architecture. We focus on a complex algorithm, that is, Cocke-Youger-Kasami (CYK) for parsing context-free grammars in Chomsky Normal Form and we propose CYKNN, a simple recurrent neural network architecture for encoding the CYK algorithm in trainable matrix-vector multiplications.We experimented with a very simple grammar with 4 variations showing that our approach outperforms existing LLMs with more than 20B parameters with an in-context learning setting and smaller LLMs of the Qwen family fine-tuned with LoRA. Our attempt paves the way to a different approach to neuro-symbolic methodologies.

AI.tldr: A recurrent neural network called CYKNN hard-codes the CYK parsing algorithm into trainable neural operations and, on a simple CFG parsing benchmark, beats much larger LLM baselines, suggesting promise for neuro-symbolic design.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to move beyond generic large language models and explore whether explicit algorithmic structure can be embedded directly into neural architectures, especially for tasks requiring precise symbolic computation like grammar parsing.
AI.method: The authors design CYKNN, a simple recurrent neural network that encodes the Cocke-Younger-Kasami (CYK) parsing algorithm for context-free grammars in Chomsky Normal Form using trainable matrix-vector multiplications.
AI.result: On a very simple grammar with four variations, CYKNN reportedly outperforms existing LLMs with over 20B parameters in in-context learning and smaller Qwen models fine-tuned with LoRA.
AI.conclusion: The paper argues that directly injecting a symbolic algorithm into neural network architecture is feasible, and that this can be an effective neuro-symbolic alternative for structured reasoning tasks such as CFG parsing.

title: Authentication of Copy Detection Patterns via Cross-Camera Dual-Synthetic Referencing
comment: To appear in Proc. ICIP2026, September 13-17, 2026, Tampere, Finland
summary: Copy Detection Patterns (CDPs) are structures printed on physical objects to enable cost-effective authentication. Verification is achieved by comparing a captured image with the digital template from which the CDP was printed. In practice, printer stochasticity and camera distortions hinder this comparison, limiting robustness against counterfeiting. Prior work addressed camera effects by synthesising reference images in the verification camera domain, but it ignored printing variability. We introduce an enrolment-based cross-camera dual-synthetic referencing framework. Each printed CDP is first captured by a controlled enrolment camera, and a deep-learning-based translator jointly exploits the digital template and the enrolled capture to generate a high-quality reference for the verification image. We provide an information-theoretic justification showing that the dual reference is more informative than template-based references. Experiments on heterogeneous mobile cameras demonstrate improved authentication performance, robustness to machine-learning-based copy attacks, and reliable verification from small CDP regions and on low-end devices.

AI.tldr: TL;DR：这篇论文通过把“数字模板+注册拍摄图像”一起用于生成验证参考图，弥补了只用模板时无法覆盖打印随机性的缺陷，因此CDP防伪在真实手机、局部裁剪和低配置设备上都更稳健，也更难被机器学习复制伪造。 / TL;DR: The paper improves CDP authentication by generating the verification reference from both the digital template and an enrolment capture, overcoming the inability of template-only methods to capture print randomness; this yields more robust real-world mobile verification and better resistance to ML-based counterfeits.
AI.motivation: 动机：现有CDP认证依赖将采集图像与数字模板比较，但打印随机性和相机畸变会破坏一致性，削弱防伪鲁棒性。已有工作主要补偿相机域差异，却忽略了打印过程中引入的个体化随机变化，因此需要一种同时建模打印差异与跨相机失真的参考生成机制。 / Motivation: Existing CDP authentication compares a captured image with the digital template, but printer stochasticity and camera distortions degrade the match and weaken anti-counterfeiting robustness. Prior work mainly compensates for camera-domain shifts while ignoring instance-specific variability introduced by printing, motivating a reference-generation approach that models both print variability and cross-camera distortions.
AI.method: 方法：作者提出一种跨相机双合成参考方法。首先对每个已打印CDP用受控注册相机采集注册图像；随后使用深度学习翻译模型，同时输入数字模板和注册图像，生成与验证相机域匹配的高质量参考图像；并用信息论分析论证双参考比单模板参考更有信息量。 / Method: The paper proposes a cross-camera dual-synthetic reference framework. Each printed CDP is first captured by a controlled enrolment camera, then a deep-learning-based translator jointly takes the digital template and the enrolment capture to synthesize a high-quality reference in the verification camera domain; an information-theoretic analysis is used to justify why the dual reference is more informative than a template-only reference.
AI.result: 结果：在异构移动相机上的实验表明，该方法提升了认证性能，提高了对机器学习复制攻击的鲁棒性，并且能够在较小CDP区域及低端设备上实现可靠验证。 / Results: Experiments on heterogeneous mobile cameras show improved authentication performance, stronger robustness against machine-learning-based copy attacks, and reliable verification from small CDP regions and on low-end devices.
AI.conclusion: 结论：基于注册阶段的跨相机双合成参考框架，利用数字模板与受控注册图像联合生成验证参考图，相比仅依赖模板的方法包含更多判别信息，能够显著提升CDP认证在异构移动相机、局部区域和低端设备条件下的鲁棒性，并增强对机器学习复制攻击的抵抗力。 / Conclusion: An enrolment-based cross-camera dual-synthetic referencing framework that jointly uses the digital template and a controlled enrolment capture to generate the verification reference provides more discriminative information than template-only approaches, substantially improving CDP authentication robustness across heterogeneous mobile cameras, small regions, and low-end devices, while strengthening resistance to ML-based copy attacks.

title: DOA: Training-Free Decoder-Only Attention Policy for Long-Form Simultaneous Translation with SpeechLLMs
summary: Simultaneous speech-to-text translation (SimulST) generates translations while speech is still unfolding, requiring a streaming policy that decides when to read and when to write. State-of-the-art approaches rely on attention-based encoder-decoder models where cross-attention provides explicit alignment signals. In contrast, Speech Large Language Models (SpeechLLMs) are decoder-only architectures relying solely on self-attention. This raises a central question: whether decoder self-attention contains sufficiently stable alignment signals to guide the streaming policy. Moreover, existing approaches typically rely on training-based adaptations or heuristic wait-$k$ policies and have not been validated in long-form settings. To fill these gaps, we propose Decoder-Only Attention (DOA), a training-free policy that enables long-form simultaneous translation with off-the-shelf SpeechLLMs by deriving a proxy alignment from self-attention. Experiments on Phi4-Multimodal and Qwen3-Omni show that DOA provides an effective alignment signal for supporting streaming decisions, enabling low-latency long-form SimulST with quality close to offline decoding without retraining.

AI.tldr: A training-free policy called DOA uses self-attention in decoder-only SpeechLLMs as a proxy alignment signal, allowing long-form simultaneous speech translation with low latency and near-offline quality.
AI.motivation: Existing SimulST methods mainly depend on encoder-decoder cross-attention for alignment, or use retraining and heuristic wait-k policies. These approaches are not well suited to decoder-only SpeechLLMs and are insufficiently validated for long-form streaming scenarios. The paper asks whether self-attention alone can provide stable alignment for streaming control.
AI.method: The paper proposes Decoder-Only Attention (DOA), a training-free simultaneous translation policy for decoder-only SpeechLLMs. DOA derives proxy alignment signals from decoder self-attention to decide when to read more speech input and when to write translation output, without retraining the model.
AI.result: Experiments on Phi4-Multimodal and Qwen3-Omni show that DOA yields effective alignment signals for streaming decisions and achieves low-latency long-form simultaneous translation with translation quality close to offline decoding, without additional training.
AI.conclusion: Decoder self-attention in decoder-only SpeechLLMs can provide a stable enough proxy alignment to drive a training-free streaming policy, enabling practical long-form simultaneous speech translation with latency-quality tradeoffs close to offline decoding.

title: TokTalk: Expressive Real-time Facial Animation from Audio-LLM Tokens
summary: Recent advances in Audio-LLMs like GPT-4o have ushered in an era of conversational interaction with language models. Conversational avatars however, still seem robotic in facial expression and conversational flow, in part due to sequential stages of speech recognition, text generation, turn-based text response, speech synthesis, and audio driven facial animation. Based on our insight that audio-tokens produced by current Audio-LLMs carry sufficient information to reconstruct a plausible facial performance, we present TokTalk, a system that directly outputs expressive facial animation in real-time from streaming audio-tokens. We construct a novel audio-token to 3D facial motion dataset, on which TokTalk is trained using a Chunk-based Conditional Flow Matching model. A lightweight adaptation strategy allows our trained model to seamlessly connect to any token-based Audio-LLM at minimal computational overhead. Our chunk-based processing further enables parametric trade-off between latency and facial quality, shown through ablation studies. We further show that the real-time performance of TokTalk is comparable in latency to prior art solutions, and significantly favorable (via a perceptual study) in terms of quality, expressivity and control of the 3D facial performance. We showcase TokTalk's flexibility using a chatbot Avatar, a voice-driven user Avatar, and an animation Director's interface, as diverse audio-visual face applications.

AI.tldr: TokTalk turns Audio-LLM audio-tokens directly into real-time expressive 3D face animation, reducing pipeline rigidity while improving perceived facial quality and keeping latency competitive.
AI.motivation: Conventional conversational avatar pipelines are robotic and delayed because they rely on multiple sequential stages such as ASR, text generation, TTS, and audio-driven facial animation; the authors aim to remove this bottleneck by predicting facial motion directly from audio-tokens.
AI.method: The paper builds a novel audio-token-to-3D facial motion dataset and trains TokTalk with a chunk-based Conditional Flow Matching model, plus a lightweight adaptation layer to connect with token-based Audio-LLMs.
AI.result: TokTalk achieves real-time performance, offers a controllable latency-quality trade-off through chunk-based processing, and outperforms prior methods in perceptual quality, expressivity, and controllability across several avatar applications.
AI.conclusion: TokTalk demonstrates that streaming audio-tokens from Audio-LLMs can directly drive real-time, expressive 3D facial animation with better perceptual quality and comparable latency to prior pipelines.

title: SCOPE: Self-Play via Co-Evolving Policies for Open-Ended Tasks
summary: Self-play can train language models without external supervision. However, existing methods require rule-checkable answers, leaving open-ended tasks dependent on curated prompts or frontier-model judges. We introduce SCOPE, a data-free self-play framework for open-ended tasks that co-evolves two policies: a Challenger that generates document-grounded tasks, and a Solver that answers them through multi-turn retrieval. A frozen copy of the initial model serves as the self-judge, which writes task-specific rubrics from the source document and grades Solver responses against them. Across three 7-8B instruction-tuned models (Qwen2.5, Qwen3, OLMo-3), SCOPE improves open-ended performance by up to +10.4 points on eight benchmarks and matches or exceeds GRPO_data trained on ~9K curated prompts. Although trained only on open-ended tasks, SCOPE also improves held-out short-form QA by up to +13.8 points on seven held-out benchmarks, surpassing GRPO_data on all three models. Ablations show that co-evolving the Challenger is necessary to keep tasks near the Solver's frontier, that gains arise from improvements in both retrieval and synthesis with the relative contribution varying by task, and that rubric generation quality is the bottleneck for self-judging.

AI.tldr: 中文：SCOPE 是一种无外部数据的开放式任务自博弈方法：让出题者和解题者共同进化，再用冻结模型按文档生成评分标准进行自评。它显著提升开放式与短答 QA 表现，关键限制在于评分 rubric 的质量。 English: SCOPE is a data-free self-play framework for open-ended tasks that co-evolves a task generator and answerer, then uses a frozen model to create rubrics and self-grade. It substantially improves both open-ended and short-form QA, with rubric quality as the main bottleneck.
AI.motivation: 中文：现有自博弈训练通常依赖可规则校验的答案，导致开放式任务仍依赖人工整理提示或更强的模型裁判。本文的动机是构建一种面向开放式任务、无需外部标注数据的自博弈框架。 English: Prior self-play methods usually require rule-checkable answers, leaving open-ended tasks dependent on curated prompts or stronger external judges. The paper aims to build a data-free self-play framework for open-ended tasks.
AI.method: 中文：方法上，SCOPE 让两个策略共同进化：Challenger 基于文档生成任务，Solver 通过多轮检索作答；同时使用初始冻结模型作为自评审，从源文档自动写出任务评分 rubric，并据此评估 Solver 回答。 English: SCOPE co-evolves two policies: a document-grounded Challenger that creates tasks and a Solver that answers via multi-turn retrieval, while a frozen initial model self-judges by generating task-specific rubrics from the source document and grading responses against them.
AI.result: 中文：在 Qwen2.5、Qwen3 和 OLMo-3 三个 7-8B 指令模型上，SCOPE 在 8 个开放式基准上最高提升 10.4 分，并在仅用开放式任务训练的情况下，在 7 个保留短答 QA 基准上最高提升 13.8 分，且在三种模型上都超过 GRPO_data。消融实验表明：Challenger 的共同进化是必要的；性能增益来自检索和综合能力的共同提升；rubric 生成质量是自评审瓶颈。 English: On three 7-8B instruction-tuned models, SCOPE improves open-ended performance by up to 10.4 points on eight benchmarks and also boosts held-out short-form QA by up to 13.8 points on seven benchmarks, outperforming GRPO_data across all three models. Ablations show challenger co-evolution is necessary, gains come from both retrieval and synthesis, and rubric quality is the main self-judging bottleneck.
AI.conclusion: 中文：SCOPE 证明了在无需外部数据或强评审模型的条件下，开放式任务也可以通过自博弈有效提升语言模型能力；其效果达到或超过基于约 9K 人工提示训练的 GRPO_data。 English: SCOPE shows that open-ended tasks can be improved via self-play without external data or frontier-model judges, matching or surpassing GRPO_data trained on about 9K curated prompts.

title: Learning from Fine-Grained Visual Discrepancies: Mitigating Multimodal Hallucinations via In-Context Visual Contrastive Optimization
summary: Multimodal hallucination remains a persistent challenge for Vision-Language Models (VLMs). Standard textual Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) often fails to mitigate it due to a lack of explicit visual supervision. While existing works introduce visual preference DPO by contrasting original images against negative ones, they suffer from a theoretically inconsistent objective caused by partition function mismatches and rely on coarse-grained negatives that could enable shortcut learning. In this work, we propose In-Context Visual Contrastive Optimization (IC-VCO). By placing contrastive images within a shared multi-image context, IC-VCO ensures a mathematically rigorous objective. We further introduce Visual Contrast Distillation (VCDist), an auxiliary reliability-gated regularizer that encourages consistency between multi-image contrastive training and single-image inference.
