Finally, we propose a contrastive sample editing strategy that generates hard negatives via precise semantic perturbations. Experiments on five benchmarks demonstrate IC-VCO's best overall performance and the effectiveness of our sample editing strategy. Code and data are available at https://github.com/OPPO-Mente-Lab/IC-VCO.

AI.tldr: IC-VCO trains VLMs against hallucination by comparing images within the same context, making visual preference optimization theoretically sound; with gated distillation and harder edited negatives, it outperforms prior methods on five benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing textual DPO lacks explicit visual supervision and is weak at mitigating multimodal hallucination. Prior visual preference DPO methods use original-versus-negative image comparisons, but their objectives are theoretically inconsistent because of partition function mismatch and their negatives are often too coarse, which may encourage shortcut learning.
AI.method: The paper proposes In-Context Visual Contrastive Optimization (IC-VCO), which puts positive and contrastive images into a shared multi-image context to avoid partition function mismatch in prior visual preference DPO. It also adds Visual Contrast Distillation (VCDist), a reliability-gated auxiliary regularizer to transfer contrastive training signals to single-image inference, and introduces a contrastive sample editing strategy that creates hard negatives through precise semantic perturbations.
AI.result: Across five benchmarks, IC-VCO achieves the best overall performance and the proposed sample editing strategy is shown to be effective, indicating stronger robustness against multimodal hallucination than prior approaches.
AI.conclusion: IC-VCO provides a mathematically consistent visual preference optimization framework for reducing multimodal hallucination in VLMs, and its hard-negative editing plus reliability-gated distillation further improve alignment between training and inference.

title: Fine-grained Verification via Diagnostic Reasoning Supervision for Aspect Sentiment Triplet Extraction
summary: Aspect Sentiment Triplet Extraction (ASTE) aims to identify aspect terms, opinion terms, and sentiment polarities as structured triplets, providing essential inputs for downstream information system applications such as opinion mining, explainable recommendations, and review summarization. Prior work mainly focuses on end-to-end extraction, while post hoc verification of extracted triplets remains comparatively underexplored. This gap limits the reliability of ASTE systems, since predicted triplets may be locally plausible while being globally invalid. Moreover, candidate invalidity is multi-faceted and candidate usability is inherently graded, motivating a fine-grained verification mechanism that can filter or re-rank outputs from diverse extractors. In this paper, we propose FiVeD, a framework for Fine-grained Verification with Diagnostic reasoning supervision. Specifically, the verifier is trained with multiple complementary objectives, including validity classification and quality score estimation as primary tasks, with error type classification and rationale generation as auxiliary tasks. We define hierarchical error categories and construct plausible incorrect triplets under semantic and syntactic constraints, and leverage an off-the-shelf LLM with task-specific rubrics to produce quality scores and diagnostic rationales. During inference, the resulting quality scores are used to filter candidate outputs, supporting adjustable precision-recall tradeoffs. Experiments across multiple ASTE baselines demonstrate that FiVeD consistently improves extraction performance by up to 3.53 F1 points as a plug-and-play verification module.

AI.tldr: FiVeD 不直接替代 ASTE 抽取器，而是在抽取后增加一个“细粒度质检器”：它判断 triplet 是否有效、质量高低、错在哪里、理由是什么，再用质量分数过滤或重排结果，因此能稳定提升 ASTE 性能与可靠性。
AI.motivation: 现有 ASTE 研究主要关注端到端抽取，但对抽取后 triplet 的事后验证研究不足，导致系统可能输出局部合理但全局无效的结果。且候选错误具有多面性、候选可用性是分级的，因此需要一种细粒度验证机制来提升不同抽取器输出的可靠性。
AI.method: 论文提出 FiVeD 框架，对候选 aspect-opinion-sentiment triplets 进行细粒度验证。训练时结合多任务目标：有效性分类、质量分数估计、错误类型分类和依据/诊断理由生成；同时定义层次化错误类别，构造在语义和句法约束下看似合理但错误的 triplets，并利用现成 LLM 根据任务 rubric 生成质量分数与诊断理由。推理时使用质量分数对候选结果进行过滤或重排序。
AI.result: 在多个 ASTE 基线系统上的实验表明，FiVeD 作为 plug-and-play 验证模块能够持续改进抽取效果，最高带来 3.53 F1 的提升，并通过质量分数支持灵活筛选候选结果。
AI.conclusion: FiVeD 作为可插拔的细粒度验证模块，能在多个 ASTE 基线模型上稳定提升性能，最高提升 3.53 个 F1 点，并支持通过质量分数进行可调的精确率-召回率权衡。

title: DecMem: Towards Minute-Long Consistent World Generation with Decoupled Memory
comment: Project page is available at https://jeffreyyzh.github.io/DecMem-Page
summary: Recent advances in video generative models have promoted rapid progress in controllable world models. However, maintaining fine-grained spatio-temporal consistency under long-horizon reasoning remains a key challenge. In this work, we move beyond explicit 3D memory and coarse frame-level implicit modeling, and propose a fine-grained, learnable, and scalable memory for consistent world generation. We first identify two fundamental limitations of naïve learnable memory architectures in long-horizon extrapolation, namely computational inefficiency and attention dispersion. Through a systematic analysis of attention dispersion, we propose DecMem, a decoupled memory architecture that employs Sparse Global Memory for efficient fine-grained access to global history and Anchored Local Memory for stable and high-quality extrapolation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DecMem significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art methods. By ensuring precise and efficient long-term memory and achieving superior extrapolation capabilities, DecMem enables minute-level controllable long video generation with high fidelity and consistency.

AI.tldr: 论文提出DecMem，把长期视频生成中的记忆拆成“全局稀疏记忆+局部锚定记忆”，解决普通可学习记忆在长时程生成中的低效和注意力分散问题，从而实现更一致、更稳定、可分钟级扩展的可控视频生成。 / The paper introduces DecMem, which splits memory for long-video generation into sparse global memory and anchored local memory to fix inefficiency and attention dispersion, enabling more consistent, stable, minute-long controllable video generation.
AI.motivation: 现有可控世界模型在长时程推理下难以保持细粒度时空一致性；显式3D记忆和粗粒度帧级隐式建模都不足以支持高质量、可扩展的长期生成。 / Existing controllable world models struggle to preserve fine-grained spatio-temporal consistency over long horizons; explicit 3D memory and coarse frame-level implicit modeling are insufficient for scalable, high-quality long-term generation.
AI.method: 提出DecMem解耦记忆架构，包含Sparse Global Memory用于高效访问全局历史，Anchored Local Memory用于稳定且高质量的局部外推；同时针对朴素可学习记忆在长时程推理中的计算低效与注意力分散问题进行分析并设计改进。 / The paper proposes DecMem, a decoupled memory architecture with Sparse Global Memory for efficient access to global history and Anchored Local Memory for stable, high-quality local extrapolation, motivated by an analysis of computational inefficiency and attention dispersion in naive learnable memory.
AI.result: 大量实验表明，DecMem显著优于当前SOTA方法，在长期记忆精度、计算效率和视频外推质量方面都有明显提升。 / Extensive experiments show that DecMem substantially outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in long-term memory precision, computational efficiency, and video extrapolation quality.
AI.conclusion: DecMem通过解耦记忆架构显著提升了长时程可控视频世界模型中的时空一致性、效率与外推能力，从而支持高保真、分钟级长视频生成。 / DecMem significantly improves spatio-temporal consistency, efficiency, and extrapolation in long-horizon controllable video world models, enabling high-fidelity minute-long generation.

title: Translation Analytics for Freelancers II: Benchmarking Local LLMs for Confidential Translation Workflows
comment: 20 pages. Accepted at EAMT-2026 (Tilburg, Netherlands, June 2026)
summary: Building on our previous work, this paper develops practical, low-barrier methods for freelance translators and smaller language service providers to evaluate translation technologies using rigorous yet accessible analytic methods. Here we address a high-stakes, specialized need: offline translation for confidentiality-sensitive domains in which privacy constraints preclude the use of cloud-based engines and commercial LLMs. We expand the Reeve Foundation Trilingual Corpus (RFTC) used in our previous work into a multilingual corpus (RFMC) by adding sentence-aligned German and Simplified Chinese reference translations. We then benchmark several locally runnable language models (via Ollama) across four language directions on 1000+ sentences selected from this corpus. We use consistent single-prompt calls without fine-tuning or domain adaptation, comparing local LLM outputs against commercial NMTs (DeepL, Baidu), a frontier LLM (GPT-5.2), and professional-grade local NMT systems (OPUS-CAT, NeuralDesktop, Promt). Automatic evaluation is conducted with MATEO. Results reveal substantial variation in local LLM performance across language directions and model sizes. The best local LLMs match or surpass local NMT systems and a frontier LLM, though they remain behind top commercial NMTs. These findings underscore the viability of carefully selected local LLM translation for privacy-constrained professionals and inform future research on model scaling and multilingual capability.

AI.tldr: 论文构建并扩展了一个多语对齐语料库，用它评测多种离线本地LLM在隐私敏感翻译任务中的表现。结论是：本地LLM已能在部分方向上达到实用水平，但总体上仍逊于顶级商用机器翻译。
AI.motivation: 动机是为自由译者和中小语言服务提供商提供一种严谨但低门槛的翻译技术评估方法，特别针对无法使用云端引擎和商用LLM的高保密离线翻译需求。
AI.method: 作者将既有RFTC扩展为含德语和简体中文参考译文的多语语料RFMC，并基于其中1000多句、覆盖四个语言方向的数据，对若干可通过Ollama本地运行的LLM进行统一单提示、无微调、无领域适配的基准测试；同时与DeepL、百度、GPT-5.2及多种专业本地NMT系统进行对比，并使用MATEO进行自动评测。
AI.result: 结果显示，本地LLM在不同语言方向和模型规模上的表现差异显著；最佳本地LLM可匹配或超过本地NMT系统以及某前沿LLM，但仍不及最强商用NMT。
AI.conclusion: 本文认为，在隐私/保密约束场景下，经过谨慎选择的本地可运行LLM已具备实际翻译可行性；其性能可达到或超过部分本地NMT与前沿LLM，但整体仍落后于顶级商用NMT。

title: DEM: A Distilled Explanation Model for Interpretable Anomaly Detection in Physiological Sensor Networks
summary: Anomaly detection in physiological sensor data from Wireless Body Area Networks (WBANs) can be caused by sensor faults, network disruptions, or missing data, leading to false alarms. Hence, it demands both high predictive accuracy and clinically interpretable explanations. Existing approaches rely either on black-box models that achieve strong performance but offer no transparency, or on post-prediction explanation methods such as SHAP and LIME. In this paper, we propose the Distilled Explanation Model (DEM), a three-stage glass-box framework that distills the non-linear knowledge of a gradient boosting expert into an interpretable decision tree operating on residuals relative to a linear baseline, so that the explanation is not an approximation but the prediction itself. DEM introduces a novel distillation fidelity metric that quantifies how faithfully the explanation tree captures the expert model's non-linear contribution, providing a principled measure of explanation trustworthiness absent from prior interpretable models. Evaluated across four physiological datasets, including MIMIC-IV, WESAD, eICU, and an in-house SmartNet WBAN corpus, DEM achieves an AUC of 0.9964 on clinical contextual anomaly detection and 0.9047 on wearable stress detection while producing human-readable if-then rules at a controllable depth. Inference requires 0.17ms per 1000 samples, rendering DEM 1235x faster than SHAP-based post-hoc explanation and suitable for real-time physiological monitoring. Ablation studies confirm that the XGBoost distillation step provides measurable gains over naive residual fitting, and depth-sensitivity analysis demonstrates an explicit, user-controlled accuracy-interpretability trade-off unique to DEM among existing intrinsically interpretable models.

AI.tldr: DEM把黑盒梯度提升模型的非线性能力蒸馏进一个浅层可解释决策树，在保持很高异常检测性能的同时，直接给出可读规则，并用保真度指标衡量解释是否真正忠实。/ DEM distills the non-linear power of a gradient-boosting black box into a shallow interpretable decision tree, retaining strong anomaly-detection performance while directly producing readable rules and a fidelity metric to verify whether the explanation is truly faithful.
AI.motivation: 现有方法要么是高性能但不可解释的黑盒模型，要么依赖SHAP/LIME等事后解释，难以保证解释忠实且实时性不足。生理传感器异常检测又要求高准确率、临床可解释性和低延迟，因此需要一种兼顾性能、透明性与可验证解释可信度的方法。 / Existing methods are either accurate but opaque black boxes, or post-hoc explainers such as SHAP/LIME that may be unfaithful and too slow for real-time use. Physiological sensor anomaly detection requires high accuracy, clinical interpretability, and low latency, motivating a method that combines performance, transparency, and verifiable explanation fidelity.
AI.method: 方法为三阶段玻璃盒框架DEM：先建立线性基线，再用梯度提升模型（XGBoost）学习非线性残差贡献，最后将该专家模型的非线性知识蒸馏到一个作用于残差的可解释决策树中；树的输出本身就是预测解释，而非事后近似。/ The method is a three-stage glass-box framework, DEM: build a linear baseline, train a gradient-boosting expert (XGBoost) to model non-linear residual contributions, and distill that expert knowledge into an interpretable decision tree operating on residuals; the tree itself is the prediction, not a post-hoc approximation.
AI.result: 在MIMIC-IV、WESAD、eICU和SmartNet四个数据集上，DEM在临床上下文异常检测中达到0.9964 AUC，在可穿戴压力检测中达到0.9047 AUC；推理速度为每1000个样本0.17ms，比基于SHAP的事后解释快1235倍。消融实验表明XGBoost蒸馏优于朴素残差拟合，深度敏感性分析展示了可控的精度-可解释性权衡。 / On MIMIC-IV, WESAD, eICU, and SmartNet, DEM achieves an AUC of 0.9964 for clinical contextual anomaly detection and 0.9047 for wearable stress detection; inference takes 0.17 ms per 1000 samples, making it 1235x faster than SHAP-based post-hoc explanation. Ablations show measurable gains from XGBoost distillation over naive residual fitting, and depth-sensitivity analysis exposes a controllable accuracy-interpretability trade-off.
AI.conclusion: DEM在生理传感器/WBAN异常检测中实现了接近黑盒模型的高精度，同时直接输出可解释规则，并通过蒸馏保真度指标量化解释可信度，适合实时临床与可穿戴监测。 / DEM delivers near black-box-level accuracy for physiological/WBAN anomaly detection while producing directly interpretable rules and a fidelity metric for explanation trustworthiness, making it suitable for real-time clinical and wearable monitoring.

title: Scaling Conversational Hungarian ASR: The BEA-Dialogue+ Corpus
summary: Conversational automatic speech recognition in Hungarian is constrained by the limited amount of publicly available dialogue-style training data. The BEA-Dialogue corpus addresses this need, but its strictly speaker-disjoint train/dev/eval split reduces the usable material to only 85 hours. In this paper, we introduce BEA-Dialogue+, an expanded version of the corpus that relaxes the split criterion for experimenters and dialogue partners while preserving complete separation of the primary speakers. This results in 200 hours of transcribed natural conversations and enables a controlled study of the trade-off between additional training data and speaker overlap across the splits. We evaluate several Whisper- and FastConformer-based models on both corpus versions, including Serialized Output Training (SOT)-based fine-tuning for dialogue transcription. Our results show that the larger corpus is more challenging for models without fine-tuning, whereas SOT-based adaptation yields consistent improvements in WER, CER, cpWER, and cpCER. Overall, BEA-Dialogue+ provides a substantially larger yet still demanding benchmark for Hungarian dialogue ASR, and a practical resource for training and evaluating dialogue transcription systems.

AI.tldr: The paper expands a Hungarian dialogue ASR corpus from 85h to 200h by loosening some speaker split rules, then shows that although the new benchmark is harder, SOT fine-tuning reliably improves Whisper and FastConformer transcription performance.
AI.motivation: Hungarian conversational ASR suffers from a shortage of publicly available dialogue-style training data. The original BEA-Dialogue corpus is useful but overly restrictive in its split policy, leaving only 85 hours for experimentation, which limits model training and analysis.
AI.method: The paper constructs BEA-Dialogue+ by relaxing speaker-disjoint constraints for experimenters and dialogue partners while keeping the main speakers separated across train/dev/eval. It then evaluates Whisper- and FastConformer-based models on both the original and expanded corpora, including Serialized Output Training (SOT)-based fine-tuning for dialogue ASR.
AI.result: BEA-Dialogue+ provides 200 hours of transcribed natural conversations, enabling controlled analysis of the trade-off between more training data and speaker overlap. Models without fine-tuning find the larger corpus more difficult, but SOT-based adaptation consistently reduces WER, CER, cpWER, and cpCER.
AI.conclusion: BEA-Dialogue+ significantly enlarges the available Hungarian conversational ASR benchmark from 85 to 200 hours while retaining primary-speaker separation. It remains challenging, but SOT-based fine-tuning consistently improves dialogue transcription quality across multiple error metrics.

title: Triangle Splatting SLAM
summary: We present a dense RGB-D SLAM system using differentiable triangles as the 3D map representation. While 3D Gaussian Splatting has emerged as the leading method for novel-view synthesis, triangles remain the standard primitive for traditional rendering hardware, game engines, and downstream tasks requiring explicit geometry such as simulation, collision, and editing. Recent offline methods have demonstrated that an unstructured 'triangle soup' can be optimised into a photorealistic mesh via Delaunay triangulation across a set of posed images. Building upon this insight, we present the first dense SLAM system to employ Triangle Splatting to perform both tracking and mapping through online differentiable rendering of a triangle soup. The map can be converted into a connected mesh on-the-fly via restricted Delaunay triangulation, enabling new online capabilities such as mesh deformation and collision checking. On Replica and TUM-RGBD, our system outperforms baselines on 3D geometry, matches the camera-tracking accuracy, and enables online mesh-based scene editing.

AI.tldr: A dense RGB-D SLAM system uses differentiable triangle splatting instead of Gaussians, builds an online triangle-soup map, converts it to a mesh with Delaunay triangulation, improves geometry quality, keeps tracking competitive, and enables real-time mesh editing.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that although 3D Gaussian Splatting is strong for novel-view synthesis, triangles remain more practical and standard for rendering hardware, game engines, and downstream applications that require explicit geometry. The work aims to bring the advantages of triangle-based photorealistic reconstruction into an online dense SLAM setting.
AI.method: The method represents the scene as a triangle soup and performs both tracking and mapping through online differentiable rendering with triangle splatting. It also converts the triangle soup into a connected mesh on the fly using restricted Delaunay triangulation, enabling explicit geometric reasoning during SLAM.
AI.result: On Replica and TUM-RGBD, the system outperforms baselines on 3D geometry reconstruction, matches camera tracking accuracy, and demonstrates online mesh-based scene editing capabilities.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that an online dense RGB-D SLAM system built on differentiable triangle splatting can achieve stronger 3D geometry quality than prior baselines, maintain comparable camera tracking accuracy, and additionally support online mesh-centric operations such as deformation, collision checking, and scene editing.

title: Physics-Informed Coarsening for Multigrid Graph Neural Surrogates
summary: Learning-based surrogates for partial differential equations have recently matched the accuracy of classical solvers while achieving orders-of-magnitude speedups, predominantly in fluid settings and structured geometries. In contrast, robust surrogates for deformable solids remain underexplored, despite the presence of nonlinear elasticity, plasticity, and transient behavior that challenge standard architectures. We introduce a multigrid graph neural network for solid mechanics that couples an encoder-processor-decoder backbone with a physics-informed coarsening strategy. Instead of downsampling via geometric heuristics, our method scores nodes using a residual-based measure of local physical activity and preferentially retains regions of high strain or stress concentration, allocating multiscale capacity where it is most needed. This preserves long-range interactions through hierarchical message passing while improving stability over long rollouts. We evaluate on multiple datasets covering linear, nonlinear, and transient regimes, and observe consistent gains in accuracy and rollout stability compared to standard sampling baselines. Our results highlight the importance of physics-informed coarsening for scalable surrogate modeling in solid mechanics.

AI.tldr: A multigrid GNN for solid mechanics uses residual-based, physics-informed coarsening to keep important high-stress/high-strain regions, improving accuracy and long-term stability over conventional downsampling methods.
AI.motivation: Existing learning-based PDE surrogates have shown strong performance mainly in fluids and structured geometries, while deformable solid mechanics remains less explored because nonlinear elasticity, plasticity, and transient dynamics are difficult for standard architectures. The work aims to build a more robust and scalable surrogate for solids.
AI.method: The paper proposes a multigrid graph neural network with an encoder-processor-decoder architecture and a physics-informed coarsening strategy. Node retention is guided by a residual-based score of local physical activity, so regions with high strain or stress concentration are preserved across scales for hierarchical message passing.
AI.result: Across multiple datasets spanning linear, nonlinear, and transient solid mechanics regimes, the proposed method consistently outperforms standard sampling baselines in prediction accuracy and rollout stability.
AI.conclusion: Physics-informed coarsening in a multigrid graph neural network improves scalable surrogate modeling for solid mechanics, yielding better accuracy and more stable long-horizon rollouts than standard sampling baselines.

title: Language Models Can Resolve Reference Compositionally, But It's Not Their Native Strength: The Case of the Personal Relation Task
comment: A pre-MIT Press publication version. Paper accepted to Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
summary: Do neural models, such as Large Language Models, genuinely acquire compositional abilities for interpretation of natural language? When we talk about semantic interpretation, we can distinguish two complementary aspects: establishing what an expression refers to in the world (which we call the Extensional task) and representing its sense in a structured way (which we call the Intensional task). We evaluate LLMs and humans on both tasks in the setting of the Personal Relation Task (Paperno 2022) in which, given a universe of people and their relationships with each other, one is asked to interpret a noun phrase such as "Amber's parent's friend". Here, for the Intensional task, the answer is the formula "friend(parent(amber))", and for the Extensional task, the person. We find that humans and LLMs show opposite strengths: humans perform better on Extensional than Intensional tasks, and LLMs vice versa. Our methodology brings greater nuance to the understanding of compositional abilities in modern machine learning models. Our results support the notion that the lack of referential grounding in LLM training is a crucial missing component in mimicking human-like language understanding.

AI.tldr: The paper splits compositional meaning into structured form vs real-world reference and shows a crossover: LLMs are better at the structured/formal side, humans are better at the grounded/reference side.
AI.motivation: The study asks whether neural models, especially LLMs, truly acquire compositional semantics. It aims to disentangle two complementary aspects of meaning, reference and structured sense, instead of treating semantic competence as a single ability.
AI.method: The paper evaluates humans and LLMs on the Personal Relation Task, separating semantic interpretation into two subtasks: Extensional interpretation (mapping a noun phrase to the correct person in a relational world) and Intensional interpretation (mapping the phrase to a compositional formal expression such as friend(parent(amber))).
AI.result: Humans perform better on extensional tasks than intensional tasks, whereas LLMs perform better on intensional tasks than extensional tasks. The contrast reveals different strengths and weaknesses in semantic processing between humans and LLMs.
AI.conclusion: LLMs appear stronger at producing structured intensional representations than at resolving grounded extensional references, while humans show the opposite pattern. This suggests that missing referential grounding is a major limitation of LLMs for human-like semantic understanding.

title: YARD: Y-Architecture Register Decoding for Efficient Hallucination Mitigation in Large Vision-Language Models
summary: Contrastive decoding (CD) seeks to mitigate hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) by contrasting the output distributions of a standard model and a visually degraded model. However, existing training-free CD methods suffer from sub-optimal degraded branches: completely dropping visual tokens is too extreme and induces language hallucinations, while corrupting input images offers coarse control over visual evidence and suffers from high inference latency due to requiring two full forward passes. To address these dilemmas, we propose YARD, a training-free Y-Architecture Register Decoding framework. Motivated by the observation that reliable text-to-vision grounding predominantly emerges in the middle decoder layers, YARD constructs the degraded branch internally by sharing shallow-layer computations and branching exactly at this critical stage. For the degraded branch, YARD replaces patch-level visual tokens with register tokens, which preserve global image semantics but lack fine-grained local evidence. This image-aware yet locally under-grounded design provides a faithful contrastive signal without extreme modality mismatch, while the Y-architecture strictly avoids a costly second forward pass. Extensive experiments on generative and discriminative hallucination benchmarks demonstrate that YARD consistently achieves state-of-the-art hallucination mitigation across multiple LVLMs, alongside a significant reduction in inference latency.

AI.tldr: YARD把对比解码的“退化分支”搬到模型内部中层来做：共享前半段计算，并用保留全局语义的register tokens替代局部视觉patch，从而以更低延迟提供更可靠的对比信号，最终更好地减少LVLM幻觉。 / YARD internalizes the degraded branch of contrastive decoding at middle decoder layers, shares early computation, and swaps local visual patches for semantic register tokens, yielding a more faithful contrastive signal, lower latency, and better hallucination reduction in LVLMs.
AI.motivation: 现有无训练CD方法的退化分支设计不理想：直接丢弃视觉token过于极端，容易引入语言幻觉；图像扰动控制粗糙且需要两次完整前向传播，推理延迟高。因此需要一种既保留图像感知、又能削弱局部证据，同时更高效的退化分支构造方式。 / Existing training-free CD methods use poor degraded branches: dropping visual tokens is too extreme and causes language hallucination, while corrupting images is coarse and requires two full forward passes, creating high latency. A more faithful and efficient degraded branch is needed.
AI.method: 提出YARD：一种training-free的Y-Architecture Register Decoding框架。它共享浅层解码计算，在中层关键grounding阶段构造退化分支；退化分支中用保留全局语义但缺乏局部细节证据的register tokens替换patch-level视觉token，再与标准分支进行contrastive decoding。 / The paper proposes YARD, a training-free Y-Architecture Register Decoding framework that shares shallow decoder computation, branches at the middle grounding-critical layers, replaces patch-level visual tokens with register tokens in the degraded branch, and performs contrastive decoding against the standard branch.
AI.result: 在生成式和判别式幻觉基准上的大量实验表明，YARD在多个LVLM上持续取得最先进的幻觉缓解效果，并显著降低推理延迟。 / Extensive experiments on generative and discriminative hallucination benchmarks show that YARD consistently delivers state-of-the-art hallucination mitigation across multiple LVLMs while significantly reducing inference latency.
AI.conclusion: YARD通过在关键中层解码层处分叉并用register tokens替代局部patch视觉token，能够在无需训练的前提下更有效、更高效地缓解LVLM幻觉，并在多个基准和模型上达到SOTA且降低推理延迟。 / YARD shows that a training-free Y-architecture with mid-layer branching and register-token-based degraded vision can mitigate LVLM hallucinations more effectively and efficiently, achieving SOTA results with lower inference latency.

title: BenHalluEval: A Multi-Task Hallucination Evaluation Framework for Large Language Models on Bengali
summary: Despite Bengali being the sixth most spoken language in the world, no prior work has systematically evaluated hallucination in large language models (LLMs) for Bengali. We introduce BenHalluEval, a fine-grained hallucination evaluation framework for Bengali covering four tasks: Generative Question Answering (GQA), Bangla-English Code-Mixed QA, Summarization, and Reasoning. We construct 12,000 hallucinated candidates using GPT-5.4 across twelve task-specific hallucination types, drawn from three existing Bengali datasets, and evaluate seven LLMs spanning reasoning-oriented, multilingual, and Bengali-centric categories under a dual-track protocol that independently measures false-positive rate on ground-truth instances (Track A) and hallucination detection rate on hallucinated candidates (Track B). To jointly penalise both failure modes and prevent inflated scores from uniform response bias, we propose BenHalluScore, a dual-track calibration metric that ranges from 7.72% to 55.42% across models and tasks, revealing substantial variation in hallucination calibration. Chain-of-thought prompting, applied as a mitigation strategy, shifts response distributions without consistently improving hallucination discrimination. BenHalluEval establishes the first dedicated hallucination benchmark for Bengali and highlights the inadequacy of single-track and prompting-only evaluation approaches for low-resource language settings. The dataset and code are available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/BanglaHalluEval-EB77.

AI.tldr: This paper builds the first Bengali hallucination benchmark, evaluates seven LLMs on 12,000 synthetic hallucination cases across four tasks, and proposes a dual-track score showing that current models are poorly and unevenly calibrated, while chain-of-thought prompting is not a reliable fix.
AI.motivation: Although Bengali is one of the most widely spoken languages, there had been no systematic benchmark for measuring hallucination in LLMs for Bengali. Existing evaluation approaches are inadequate for low-resource language settings, especially when they rely on only one track or prompting-based mitigation.
AI.method: The paper introduces BenHalluEval, a fine-grained Bengali hallucination evaluation framework over four tasks: generative QA, Bangla-English code-mixed QA, summarization, and reasoning. It constructs 12,000 hallucinated candidates with GPT-5.4 across twelve task-specific hallucination types from three Bengali datasets, evaluates seven LLMs under a dual-track protocol, and proposes BenHalluScore to jointly measure false positives on ground-truth instances and hallucination detection on hallucinated candidates.
AI.result: Across models and tasks, BenHalluScore ranges from 7.72% to 55.42%, indicating large differences in hallucination calibration. The experiments show that chain-of-thought prompting changes response distributions but does not consistently improve hallucination discrimination.
AI.conclusion: BenHalluEval is the first dedicated benchmark for evaluating hallucination in Bengali LAG/LLM settings, and the study shows that hallucination calibration varies substantially across models. It also finds that single-track evaluation and prompting-only mitigation, such as chain-of-thought, are insufficient for reliably assessing or reducing hallucinations in low-resource languages.

title: Astra: a generalizable report generation foundation model for 3D computed tomography
summary: CT interpretation requires radiologists to review hundreds of volumetric slices per examination, making reporting time-consuming and highly expertise-dependent. Automated CT report generation offers a promising route to improving clinical efficiency, yet the field still lacks a generalizable CT report generation foundation model that supports multi-region reporting and remains robust across external real-world cohorts. Intrinsic inconsistencies in reporting style and diagnostic terminology across cohorts make naive joint training prone to noisy textual supervision, thereby limiting model generalizability. Here we present Astra, a generalizable CT report generation foundation model trained on 90,678 thoracoabdominal CT-report pairs (CTRgDB) with 353,671 abnormalities spanning eight organ systems. By harmonizing report style and further refining diagnostic consistency via reinforcement learning, Astra achieves style-consistent and diagnostically accurate report generation across diverse anatomical regions and institutions. Evaluating on CTRgDB and six external cohorts, Astra achieves state-of-the-art performance with a 44.1% average improvement in fine-grained diagnostic metrics (P<0.001). In real-world clinical workflows, Astra assistance accelerates chest report drafting by 29.6% and improves abdominal report completeness by 11.3% (P<0.001). Furthermore, Astra also demonstrates broad utility as a foundation for CT AI development, improving downstream diagnostic performance and scaling vision-language pretrain through high-quality report synthesis. Overall, Astra serves as a broadly accessible clinical assistant and a pivotal infrastructure for the next generation of AI-powered healthcare.

AI.tldr: Astra trains a large CT report generation model on a harmonized multi-institution thoracoabdominal dataset and uses reinforcement learning to improve diagnostic consistency, leading to more accurate, style-consistent reports and measurable gains in both benchmark performance and real clinical efficiency.
AI.motivation: CT interpretation is labor-intensive because radiologists must review hundreds of slices per study. Existing automated CT report generation methods lack a generalizable foundation model for multi-region reporting and are vulnerable to cross-cohort inconsistencies in reporting style and diagnostic terminology.
AI.method: The paper builds Astra using 90,678 thoracoabdominal CT-report pairs from CTRgDB with 353,671 abnormalities across eight organ systems. It harmonizes report style across cohorts and further refines diagnostic consistency using reinforcement learning to reduce noisy textual supervision from heterogeneous reporting styles and terminology.
AI.result: On CTRgDB and six external cohorts, Astra achieves state-of-the-art performance with a 44.1% average improvement in fine-grained diagnostic metrics (P<0.001). In clinical workflows, Astra assistance speeds up chest report drafting by 29.6% and improves abdominal report completeness by 11.3% (P<0.001). It also benefits downstream diagnostic tasks and vision-language pretraining through high-quality synthetic reports.
AI.conclusion: Astra is a generalizable CT report generation foundation model that produces style-consistent and diagnostically accurate multi-region reports across institutions, improves clinical workflow efficiency, and serves as useful infrastructure for downstream CT AI development.

title: Annealed Softmax Greedy in Many-Armed Bayesian Bandits
summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) and group-based policy optimization methods such as GRPO update a stochastic policy by sampling multiple completions per prompt and increasing the policy's probability on those with higher reward, regularized by a KL penalty toward a reference policy. These updates do not include explicit mechanisms that track epistemic uncertainty. This paper studies a stylized explanation for why such uncertainty-agnostic updates can nevertheless be effective. We analyze an annealed softmax (Boltzmann) policy that selects actions according to a softmax of empirical mean rewards in a many-armed Bayesian Bernoulli bandit. Under a linear upper-tail condition on the prior (the $β=1$ case of $β$-regularity), which implies an abundance of near-optimal arms, we prove that annealed softmax greedy achieves Bayes regret $\tilde{O}(m + T/m)$, and in particular $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{T})$ when the number of arms scales as $m = Θ(\sqrt{T})$. This is the near-optimal Bayes regret rate in this regime, attained also by empirical-mean greedy. Under $β$-regularity, many arms maintain empirical means close to the optimum throughout learning, so when softmax samples an arm other than the empirically best, that arm tends to be another near-optimal one rather than a clearly inferior one. By contrast, with a small number of arms, the same kind of softmax policy can suffer linear regret. The result also provides a structural analogy to RLVR, where a base policy with a non-negligible probability of producing a correct completion plays the role of $β$-regularity.

AI.tldr: 论文证明：在“好答案很多”的 many-armed bandit 里，只按经验均值做退火 softmax 采样，即使不建模不确定性，也能达到接近最优的 \tilde{O}(\sqrt{T}) Bayes regret；但如果可选臂太少，这种方法可能退化到线性 regret。这为 RLVR/GRPO 为什么常常有效提供了一个理论化解释。
AI.motivation: RLVR 和 GRPO 通过基于奖励提升高回报输出概率，并用 KL 约束参考策略，但没有显式跟踪 epistemic uncertainty。作者希望解释：为什么这种对不确定性不敏感的更新在实践中仍可能表现良好。
AI.method: 论文在 many-armed Bayesian Bernoulli bandit 中分析一种退火 softmax（Boltzmann）策略：根据各臂经验平均奖励的 softmax 分布采样动作，并研究其 Bayes regret。在 β=1 的上尾正则条件下给出理论证明，并与 empirical-mean greedy 以及小臂数情形做对比。
AI.result: 主要结果是：在 many-armed、存在大量近优臂的先验结构下，annealed softmax greedy 的探索即使不依赖显式不确定性估计，也不会频繁落到明显劣质臂上，因此可实现 \tilde{O}(m + T/m) 的 Bayes regret；而在小臂数情形下，同类 softmax 策略可能遭受线性 regret。论文还指出这与 RLVR 的结构类比：基础策略若对正确答案已有非忽略概率质量，就类似于 β-regularity。
AI.conclusion: 在满足线性上尾先验条件（β=1 regularity）且存在大量近最优臂时，不显式建模认知不确定性的退火 softmax greedy 仍可达到近最优 Bayes regret：\tilde{O}(m + T/m)，当 m=Θ(\sqrt{T}) 时为 \tilde{O}(\sqrt{T})。这解释了为何类似 RLVR/GRPO 这类 uncertainty-agnostic 更新在合适结构条件下依然有效。

title: An Efficient and Scalable Graph Condensation with Structure-Preserving
summary: Graph condensation (GC) is pivotal for enabling Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) deployment in resource-constrained scenarios by compressing large-scale graphs into compact synthetic counterparts. Existing GC methods commonly suffer from computational inefficiency due to coupled optimization as well as encountering poor generalization across GNN architectures. To address these challenges, this study proposes an Efficient and Scalable Graph Condensation with Structure-Preserving (SP-ESGC), which possesses a decoupled design that separates node condensation from graph structure generation. Specifically, it first employs heat kernel feature propagation to generate node representation via spectral graph theory-inspired diffusion. Further, a novel hybrid clustering strategy is designed to extracts discriminative intra-class centroids from the node representation. Finally, a pre-trained edge predictor infers transferable structural patterns from the original graph, ensuring accurate synthetic graph generation. Extensive experiments on real-world graph datasets demonstrate that the proposed SP-ESGC implementes a precise GC with significantly high computational efficiency. Moreover, SP-ESGC also generalizes well across diverse GNN architectures.

AI.tldr: SP-ESGC is a decoupled graph condensation method that builds compact synthetic graphs efficiently by combining heat-kernel node encoding, hybrid clustering, and a pre-trained edge predictor; it is faster and generalizes better across GNNs than prior GC methods.
AI.motivation: Existing graph condensation methods are often computationally expensive because of coupled optimization and tend to generalize poorly across different GNN architectures. The paper aims to make graph condensation both more efficient and more architecture-transferable for resource-constrained deployment.
AI.method: The method uses a decoupled pipeline: (1) heat-kernel-based feature propagation to obtain node representations, (2) a hybrid clustering strategy to extract discriminative intra-class centroids as condensed nodes, and (3) a pre-trained edge predictor to generate the synthetic graph structure by transferring structural patterns from the original graph.
AI.result: Experiments on real-world graph datasets show that SP-ESGC achieves precise graph condensation with substantially improved computational efficiency and good generalization across diverse GNN backbones.
AI.conclusion: SP-ESGC enables accurate and efficient graph condensation by decoupling node condensation and structure generation, while preserving transferable graph structure and showing strong cross-architecture generalization on multiple real-world datasets.

title: Are Full Rollouts Necessary for On-Policy Distillation?
summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) provides dense teacher feedback along rollouts generated by the student and has emerged as a promising post-training paradigm for long-horizon reasoning. However, standard OPD typically generates full rollouts during training, which is computationally expensive and may expose the student to unreliable teacher feedback at late rollout positions, especially during early training. We identify the rollout horizon as a key bottleneck in OPD that substantially impacts training efficiency. Unlike Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR), OPD does not require a complete trajectory or a final answer reward to provide learning signals. This observation suggests that full rollouts may not always be necessary for effective OPD. Motivated by this insight, we propose two simple horizon-control strategies: Progressive OPD (POPD), which gradually expands the rollout horizon during training, and Truncated OPD (TOPD), which permanently performs distillation on reliable truncated rollouts. Experiments on mathematical reasoning show that POPD improves the training efficiency of OPD by up to 3$\times$, while TOPD matches OPD performance using only 10\% of the rollout horizon, leading to substantial wall-clock and memory reductions. These results demonstrate that controlling the rollout horizon offers a simple and practical path to more efficient OPD.

AI.tldr: 通过缩短或逐步增加蒸馏时的rollout长度，作者让OPD更便宜、更快，并基本保持原有效果。 / By shortening or gradually increasing the rollout length used for distillation, the authors make OPD cheaper and faster while largely preserving performance.
AI.motivation: 标准OPD通常需要生成完整rollouts，计算成本高，而且在训练早期后段位置的教师反馈可能不可靠；作者因此将rollout horizon识别为影响效率的关键瓶颈，并指出OPD不像RLVR那样必须依赖完整轨迹或最终奖励。 / Standard OPD relies on full rollouts, which are computationally expensive, and late-step teacher feedback can be unreliable early in training; the authors therefore identify rollout horizon as a key efficiency bottleneck and note that OPD, unlike RLVR, does not inherently require full trajectories or final-answer rewards.
AI.method: 论文提出两种horizon-control策略：Progressive OPD (POPD)，在训练过程中逐步扩大rollout horizon；Truncated OPD (TOPD)，始终只在截断且更可靠的rollouts上进行蒸馏。 / The paper proposes two horizon-control strategies: Progressive OPD (POPD), which gradually expands the rollout horizon during training, and Truncated OPD (TOPD), which always distills on truncated, more reliable rollouts.
AI.result: 在数学推理实验中，POPD将OPD训练效率最高提升到3倍；TOPD仅使用10%的rollout horizon即可达到与标准OPD相当的性能，同时显著降低训练时间和内存消耗。 / In mathematical reasoning experiments, POPD improves OPD training efficiency by up to 3x; TOPD matches standard OPD performance using only 10% of the rollout horizon, substantially reducing training time and memory usage.
AI.conclusion: 控制OPD中的rollout horizon能够在不显著损失性能的前提下，大幅提升训练效率并降低墙钟时间与显存开销。 / Controlling the rollout horizon in OPD substantially improves training efficiency while reducing wall-clock time and memory cost without meaningful performance loss.

title: VisionPulse: Dynamic Visual Sparsity for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning
summary: With the rapid advancement of large multimodal models (LMMs), inference-time overhead has become a key bottleneck for real-world deployment. Existing methods typically prune visual tokens at prefill, assuming the required visual evidence remains static during reasoning. However, we empirically show that visual evidence is strongly step-dependent: only a sparse subset of visual tokens is critical at each decoding step, and the critical set evolves across reasoning. Furthermore, we identify a coupled bottleneck where redundant visual context can steer the model toward query-irrelevant regions, lengthening the reasoning trace. Guided by these insights, we propose VisionPulse, a step-wise visual token pruning framework during reasoning. VisionPulse computes a lightweight visual attention mass to estimate the step-wise retention budget by exploiting its strong positive correlation with LMMs' effective visual token usage and retain only the most critical tokens under this budget. By enforcing visual sparsity during reasoning, VisionPulse filters redundant visual context while preserving relevant visual evidence, shortening reasoning traces naturally. Extensive experiments show that VisionPulse only retains 5% of visual tokens per step with reasoning traces shortened by 11.2%, while keeping accuracy almost unchanged.

AI.tldr: VisionPulse prunes visual tokens dynamically at each reasoning step instead of once at prefill, using attention mass to estimate how many tokens to keep. This removes redundant visual context, shortens reasoning, and preserves accuracy while using only about 5% of visual tokens per step.
AI.motivation: Existing multimodal acceleration methods usually prune visual tokens only at prefill, assuming needed visual evidence is fixed throughout reasoning. The paper argues this assumption is wrong because important visual tokens change across decoding steps, and redundant visual context can distract the model toward irrelevant regions and increase inference cost.
AI.method: The paper proposes VisionPulse, a step-wise visual token pruning framework used during reasoning. It estimates a per-step token retention budget with a lightweight visual attention mass metric, then keeps only the most critical visual tokens at each decoding step under that budget.
AI.result: Across extensive experiments, VisionPulse retains only 5% of visual tokens per decoding step, shortens reasoning traces by 11.2%, and keeps task accuracy almost unchanged.
AI.conclusion: VisionPulse demonstrates that visual evidence usage in large multimodal models is step-dependent during decoding, so step-wise pruning is more effective than static prefill pruning. It can keep accuracy nearly unchanged while greatly reducing visual token usage and shortening reasoning traces.

title: Augmented Lagrangian Predictive Coding
summary: Predictive coding (PC) is a local-learning alternative to backpropagation (BP), training deep networks via local energy-minimization dynamics rather than a global backward pass. We introduce Augmented Lagrangian Predictive Coding (PC-ALM), which maintains PC's inference budget but aligns each weight update toward BP by accumulating per-layer constraint errors into a layer-local Lagrange multiplier. In linear PC networks, PC-ALM converges to an equilibrium with exact BP gradients distributed across the network via only layer-local updates. We analyze PC-ALM in nonlinear PC networks up to depth 128 and show that it matches BP performance across all width-depth regimes, notably in deep narrow networks where PC underperforms. PC-ALM introduces recurrent dynamics in each layer's activations. Compared to PC's heat flow on a scalar energy, PC-ALM dynamics are driven by dual ascent on the augmented Lagrangian. We observe "ballistic" credit propagation across very deep networks, with credit signals evenly distributed across layers, compared to PC's slow, diffusive credit propagation. Beyond the algorithm itself, the augmented Lagrangian framework offers a generalization of PC, and may yield insights into how distributed systems could compute and propagate BP-like credit signals through purely local dynamics.

AI.tldr: PC-ALM adds local Lagrange multipliers to predictive coding so deep networks can propagate BP-like credit signals through purely local dynamics; it provably recovers exact BP gradients in linear nets and empirically matches BP in very deep nonlinear nets.
AI.motivation: Standard predictive coding is appealing as a biologically and locally plausible alternative to backpropagation, but its credit propagation is slow and can diverge from BP, especially in deep narrow networks. The work aims to keep PC's local-learning character and inference budget while making its updates align much more closely with BP.
AI.method: The paper proposes Augmented Lagrangian Predictive Coding (PC-ALM). It augments standard predictive coding with per-layer constraint-error accumulation through local Lagrange multipliers, and performs learning through local recurrent activation dynamics plus dual ascent on an augmented Lagrangian instead of only minimizing a scalar energy.
AI.result: In linear PC networks, PC-ALM reaches an equilibrium that distributes exact BP gradients using only layer-local updates. In nonlinear networks up to depth 128, it matches BP across width-depth settings and substantially improves over standard PC in regimes where PC struggles, with faster, more evenly distributed 'ballistic' credit propagation across layers.
AI.conclusion: PC-ALM extends predictive coding with layer-local Lagrange multipliers so that local inference dynamics can recover backpropagation-consistent credit assignment. In linear networks it converges to exact BP gradients, and in deep nonlinear networks it reaches BP-level performance while preserving local updates.
